Real-world success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data strategies, and combining KD with complementary compression methods and task-aware engineering to mitigate robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift challenges.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Practical and Robust Knowledge Distillation for Deployable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central tool for compressing large deep models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and power constraints. Beyond matching teacher output probabilities, modern distillation should transfer internal structure, be tailored to domain and modality differences, and integrate with quantization, privacy, and data-limited settings. When applied with methods that address representation mismatch, optimization challenges, and curriculum of supervisory signals, distillation enables small models that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Pragmatic Tool for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely one technique among many for model compression: when applied thoughtfully it is a central, practical lever for producing small, fast models that retain much of the performance, robustness, and task-specific behavior of large teachers. Best practice couples KD with representation-level supervision, teacher-student co-design, data and privacy strategies, and complementary compression methods so that compact models meet real-world latency, memory and heterogeneity constraints.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. The literature frames distillation as a multifaceted toolkit — including soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi- and self-teaching, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols — that is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and task-aware engineering. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity and data constraints, and on explicitly addressing failure modes such as transferred biases, optimization mismatch, and poor handling of low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Advantages, Limits, and Design Guidelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic framework for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. When integrated with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and thoughtful data strategies, KD routinely yields strong size–performance trade-offs across vision and language tasks. However, realizing KD’s full potential in production demands context-sensitive choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to address robustness, fairness, privacy, and domain-shift concerns. I argue KD should be treated as the central, configurable element of compression pipelines, paired with concrete safeguards and evaluation practices to avoid well-known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Garner
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade the field has expanded from soft-target/logit matching to include intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational and set-oriented objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware protocols (including data-free and zero-shot approaches). Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, combining KD with other compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search), addressing data and privacy constraints, and evaluating robustness and fairness under distribution shift. While KD routinely yields strong efficiency–performance trade-offs, open problems remain around optimization dynamics, preservation of rare behaviours, and principled data-synthesis strategies.

papers_seen.author: Juarez
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical family of techniques that transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models so students can meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, energy, or privacy) while retaining much of teacher performance. The literature describes a spectrum of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational maps, and module-level behaviors), teacher–student variants (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation), and data regimes (full-data, few-shot, and data-free adversarial synthesis). KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, progressive module replacement) and when practitioners attend to teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and robustness or fairness requirements. Open challenges include distillation under severe data heterogeneity, preserving rare-token or fine-grained behavior, and principled guarantees about robustness and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Wide Neural Networks: Risk Bound, Data Efficiency and Imperfect Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a strategy of training a student network with guide of the soft output from a teacher network. It has been a successful method of model compression and knowledge transfer. However, currently knowledge distillation lacks a convincing theoretical understanding. On the other hand, recent finding on neural tangent kernel enables us to approximate a wide neural network with a linear model of the network's random features. In this paper, we theoretically analyze the knowledge distillation of a wide neural network. First we provide a transfer risk bound for the linearized model of the network. Then we propose a metric of the task's training difficulty, called data inefficiency. Based on this metric, we show that for a perfect teacher, a high ratio of teacher's soft labels can be beneficial. Finally, for the case of imperfect teacher, we find that hard labels can correct teacher's wrong prediction, which explains the practice of mixing hard and soft labels.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Romero
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision and NLP, KD has evolved from soft-target matching into a flexible toolbox that includes representation-level alignment, attention and relational signals, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data strategies such as augmentation or synthetic/data-free generation. KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful engineering to match student capacity, select appropriate signals, and manage data or privacy constraints. While KD routinely yields substantial efficiency gains with modest accuracy loss, practitioners must address failure modes such as capacity mismatch, distribution shift, degraded rare-token behavior, and propagation of teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD methods span softened-output matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational or ensemble signals, and a range of training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, self‑distillation and data‑free approaches). In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when the distillation pipeline is matched to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. Key limitations remain in handling capacity and optimization mismatch, low-frequency or rare-token behavior, robustness under distribution shift, and the risk of propagating teacher biases; addressing these requires careful signal selection, teacher–student co-design, appropriate data strategies (including synthetic data), and principled evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Drake
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Composable Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Sensitive Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for producing compact deep and NLP models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD delivers strong size–performance trade-offs when its signals, data strategy, and student capacity are aligned with deployment constraints, but it requires explicit handling of capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity, rare-token behaviors, and bias to be reliable in production.

papers_seen.author: Guerrero
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated as a flexible, central component of compression pipelines rather than a single fixed recipe. When combined with representation-level supervision, teacher–student co-design, data-aware strategies, and complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), KD enables small, efficient models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD also carries risks—transfer of teacher biases, sensitivity to data heterogeneity, and capacity mismatch—that require careful mitigation and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Burgess
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective family of techniques for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers so they can be deployed under compute, memory, latency, or privacy constraints. KD ranges from matching softened teacher outputs to aligning intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational structures, and it is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and careful engineering of teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and robustness/fairness evaluations. Practical deployment emphasizes student capacity, data curricula (including synthetic or privacy‑aware data), and targeted diagnostics for long‑tail or distributional failures.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach that enables deployment of large deep and language models by training smaller students to retain much of teacher performance. KD supports a range of transfer signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, relational signals) and composes naturally with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design). When designed as a tailored pipeline—matching distilled signals, student capacity, and data strategy—KD delivers substantial runtime and memory savings with modest accuracy loss. However, KD is not a universal cure: preserving rare-case behavior, avoiding propagation of teacher flaws, and handling data- or privacy-constrained settings require explicit engineering and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models by transferring information from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student, enabling deployment under computation, memory, and latency constraints. A range of techniques—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, multi-stage pipelines, and data synthesis—have been developed to address diverse practical needs such as on-device inference, privacy-sensitive releases, federated settings, and domain shifts. Combining KD with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and adapting distillation signals to task and deployment constraints yields the best real-world outcomes, while open challenges remain around handling distribution shift, data scarcity, and student–teacher capacity mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Riggs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. While KD often recovers much of a teacher’s utility under resource constraints, realizing its benefits in production requires deliberate choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to mitigate transferred errors and biases. A pragmatic KD pipeline combines soft-target matching with representation-level supervision, architecture-aware adaptation, and complementary compression methods to balance accuracy, latency, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Avila
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring supervisory signals richer than hard labels. A broad toolkit exists—soft logits, intermediate-feature alignment, attention or relational signals, multi-teacher and self-distillation schedules, and data strategies that range from using original datasets to synthetic or data-free approaches. KD is most effective when treated as a composable part of a compression pipeline that includes pruning, quantization, or architecture redesign, and when distillation objectives and curricula are matched to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. Remaining practical challenges center on teacher–student mismatch, degraded long-tail or rare-token behavior, distribution shift, privacy constraints, and the potential propagation of teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies enable smaller, faster models to inherit performance from larger teachers by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble knowledge. Techniques range from logit-based soft-target distillation to feature- and attention-level mimicry, multi-teacher and task-adaptive pipelines, and methods that relax the need for original training data or strong teachers. Across computer vision and natural language processing tasks, distilled students can approach teacher accuracy while drastically reducing parameters and latency; complementary strategies such as careful pre-training of compact models and architecture search further improve trade-offs between efficiency and effectiveness. Key challenges remain in preserving rare-token behavior, aligning heterogeneous teacher–student inputs, and ensuring privacy and robustness during compression.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach that enables deployment of large deep and language models by training smaller students to retain much of teacher performance. KD supports a range of transfer signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, relational signals) and composes naturally with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design). When designed as a tailored pipeline—matching distilled signals, student capacity, and data strategy—KD delivers substantial runtime and memory savings with modest accuracy loss. However, KD is not a universal cure: preserving rare-case behavior, avoiding propagation of teacher flaws, and handling data- or privacy-constrained settings require explicit engineering and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Reyes
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a pragmatic, flexible pathway to compress large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. As a composable toolset rather than a single recipe, KD transfers soft targets, intermediate representations, and relational signals; composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design; and can be adapted for multi-teacher, data-limited, and privacy-aware regimes. Real-world success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, designing layer-aware objectives and curricula, and mitigating known failure modes such as data scarcity, teacher–student mismatch, robustness degradation, and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and Engineering Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically effective toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers richer supervision than hard labels—soft targets, intermediate representations, relational signals—and when integrated with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful data and optimization strategies it yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, KD is context-sensitive: its benefits depend on what is transferred, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as capacity mismatch, domain shift, rare-token degradation, and bias transfer. Responsible deployment therefore requires engineering pipelines that combine tailored distillation objectives, curriculum-style schedules, targeted augmentation or data synthesis, and evaluation beyond aggregate accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Flores
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Powerful, Versatile, but Not a Silver Bullet
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central and pragmatic approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones. It offers a flexible set of supervision signals (soft targets, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals) and workflows (multi-teacher, online, data-free, task-aware) that enable strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. At the same time, KD’s effectiveness depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, how to handle limited or private data, and how to mitigate the propagation of biases. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and principled evaluation, KD unlocks practical deployment while exposing clear research and engineering challenges around robustness, domain shift, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Alexander
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Balanced Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-ready approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD often recovers much of a teacher's performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but its success depends on careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align architectures and representations, and how to manage data and robustness trade-offs. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and deployment-aware protocols, KD is the most practical route to widely useful compressed models — provided practitioners explicitly address optimization mismatch, data scarcity, and fairness/robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce computation, memory and latency of large deep models by transferring information from high-capacity "teacher" models to smaller "student" models. A range of approaches have been developed: soft-target (logit) distillation, feature- and layer-wise matching, data-augmentation and data-free synthesis, multi-teacher and curriculum strategies, and teacher-aware or teacher-training modifications. These methods are applied across modalities (NLP, vision, multimodal) and settings (limited data, federated or resource-constrained deployments), and combine naturally with quantization and low-precision inference. Empirical and theoretical work shows gains arise both from conveying inter-class similarities (dark knowledge) and from the regularization effect of softened targets; more recent work focuses on selecting or synthesizing the most useful knowledge for a given student and task.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD methods operate at multiple granularities (soft-label/logit matching, intermediate-feature imitation, module- or layer-wise mapping) and appear across domains including NLP, vision, multimodal, federated, and graph settings. Practical pipelines combine KD with data strategies, teacher adaptation, and complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search), but open challenges remain around data heterogeneity, teacher imperfections, and preserving properties such as low-frequency token fidelity, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from larger, often pre-trained teacher models into smaller, efficient student models in order to reduce latency, memory, and deployment cost while retaining task performance. Methods span matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, attention- or relation-based feature matching, curriculum strategies for progressively harder supervision, and task- or data-aware architecture search. Practical success depends on student capacity, availability and quality of data, whether the student itself is pre-trained, and choices about what to transfer; open challenges include preserving fairness and robustness, aligning heterogeneous architectures, and operating under privacy or data-limited conditions.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and empirically grounded approach for producing compact models by transferring richer supervisory signals from large teacher models into smaller students. KD operates at multiple granularities (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals) and can be applied in offline, online, multimodal, and data-limited regimes. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and with careful attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data strategies, and evaluation of robustness and fairness, KD routinely yields substantial accuracy-efficiency trade-offs that enable real-world deployment across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. Practical pipelines emphasize which signals to transfer, how to align layers or representations, augmentation or data-synthesis strategies when original data are scarce, and safeguards against propagated biases or degraded rare-case behavior.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Context‑Sensitive Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for converting large, high‑capacity models into smaller, faster students that meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). KD operates at multiple granularities — softened logits, intermediate features, attention or channel maps, and relational signals — and can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies (including data‑free synthesis) to yield strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. However, its success is context dependent: KD can propagate teacher errors, struggle under domain shift or data scarcity, and interact with architectural or optimization mismatch. Thus, KD should be treated as the central tool in model compression pipelines, applied with explicit design choices, complementary compression methods, and safeguards for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Stein

Its success in production settings depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle scarce or sensitive data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign).

papers_seen.author: Rogers

However, naive distillation that only matches teacher soft-labels is often insufficient. A more reliable strategy combines distillation of internal representations and features, task- or domain-adaptive compression, and architecture-aware search or adaptation. When applied with care — addressing optimization issues, data or privacy limits, and mismatch between teacher and student capacities — distillation enables compact, fast models that approach teacher performance across speech, NLP and vision tasks.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

However, distillation is not without limits: it can propagate teacher biases, depends on careful choice of what and how to transfer, and requires task- and data-aware engineering to be robust in low-data or privacy-sensitive settings. A pragmatic pipeline therefore treats KD as the central tool but couples it with targeted strategies for representation alignment, sample selection, and evaluation under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. Code available at: https://github.com/polo5/ZeroShotKnowledgeTransfer

papers_seen.title: Reframing Knowledge Distillation: Beyond Strong Teachers to Regularization, Representations, and Practical Variants
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful tool for compressing deep models, but its benefits arise from multiple mechanisms beyond mere imitation of a stronger teacher. Empirical and theoretical work indicates that distillation combines regularization effects of soft targets, representational alignment, and optimization dynamics; these insights motivate a broader set of practical strategies (teacher-free or data-free distillation, feature-based objectives, contrastive and adversarial losses, ensembles, and co-training of teacher/student) to obtain compact models that generalize well. This paper argues that practitioners should select KD variants depending on data availability, deployment constraints, and the nature of the task, and that future research should prioritize understanding optimization and representation transfer rather than treating teacher capacity as the sole determinant of success.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high‑capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has grown from matching softened teacher logits to a diverse toolkit including intermediate‑representation and attention alignment, multi‑teacher and self‑distillation variants, data‑aware and data‑free workflows, and task‑aware layer mapping. In practice KD is most effective when composed with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign/search) and when designers adapt distillation signals, data strategies, and curricula to student capacity and deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include teacher–student capacity mismatch, distributional shift and long‑tail/rare‑token behavior, robustness and fairness risks, and deploying under privacy or data‑scarce regimes.

papers_seen.author: Malone
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Benefits, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-oriented approach for producing compact neural models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Treated as a central element of compression pipelines and combined with complementary techniques, KD enables deployments that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Realizing those gains in practice requires careful selection of distillation signals, attention to data and optimization mismatches, and explicit evaluation of robustness and bias.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Uses, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and multimodal tasks, a family of techniques—soft-label matching, feature and attention imitation, layer mapping, multi-teacher and curriculum schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols—enables students to recover much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Practical success depends on task- and deployment-aware choices (distilled signal, student capacity, data availability, and augmentation), and remaining challenges include robustness to distribution shift, preservation of rare-token or fine-grained behaviors, and distillation under privacy or data-scarce conditions.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Medina
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Modern KD spans matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, layerwise and relational losses, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, and data-aware or data-free workflows. Empirical practice shows KD recovers much of teacher performance when combined with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture design), careful data and curriculum choices, and explicit handling of capacity, optimization, and distribution-shift failure modes. This synthesis summarizes practical techniques, common challenges, and recommended workflows for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Promise, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully and combined with complementary techniques—layer- and task-aware transfer, multi-teacher schemes, data synthesis or privacy-aware protocols, and hardware-aware downstream optimization—KD enables substantial reductions in size and latency while retaining much of a teacher's utility. However, its practical success is engineering-dependent: careful choices about distilled signals, student preparation, data availability, and mitigation of transferred errors or biases are required to realize reliable, fair, and robust compressed models.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD methods operate at multiple granularities (soft-label/logit matching, intermediate-feature imitation, module- or layer-wise mapping) and appear across domains including NLP, vision, multimodal, federated, and graph settings. Practical pipelines combine KD with data strategies, teacher adaptation, and complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search), but open challenges remain around data heterogeneity, teacher imperfections, and preserving properties such as low-frequency token fidelity, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for producing compact, deployable models from large pretrained teachers. When applied thoughtfully—by choosing appropriate transfer signals, addressing teacher–student capacity mismatch, and combining KD with architecture search, quantization, or data strategies—KD enables strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs for real-world NLP deployment. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: practitioners must attend to robustness, fairness, data availability, and teacher quality to avoid transferring undesirable behaviors and to retain performance under domain shift.

papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. The literature shows a diverse toolkit—softened-logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, layer-mapping strategies, online/multi-teacher/self-distillation variants, and data-aware or data-free workflows—often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture redesign. Empirical work demonstrates KD frequently recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but success depends on student capacity, data availability, signal selection, and careful attention to robustness, fairness, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Is Central to Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile route to compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones while preserving much of their performance. Across domains and deployment constraints—multi-task learning, low-resource devices, federated settings, data-free scenarios, and generative or detection tasks—KD enables targeted transfer of behavior, representations, and robustness. However, realizing KD's potential requires task-aware choices: which teacher(s) to use, what intermediate signals to mimic, how to select or synthesize training samples, and whether to incorporate adversarial or ensemble strategies. When combined with appropriate pre-training, selective sample strategies, and representation-level objectives, KD produces compact models that are accurate, efficient, and more widely deployable than large models alone.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for NLP: Strengths, Limits, and a Recipe for Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most practical and widely adopted strategy for compressing large NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, using task-aware layer mapping, and addressing data or privacy constraints—KD recovers most of a teacher’s performance while enabling large reductions in storage, latency, and power. However, effective deployment requires recognizing and mitigating limits such as capacity mismatch, distributional heterogeneity, and the risk of transferring teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has grown from simple soft-target matching into a flexible toolkit that includes representation-level alignment, multi-stage and multi-teacher schemes, data-free and federated protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirically, KD often yields substantial gains in student performance versus training from scratch and enables deployment under constraints of latency, memory, and privacy, but outcomes depend on choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and checks for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Complementary Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but it is not a standalone solution: its best results arise when combined with task-aware layer alignment, data strategies (augmentation or synthesis), architecture-aware compression, and careful teacher design. This position argues KD should be treated as the core of compression pipelines while acknowledging its failure modes and articulating practical mitigations.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Herring
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models so they can meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, compute, and privacy. KD spans simple soft-label matching and richer forms of transfer — intermediate feature and attention alignment, multi-stage or multi-teacher pipelines, data-free or synthesized-data approaches, and online or mutual distillation. In practice, KD is most effective when its signal, data strategy, and architectural alignment are chosen with the task and deployment constraints in mind and when distillation is combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Despite strong empirical gains across modalities, limitations remain: teacher imperfection, teacher–student capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity, and degradation on rare or low-frequency behaviors can reduce fidelity and robustness, so practitioners should treat KD as a flexible toolbox rather than a plug-and-play solution.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques enable deployment of large deep models by transferring knowledge to smaller, faster, or lower-precision models. Existing work spans pre-training compact models, teacher-to-student soft-target transfer, data-free and teacher-free approaches, self-distillation, architecture- and task-specific adaptations, and combinations with quantization or pruning. Empirical results show that distilled students can approach teacher performance across classification, ranking, speech, and generation tasks, while specialized strategies address limited task data, privacy constraints, and heterogeneous deployment settings. Open challenges include handling domain shift, designing teacher-student curricula, and developing universally effective objectives for diverse architectures and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted, Practical Engine for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single trick of copying a stronger model but as a multifaceted training paradigm that can compress, regularize, and adapt models for deployment. When practitioners choose the right distillation signals (soft targets, intermediate features, attention mappings), tailor objectives to data and privacy constraints, and combine KD with complementary techniques (architecture-aware design, quantization, data synthesis), they can produce compact students that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and robustness requirements. Effective use of KD requires attention to representation alignment, optimization schedules, and the constraints of the deployment setting.

papers_seen.author: Shelton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Design-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has proven a practical route to compress large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students across vision and language tasks. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone — including softened outputs, intermediate representations, and relational structure — and works best when combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful data and curriculum choices. However, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: its success depends on matching transferred signals to student capacity, preparing suitable data or synthetic examples, and explicitly measuring effects on robustness, fairness, and distributional generalization.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Lindsey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context‑Sensitive Engine of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance. KD encompasses a family of targets (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention/relational signals) and training regimes (offline, online/self-distillation, data-free or synthetic data) and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques and deployment-aware design. While KD routinely yields favorable size–accuracy trade-offs, its success is context-sensitive: careful teacher–student co-design, data strategies, and explicit checks for robustness, fairness, and rare-token fidelity are required to avoid well-known failure modes. This essay argues that KD should be treated as the practical core of model-compression pipelines and gives recommended practices for realizing reliable, efficient students in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation: Versatile Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and powerful approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient ones. Beyond simple size reduction, KD enables transfer of capabilities across modalities, supports domain adaptation, improves deployment in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings, and can be adapted to distributed training. However, benefits are not automatic: careful design of teacher-student alignment, training data, and distillation objectives is required to preserve task performance and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Lester
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Context-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile toolkit for producing compact deep and NLP models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers while meeting deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). When integrated thoughtfully with complementary compression methods and data strategies, KD yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, realizing these gains in practice requires careful teacher–student co-design, appropriate distillation signals, and explicit attention to robustness, rare-token behavior, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Maynard
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. The practice spans matching softened logits to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational structure, and is often combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and data strategies (real, augmented, or synthetic). KD is a flexible, deployment-oriented paradigm that routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs but is context-sensitive: outcomes depend on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Browning
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applied set of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision and NLP, KD operates at multiple granularities (softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and training dynamics) and is typically combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free approaches). Empirical work shows KD often recovers much of a teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost, but practical success depends on careful alignment of teacher signals, student capacity, and available data; known limitations include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, sensitivity under domain shift, and degraded performance on rare or low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable strategy for producing compact, deployable models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD works across modalities and deployment constraints, and supports extensions for data-free, federated, and privacy-sensitive settings. However, realizing KD’s full potential requires careful choices about what signals to transfer (logits, features, relational signals), how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to mitigate transferred harms such as bias or degraded rare-token behavior. When combined with complementary methods (augmentation, layer-aware mapping, multi-teacher ensembles, or differential-privacy mechanisms), KD becomes a flexible core of effective compression pipelines for real-world NLP and deep-learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Day
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When integrated into a wider compression pipeline and matched to task and deployment constraints, KD can preserve much of a teacher’s predictive capability while reducing latency, memory, and energy costs. However, KD is context-sensitive: its success depends on what signals are transferred, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability (or synthetic-data workarounds), and explicit mitigation for transferred biases or distribution shift. A pragmatic stance treats KD as the central, composable tool for compression, applied with task-aware design, complementary methods, and principled evaluation to address its known limits.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Considerations, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A mature toolkit includes softened-logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, self- and online-distillation, multi-teacher and ensemble-to-singleton transfer, task-adaptive architecture search, and data-free or privacy-aware synthesis. Empirical practice shows KD routinely improves compact models' accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, but success depends on what signals are transferred, how student and teacher are aligned (architecturally and in optimization), and how data constraints, distribution shift, and downstream robustness or fairness needs are handled.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Model Compression in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. KD works across modalities and tasks, and its effectiveness depends on matching distillation techniques to data and deployment constraints. When combined with careful model and data design, KD enables practical deployment of advanced models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Versatile Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones while retaining much of their effectiveness. When combined with task-specific adaptations (layer mapping, data-free synthesis, federated protocols, quantization, or self-supervision), KD enables deployment in low-resource, privacy-sensitive, and domain-specific settings. Success depends on designing appropriate alignment mechanisms, data strategies, and fairness safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Hamilton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable approach for compressing large deep models into compact students that meet real-world constraints on latency, memory, and deployment. When matched to task needs and combined with representation-aware objectives, data strategies, and robustness or privacy-aware adaptations, KD enables small models to retain much of teachers' performance across modalities. However, KD is context-sensitive: teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and the chosen distillation signal determine outcomes. A pragmatic pipeline blends logit and feature matching, targeted data augmentation or synthesis, and complementary compression methods to achieve robust, efficient deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hodge
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high‑capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision and language, distillation techniques—ranging from softened logits to intermediate‑representation matching and architecture‑aware schedules—enable deployment under compute, latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Distillation is most effective when combined with complementary compression tools and careful data or curriculum design; open issues include capacity mismatch, data scarcity, robustness under distribution shift, and preserving rare or low‑frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-ready approach for shrinking large neural models into compact, deployable students. As a composable toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD can transfer softened outputs, intermediate features, and relational structure, and it composes naturally with pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, and data strategies to meet real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile method for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from teacher models, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. The approach spans simple soft-target matching to richer strategies that align intermediate features, use online or multi-teacher schemes, and combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. When applied with attention to teacher design, student capacity, data availability, and fairness/robustness checks, KD provides an effective toolkit for producing compact models suited to real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Butler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Representation‑Aware Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible training paradigm for producing compact deep and language models that meet real deployment constraints. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels—ranging from softened outputs to intermediate representations and relational signals—KD enables substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often preserving most of a teacher’s performance. Realistic compression pipelines pair KD with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful data strategies (real, public, synthesized, or data‑free) to balance accuracy, latency, and privacy. Responsible deployment requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to evaluate robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Webb
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. A broad toolkit—softened logits, intermediate representation and attention alignment, multi-teacher curricula, and data‑free synthesis—has been developed and commonly combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign). Practical success depends on aligning what is transferred to student capacity, handling limited or private data, and combining distillation with deployment-aware engineering to manage robustness, rare-token behaviors, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Hardy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly used approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels—such as softened output distributions, intermediate representations, attention/relational structure, or many-to-many layer mappings—KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of a teacher model’s performance. Effective distillation is context-sensitive: choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, what data to use or synthesize, and how to combine KD with complementary compression techniques determine outcomes. While KD routinely yields favorable size/accuracy trade-offs in vision and language tasks, practical adoption requires engineered pipelines to manage capacity mismatch, teacher imperfections, distributional shift, privacy constraints, and robustness or fairness risks.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Newton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Practitioners apply distillation across logits, intermediate representations, attention/relational maps, and with varied workflows (offline multi-stage, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher, or data-free). In production settings distillation is normally combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and adapted to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. While distillation routinely yields strong size–performance trade-offs, important challenges remain in aligning teacher and student, preserving rare or long‑tail behaviors, avoiding bias amplification, and ensuring robustness and privacy in real‑world deployments.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a suite of methods for transferring information from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models so they can be deployed under compute, memory, and privacy constraints. KD encompasses matching teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations, online and multi-teacher workflows, and data-aware or data-free strategies. Empirically KD often yields compact students that approach teacher performance and can improve generalization, but practical success hinges on teacher-student alignment, data strategy, and addressing robustness and distribution-shift issues. Open directions include distillation without original data, preserving fine-grained sequence behavior, and adapting KD to heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Hayden
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Sensitive Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the practical core of model compression for deep learning and NLP because it is a flexible, empirically effective paradigm that transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels, composes naturally with pruning/quantization/architecture changes, and supports privacy- and deployment-aware workflows. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its reliability depends on aligning distillation signals with student capacity, addressing data availability or privacy constraints, and explicitly mitigating risks such as optimization mismatch, degraded rare-token performance, and the propagation of teacher harms. To maximize KD’s practical value, practitioners should adopt signal- and data-aware distillation objectives, combine KD with complementary compression primitives, and expand evaluation beyond aggregate accuracy to include robustness, fairness, and long-tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Gay
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted set of techniques for transferring information from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD methods operate at multiple granularities — softened outputs, intermediate feature or attention alignment, relational signals, and synthesized or public-data training — and are often combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and data strategies (augmentation, curriculum, or data-free synthesis). Empirically, KD routinely yields strong size–accuracy trade-offs across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, but its success depends on careful alignment of teacher signals to student capacity, attention to data availability and domain shift, and checks for transferred biases and rare-token degradation. Remaining challenges include theoretical understanding of when distillation helps, preserving low-frequency behaviors in sequence models, and robustly distilling across heterogeneous architectures or privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mack
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels.
