papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression, with Design-Sensitive Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical core of model-compression pipelines in deep learning and NLP because it transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels and reliably improves student performance under resource constraints. However, KD is not a plug-and-play cure: real-world deployment requires careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student co-design, data strategies (including data-free or domain-adaptive approaches), and complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to address capacity mismatch, distribution shift, rare-token behavior, and fairness or privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer predictive capacity from large, expensive models into smaller, faster models while preserving performance. Approaches vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, feature projectors), how teachers are constructed (single teacher, multi-teacher, self-teaching, or meta-learned teachers), and what resources are available (original data, public data, or no data). Practical extensions address domain-specific needs (e.g., BERT compression, low-precision deployment, privacy-preserving and federated settings) and include strategies such as progressive module replacement, multi-stage distillation, adversarially generated synthetic data, and self-supervised distillation. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both the power of soft targets as a regularizer and the importance of aligning internal representations and layer correspondences to improve student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Effective Knowledge Distillation: Representation, Selection, and Practical Constraints
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to compress and adapt large deep models for deployment in resource- or privacy-constrained settings. Effective distillation goes beyond matching teacher logits: transferring internal representations, choosing which teacher signals to trust, and accommodating deployment constraints (limited data, communication, low-precision hardware) are all decisive. I argue that the most reliable distillation pipelines combine representation-level objectives, selective/sample-aware strategies, and engineering choices that address privacy and efficiency, yielding compact students that retain teacher strengths across NLP, vision, and graph domains.

papers_seen.author: Stephens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practical approach for compressing large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers richer supervision than hard labels alone — for example softened outputs, intermediate representations, or relational/attention signals — and is typically used as the central element of a broader compression pipeline that also employs pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, addressing data limitations through augmentation or synthesis, and explicitly checking robustness and fairness. While KD often yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across modalities, careful pipeline engineering is required to mitigate failure modes such as teacher–student mismatch, rare-token degradation, bias transfer, and distribution-shift fragility.

papers_seen.author: Griffith
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. The field has evolved from simple softened-logit matching to a diverse toolbox that includes intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-aware and data-free synthesis, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirical practice shows KD routinely improves accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when pipelines are adapted to student capacity, available data, and deployment constraints, but remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, distribution shift, robustness, fairness, and privacy-sensitive or data-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Landscape of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models by transferring useful information from a teacher to a student, enabling deployment in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Methods differ in what is transferred (soft labels, intermediate representations, attention maps, relations) and how (feature matching, channel- or layer-wise alignment, augmentation, self- or data-free schemes). Distillation also serves broader roles beyond compression—regularization, bias transfer or mitigation, domain adaptation, and enabling multi-task or modality conversions. Practical effectiveness depends on choices of distilled signal, student capacity, data availability and augmentation, and deployment constraints; these choices shape trade-offs in accuracy, robustness, and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Short
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Sensitive Toolbox
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single algorithm but as the practical centerpiece of model‑compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. KD consistently enables large reductions in model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but its success depends on matching what is transferred to student capacity, choosing appropriate data strategies (including data‑free or synthetic approaches), and combining distillation with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign. Responsible deployment requires explicitly addressing failure modes—teacher bias, optimization mismatch, domain shift, and poor handling of low‑frequency phenomena—through careful pipeline design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Bowers
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring behavioral and representational knowledge from teacher models. A rich family of distillation techniques—ranging from soft-target (logit) matching to intermediate feature imitation, layer-mapping, projector-based transforms, and meta-learned teachers—enables practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and deployability across vision and language tasks. Practical success depends on choosing appropriate distillation signals, adapting teacher behavior to student capacity, and addressing data or deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Baird
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used, practical strategy for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Research over the last decade has extended KD from simple softened-logit matching into a flexible toolkit that transfers soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention and relational structure, and curriculum or ensemble signals. In practice KD is typically combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies) and used with task-aware choices about distilled signals and training data. KD routinely improves compact models over training from scratch, but its effectiveness depends on student capacity, data availability or synthesis, teacher–student alignment, and explicit handling of robustness and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. A mature toolbox has emerged that includes soft-label/logit matching, feature- and layer-level imitation, attention and relational alignment, multi-teacher schedules, and data strategies (real, augmented, synthesized, or data-free). KD is most effective when integrated into broader compression pipelines (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and when teacher–student alignment, training curricula, and data availability are carefully addressed. Practical deployment requires attention to capacity mismatch, potential bias transfer, and robustness under distributional shifts; nonetheless, well‑designed KD pipelines routinely produce compact models that approach teacher performance across vision, language, speech, graph, and recommendation tasks.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central practical tool for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably delivers strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs when its objectives, data, and architectural choices are matched to the student’s capacity and deployment constraints. However, KD is not a plug-and-play remedy: robust, fair, and private compression requires pre-training, careful signal selection, alignment strategies, and combination with complementary methods such as pruning and quantization.

papers_seen.author: Reese
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a set of techniques that transfer information from larger, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster student models so they can be deployed under constraints of latency, memory, or privacy. Methods range from matching softened teacher outputs to aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational structure, and using synthesized or public data; practitioners routinely combine KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign. KD often recovers most of the teacher’s performance but requires careful choices about the distillation signal, teacher–student capacity matching, and data handling. Ongoing challenges include robustness under distribution shift, preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors, and adapting KD to heterogeneous architectures and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Berger
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has evolved from softened-logit matching to a diverse toolbox that includes intermediate-representation alignment, attention- and relation-based objectives, multi-teacher and self-distillation schedules, and data-aware or data-free workflows. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and appropriate data or curriculum engineering, KD enables compact models that meet deployment constraints while preserving much of teacher performance. Persistent challenges include student–teacher capacity mismatch, data scarcity or privacy concerns, robustness under distribution shift, and preserving rare or long‑tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Durham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and production-oriented approach for shrinking large models into smaller, deployable students. When used as a central tool within compression pipelines and combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, or data strategies), KD can deliver large reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of a teacher’s performance. However, KD is context-sensitive: its success depends on choices of distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and explicit checks for robustness and bias. Careful pipeline design and targeted mitigations are therefore required for reliable deployment of distilled models.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile, and central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones while preserving most of their performance. KD works across modalities and tasks, integrates naturally with complementary compression strategies, and supports deployment under privacy- and resource-constrained settings. Realizing KD’s full potential requires attention to what signals are distilled (logits, features, relations), how data are managed or synthesized, and how teacher–student alignment and curricula are designed.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Task‑Aware Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD succeeds when the distillation signals, data strategy, and architecture choices are matched to deployment constraints; its most reliable use combines logits-based supervision with representation-level alignment, multi-stage curricula, and complementary compression techniques. However, KD is not a universal remedy: careful pipeline design is required to avoid transferring teacher errors, to handle low-frequency phenomena and domain shifts, and to meet privacy or data-limited requirements.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce compute, memory, and latency while preserving task performance. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, KD has been adapted into many forms—soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, attention and relational transfers, multi-teacher ensembles, online distillation, and task-adaptive pipelines—and combined with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to enable deployment in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Empirical work shows KD often recovers most of a teacher's utility in a much smaller footprint, but success depends on teacher quality, the choice of distilled signals, data availability and domain shift, and robustness and privacy constraints. The field continues to refine objectives, layer-mapping strategies, and workflows that make distillation effective across modalities and large pretrained models in practical deployments.

papers_seen.author: Vasquez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Balanced Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and widely applicable route to producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. When adopted as the centerpiece of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and thoughtful data and evaluation strategies, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is context-sensitive: its success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, addressing data and privacy limits, and explicitly evaluating robustness, rare-case behavior, and fairness. Practical deployment therefore requires both engineering recipes and governance guardrails to reap KD’s efficiency benefits without amplifying harms or brittle behavior.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: What is known about Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide practical ways to transfer predictive capacity from larger teacher models (or ensembles) into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. The field encompasses simple soft-target matching as well as richer forms of transfer such as intermediate representation alignment, attention- or feature-level matching, multi-stage and multi-teacher pipelines, self-distillation, and data- or privacy-aware variants. Empirical work shows distilled students can approach teacher performance while offering large gains in latency, memory, and deployability; theoretical and empirical analyses emphasize mechanisms including soft-target regularization, representational alignment, and optimization dynamics. Practical success depends on careful choices of what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to use data (including synthetic or public data), and how to address robustness, fairness, and distributional shifts.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision, language, graph, and speech tasks, KD variants (logit/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, relational transfer, multi-stage or multi-teacher schedules, and privacy-aware procedures) enable substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while often preserving most of the teacher's performance. Practical deployments pair KD with pretraining, sample-selection, and complementary compression techniques to meet latency, device, and privacy constraints; however, challenges remain around capacity mismatch, data scarcity, domain shift, and preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible route for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD reduces inference cost and often preserves much of teacher performance when combined with architecture-aware design and complementary compression steps. However, KD is not a plug‑and‑play fix: realizing its benefits in production requires explicit teacher–student co‑design, attention to data regimes and rare‑token behaviors, and systematic evaluation for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while preserving performance. The literature documents a spectrum of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or channel maps, and relational signals), a variety of optimization and architectural practices (layer mapping, projectors, multi-stage training, and student-friendly teacher design), and deployment workflows for constrained settings (data-free, federated, and domain-adaptive distillation). Empirical and theoretical work highlights multiple mechanisms that make KD effective (regularization via soft targets, representation alignment, and optimization/inductive-bias transfer), while also identifying persistent challenges such as aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving low-frequency behavior, and selecting what and when to transfer. Practical recommendations center on matching distillation signals to student capacity, using feature- or layer-aware objectives when internal alignment matters, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Whitney
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD has evolved from simple soft-target (logit) matching to a flexible toolbox that includes representation- and relation-level transfers, multi-stage curricula, data-aware and data-free strategies, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptations. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and power while retaining much of teacher performance, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data regimes, and careful pipeline design to avoid failure modes such as capacity mismatch, degraded long-tail behavior, or the propagation of teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Richardson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses capabilities from large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. KD includes matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations or attention, using multi-teacher and online schemes, and working with or without original data through synthesis or data‑free approaches. When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task‑aware training curricula, KD yields practical size–performance trade‑offs for deployment. Real‑world reliability requires careful teacher–student co‑design, data strategies, and explicit evaluation of robustness, fairness, and rare‑case behavior.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Cornerstone for Compressing Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile mechanism for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones in NLP and related modalities. When paired with targeted choices—what signals to transfer (logits versus features), how to align layers, teacher design, and data strategies—KD preserves much of the teacher’s capability while reducing compute, memory, and latency. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on optimization details, data availability, and careful engineering to handle distribution shift, rare behaviors, and student–teacher mismatches.

papers_seen.author: Pena
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-oriented paradigm for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. Beyond pure compression, KD can act as a regularizer and a mechanism for transferring internal representations, enabling trade-offs among accuracy, latency, privacy, and robustness. Effective KD pipelines combine multiple signals (soft targets, intermediate features, attention maps), data strategies (including data-free synthesis), and deployment-aware techniques (privacy-preserving queries, architecture adaptation). I argue that KD should be treated as the central, organizing method in any practical compression workflow, but that realizing its benefits requires task-aware choices about what to transfer and how to mitigate known failure modes such as teacher–student mismatch and degraded modeling of rare phenomena.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. The approach is broadly applicable across modalities and is most effective when treated as a flexible toolkit — combining softened-output matching, representation-level alignment, multi-teacher or online schemes, and data-aware strategies — and integrated with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design). Practical success depends on teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability or synthesis, and evaluation for robustness, rare-case fidelity, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Haney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Mechanisms, Methods, and Integration
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, deployment-oriented approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, faster students. KD works through multiple mechanisms—from soft-target regularization to representation transfer—and a variety of techniques such as logit matching, feature alignment, and projector-enabled feature distillation. Treated as the central element of a compression pipeline and combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization), KD produces practical size–performance trade-offs. Real-world success requires context-sensitive choices about what to transfer, how to map layers, and how to mitigate distributionshift, bias, and optimization mismatch.

When KD is broadened beyond simple soft-label matching to include intermediate representation transfer, multi-teacher schedules, data strategies, and integration with pruning/quantization, it yields compact students that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD is not a silver bullet: careful signal design, student capacity matching, and complementary compression techniques are required to handle domain shift, rare-token behaviors, and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Day

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. However, KD is context-sensitive: its success depends on what signals are transferred, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability (or synthetic-data workarounds), and explicit mitigation for transferred biases or distribution shift. A pragmatic stance treats KD as the central, composable tool for compression, applied with task-aware design, complementary methods, and principled evaluation to address its known limits.

However, KD is context-sensitive: capacity mismatch, data scarcity, teacher errors, and distributional or rare-token failures require deliberate pipeline design, diagnostics, and targeted mitigation.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.

Advances include theoretical reframings that connect KD to regularization, a range of strategies for aligning outputs and internal representations, methods that restructure or progressively replace model components, and practical systems that enable heterogeneous and privacy-sensitive deployments. Despite clear empirical gains, open problems remain in understanding when and why different distillation targets (soft outputs, internal features, attention maps, module behavior) are most effective, and how to balance compression with robustness and interpretability.

Distillation has been applied across classification, generation, retrieval, speech, and structured prediction, and it also offers avenues to transfer inductive biases, improve robustness, and preserve privacy. Empirical and theoretical work has clarified when distillation helps, what kind of "dark knowledge" is useful, and how regularization-like effects of soft targets can be harnessed even without a superior teacher.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Ferguson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and pragmatic approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing which teacher signals to transfer, aligning student capacity and architecture, and combining distillation with complementary compression steps—KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: data availability, teacher–student mismatch, and distributional or privacy concerns require targeted design choices and evaluation to produce robust, fair, and deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. KD is versatile across modalities and workflows: it can match softened logits, align intermediate representations or attention maps, operate with or without original training data, and integrate with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success requires careful teacher–student co‑design, data and signal selection, staged training, and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and domain generalization. Despite strong empirical gains in efficiency and deployability, open problems remain in theoretical understanding, robustness under distribution shift, preserving rare or long-tail behaviors, and avoiding transfer of teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Adapt-and-Distill: Developing Small, Fast and Effective Pretrained Language Models for Domains
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have achieved great success in many natural language processing tasks. However, when they are applied in specific domains, these models suffer from domain shift and bring challenges in fine-tuning and online serving for latency and capacity constraints. In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. Then we systematically explore different strategies to compress the large pre-trained models for specific domains. We conduct our experiments in the biomedical and computer science domain. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves better performance over the BERT BASE model in domain-specific tasks while 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://aka.ms/adalm.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Context‑Sensitive Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for converting large, high‑capacity models into smaller, faster students that meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). KD operates at multiple granularities — softened logits, intermediate features, attention or channel maps, and relational signals — and can be combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies (including data‑free synthesis) to yield strong accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. However, its success is context dependent: KD can propagate teacher errors, struggle under domain shift or data scarcity, and interact with architectural or optimization mismatch. Thus, KD should be treated as the central tool in model compression pipelines, applied with explicit design choices, complementary compression methods, and safeguards for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Gutierrez
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large ‘‘teacher’’ models to smaller ‘‘student’’ models so students are deployable under constraints of latency, memory, energy, or privacy. KD goes beyond matching hard labels: it uses softened outputs, intermediate-feature matching, relational or attention maps, and curricula or synthetic data to shape student learning. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and when practitioner choices (distillation signal, teacher selection, data strategy, and evaluation on robustness and long-tail behavior) are matched to the deployment context. Open problems remain around data-limited or privacy-sensitive settings, heterogenous teacher–student architectures, preservation of rare-token / low-frequency behaviors, and principled guarantees about robustness and fairness.

KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels—soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational structure—and when combined with architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, and data strategies it routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, KD’s success is context-sensitive: it depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability (including synthetic or privacy-preserving data), and explicit robustness and fairness checks. Responsible deployment therefore treats KD as a flexible, design-aware toolbox rather than a turnkey solution.

papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible paradigm for producing compact models that preserve much of the performance of larger teachers. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels—ranging from softened outputs to internal representations and relational objectives—KD composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Successful application requires careful choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and explicit validation for robustness and long-tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Chandler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Task-Aware Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for turning large, high-performing deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD succeeds by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone, and when combined with complementary techniques (architecture search, pruning, quantization, data augmentation, and multi-teacher curricula) it enables substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is context-sensitive: choices about what to transfer (logits, features, relational signals), how to produce or augment training data, and how to align teacher and student architectures determine outcomes. Effective deployment therefore treats KD as a central tool in compression pipelines but tailors the pipeline to task constraints, data availability, and robustness/fairness goals.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller students while preserving much of performance. Treated as a central element of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), KD enables deployable models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data or synthesis strategies, and explicitly diagnosing robustness, fairness, and distributional risks. I argue KD should be the default core of compression workflows, applied with task‑aware design, multi‑stage training, and explicit safeguards against teacher errors and long‑tail failures.

papers_seen.author: Molina
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD encompasses a range of targets and workflows—soft-output matching, intermediate-feature alignment, attention or relational losses, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free variants—and is most effective when combined with complementary compression tools and deployment-aware design choices. However, its success depends on careful choices about distillation signals, data strategies, architectural alignment, and mitigation of optimization and robustness failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Frank
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone — including softened outputs, intermediate representations, and relational or layer-wise information — and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and task- or deployment-aware design choices. The method yields favorable size–performance trade-offs across modalities, but its success depends on careful teacher–student co-design, appropriate choice of distilled signals, data strategies for training (including data-free or synthesized-data regimes), and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and rare-token or distribution-shift behavior.

papers_seen.author: Mata
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical, Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and flexible approach to compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely delivers strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when practitioners choose appropriate distillation signals, address teacher–student mismatches, and combine KD with complementary steps like pruning, quantization, or architecture adaptation. At the same time, KD’s benefits depend on data availability, teacher quality, optimization dynamics, and explicit mitigation of robustness, privacy, and long‑tail failure modes. A production‑grade pipeline therefore treats KD as the central tool but integrates data‑aware strategies and targeted remedies for known limits.

papers_seen.author: Mccall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression — Powerful but Context‑Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models so they meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD routinely improves student performance relative to training from scratch and composes well with complementary compression methods, but its success depends on student capacity, what signals are transferred, data availability, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and distribution shift. Treating KD as the central element of a compression pipeline—rather than a standalone cure—yields the best practical outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models so they meet real-world constraints on latency, memory, and deployment. Across vision, language, generative, and structured prediction tasks, KD has been adapted from simple soft-label matching into a rich toolbox that includes intermediate-layer supervision, multi-teacher schedules, student-aware teacher training, data- and augmentation-aware pipelines, and combinations with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). When applied with attention to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints, KD reliably improves size–performance trade-offs, but its success depends on careful signal selection, teacher–student alignment, and strategies to mitigate capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and transferred teacher artifacts.

papers_seen.author: Johnston
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the last decade KD has evolved into a flexible toolkit—matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations or attention, using multi-teacher or self-distillation schedules, and operating with or without original training data. In practice KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when pipelines are tailored to data availability, student capacity, and deployment constraints. Persistent challenges include teacher–student capacity mismatch, data and privacy constraints, robustness and fairness, and preservation of rare-token behavior; addressing these requires task-aware design, careful evaluation, and targeted remedies.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while preserving performance. Methods extend beyond matching soft output logits to include intermediate feature/representation matching, layer-wise alignment, adversarial or curriculum-driven sample selection, and data-free or privacy-aware synthesis. Distillation is widely applicable across modalities (vision, speech, language, multimodal) and use cases (on-device deployment, federated learning, low-precision inference), but success depends on careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to handle data availability or heterogeneity, and how to align teacher and student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Morris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Practical Patterns, Mechanisms, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used approach to compress large, high-performing deep learning and NLP models into smaller, faster students that are suitable for deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. The literature frames KD as a flexible toolkit—covering soft-label matching, intermediate-representation alignment, relational and attention-based objectives, multi-teacher regimes, and data-free strategies—that typically works best when combined with complementary compression methods and careful data or curriculum design. While KD often preserves much of teacher performance, its success depends on student capacity, signal selection, data availability, and deployment-aware engineering; open challenges include capacity/optimization mismatch, preserving long-tail behaviors, mitigating transferred biases, and enabling reliable distillation without access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Sensitive Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, pragmatic approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with attention to the match between distilled signals and student capacity, appropriate data strategies, and complementary compression methods, KD consistently yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. Responsible deployment requires explicit handling of optimization gaps, distributional shift, rare-token behavior, privacy constraints, and fairness concerns. I argue KD should be treated as the practical centerpiece of compression pipelines, but only when used as a context‑sensitive toolbox combined with principled safeguards and complementary techniques.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central approach to compress large deep models into smaller, faster, and often more deployable student models. KD techniques range from classic teacher-to-student soft-target training to recent advances including data-free distillation, multi-teacher strategies, meta-learned teachers, and compression combined with pruning or structural sparsity. In NLP applications KD is used to shrink pre-trained transformers, accelerate inference for production systems, enable non-autoregressive generation, and adapt large models to resource-constrained or heterogeneous environments. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while producing models with far lower latency and storage cost, but theoretical understanding, sensitivity to data and teacher quality, and robustness under distributional shifts remain active research areas.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Methods range from matching softened logits to imitating internal representations, attention maps, or channel-wise activations, and can be combined with quantization, low-precision numerics, architecture-aware design, and data- or teacher-aware training regimes. In practice, distillation is a multifaceted toolkit that must be tailored to deployment goals (latency, memory, domain adaptation, privacy, robustness), and remaining challenges include principled sample selection, representation alignment across heterogeneous architectures, and preserving robustness and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Snyder
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible family of techniques for turning large, high‑capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. KD methods span matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, relation- or attention-based transfers, and variants that operate offline, online, or without access to the original training data. In practice KD is combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, and architecture design) and data strategies (pretraining compact models, augmentations, or synthetic data) to meet deployment constraints. While KD routinely improves accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, realizing robust, fair, and domain‑aware distilled systems requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to mitigate preserved teacher errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Kane
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Extensions, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, task- and deployment-aware toolkit for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a composable component — combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies (public, synthesized, or online), and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization) — KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, KD is not a universal fix: its practical success depends on careful teacher design, attention to student capacity and data regimes, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as distribution shift, poor rare-token transfer, federated-data heterogeneity, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring predictive behavior and internal knowledge. Across vision and language tasks, KD is used to reduce inference cost, enable deployment on resource-constrained devices, and retain performance through techniques that go beyond matching final outputs—including intermediate representation imitation, data-aware training, multi-teacher strategies, and teacher-free or data-free approaches. Empirical work demonstrates both consistent gains and important failure modes (e.g., loss of low-frequency lexical information or sensitivity to domain shift), motivating refinements such as internal representation distillation, curriculum or sample selection, data augmentation choices, and dynamic teacher weighting. Open challenges remain in understanding what components of teacher knowledge most benefit students, how to handle heterogeneity between teacher and student architectures, and how to distill effectively without access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical set of techniques for transferring information from large, high-capacity 'teacher' models to smaller, efficient 'student' models so they can meet real-world constraints (compute, memory, latency, privacy). KD methods operate at multiple granularities — softened output logits, intermediate feature or attention matching, relational and module-level objectives — and are frequently combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design, or data synthesis). Empirically, KD routinely improves student performance compared to training from scratch and enables deployment across modalities and constrained settings, though challenges remain in robustness, low-frequency behavior, domain shift, and distillation without original data. This synthesis summarizes core methods, practical workflows, empirical benefits, and open problems to guide applied KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Efficient and Responsible NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, versatile approach for compressing large models and enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. Beyond raw compression, KD supports domain adaptation, data-free scenarios, improved inference speed, and novel training regimes for specialized tasks. However, distillation is not a panacea: it can amplify teacher biases, interact with regularization techniques in subtle ways, and benefits most when combined with complementary methods such as architecture-aware training, generator-based sample synthesis, or instance-aware losses.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression strategies are widely used to produce smaller, faster models by transferring knowledge from larger or ensemble teachers to compact students. These techniques span supervised distillation, self-distillation, data-free and adversarial approaches, layer- and task-aware mappings, and distributed/online schemes. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance across modalities (classification, detection, generation, and language tasks) while enabling practical deployment; theoretical and practical challenges remain around data dependence, teacher imperfection, robustness, and optimal student–teacher alignment.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Practical and Robust Knowledge Distillation for Deployable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central tool for compressing large deep models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and power constraints. Beyond matching teacher output probabilities, modern distillation should transfer internal structure, be tailored to domain and modality differences, and integrate with quantization, privacy, and data-limited settings. When applied with methods that address representation mismatch, optimization challenges, and curriculum of supervisory signals, distillation enables small models that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable ones by transferring predictive behavior or internal structure. A range of techniques — from matching teacher soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations, synthesizing or augmenting data, and coordinating multi-teacher or online protocols — enable practical trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and resource constraints. Success depends on task-aware design choices, student capacity, data availability, and careful handling of robustness and social-impact concerns.

papers_seen.author: Drake
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical, Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic set of techniques for producing compact, deployable deep models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When treated as a central, composable component of an engineering pipeline and combined with complementary compression tools and careful data and evaluation practices, KD yields strong size/performance/latency tradeoffs. Real-world success requires adapting the distillation signals to student capacity, addressing representation mismatch and data limitations, and explicitly auditing for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Hoover
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be the Central Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated method for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When treated as the central component of compression pipelines and combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and data-aware engineering (augmentation, curricula, multi-stage or multi-teacher schemes), KD enables deployable models across latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained settings. Responsible use requires explicit attention to capacity alignment, data limitations, and risks of transferring biases or teacher errors, together with targeted mitigation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Powerful, Flexible, but Context-Sensitive for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are practical, widely applicable tools for shrinking large models and transferring capability to smaller models. KD can preserve performance while reducing inference cost, enable cross-modal and cross-task transfer, and be adapted to constrained settings (few-shot, edge devices). However, KD is not a plug-and-play cure: its benefits depend on what is distilled (logits vs. features vs. internal structure), teacher-student design, data regime, and optimization choices. Careful method design — including feature-based objectives, intermediate-layer alignment, self-distillation or meta-learned teachers, and task-aware curricula — is required to realize robust gains without amplifying teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile training paradigm that reliably improves the accuracy–efficiency tradeoff of compact models. When treated as the central component of a compression pipeline and adapted to the student’s capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, KD yields deployable models that meet latency, memory, and privacy requirements while preserving much of teacher performance. Realizing KD’s practical benefits requires pairing distillation objectives with representation-aware alignment, complementary compression tools, careful data strategies, and systematic validation for robustness and long‑tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Nunez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Engineering-Dependent Route to Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students, enabling reduced inference cost and deployment on constrained devices. KD can match final outputs or internal representations and is often combined with complementary compression techniques; however, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align architectures, and how to handle data and optimization mismatches. I argue that KD should be treated as an essential, task-aware component of compression pipelines rather than a plug-and-play solution, and I offer practical directions to maximize its benefits while mitigating common failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When engineered as part of a broader compression pipeline, KD can deliver strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs while remaining compatible with pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, and data strategies. However, KD is not a plug‑and‑play cure: its success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, which data to use (including data-free or synthesized samples), and how to evaluate and mitigate transferred biases and distributional failures. I argue that KD should be treated as the central, configurable element of compression workflows, applied with task‑aware signal selection, staged curricula, and complementary compression primitives to manage its limits in practice.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Bowen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Power, Limits, and Responsible Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable strategy for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone and can be combined with other compression tools to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey cure: its effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and careful engineering to avoid degraded performance on rare or out-of-domain behaviors. A production-ready compression pipeline treats KD as the central mechanism but pairs it with curriculum design, multi-teacher strategies, representation alignment, and orthogonal compression methods while explicitly validating robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Matthews
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable set of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models so they meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, and privacy. KD spans simple soft-target matching to richer objectives that align intermediate features, attention or relational structure, and layer mappings. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, or data synthesis) and applied with task- and data-aware design, KD routinely yields favorable size–performance trade-offs in vision, language, graph, and multimodal settings. Yet KD has limits: capacity mismatch, optimization dynamics, teacher imperfection, distribution shift, and loss of rare or fine-grained behaviors require careful pipeline choices, diagnostics, and often hybrid methods to produce robust, deployable students.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Path to Deployable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for producing compact, faster models that retain much of the capability of larger teachers. Beyond simple logit matching, modern KD leverages internal representation transfer, selective data strategies, and integration with pruning, architecture search, or federated protocols to meet latency, privacy, and device-heterogeneity constraints. When applied thoughtfully, KD enables efficient deployment across modalities while posing clear methodological trade-offs and open challenges that guide future research.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Hall
