papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring supervision richer than hard labels. KD methods act across output distributions and internal representations, and are most effective when integrated with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression practices. Applied thoughtfully, KD yields substantial latency and memory improvements while retaining much of the teacher’s performance; however, achieving reliable deployment requires attention to capacity matching, data regimes, robustness to distribution shift, and mitigation of propagated teacher flaws.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across computer vision and NLP, practitioners use KD to reduce inference cost, enable on-device deployment, and adapt large pretrained models to constrained settings. KD techniques vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), how training data are handled (real, augmented, synthesized, or none), and how teachers and students are aligned architecturally and procedurally. When design choices are matched to the task and constraints, KD enables substantial compression with modest performance loss; however, challenges remain for heterogeneous architectures, generative tasks, privacy-sensitive settings, and preserving rare-token or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core for Model Compression with Design-Sensitive Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and broadly applicable approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD can transfer predictive behavior, internal representations, and inductive biases to students so they recover much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and deployment cost. In practice KD succeeds when paired with careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, or layer-wise signals), teacher-student co-design, data strategies (including synthetic or unlabeled data), and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD is not a turnkey fix: optimization mismatch, data scarcity or mismatch, and certain fine-grained behaviors (e.g., low-frequency tokens) remain challenges that require targeted remedies.

papers_seen.author: Palmer
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while attempting to preserve predictive performance. The literature provides a flexible toolbox — matching softened logits, imitating intermediate features or attention, relational losses, multi- and self-teaching regimes, and data-aware or data-free strategies — and emphasizes composing KD with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, or neural architecture search for realistic deployment. Empirical work shows KD often recovers most teacher performance in practice, but success depends on student capacity, signal selection, data availability, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy. Open challenges include handling distribution shift, preserving rare-token or low-frequency behaviors, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, and developing stronger theoretical explanations for when and why distillation helps.

papers_seen.author: Bowers

Practical success depends on choosing appropriate distillation signals, adapting teacher behavior to student capacity, and addressing data or deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Tucker

A pragmatic pipeline therefore treats KD as the central tool but couples it with targeted strategies for representation alignment, sample selection, and evaluation under deployment constraints.

Careful design around teacher quality, student capacity, and data regimes is necessary to avoid transferring biases or degrading robustness.

papers_seen.author: Miller

papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP

Practical application of KD requires matching the distilled signals and workflows to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; addressing failure modes such as transferred biases or poor handling of low-frequency phenomena; and integrating distillation into a broader compression pipeline to meet latency, memory, and privacy goals.

papers_seen.author: Juarez
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical family of techniques that transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models so students can meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, energy, or privacy) while retaining much of teacher performance. The literature describes a spectrum of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational maps, and module-level behaviors), teacher–student variants (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation), and data regimes (full-data, few-shot, and data-free adversarial synthesis). KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, progressive module replacement) and when practitioners attend to teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and robustness or fairness requirements. Open challenges include distillation under severe data heterogeneity, preserving rare-token or fine-grained behavior, and principled guarantees about robustness and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Griffith
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile engineering approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. The practice has evolved from matching softened output distributions to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate-representation and attention alignment, multi- and self-teaching, data-aware and data-free protocols, and integration with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design). Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data strategies (including selective or synthesized examples), and addressing deployment concerns such as latency, memory, robustness, and fairness. Remaining challenges include capacity and optimization mismatch, distributional shift and rare-case degradation, and the risk of transferring teacher artifacts; addressing these requires task-aware choices about what and how to transfer, careful teacher–student alignment, and combinations of distillation with other compression and robustness techniques.

papers_seen.author: Hopkins
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP

At the same time, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to produce or select data, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to diagnose and mitigate failure modes such as transferred bias, degraded long-tail behavior, and distribution shift. A responsible KD pipeline therefore treats distillation as the engine of compression while layering task-aware design, privacy safeguards, and robustness checks around it.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD spans simple soft-target matching to richer forms of transfer (intermediate-feature and layer-wise matching, attention or relational signals), and is commonly combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and data strategies (public, synthetic, or data-free approaches). Empirical work shows KD routinely narrows the gap between teacher and student performance across modalities, but practical success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to obtain or synthesize training data, and how to mitigate failures such as degraded rare-token behavior, robustness issues, and amplified biases.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most pragmatic and versatile foundation for compressing large deep and NLP models for deployment. When KD is broadened beyond simple soft-label matching to include intermediate representation transfer, multi-teacher schedules, data strategies, and integration with pruning/quantization, it yields compact students that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD is not a silver bullet: careful signal design, student capacity matching, and complementary compression techniques are required to handle domain shift, rare-token behaviors, and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a primary approach for turning large, high‑capacity deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. Practical KD pipelines combine multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), data strategies (augmented, synthesized, or data‑free), and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, preparing students via pretraining or layer mapping, and explicitly addressing distribution shift, rare‑token behavior, and the risk of transferring undesirable teacher properties. While KD routinely preserves substantial teacher utility, its limits motivate richer targets, multi‑teacher or online schemes, adversarial feature alignment, and careful evaluation of robustness and fairness in compressed models.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic framework for transferring knowledge from large teacher models into smaller student models so they meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, and privacy. The literature shows KD has evolved from simple softened-logit matching to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate-representation and attention-level alignment, multi-stage and multi-teacher schedules, data-aware and data-free workflows, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Practical success hinges on matching distilled signals to student capacity, selecting or synthesizing appropriate training data, co-designing teacher and student architectures, and evaluating for robustness, long-tail behavior, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Greene
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Sensitive Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical approach for converting large, high‑capacity deep models into smaller, deployable students. When designed as part of an explicit compression pipeline—choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining distillation with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search—KD reliably improves size–performance tradeoffs. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: success depends on data regime, optimization and capacity matching, and explicit mitigation strategies for fairness, robustness, and low‑frequency behavior. Treated as the central, task‑aware component of compression workflows, KD delivers strong gains for real‑world deployment while requiring careful engineering and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Kelley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance models into smaller, deployable students by transferring useful behavior or representations. Across vision, language, generative, and graph domains, KD operates via multiple signals (soft logits, intermediate features, relational or ensemble knowledge) and is typically combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can both convey additional task signal and act as a regularizer that improves student generalization relative to training from scratch, but its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, data availability or synthesis, teacher quality, and deployment constraints. Practical use requires tailoring distillation recipes to student capacity and application-specific constraints (latency, privacy, domain shift), and open problems remain around optimization mismatches, rare-token or low-frequency behavior, and privacy-sensitive or heterogeneous-data settings.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal knowledge. Across vision, language, and generative domains, methods range from matching teacher soft targets to aligning intermediate representations, synthesizing surrogate data when originals are unavailable, and coordinating multi-teacher or online protocols. Practical pipelines commonly combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Effectiveness depends on student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, data availability, and attention to robustness and fairness; these trade-offs guide ongoing research and engineering practice.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and a Design Recipe
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student design, handling data constraints, and combining KD with complementary compression methods—distillation routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. KD has clear failure modes (propagating teacher errors, difficulty with low-frequency behaviors, distribution shift, and robustness/privacy concerns) that require principled pipelines, diagnostics, and mitigation strategies. I argue KD should be treated as the central component of compression pipelines but only effective when integrated with representation-aware objectives, data-aware strategies, and robustness/privacy-aware techniques.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used framework for compressing large, high‑performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. KD operates at multiple levels (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention and relational structure), and is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, and data strategies (including synthetic or data‑free approaches) to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but success depends on careful choice of distillation targets, teacher–student alignment, data availability, and mitigation of risks such as capacity mismatch, robustness degradation, privacy leakage, and poor long‑tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Olson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an empirical framework for transferring knowledge from large teacher models to smaller, more efficient student models so they meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, compute or privacy) while retaining much of the teacher’s utility. KD operates at multiple granularities — softened output distributions, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and training dynamics — and is commonly combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data and curricula (including data augmentation or synthesis when original data are limited), and evaluating for robustness, fairness, and distributional shift. Despite broad empirical gains across modalities, open problems remain around theory, transfer of rare or long-tail behaviors, propagation of teacher errors or biases, and distillation without original data.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Browning
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applied set of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision and NLP, KD operates at multiple granularities (softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and training dynamics) and is typically combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free approaches). Empirical work shows KD often recovers much of a teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost, but practical success depends on careful alignment of teacher signals, student capacity, and available data; known limitations include capacity mismatch, propagation of teacher errors or biases, sensitivity under domain shift, and degraded performance on rare or low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. The approach includes matching teacher soft logits, aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, and using multi-teacher, self-distillation, and data‑aware or data‑free workflows. KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and when the distilled signals, student capacity, and data strategies are chosen to match deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include robustness under distribution shift, preserving low-frequency or rare-token behavior, avoiding transfer of teacher biases, and meeting privacy constraints in distributed or data-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses behavioral and representational knowledge from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. The literature presents a broad toolbox—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, self- and meta-distillation, data-free or data-scarce strategies, and layer- or relation-focused transfers—often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. Empirical and conceptual work shows KD can also regularize students and sometimes improve generalization or robustness, but practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how teacher and student capacities are aligned, and how data (real, augmented, or synthesized) are used. Open issues include distribution shift, rare-token behavior in sequence models, privacy constraints, and principled objectives for heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad family of techniques that transfer knowledge from larger, more expensive models (teachers) into smaller, efficient models (students) to improve inference speed, reduce memory, or enable deployment in resource-constrained settings. Across vision, language, graph, and generative modeling, KD has been instantiated as matching soft outputs, aligning internal representations, or supervising task-specific components. Practical work has shown KD can produce compact models with strong empirical performance, but success depends on many factors including student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, availability of data, training efficiency, and privacy constraints. Recent research has focused on richer teacher-to-student signals (intermediate layers, attention-based fusion), teacher adaptation strategies, data and augmentation strategies for better transfer, and integrating KD with pruning and other compression methods. Important open issues remain around optimization limits, data heterogeneity, and privacy-preserving distillation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, practical technique for compressing and adapting large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD is versatile: it transfers predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and ensemble knowledge; supports data-free or privacy-sensitive settings; and can improve robustness and calibration when combined with complementary methods. Realizing KD’s full potential requires matching the distillation recipe to deployment goals and addressing failure modes such as optimization mismatches, bias transfer, and poor handling of low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context‑Sensitive Toolbox for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical centerpiece for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When used thoughtfully — selecting what to transfer, adapting objectives to teacher and student capacities, and combining distillation with complementary methods like pruning, quantization, or data synthesis — KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. However, distillation’s effectiveness varies with task, data regime, and deployment constraints, so practitioners should treat it as a flexible set of techniques rather than a single plug‑and‑play algorithm.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce model size or communication cost by transferring knowledge from larger or multiple models (teachers) to smaller or otherwise constrained models (students). Methods vary from matching soft outputs to transferring intermediate features, training teachers to be student-friendly, coordinating multiple teachers, and combining distillation with pruning or federated/online schemes. Empirical and theoretical work highlights how distilled "dark knowledge" improves student generalization, how architectural components (e.g., projectors) shape transfer, and how distillation can be adapted for privacy, heterogeneity, and large-scale or multi-task NLP applications.

papers_seen.author: Oneill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Articles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models so they meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-label matching into a diverse toolkit that also transfers intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational signals; operates in offline, online, multi-teacher, and data-free regimes; and is commonly combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can substantially improve student performance when student capacity, signal choice, and data strategies are well matched, but important challenges remain around distribution shift, rare-token or low-frequency behavior, heterogeneous teacher–student alignment, and reliable data-free distillation.

papers_seen.author: Hart
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring supervisory signals richer than hard labels. A broad set of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), training workflows (single- and multi-stage, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher), and data strategies (original, augmented, synthesized, or absent) have been developed. KD is most effective when integrated into a larger compression pipeline—paired with pruning, quantization, or architecture redesign—and when distillation signals and curricula are matched to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. Remaining practical challenges include managing teacher–student mismatch, preserving long-tail behaviors, operating under privacy or data-scarce settings, and ensuring robustness and fairness under domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central practical tool for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably delivers strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs when its objectives, data, and architectural choices are matched to the student’s capacity and deployment constraints. However, KD is not a plug-and-play remedy: robust, fair, and private compression requires pre-training, careful signal selection, alignment strategies, and combination with complementary methods such as pruning and quantization.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Bray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple soft-target matching to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate-representation alignment, multi-teacher and ensemble schemes, adversarial and data-free methods, and tight integration with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. Practical success requires matching distilled signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data strategies, and addressing robustness, low-frequency behaviors, and privacy when moving models into deployment.

papers_seen.author: Oconnor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. The technique spans simple logit/soft-label matching to richer targets such as intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational objectives, and it is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, or architecture search) and deployment-aware data strategies. KD supports use cases ranging from latency- and memory-constrained inference to privacy-sensitive and federated deployments, but realizing its benefits requires careful choices about distillation signals, teacher–student alignment, data availability (including data-free approaches), and explicit evaluation of robustness, fairness, and long-tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical, Task-aware Path for Efficient NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical route to deploy large deep models in resource- and privacy-constrained environments. When applied thoughtfully—matching the distilled signal to the student’s capacity and the target task, incorporating representation-level objectives, and combining KD with complementary compression strategies—distillation yields compact models that preserve much of the teacher’s utility. However, KD is not a silver bullet: optimization difficulties, teacher imperfections, domain shift, and fidelity losses on rare tokens or protected subgroups can degrade student performance unless addressed by task-aware design choices, domain adaptation, or multi-teacher/online schemes. This essay argues that KD should be treated as a core, adaptable toolkit for compression whose effectiveness depends on principled choices about what to transfer, how to train students, and how to combine distillation with orthogonal techniques.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, high-impact way to compress large models into smaller, efficient ones while retaining most task performance. Modern KD methods extend beyond matching final logits to include layer- and feature-level imitation, task-aware selection of distilled information, data-free or few-shot regimes, and multi-teacher or self-distillation strategies. When combined with architecture-aware compression or search, KD enables task-adaptive, privacy-conscious, and efficient deployment of deep models in real-world NLP and vision applications.

papers_seen.author: Atkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. A broad family of KD techniques—matching softened teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations and attention, transferring relational structure, and using synthesized or public data—enables substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often retaining most of teacher performance. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, choosing data strategies (including data-free or synthesized data) when original data are unavailable, and combining KD with complementary compression tools such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Important open issues remain around capacity mismatch, distributional shift, rare-token/long-tail behaviors, and propagation of teacher biases; addressing these requires methodical engineering, careful evaluation, and continued empirical and theoretical work.

papers_seen.author: Guerrero
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory footprint, and latency while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Over the past decade, KD has expanded from soft-target (logit) matching to include feature- and layer-level alignment, attention- and relation-based signals, multi-teacher and multi-stage pipelines, self-distillation, and data-aware or data-free training regimes. In practice KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when the distillation protocol is tailored to student capacity, available data, and deployment constraints. Important limits remain — including optimization and capacity mismatch, reduced fidelity on rare tokens or out-of-distribution data, and the risk of transferring teacher biases — which require careful pipeline design, data strategies, and evaluation to mitigate.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger, expensive teacher models to smaller, efficient student models. Across vision, language, and other modalities, KD operates at multiple granularities (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or channel maps, and module-level replacements) and can serve both as a compression mechanism and as a broader training paradigm that improves calibration, generalization, and domain adaptation. Practical variants address constraints such as limited or private data, mismatched architectures, and deployment latency; persistent challenges include optimization failure modes, preserving rare-token or low-frequency behavior, and aligning internal representations between heterogeneous teacher–student pairs.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical, Design‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, flexible, and production-ready approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a core, composable element of a compression pipeline and combined with architecture-aware design, complementary compression techniques, and careful data strategies, distillation routinely produces compact models that retain most of a teacher's utility. Real-world success requires deliberate design choices to match distillation signals to student capacity and deployment constraints, and to mitigate limitations such as data scarcity, capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and the propagation of teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central practical technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring useful information from one or more high-capacity teachers. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft output distributions, intermediate features, relational structure) and how the transfer is scheduled or combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture modification). KD has enabled substantial reductions in model size and latency across vision and language tasks while retaining much of teacher performance, but its empirical success depends on student capacity, choice of distillation signals, data availability (or synthetic-data methods), and careful engineering to address optimization mismatch, distribution shift, and potential transfer of teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically essential approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD enables reduced storage and faster inference while preserving much of teacher performance when paired with appropriate distilled signals, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques. However, distillation is not a panacea: it can propagate teacher biases, struggle when training data are unavailable or misaligned with deployment distributions, and interact subtly with optimization and architecture mismatch. A pragmatic pipeline treats KD as the central tool but couples it with targeted strategies—feature- and layer-level objectives, data-free or synthesized-data protocols when needed, curriculum or sample-weighting policies, and hardware-aware pruning or architecture search—to maximize efficiency without sacrificing robustness or task-specific fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Molina
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD encompasses a range of targets and workflows—soft-output matching, intermediate-feature alignment, attention or relational losses, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free variants—and is most effective when combined with complementary compression tools and deployment-aware design choices. However, its success depends on careful choices about distillation signals, data strategies, architectural alignment, and mitigation of optimization and robustness failure modes.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Schmidt
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-oriented strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining KD with complementary compression primitives and data strategies—KD frequently delivers substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a panacea: it can propagate teacher weaknesses, requires careful handling of data or privacy constraints, and must be adapted to task and deployment requirements. I argue KD should be treated as the central component of a compression pipeline, integrated with architecture-aware design, data-aware training, and explicit checks for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact, deployable deep and language models by transferring information from large teacher models to smaller students. When treated as the center of a compression pipeline and combined with pretraining, architecture-aware design, data strategies (including data-free synthesis), and complementary compression techniques, KD routinely yields substantial reductions in size and latency while retaining much of teacher utility. However, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: its effectiveness depends on careful choice of distillation signals, student capacity, data availability or synthesis, and evaluation for robustness and distributional or fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical engine of model compression for deep learning and NLP: it provides flexible, high-utility transfer mechanisms that—when combined with complementary compression primitives and data strategies—enable compact, deployable models that approach teacher performance. Its success is not automatic; careful signal choice, teacher–student alignment, data handling, and explicit checks for robustness and fairness are required for reliable production results.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Patterns
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information from teachers through softened outputs, intermediate representations, or training dynamics. A range of techniques — including self-distillation, multi-stage curricula, feature alignment, online and adversarial schemes, and combinations with pruning or architecture-aware design — enable favorable trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and resource constraints. Practical success depends on student capacity, the choice of distillation targets, data availability or synthesis, and safeguards for robustness, privacy, and long-tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Task-Aware Path to Model Compression in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a flexible and practical framework for compressing large models and transferring capabilities to smaller ones. When applied thoughtfully — using layer-aware alignment, attention-guided feature matching, dynamic multi-teacher strategies, and privacy- or deployment-aware protocols — distillation enables substantial speedups, reduced footprint, and cross-modal or cross-device applicability with small drops (or even gains) in task performance. Distillation is not a plug-and-play cure: optimization challenges, teacher-student mismatch, and task-specific redundancy mean methods must be adapted to the target architecture and data regime to realize consistent benefits.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer predictive performance and internal representations from large, expensive teacher models to smaller, faster student models. Work in this area spans theoretical analyses, practical compression recipes for language and vision models, approaches that avoid access to original training data, and methods that target robustness, privacy, or device heterogeneity. The field balances trade-offs among student capacity, teacher imperfection, data availability, and downstream task requirements, producing a range of techniques—logit-level distillation, layer-wise and module-level matching, progressive replacement, data-free generation, and combined compression with low-precision numerics—that are evaluated across tasks from BERT compression to multimodal and 3D detection. This synthesis summarizes prevailing methods, motivations, and recurring challenges emerging from recent literature.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Reframing Knowledge Distillation: Beyond Strong Teachers to Regularization, Representations, and Practical Variants
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful tool for compressing deep models, but its benefits arise from multiple mechanisms beyond mere imitation of a stronger teacher. Empirical and theoretical work indicates that distillation combines regularization effects of soft targets, representational alignment, and optimization dynamics; these insights motivate a broader set of practical strategies (teacher-free or data-free distillation, feature-based objectives, contrastive and adversarial losses, ensembles, and co-training of teacher/student) to obtain compact models that generalize well. This paper argues that practitioners should select KD variants depending on data availability, deployment constraints, and the nature of the task, and that future research should prioritize understanding optimization and representation transfer rather than treating teacher capacity as the sole determinant of success.

papers_seen.author: Brewer
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful, engineering-centered paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Research and practice show KD can transfer richer supervisory signals than hard labels, be combined with pruning/quantization/architecture search, and be adapted to settings with limited or private data. While KD routinely recovers a large fraction of teacher performance across vision, language, graph, and generative tasks, its success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and careful handling of robustness, fairness, and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A broad toolkit—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, transferring relational signals or dynamics, and using variants such as multi-teacher, online/self-, and data-free distillation—has been developed and is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Practical success depends on teacher–student co‑design, data strategy, and careful evaluation for robustness, fairness, and long‑tail behavior; important open problems remain in handling capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and distillation without original data.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Compression: Effective but Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and practical approach to compress large neural models into smaller, faster, or more hardware-friendly students while retaining much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness spans supervised, self-supervised, and cross-modal settings, but the choice of what to transfer (logits, features, intermediate representations, attention), how to measure discrepancy, and how to combine KD with pruning or quantization critically determines success. I argue that KD should be treated as a toolbox of complementary techniques whose components must be matched to task, teacher quality, and deployment constraints to obtain reliable and robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Silva

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile, and central technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones while preserving most of their performance. KD works across modalities and tasks, integrates naturally with complementary compression strategies, and supports deployment under privacy- and resource-constrained settings. Realizing KD’s full potential requires attention to what signals are distilled (logits, features, relations), how data are managed or synthesized, and how teacher–student alignment and curricula are designed.

papers_seen.author: Jordan

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied with care to teacher signals, data selection, and student capacity, KD enables large reductions in size and latency while retaining much of a teacher’s performance, but meaningful limitations remain (optimization difficulty, capacity mismatch, and potential transfer of biases) that must be managed in deployment.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Practical Core of Model Compression — Central, Useful, but Not Enough Alone
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and empirically effective approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When engineered to match student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints, KD produces strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs and integrates well with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies. However, KD must be combined with representation-aware objectives, task-aware layer mapping, and safeguards for robustness and fairness to avoid transferring teacher imperfections and to preserve rare or out-of-distribution behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as the most practical and widely applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students for vision, language, and other modalities. When applied thoughtfully — selecting what to transfer (logits, features, attention), designing teacher-student pairs, and combining KD with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, data synthesis) — distillation recovers much of a teacher’s performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD also serves beyond compression as a regularizer that can improve robustness and generalization, but it is not a panacea: capacity mismatch, domain shift, optimization differences, and risks of transferring biases or vulnerability must be managed through targeted practices and evaluations.

KD delivers substantial practical gains in latency, memory, and deployability, but realizing those gains requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or no access to original data, and how to diagnose and mitigate failures such as capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and fairness harms.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Promise, Limits, and a Pipeline Prescription
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and widely applicable approach for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and NLP. When treated as a central component of an engineering pipeline and combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and appropriate data strategies, KD routinely produces favorable accuracy–efficiency tradeoffs. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its benefits depend on what signals are transferred, student capacity, data availability and distributional match, and explicit measures for robustness and fairness. Responsible, reliable compression therefore requires pipeline thinking, targeted augmentations, and diagnostics to detect transferred errors or degraded long‑tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Scenarios, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce the computational and storage footprint of large neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller students. Approaches span matching outputs (soft labels), transferring intermediate representations (feature or layer-wise distillation), adapting teacher selection and weighting, and operating under constraints such as missing original data, privacy, or multi-modal inputs. Practical work on language models, vision-language systems, and other domains highlights gains from task-aware selection of distilled information, architectural adapters between teacher and student, and advanced training schemes (e.g., adversarial sample generation, meta-learning of teachers). Empirical results and surveys show KD is versatile: it improves student accuracy over training from scratch, enables deployment in resource-constrained settings, and can be extended to preserve privacy and support domain adaptation, while theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when and why distillation helps and what challenges remain.

However, KD is not automatic: capacity mismatch, data scarcity, distribution shift, and the risk of transferring undesirable teacher behaviors require targeted design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses or transfers knowledge from larger or multiple models into smaller, faster models by leveraging softer training signals, intermediate representations, or alternate training protocols. Research has explored KD’s theoretical underpinnings, practical training strategies (including teacher-ensemble and teacher-free variants), privacy- and communication-aware settings, and extensions beyond classification to generation and structured prediction. Empirical work demonstrates KD’s ability to reduce deployment cost while retaining or sometimes even improving downstream performance, but trade-offs remain around data availability, representation matching, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Fuller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large “teacher” models into smaller “student” models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. KD spans soft-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, attention/relational objectives, and data strategies that include using original data, augmentation, or synthesized examples. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and matched to deployment constraints, KD reliably improves size/accuracy/latency trade-offs across vision and language tasks. Practical success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to evaluate and mitigate limits such as bias transfer, rare-token degradation, and robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Whitney
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD has evolved from simple soft-target (logit) matching to a flexible toolbox that includes representation- and relation-level transfers, multi-stage curricula, data-aware and data-free strategies, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptations. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and power while retaining much of teacher performance, but its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data regimes, and careful pipeline design to avoid failure modes such as capacity mismatch, degraded long-tail behavior, or the propagation of teacher biases.

papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Composable Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Sensitive Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for producing compact deep and NLP models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD delivers strong size–performance trade-offs when its signals, data strategy, and student capacity are aligned with deployment constraints, but it requires explicit handling of capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity, rare-token behaviors, and bias to be reliable in production.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.
