papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied compression techniques transfer information from large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable students so systems meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of the teacher’s effectiveness. The literature shows a spectrum of distillation targets — softened logits, intermediate features and attention maps, relational structure, and iterative or multi-teacher curricula — and complementary methods such as pruning, layer skipping, module replacement, and data synthesis. Practical success depends on aligning what is transferred to student capacity, handling limited or private data, and combining KD with architecture-aware design and validation to avoid optimization mismatches and unwanted bias transfer. Remaining gaps include robustness under domain shift, principled selection of distilled signals, and theoretical accounts that predict when KD will provide large gains.

papers_seen.author: Brooks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Promise, Limits, and Practical Remedies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, deployment-oriented toolkit for shrinking large deep and NLP models into smaller, faster students. When combined with complementary compression techniques and task-aware engineering, KD can achieve strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs for real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: it requires careful choices about teacher and student design, what signals to transfer, how to source or synthesize data, and how to evaluate and mitigate transferred biases, distributional failures, and rare-token degradation. A practical KD-centered pipeline pairs richer distillation objectives with data and architecture strategies and targeted diagnostics to ensure reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated method for producing compact models that preserve much of the performance and useful behavior of larger teacher models. KD works by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone and is most effective when integrated with complementary techniques (architecture-aware compression, pruning, quantization) and careful data and evaluation practices. However, KD is context-sensitive: its success depends on teacher quality, what signals are distilled, student capacity, data availability or synthesis, and explicit checks for robustness and fairness. Practical adoption therefore requires principled pipeline choices, staged training, and targeted mitigation of known failure modes.

Thus KD should be the default core of compression pipelines but applied with task‑aware engineering and explicit mitigations for its limitations.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile technique for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable ones. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, or relational signals—KD reduces inference cost while preserving much of teacher behavior. KD is not a single recipe but a flexible toolbox: its success depends on teacher design, the choice of distilled signal, data availability, and combination with complementary compression methods. When matched to task and deployment constraints, KD enables real-world use of pretrained models across vision, language, speech, graphs, and structured prediction, while open challenges remain around distribution shift, rare-token fidelity, and privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Gay
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely adopted set of techniques for transferring information from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD methods operate at multiple granularities — softened outputs, intermediate feature or attention alignment, relational signals, and synthesized or public-data training — and are often combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and data strategies (augmentation, curriculum, or data-free synthesis). Empirically, KD routinely yields strong size–accuracy trade-offs across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, but its success depends on careful alignment of teacher signals to student capacity, attention to data availability and domain shift, and checks for transferred biases and rare-token degradation. Remaining challenges include theoretical understanding of when distillation helps, preserving low-frequency behaviors in sequence models, and robustly distilling across heterogeneous architectures or privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Carter
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students that retain much of the teacher’s performance. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple softened-output matching to a toolkit that includes intermediate-representation alignment, layer-wise and relational objectives, online and multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free workflows. In practice KD is commonly combined with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and requires careful attention to teacher–student capacity, data strategies, and robustness or fairness concerns to succeed in real-world deployments.

papers_seen.author: Wallace
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic framework for transferring knowledge from large teacher models into smaller student models so they meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, and privacy. The literature shows KD has evolved from simple softened-logit matching to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate-representation and attention-level alignment, multi-stage and multi-teacher schedules, data-aware and data-free workflows, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Practical success hinges on matching distilled signals to student capacity, selecting or synthesizing appropriate training data, co-designing teacher and student architectures, and evaluating for robustness, long-tail behavior, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and production-oriented approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. When applied as a flexible toolkit—choosing appropriate supervision signals, aligning architectures, and integrating complementary compression methods—KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. At the same time, KD has predictable limitations (teacher flaws, capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and low-frequency behavior loss) that require pipeline-aware engineering and targeted mitigation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Remains Central to Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach to compressing large deep learning models into smaller, faster, and often more deployable ones. When combined with targeted strategies—such as pre-training compact architectures, layer-level alignment, selective sample choices, careful data augmentation, and privacy-aware protocols—distillation can preserve most of the teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. I argue that KD should be treated as a core component of any compression pipeline because it unifies improvements across accuracy, generalization, efficiency, and privacy without requiring wholesale re-engineering of tasks or architectures.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Across modalities and deployment regimes, KD can be adapted to match soft outputs, internal representations, or training dynamics, and it plays well with complementary techniques (architecture changes, pruning, data augmentation, and online/distributed protocols). However, realizing KD's benefits in practice requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to produce or curate training data, and how to mitigate transferred harms such as bias or degraded rare-token behavior. I argue KD should be treated as a central component in compression pipelines while being combined with representation-aware objectives, deployment-aware protocols, and safeguards for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Promise, Limits, and Deployment Recipes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and pragmatic approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels — from softened outputs to intermediate representations — KD reduces inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Its greatest practical value lies in being a flexible, composable tool: KD integrates with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-synthesis strategies to meet diverse deployment constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution; careful design is required to address data scarcity and privacy, teacher–student mismatch, optimization instability, and the preservation of rare-token or long-tail behavior. Practical pipelines therefore combine task-aware distillation targets, teacher–student co-design, staged training, and robustness and fairness evaluation to realize reliable compressed systems.

papers_seen.author: Rowe
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly applicable strategy for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing which signals to transfer, matching student capacity to tasks, and combining distillation with architectural and data strategies—KD produces favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs for on-device, latency-sensitive, and domain-specific NLP systems. Its advantages are balanced by contextual failure modes (teacher imperfections, distribution shift, rare-token fidelity) that require pipeline-level engineering, careful evaluation, and complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a flexible, empirically grounded route to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When used as a central, task-aware component of a broader compression pipeline — together with layer-aware mapping, student-friendly teacher design, data strategies, and complementary techniques such as pruning or quantization — KD can deliver substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Real-world use requires deliberate engineering to mitigate transferred biases, alignment and optimization gaps, and distributional mismatches.

papers_seen.author: Herring
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models so they can meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, compute, and privacy. KD spans simple soft-label matching and richer forms of transfer — intermediate feature and attention alignment, multi-stage or multi-teacher pipelines, data-free or synthesized-data approaches, and online or mutual distillation. In practice, KD is most effective when its signal, data strategy, and architectural alignment are chosen with the task and deployment constraints in mind and when distillation is combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Despite strong empirical gains across modalities, limitations remain: teacher imperfection, teacher–student capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity, and degradation on rare or low-frequency behaviors can reduce fidelity and robustness, so practitioners should treat KD as a flexible toolbox rather than a plug-and-play solution.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller models by transferring predictive and representational information from teachers to students. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical pipelines combine soft-target matching, representation-level imitation, architecture-aware design and search, and data strategies (including data-free or privacy-preserving synthesis). While KD often recovers much of a teacher's performance and can enable students that are substantially faster and smaller, success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align representations, and how to manage data and teacher quality; important open problems remain in robustness, domain shift, and theoretical explanation.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers behavior from large teacher models into smaller students to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher's capability. KD is flexible: it can match logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational signals; it can be combined with augmentation, architecture search, pruning, or task adaptation; and it can operate with or without original training data. When applied with careful choices about what to transfer, how to align representations, and how to address data or optimization mismatches, KD enables practical deployment of compact models across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central component of any compression strategy and summarizes concrete practices to maximize its effectiveness and mitigate known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods transfer behavior from large teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. Across vision and language, practitioners match softened outputs, align internal representations, or transfer relational signals, often combining distillation with quantization, architecture adaptation, or data selection to meet deployment constraints. KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance, but success depends on student capacity, the distilled signals chosen, data availability or synthesis, and strategies for aligning heterogeneous architectures and preserving robustness.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce compute, memory, and latency while preserving task performance. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, KD has been adapted into many forms—soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, attention and relational transfers, multi-teacher ensembles, online distillation, and task-adaptive pipelines—and combined with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to enable deployment in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Empirical work shows KD often recovers most of a teacher's utility in a much smaller footprint, but success depends on teacher quality, the choice of distilled signals, data availability and domain shift, and robustness and privacy constraints. The field continues to refine objectives, layer-mapping strategies, and workflows that make distillation effective across modalities and large pretrained models in practical deployments.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision, language, graph, and speech tasks, KD variants (logit/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, relational transfer, multi-stage or multi-teacher schedules, and privacy-aware procedures) enable substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while often preserving most of the teacher's performance. Practical deployments pair KD with pretraining, sample-selection, and complementary compression techniques to meet latency, device, and privacy constraints; however, challenges remain around capacity mismatch, data scarcity, domain shift, and preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, context‑sensitive mechanism in practical model compression. When carefully designed and combined with complementary tools — pruning, quantization, architecture search, synthetic or privacy‑aware data, and task‑aware curricula — KD produces compact models that retain much of a teacher’s performance across modalities and deployment constraints. However, KD is not automatic: success requires explicit choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or private data, and how to mitigate harmful teacher behaviors. A principled KD pipeline that adapts to task, data, and hardware needs yields the best tradeoff between efficiency and utility.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones. When combined with careful choices—such as pre-training compact students, data-free distillation for privacy, adaptive multi-teacher strategies, feature-level imitation, and teacher-side learning—KD can deliver strong task performance with much smaller inference cost. However, KD is not a panacea: optimization gaps between teacher and student, propagation of teacher biases, and dataset mismatches can limit gains unless explicitly addressed. A pragmatic KD pipeline therefore integrates algorithmic innovations and fairness/optimization checks to realize both efficiency and reliable behavior in production NLP and deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Estes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practitioner-oriented technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones suitable for deployment. When paired with complementary methods (architecture-aware design, pruning/quantization, data augmentation, and privacy-aware protocols), KD yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across modalities. Realizing those gains requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to source or synthesize data, how to align heterogeneous teacher–student architectures, and how to evaluate robustness and social harms under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Fuller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large “teacher” models into smaller “student” models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. KD spans soft-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, attention/relational objectives, and data strategies that include using original data, augmentation, or synthesized examples. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and matched to deployment constraints, KD reliably improves size/accuracy/latency trade-offs across vision and language tasks. Practical success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to evaluate and mitigate limits such as bias transfer, rare-token degradation, and robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving performance. KD encompasses soft-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, and relational or attention-based objectives and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques, appropriate data strategies, and teacher–student co-design. Open challenges include capacity mismatch, preservation of long‑tail behaviors, robustness and fairness transfer, and distillation under data or privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable, empirically effective approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. It supports multiple transfer signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps), operates with or without original training data, and composes naturally with complementary methods (pre-training of compact models, pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much teacher performance, but it is not a panacea: practitioners must address capacity mismatch, data or distributional heterogeneity, and the risk of transferring undesirable behaviors (biases or adversarial vulnerabilities). A pragmatic deployment pipeline treats KD as one component in a compression strategy, matched to task constraints and combined with targeted mitigations for fairness, robustness, and heterogeneous-data scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Design‑Sensitive Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the practical heart of model‑compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP: it reliably transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels, enables substantial reductions in inference cost, and composes naturally with complementary techniques. However, KD is not a turnkey cure — its effectiveness depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to evaluate and mitigate failure modes such as distribution shift, rare-token degradation, bias transfer, and privacy leakage. A production-ready approach treats KD as a flexible toolbox integrated with pruning, quantization, architecture design, data strategies (including data‑free methods), and explicit robustness/fairness checks.

papers_seen.author: Pearson
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible set of techniques for reducing the computational and memory cost of large neural models while preserving much of their predictive behavior. The family of methods includes transferring softened teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention patterns, distilling relational structure, applying self-distillation, and using data-aware or data-free sampling and synthesis. In practice KD is most effective when treated as a component of a broader compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, and careful data and training curricula—and when designers attend explicitly to student capacity, teacher–student alignment, data regimes, and deployment constraints such as latency, privacy, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Domains, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer knowledge from larger, costly models (teachers) into smaller, faster models (students) so that the students retain much of the teachers' accuracy while meeting deployment constraints. Across vision, language, graphs, and generative models, researchers have developed complementary approaches — from matching soft logits to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, channels, and global embedding topologies — and combined distillation with architecture search, pruning, and continual adaptation. Empirical work shows distillation can produce compact models that preserve or even improve task performance, but success depends on careful alignment of teacher-student inputs/representations, task- and domain-specific strategies, and trade-offs such as bias–variance effects introduced by soft labels. Important challenges remain around layer mismatches, low-frequency token handling, domain shift, and fundamental limits of compressibility for certain model families.

papers_seen.author: Hubbard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Efficacy, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically proven approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, graph, and generative-model settings. When treated as the central component of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis), KD enables strong size–accuracy–latency trade-offs. However, KD is not a panacea: success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, data availability or synthesis, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and rare-token or long-tail behaviors. Practical deployment therefore requires staged, context-sensitive distillation recipes that align signals to student capacity and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high‑capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has grown from matching softened teacher logits to a diverse toolkit including intermediate‑representation and attention alignment, multi‑teacher and self‑distillation variants, data‑aware and data‑free workflows, and task‑aware layer mapping. In practice KD is most effective when composed with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign/search) and when designers adapt distillation signals, data strategies, and curricula to student capacity and deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include teacher–student capacity mismatch, distributional shift and long‑tail/rare‑token behavior, robustness and fairness risks, and deploying under privacy or data‑scarce regimes.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Techniques, and Caveats
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applicable approach for compressing models and transferring knowledge across architectures and modalities. By training compact students under the guidance of larger teachers, KD enables substantial reductions in memory, compute, and inference latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Its flexibility supports many modalities (vision, language, speech, 3D, and generative models) and deployment constraints, but realizing its benefits in practice requires careful choices about what to transfer (logits vs. features), which samples to use, and how to handle limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models so that students retain much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, memory, and latency. KD methods range from matching softened outputs to imitating intermediate features, attention maps, and relational structure, and they are most effective when combined with architecture-aware design, complementary compression methods, and careful data strategies. Practical success depends on matching the distilled signals to student capacity, managing data or privacy constraints, and explicitly evaluating robustness and distributional generalization. Despite wide empirical success, open challenges remain around capacity mismatch, rare-token behavior in sequence models, optimization dynamics, and avoiding propagation of teacher artifacts.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Landscape of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses high-capacity models by transferring useful information from a teacher to a student, enabling deployment in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Methods differ in what is transferred (soft labels, intermediate representations, attention maps, relations) and how (feature matching, channel- or layer-wise alignment, augmentation, self- or data-free schemes). Distillation also serves broader roles beyond compression—regularization, bias transfer or mitigation, domain adaptation, and enabling multi-task or modality conversions. Practical effectiveness depends on choices of distilled signal, student capacity, data availability and augmentation, and deployment constraints; these choices shape trade-offs in accuracy, robustness, and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A broad set of techniques has been developed — matching softened logits, aligning intermediate features or attention maps, mapping teacher layers to student layers, and operating in online, offline, multi-teacher, federated, or data-free regimes. Distillation is typically combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic-data, selective sampling). In practice, distillation often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing inference cost and memory, but its success depends on student capacity, representation alignment, data availability, and attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy.

The literature spans simple soft-target matching to richer strategies—intermediate representation imitation, attention- and relation-based losses, curriculum and teacher-design methods, data-free synthesis, and combinations with pruning or architecture-aware compression. Practical success depends on choices about distillation signals, data availability and synthesis, teacher–student alignment, and complementary compression techniques; open issues include handling teacher imperfections, low-frequency behaviors, distribution shift, and privacy-sensitive or federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Harrison

Persistent challenges include capacity and optimization mismatch, preserving low-frequency or rare-token behavior, mitigating transfer of teacher biases, and ensuring generalization under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Collins

However, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to prepare students (including pre-training), how to handle limited or heterogeneous data, and how to mitigate transferred biases or adversarial vulnerability. Combining distillation with complementary strategies—layer-aware matching, feature-level mimicry, data synthesis or augmentation, teacher optimization, and robustness-aware objectives—gives the most reliable practical outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

However, realizing these gains reliably requires attention to what is transferred (logits, features, relations), how teachers and data are chosen, and hardware- or deployment-aware compression strategies.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Composable Core of Model Compression: Practical Benefits, Limits, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated not simply as a single recipe for compression but as the composable core of real-world model-compression pipelines. KD reliably reduces inference cost while preserving much of a teacher’s performance across modalities, and it naturally composes with pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis, and domain-adaptive procedures. To deploy reliable compressed models practitioners must pair KD with careful teacher/student design, data and sample-selection strategies (including data-free synthesis where necessary), evaluation for robustness and fairness, and complementary compression steps that meet hardware constraints. This paper argues for a pragmatic, pipeline-oriented view of KD and outlines targeted practices to maximize utility while mitigating known failure modes.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a necessary tool for compressing large deep and NLP models into efficient students suitable for deployment. However, naive KD that only matches teacher soft-labels is often insufficient. Effective distillation combines richer knowledge targets (internal features, attention, and layerwise signals), data-aware augmentations, selective sample strategies, and privacy- or domain-aware procedures. The best practical pipelines treat KD as a toolbox: choose which knowledge to transfer based on student capacity and task needs, use augmentation or self-distillation to improve generalization when data are scarce, and apply selective or privacy-preserving queries where constraints require it.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP — Powerful but Not Sufficient Alone
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-ready toolkit for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone, KD enables on-device deployment, domain adaptation, ensemble condensation, and improved efficiency with modest performance loss. However, KD has predictable failure modes (capacity mismatch, transferred biases, poor handling of rare or low-frequency behaviors) and must be combined with complementary compression techniques, robust data strategies, and evaluation under deployment constraints to be reliably effective.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Romero
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A broad set of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), training regimes (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher), and data strategies (original, public, synthesized, or data-free) have been developed. Distillation is typically used as the central component of a broader compression pipeline that includes pruning, quantization, and architecture design; its practical success depends on matching transfer signals to student capacity, teacher quality, and data availability while attending to robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift concerns.

papers_seen.author: Dodson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile empirical framework for compressing high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, and structured prediction, KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone (e.g., softened outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, or relational structure) and is commonly integrated with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies to meet latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Practical pipelines emphasize task- and student-aware design, careful teacher selection or training, and data-management choices; when applied thoughtfully KD can recover much of a teacher's performance but still faces challenges in robustness, domain shift, fairness, and theoretical understanding.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Balanced Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD can transfer soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention maps, or ensemble behavior into compact models that meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. However, KD is not a panacea: its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability and synthesis strategies, and explicit attention to robustness, optimization, and long-tail behavior. A disciplined pipeline that selects appropriate distillation signals, augments or synthesizes data when needed, and composes KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) yields the best practical outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression methods transfer behavior from large teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models. Across vision and language, practitioners match softened outputs, align internal representations, or transfer relational signals, often combining distillation with quantization, architecture adaptation, or data selection to meet deployment constraints. KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance, but success depends on student capacity, the distilled signals chosen, data availability or synthesis, and strategies for aligning heterogeneous architectures and preserving robustness.

papers_seen.author: Jimenez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Tool for Compressing and Adapting Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and empirically effective approach for producing compact models suitable for deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When framed as a central component of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary techniques and data strategies, KD yields strong size–performance trade-offs while enabling domain adaptation and robustness improvements. However, realizing those benefits in production requires careful design choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, and how to diagnose and mitigate transferred biases and rare-case degradation.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context‑Sensitive Toolbox for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical centerpiece for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When used thoughtfully — selecting what to transfer, adapting objectives to teacher and student capacities, and combining distillation with complementary methods like pruning, quantization, or data synthesis — KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. However, distillation’s effectiveness varies with task, data regime, and deployment constraints, so practitioners should treat it as a flexible set of techniques rather than a single plug‑and‑play algorithm.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research spans a range of goals — shrinking model size and latency, preserving privacy, enabling distributed learning, and retaining task- or robustness-related properties — and a correspondingly diverse set of techniques including logit and feature matching, layer-wise and many-to-many mapping, adversarial generation of training examples, and architecture-aware pruning and replacement. Empirical work shows effective trade-offs across vision, multimodal, and language tasks, while recent methods also tackle practical constraints such as lack of original data, privacy requirements, and distributed communication budgets.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of methods for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under compute, latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD spans soft-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, attention- and relation-based transfers, multi-teacher and self-distillation regimes, and data-aware workflows (including synthesized or data-free approaches). When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and task-aware data strategies, KD routinely produces compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while enabling deployment. Realizing these gains in practice requires careful choices about transfer targets, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability or synthesis, and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and rare-case fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Baird
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used, practical strategy for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Research over the last decade has extended KD from simple softened-logit matching into a flexible toolkit that transfers soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention and relational structure, and curriculum or ensemble signals. In practice KD is typically combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies) and used with task-aware choices about distilled signals and training data. KD routinely improves compact models over training from scratch, but its effectiveness depends on student capacity, data availability or synthesis, teacher–student alignment, and explicit handling of robustness and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Branch
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information beyond hard labels—via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and ensemble guidance—and is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or data synthesis to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and deployment-aware evaluation. Open challenges include preserving robustness and low-frequency behavior, avoiding transferred biases, and principled data-free distillation.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Integrations, and Design Sensitivities
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most practical and versatile core technique for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a central component of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary methods (architecture adaptation, pruning, quantization, data strategies, and training curricula), KD routinely yields favorable size–performance trade-offs. Practical success requires matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling data or privacy constraints, and explicitly addressing robustness and long-tail behaviors; when these design sensitivities are respected, KD enables reliable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large neural networks by training smaller student models to reproduce useful behavior of larger teacher models. Across vision, language, speech and graph settings, KD variants—matching softened teacher logits, aligning intermediate features, adversarial and contrastive objectives, multi-stage or multi-teacher pipelines, and data- or privacy-aware synthesis—enable large reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Realizing these gains requires task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to map layers between architectures, how to select or synthesize training data, and how to balance regularization from soft targets with student capacity and robustness considerations.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile toolkit for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and communication costs. KD techniques range from matching softened outputs to aligning internal representations, synthesizing surrogate data when originals are unavailable, and co-designing compact architectures. However, KD is context-sensitive: its success depends on the distillation signal, data regime, teacher–student alignment, privacy constraints, and explicit checks for robustness and fairness. Treating KD as a central component of a broader compression pipeline — combined with architecture search, task-aware objectives, and privacy- or data-aware procedures — yields the most reliable path to efficient, deployable models.

papers_seen.author: Parks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Practical Principles and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practically oriented approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller students that meet deployment constraints. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone and is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and careful engineering of data, teacher–student alignment, and evaluation. The method reduces inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but deployment requires attention to capacity mismatch, data regimes, distributional shift, and risks of transferring biases or brittle behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Lucas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical, but Context‑Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students that preserves much of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and energy costs. KD succeeds across modalities by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels, but its practical effectiveness depends on choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to supply or synthesize data, and how to diagnose and mitigate failure modes such as capacity mismatch, bias transfer, and degradation on rare or out‑of‑distribution cases. A responsible engineering approach treats KD as the central component of a compression pipeline that must be combined with complementary methods, careful curricula, and deployment‑oriented evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency. KD encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention/relational signals, and can be combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies (including synthesized or data-free approaches). Empirical work shows KD routinely improves student performance when design choices are matched to student capacity and deployment constraints, but practitioners must address challenges such as distribution shift, low-frequency behavior loss, and transfer of undesirable teacher properties.

papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Essential, Practical, and Context‑Sensitive for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central method for turning large, high‑performing models into compact students suitable for deployment. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what to transfer, how to obtain or synthesize data, and how to align teacher and student architectures—KD yields large gains in latency, memory, and deployability while preserving much of a teacher’s performance. However, KD is not a one‑size‑fits‑all recipe: naive soft‑label matching often underperforms, data availability or privacy constraints can require data‑free or zero‑shot strategies, and representation or optimization mismatches can harm rare‑token behavior, robustness, and fairness. Effective pipelines therefore treat KD as a toolbox to be combined with architecture design, data strategies, and targeted regularization to meet specific deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Path to Efficient Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation provides a pragmatic and versatile set of techniques to compress large neural models into compact, faster students while retaining much of their performance. Across NLP and vision, modern distillation variants — including multi-teacher pipelines, self-distillation, teacher optimization, and task-aware layer alignment — address core challenges such as capacity gaps and task-specific redundancy. When combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, low-precision arithmetic, architecture search), distillation enables deployment of high-performing models under tight resource or latency constraints.

papers_seen.author: Webb
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. A broad toolkit—softened logits, intermediate representation and attention alignment, multi-teacher curricula, and data‑free synthesis—has been developed and commonly combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign). Practical success depends on aligning what is transferred to student capacity, handling limited or private data, and combining distillation with deployment-aware engineering to manage robustness, rare-token behaviors, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Lambert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When integrated with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture modification, or progressive module replacement) and paired with careful choices about what signals to transfer and which data to use, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while preserving much of teacher performance. Real-world use also requires attention to teacher design, optimization gaps, and risks such as propagated biases or degraded rare-token behavior.

papers_seen.author: Salas
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a central, practical set of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. The field unifies multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals), diverse training workflows (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation, data-free), and combinations with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation). Effective distillation depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data strategies, and guarding against transferred teacher errors and distributional or low-frequency failure modes. Applications span NLP, vision (including vision transformers), multimodal generation, and industrial prediction systems, and open challenges remain in robustness, domain adaptation, and automated architecture-aware compression.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully — choosing appropriate distillation signals, handling data constraints, and combining KD with complementary techniques — KD can recover most of a teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements. However, KD is not a panacea: its success depends on student capacity, representation alignment, optimization schedules, and careful mitigation of teacher biases and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Weber
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. The field encompasses matching softened teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations and attention, online/cooperative schemes, and data- or privacy-aware variants. Distillation routinely combines with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet latency, memory, and regulatory constraints. Practical effectiveness depends on choices about which signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to source or synthesize training data, and how to preserve robustness, rare-token behavior, and fairness under distributional shift.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Reframing Knowledge Distillation: Beyond Strong Teachers to Regularization, Representations, and Practical Variants
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful tool for compressing deep models, but its benefits arise from multiple mechanisms beyond mere imitation of a stronger teacher. Empirical and theoretical work indicates that distillation combines regularization effects of soft targets, representational alignment, and optimization dynamics; these insights motivate a broader set of practical strategies (teacher-free or data-free distillation, feature-based objectives, contrastive and adversarial losses, ensembles, and co-training of teacher/student) to obtain compact models that generalize well. This paper argues that practitioners should select KD variants depending on data availability, deployment constraints, and the nature of the task, and that future research should prioritize understanding optimization and representation transfer rather than treating teacher capacity as the sole determinant of success.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Over the past decade this has grown from simple logit-matching into a toolkit that includes internal representation alignment, layer-mapping strategies, data and privacy-aware procedures, adversarial and robustness-aware objectives, online and distributed schemes, and methods tailored for specific architectures such as pre-trained language models. Distillation often recovers much of a teacher’s performance when deliberately designed (choice of signals, data, and architecture), but it faces limits from optimization difficulties, capacity mismatch, distributional shift, and the risk of transferring undesirable teacher behaviors such as bias. Practical success therefore depends on combining multiple transfer signals, handling data constraints, and adapting both teacher and student to the deployment context.

papers_seen.author: Dean
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal information. Methods range from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate features or relational structure, and KD is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign to meet deployment constraints. Empirical work shows strong practical gains across vision and NLP, but challenges remain around representation alignment, robustness, rare-token fidelity, privacy, and data heterogeneity — motivating richer distillation targets and deployment-aware pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, engineering-friendly family of techniques that enables large neural models to be converted into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. When paired with complementary compression tools and careful data or curriculum design, KD supports real-world constraints such as latency, memory, privacy, and heterogeneous deployment. However, its practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, addressing data scarcity and teacher bias, and evaluating robustness under distribution shifts.
