papers_seen.author: Kane
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Extensions, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, task- and deployment-aware toolkit for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a composable component — combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies (public, synthesized, or online), and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization) — KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, KD is not a universal fix: its practical success depends on careful teacher design, attention to student capacity and data regimes, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as distribution shift, poor rare-token transfer, federated-data heterogeneity, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Palmer
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while attempting to preserve predictive performance. The literature provides a flexible toolbox — matching softened logits, imitating intermediate features or attention, relational losses, multi- and self-teaching regimes, and data-aware or data-free strategies — and emphasizes composing KD with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, or neural architecture search for realistic deployment. Empirical work shows KD often recovers most teacher performance in practice, but success depends on student capacity, signal selection, data availability, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy. Open challenges include handling distribution shift, preserving rare-token or low-frequency behaviors, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, and developing stronger theoretical explanations for when and why distillation helps.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. Modern KD goes beyond matching logits: it includes feature- and representation-level transfers, multi-teacher and self-distillation strategies, and workflows that integrate augmentation, data-free synthesis, pruning, and quantization to meet latency, memory, and privacy requirements. Practical success depends on matching distillation technique to deployment objectives, careful design of layer mappings and loss terms, attention to teacher quality and data availability, and combinations with other compression tools to preserve robustness and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical set of techniques for transferring information from large, high-capacity 'teacher' models to smaller, efficient 'student' models so they can meet real-world constraints (compute, memory, latency, privacy). KD methods operate at multiple granularities — softened output logits, intermediate feature or attention matching, relational and module-level objectives — and are frequently combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design, or data synthesis). Empirically, KD routinely improves student performance compared to training from scratch and enables deployment across modalities and constrained settings, though challenges remain in robustness, low-frequency behavior, domain shift, and distillation without original data. This synthesis summarizes core methods, practical workflows, empirical benefits, and open problems to guide applied KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: What is known about knowledge distillation and model compression in deep learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful and practical approach for turning large, high‑capacity teacher models into smaller, faster, and more deployable student models. Across vision, language, multimodal, and federated settings, KD techniques include matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations or attention, many‑to‑many layer mapping, multi‑teacher and online/meta‑teaching schemes, and data‑ or privacy‑aware synthesis. KD delivers strong empirical size/latency gains when combined with architecture preparation and task‑aware choices, but its effectiveness is bounded by optimization mismatch, teacher imperfections, data or distribution shift, and robustness/fairness concerns. Best practices emphasize combining logits and feature objectives, addressing representation mismatch (layer mapping, pretraining), and using data‑aware or privacy‑preserving strategies for constrained deployments.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Christian
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and, in many variants, internal representations. A broad toolkit — soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi- and self-distillation, online and data-free protocols — combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) yields compact models that often recover a large fraction of teacher performance. Practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, student capacity, data availability or synthesis, and defenses against optimization mismatches, distribution shift, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Levine
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers richer supervision than hard labels—ranging from softened logits to intermediate representations and relational signals—and is most effective when integrated with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). While KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, realizing those gains in production requires attention to student capacity, data availability (including data-free or synthesized-data approaches), optimization dynamics, and explicit evaluation for robustness, privacy, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly practical family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods transfer predictive behavior or internal representations from teachers to students and are effective across modalities and tasks when combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression methods. Success depends on principled choices about distillation targets, student capacity, data selection or synthesis, and mitigation of distribution-shift, rare-token, and bias-amplification failures. KD therefore functions best as a central, design-sensitive component of end-to-end model-compression pipelines that balance accuracy, latency, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression in NLP: Benefits, Techniques, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible method for transferring the capabilities of large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary techniques (architecture-aware design, quantization, data synthesis, or curriculum learning), KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of the original performance. However, its success depends on careful choice of what signals to transfer, availability or synthesis of training data, and explicit handling of domain shift, student capacity mismatches, and potential amplification of teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation: Versatile Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and powerful approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient ones. Beyond simple size reduction, KD enables transfer of capabilities across modalities, supports domain adaptation, improves deployment in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings, and can be adapted to distributed training. However, benefits are not automatic: careful design of teacher-student alignment, training data, and distillation objectives is required to preserve task performance and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Boyd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques that transfer information from larger, higher‑capacity teacher models (or ensembles) to smaller, faster student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Methods span matching teacher soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention, designing teacher training to ease transfer, selecting or synthesizing distillation data, and combining distillation with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can retain much teacher performance when carefully applied, but practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to handle student capacity and data heterogeneity, and how to mitigate teacher imperfections and robustness or fairness tradeoffs.

papers_seen.author: Bailey
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used paradigm for transferring behavior from large “teacher” models into smaller “student” models to reduce inference cost while preserving much of predictive performance. The literature shows a spectrum of distillation targets (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure), data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or no-data approaches), and workflows (offline, online, multi-teacher, federated). Empirical and conceptual work emphasizes the importance of teacher–student capacity alignment, choice of distillation signal, and combination with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation). Despite frequent success across vision, language, speech, and graphs, open challenges include optimization barriers that prevent perfect imitation, preserving rare or long-tail behaviors, robustness under distribution shift, privacy-sensitive deployments, and adapting distillation to heterogeneous device or federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer predictive and representational information from larger teacher models to smaller students so models can be deployed under compute, memory, latency, or privacy constraints. The literature spans simple soft-target matching to richer strategies—intermediate representation imitation, attention- and relation-based losses, curriculum and teacher-design methods, data-free synthesis, and combinations with pruning or architecture-aware compression. Practical success depends on choices about distillation signals, data availability and synthesis, teacher–student alignment, and complementary compression techniques; open issues include handling teacher imperfections, low-frequency behaviors, distribution shift, and privacy-sensitive or federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Durham
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Practical KD spans matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention, multi‑teacher schedules, and data-aware or data‑free workflows, and it is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and deployment‑aware design. This synthesis summarizes methods, empirical strengths, typical failure modes, and best practices for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger, expensive models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students). KD has been applied across vision, language, generative modeling, and privacy-sensitive settings to reduce storage, latency, and energy while attempting to preserve accuracy and desirable properties. Practical approaches range from soft-label matching and feature imitation to many-to-many layer mappings and self-distillation; theoretical work links KD to regularization effects and label smoothing. Despite clear empirical successes in compressing large pretrained language models and vision networks, important challenges remain: students often fail to replicate teachers' internal representations, robustness and fairness do not automatically transfer, and privacy or heterogeneous-data settings impose additional constraints. Ongoing advances focus on richer targets (internal features, layer mappings), alternate training regimes (self- and teacher-free distillation), and task-aware strategies for robust and private compression.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible toolkit for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD transfers information at multiple levels—soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals—and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), careful student–teacher alignment, and data strategies adapted to privacy or scarcity constraints. While KD often yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, reliable deployment requires targeted engineering to manage capacity mismatch, robustness, bias transfer, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Dougherty
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Aware Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical method for compressing deep and NLP models into deployable students. KD provides a flexible toolkit that preserves much of teacher behavior while enabling dramatic reductions in latency, memory, and energy, but its success depends on careful choices about transferred signals, student architecture, data strategy, and robustness/fairness diagnostics.

papers_seen.author: Reed
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Balanced Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile, production-ready approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, faster students. When engineered carefully—selecting what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student representations, managing or synthesizing data, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods—KD yields large efficiency gains while preserving most task performance. However, KD is not automatic: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data and curriculum choices, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate-representation matching, layerwise alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation, curriculum and augmentation strategies, and privacy- or data-free procedures. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and task-aware choices about what and how to transfer, KD enables practical deployment of high-performing models across modalities while raising open issues in robustness, fairness, and distributional generalization.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other forms of learned structure so students retain much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost. KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a broad toolkit that includes feature- and representation-level objectives, multi-teacher schemes, data- and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with pruning or quantization. Practical application requires task- and deployment-aware choices that balance accuracy, latency, data availability, and social/robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Ruiz
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of methods for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models so they can be deployed under compute, memory, latency, or privacy constraints. KD expands beyond matching teacher soft labels to include intermediate-representation and relational matching, multi-stage or online training regimes, and data strategies that range from using original training data to synthetic or data‑free approaches. When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign) and careful engineering of teacher–student alignment and data curricula, KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Key open problems include capacity and optimization mismatch, preserving long‑tail or rare behaviors, robustness and fairness transfer, and distillation under severe data or privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Approaches and Applications of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, more costly models to smaller, deployable models. Modern work expands beyond simple soft-label matching to include distillation of internal representations, feature-level imitation, privacy-preserving and data-free strategies, task-adaptive compression, and adaptations to specialized architectures (e.g., GANs, detectors, and transformers). These methods aim to preserve accuracy, robustness, and efficiency (compute, memory, or communication) while enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices or in privacy-sensitive and distributed settings.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Efficient and Responsible NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, versatile approach for compressing large models and enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. Beyond raw compression, KD supports domain adaptation, data-free scenarios, improved inference speed, and novel training regimes for specialized tasks. However, distillation is not a panacea: it can amplify teacher biases, interact with regularization techniques in subtle ways, and benefits most when combined with complementary methods such as architecture-aware training, generator-based sample synthesis, or instance-aware losses.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. The practice has evolved from logits matching into a flexible toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-augmentation and data-free strategies, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. When matched to task requirements, student capacity, and data constraints, distillation reliably improves size–performance trade-offs for vision and language models, though practical success requires careful design to manage capacity mismatch, distribution shift, privacy, and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Colon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully — choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining KD with complementary compression methods and data strategies — KD enables large reductions in inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is context-sensitive: its success depends on data availability, capacity matching, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Mckinney
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely adopted approach for turning large, high‑performing models into compact students that can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD is flexible in what it transfers (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational signals) and in how it is applied (offline teacher–student training, online/self-distillation, multi‑teacher ensembles, and data‑free procedures). Practical success depends on matching the distillation signals to student capacity, combining KD with complementary compression techniques, and engineering data and optimization workflows that mitigate distribution shift, bias transfer, and long‑tail degradation.

papers_seen.author: Gregory
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of methods for transferring information from large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable students so the students retain much of the teacher’s utility while reducing inference cost, memory, and latency. KD operates at multiple granularities (softened outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational signals) and is most effective when integrated into a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture-aware design, pruning/quantization, careful data strategies, and diagnostics for robustness, fairness, and privacy. Empirical and methodological work shows broad applicability across modalities but also identifies concrete limits—capacity mismatch, distribution shift, rare-token degradation, and propagation of teacher biases—motivating task-aware design and complementary techniques.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) frames model compression as transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. KD encompasses soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, online/self-distillation, and data-aware or data-free workflows. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and matched to student capacity and data availability, KD routinely yields large reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. However, its success is context-sensitive: careful choices of distilled signals, data regime, teacher–student alignment, and mitigation of robustness and fairness issues are required. Open problems include principled data selection or synthesis, preserving rare-token or low-frequency behaviors, matching heterogeneous architectures, and preventing transfer of undesired biases.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully — choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student representations, and integrating complementary compression methods — KD frequently yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance. However, KD is not automatic: careful engineering is required to handle capacity mismatch, data scarcity, low-frequency behaviors, and the risk of propagating teacher biases. Best practice treats KD as a flexible pipeline that is adapted to task, data, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Reframing Knowledge Distillation: Beyond Strong Teachers to Regularization, Representations, and Practical Variants
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful tool for compressing deep models, but its benefits arise from multiple mechanisms beyond mere imitation of a stronger teacher. Empirical and theoretical work indicates that distillation combines regularization effects of soft targets, representational alignment, and optimization dynamics; these insights motivate a broader set of practical strategies (teacher-free or data-free distillation, feature-based objectives, contrastive and adversarial losses, ensembles, and co-training of teacher/student) to obtain compact models that generalize well. This paper argues that practitioners should select KD variants depending on data availability, deployment constraints, and the nature of the task, and that future research should prioritize understanding optimization and representation transfer rather than treating teacher capacity as the sole determinant of success.

papers_seen.author: Nunez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Engineering-Dependent Route to Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students, enabling reduced inference cost and deployment on constrained devices. KD can match final outputs or internal representations and is often combined with complementary compression techniques; however, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align architectures, and how to handle data and optimization mismatches. I argue that KD should be treated as an essential, task-aware component of compression pipelines rather than a plug-and-play solution, and I offer practical directions to maximize its benefits while mitigating common failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Barton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical but Design-Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary compression techniques and careful data and architecture choices, KD often yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: its effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred, how student and teacher are aligned, data quality and selection, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Terry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational signals. Over the last decade KD has evolved from soft-label matching into a flexible toolbox—incorporating feature- and layer-level objectives, multi-teacher and self-distillation regimes, data synthesis or data-free workflows, and integrations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to align architectures and capacities, what data to use (or synthesize), and how to mitigate robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift problems.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information that goes beyond hard labels. Across vision and language tasks, KD has evolved from soft-label matching to a toolbox of techniques that include intermediate-feature alignment, multi-teacher curricula, self-distillation, and data-aware or data-free workflows. This synthesis summarizes the principal methods, practical combinations with other compression techniques, and the main limitations and open problems that shape current research and deployment choices.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers predictive behavior and internal representations through soft targets, feature alignment, and layer-aware signals. While it reliably improves compact-model performance relative to training from scratch, KD’s success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to handle data limitations, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression techniques. Responsible deployment requires adapting KD to task constraints, diagnosing failure modes (e.g., capacity mismatch, domain shift, rare-token degradation, biased transfer), and using engineering practices such as curriculum-style annealing, targeted augmentation, and hybrid losses.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Practical Core for Model Compression — A Qualified Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, practical core of model-compression pipelines in deep learning and NLP because it reliably transfers richer supervision from large teachers into smaller students and composes with complementary compression primitives. However, KD is design-sensitive: its practical success depends on student capacity, data strategies (including synthesis or privacy-aware protocols), teacher–student alignment, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias, rare-token degradation, and distribution shift. A production-ready approach embeds KD in an engineering-aware pipeline that pairs appropriate distillation signals with architecture-aware design, data curricula, and robustness/fairness evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Across vision, language, multimodal, graph, and recommender settings, KD has evolved from soft-target (logit) matching to a broader toolbox that includes intermediate-feature alignment, attention and relational transfers, online and multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free workflows. When KD is treated as the central element of an engineering-aware compression pipeline and combined with complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, privacy-aware approaches), it routinely yields strong size–performance trade-offs. Practical success requires matching distilled signals to student capacity, addressing distribution shift and long-tail behaviors, and guarding against transferring teacher weaknesses; these remain active areas for research and careful production practice.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and production-oriented approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. When applied as a flexible toolkit—choosing appropriate supervision signals, aligning architectures, and integrating complementary compression methods—KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. At the same time, KD has predictable limitations (teacher flaws, capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and low-frequency behavior loss) that require pipeline-aware engineering and targeted mitigation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Matthews
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Practical Methods, Trade-offs, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) serves as a practical, widely adopted approach to compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone—such as softened logits, intermediate features, attention maps, or relational structure—KD reduces latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. In practice KD is used as a composable component of broader compression pipelines together with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data strategies. Its success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability (including data-free methods), and explicit handling of robustness, domain shift, privacy, and fairness. Key engineering practices include multi-signal objectives, staged or progressive compression, and diagnostics for bias and rare-token fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller ones by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other structural knowledge from teacher(s) to student(s). Approaches range from classic logit-matching to feature- and channel-wise transfer, multi-teacher schemes, self-distillation, data-free adversarial methods, and adaptations for distributed or heterogeneous settings. Empirical work shows that properly designed distillation can preserve much of teacher performance while greatly reducing size and latency; practical success depends on choices like what form of knowledge to transfer, whether and how to augment or synthesize data, and how to handle heterogeneous compute or domain shifts.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Over the past decade the approach has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a toolkit that includes representation-level alignment, multi-teacher and online schedules, and data-aware or data-free workflows. When combined with complementary compression primitives and careful engineering, distillation routinely produces compact models that trade only modest performance for large gains in latency, memory, and energy efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Uses, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and multimodal tasks, a family of techniques—soft-label matching, feature and attention imitation, layer mapping, multi-teacher and curriculum schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols—enables students to recover much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Practical success depends on task- and deployment-aware choices (distilled signal, student capacity, data availability, and augmentation), and remaining challenges include robustness to distribution shift, preservation of rare-token or fine-grained behaviors, and distillation under privacy or data-scarce conditions.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Learning Student Networks via Feature Embedding
papers_seen.abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks have been widely used in numerous applications, but their demanding storage and computational resource requirements prevent their applications on mobile devices. Knowledge distillation aims to optimize a portable student network by taking the knowledge from a well-trained heavy teacher network. Traditional teacher-student based methods used to rely on additional fully-connected layers to bridge intermediate layers of teacher and student networks, which brings in a large number of auxiliary parameters. In contrast, this paper aims to propagate information from teacher to student without introducing new variables which need to be optimized. We regard the teacher-student paradigm from a new perspective of feature embedding. By introducing the locality preserving loss, the student network is encouraged to generate the low-dimensional features which could inherit intrinsic properties of their corresponding high-dimensional features from teacher network. The resulting portable network thus can naturally maintain the performance as that of the teacher network. papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible toolkit for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD transfers information at multiple levels—soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals—and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), careful student–teacher alignment, and data strategies adapted to privacy or scarcity constraints. While KD often yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, reliable deployment requires targeted engineering to manage capacity mismatch, robustness, bias transfer, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Lane
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. Methods operate at multiple granularities — softened outputs (logits), intermediate feature alignment, attention/relational transfers, and module- or layer-wise mappings — and are commonly combined with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation). Practical pipelines emphasize teacher–student co‑design, capacity-aware selection of distilled signals, and careful evaluation for robustness, rare-token behavior, privacy, and distributional shift. While distillation routinely recovers much of a teacher’s performance in smaller footprints, open challenges remain in theory, handling imperfect or heterogeneous teachers, and preserving long‑tail and safety properties under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques aim to transfer information from large, expensive teacher models into smaller, faster students while preserving performance. This synthesis summarizes methodological families (soft-label distillation, representation distillation, adversarial and decision-boundary approaches, data-free and domain-adaptive strategies), theoretical insights about when and why distillation helps, and practical considerations including robustness, privacy, and architecture-aware compression. It highlights representative results and trade-offs reported across recent work, and outlines open directions for improving optimization, preserving robustness, and adapting distillation to domain and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Practical and Robust Knowledge Distillation for Deployable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a central tool for compressing large deep models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and power constraints. Beyond matching teacher output probabilities, modern distillation should transfer internal structure, be tailored to domain and modality differences, and integrate with quantization, privacy, and data-limited settings. When applied with methods that address representation mismatch, optimization challenges, and curriculum of supervisory signals, distillation enables small models that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the central, practical component of model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. When used as a flexible toolbox—choosing appropriate distillation targets, aligning teacher and student representations, designing student-aware architectures, and combining distillation with complementary compression primitives—KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Real-world application requires careful engineering to address capacity mismatch, distributional shift, long-tail behaviors, and potential transfer of teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. A broad toolkit has emerged—soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation, and data-aware or data-free protocols—that, when combined with complementary compression methods and careful teacher–student co-design, yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, student capacity, data availability, and mitigation of robustness and bias risks.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression encompass a family of methods that transfer information from larger, high-capacity models (teachers) to smaller, efficient models (students). These approaches aim to retain predictive performance while reducing model size, latency, or enabling deployment under privacy or communication constraints. Recent work broadens distillation beyond logits to intermediate features, attention maps, multi-teacher setups, and data-limited or privacy-preserving regimes, producing task- and domain-aware compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Reese
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a set of techniques that transfer information from larger, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster student models so they can be deployed under constraints of latency, memory, or privacy. Methods range from matching softened teacher outputs to aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational structure, and using synthesized or public data; practitioners routinely combine KD with pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign. KD often recovers most of the teacher’s performance but requires careful choices about the distillation signal, teacher–student capacity matching, and data handling. Ongoing challenges include robustness under distribution shift, preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors, and adapting KD to heterogeneous architectures and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. The field has broadened from soft-logit matching to include feature- and layer-level alignment, relational and attention-aware transfers, data-free synthesis, adversarially-aware objectives, and curriculum or multi-teacher schemes. Practical success depends on choices about the distillation signal, data availability or synthesis, teacher–student architectural alignment, and training curricula; open challenges include preserving rare or long-tail behaviors, maintaining robustness and privacy, and adapting distillation to domain shifts and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Approaches and Understandings of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer predictive or representational information from larger, more expensive models (or ensembles) to smaller, cheaper models while retaining as much performance as possible. Recent work has expanded KD beyond simple soft-label matching to include intermediate-layer supervision, task-adaptive architecture search, online and federated variants, teacher optimization, and careful consideration of data and augmentation strategies. These advances enable practical compression for NLP and wider deep-learning applications by improving efficiency, robustness, and suitability for resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Harrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical, Design-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When paired with careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data and privacy constraints, KD routinely yields compact models that preserve most of a teacher's utility while meeting real-world constraints. However, KD is not automatic: capacity mismatch, data scarcity, distribution shift, and the risk of transferring undesirable teacher behaviors require targeted design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer predictive capacity from large, expensive models into smaller, faster models while preserving performance. Approaches vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, feature projectors), how teachers are constructed (single teacher, multi-teacher, self-teaching, or meta-learned teachers), and what resources are available (original data, public data, or no data). Practical extensions address domain-specific needs (e.g., BERT compression, low-precision deployment, privacy-preserving and federated settings) and include strategies such as progressive module replacement, multi-stage distillation, adversarially generated synthetic data, and self-supervised distillation. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both the power of soft targets as a regularizer and the importance of aligning internal representations and layer correspondences to improve student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Versatile Tool for Compression in NLP: Promise, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students that retain much of the teacher's performance. In natural language processing, KD can operate at multiple granularities — from logits to intermediate representations or entire modules — and can be combined with pre-training, pruning, and low-precision inference to meet real-world deployment constraints. However, distillation is not a turnkey solution: optimization difficulties, mismatches in internal representations, and task-specific redundancies can limit benefits unless methods are adapted to the model size, pre-training regimen, and downstream objectives. When applied thoughtfully (e.g., pre-training compact students, selectively transferring internal features, and using task-aware layer-wise matching), KD yields efficient models that generalize well across tasks and settings.
