papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: What is known about knowledge distillation and model compression in deep learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful and practical approach for turning large, high‑capacity teacher models into smaller, faster, and more deployable student models. Across vision, language, multimodal, and federated settings, KD techniques include matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations or attention, many‑to‑many layer mapping, multi‑teacher and online/meta‑teaching schemes, and data‑ or privacy‑aware synthesis. KD delivers strong empirical size/latency gains when combined with architecture preparation and task‑aware choices, but its effectiveness is bounded by optimization mismatch, teacher imperfections, data or distribution shift, and robustness/fairness concerns. Best practices emphasize combining logits and feature objectives, addressing representation mismatch (layer mapping, pretraining), and using data‑aware or privacy‑preserving strategies for constrained deployments.

papers_seen.author: Lindsey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context‑Sensitive Engine of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance. KD encompasses a family of targets (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention/relational signals) and training regimes (offline, online/self-distillation, data-free or synthetic data) and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques and deployment-aware design. While KD routinely yields favorable size–accuracy trade-offs, its success is context-sensitive: careful teacher–student co-design, data strategies, and explicit checks for robustness, fairness, and rare-token fidelity are required to avoid well-known failure modes. This essay argues that KD should be treated as the practical core of model-compression pipelines and gives recommended practices for realizing reliable, efficient students in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Palmer
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while attempting to preserve predictive performance. The literature provides a flexible toolbox — matching softened logits, imitating intermediate features or attention, relational losses, multi- and self-teaching regimes, and data-aware or data-free strategies — and emphasizes composing KD with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, or neural architecture search for realistic deployment. Empirical work shows KD often recovers most teacher performance in practice, but success depends on student capacity, signal selection, data availability, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy. Open challenges include handling distribution shift, preserving rare-token or low-frequency behaviors, avoiding propagation of teacher biases, and developing stronger theoretical explanations for when and why distillation helps.

papers_seen.author: Hamilton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-oriented family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models so they meet deployment constraints while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD encompasses matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, multi-stage or self-distillation schemes, and data-aware variants (including data-free or synthesized-data protocols). When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware training, KD routinely yields compact models that are practical for real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Important practical concerns remain—capacity mismatch, domain shift, rare-token/long-tail degradation, and transfer of teacher biases—and addressing them requires careful selection of distillation signals, teacher shaping, data strategies, and evaluation protocols.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation in NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as a central, practical technique for compressing and adapting large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD is versatile: it transfers predictive behavior, intermediate representations, and ensemble knowledge; supports data-free or privacy-sensitive settings; and can improve robustness and calibration when combined with complementary methods. Realizing KD’s full potential requires matching the distillation recipe to deployment goals and addressing failure modes such as optimization mismatches, bias transfer, and poor handling of low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Theory, and Applications
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models by transferring information from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student, using signals beyond hard labels to preserve generalization while reducing compute and memory. Modern work expands KD beyond soft logits to intermediate features, layer mappings, adversarial and attention-based objectives, and data- or resource-constrained settings. Empirical results across vision, speech and NLP show that tailored distillation strategies can recover much of a teacher's performance in compact models, though challenges remain in data-free scenarios, handling imperfect teachers, and preserving rare-token fidelity in sequence tasks.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Distilling Object Detectors with Fine-grained Feature Imitation
papers_seen.abstract: State-of-the-art CNN based recognition models are often computationally prohibitive to deploy on low-end devices. A promising high level approach tackling this limitation is knowledge distillation, which let small student model mimic cumbersome teacher model's output to get improved generalization. However, related methods mainly focus on simple task of classification while do not consider complex tasks like object detection. We show applying the vanilla knowledge distillation to detection model gets minor gain. To address the challenge of distilling knowledge in detection model, we propose a fine-grained feature imitation method exploiting the cross-location discrepancy of feature response. Our intuition is that detectors care more about local near object regions. Thus the discrepancy of feature response on the near object anchor locations reveals important information of how teacher model tends to generalize. We design a novel mechanism to estimate those locations and let student model imitate the teacher on them to get enhanced performance. We first validate the idea on a developed lightweight toy detector which carries simplest notion of current state-of-the-art anchor based detection models on challenging KITTI dataset, our method generates up to 15% boost of mAP for the student model compared to the non-imitated counterpart. We then extensively evaluate the method with Faster R-CNN model under various scenarios with common object detection benchmark of Pascal VOC and COCO, imitation alleviates up to 74% performance drop of student model compared to teacher. Codes released at https://github.com/twangnh/Distilling-Object-Detectors

papers_seen.author: Parks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Practical Principles and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practically oriented approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller students that meet deployment constraints. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone and is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and careful engineering of data, teacher–student alignment, and evaluation. The method reduces inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but deployment requires attention to capacity mismatch, data regimes, distributional shift, and risks of transferring biases or brittle behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Theory, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses and transfers knowledge from larger, often ensemble or teacher models into smaller student models to enable efficient deployment and improved generalization under resource constraints. Techniques range from matching final soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations, leveraging self-supervision, adversarial objectives, or curriculum and sample selection strategies. Distillation has been applied across classification, generation, retrieval, speech, and structured prediction, and it also offers avenues to transfer inductive biases, improve robustness, and preserve privacy. Empirical and theoretical work has clarified when distillation helps, what kind of "dark knowledge" is useful, and how regularization-like effects of soft targets can be harnessed even without a superior teacher.

papers_seen.author: Herman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Power, Patterns, and Precautions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile method for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance while reducing latency and memory. KD succeeds by transferring richer supervision than hard labels (soft targets, intermediate features, attention/relational signals), and it composes naturally with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: realizing its benefits in production requires task- and data-aware choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to design data augmentation or synthetic-data strategies, and how to mitigate robustness, fairness, and privacy risks.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while preserving performance. Research has developed multiple distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, and relational signals), architectural and optimization strategies (projectors, multi-teacher weighting, student-friendly teacher training), and workflows for constrained scenarios (data-free distillation, federated or black-box settings, and task-adaptive compression). Empirical and theoretical work highlights when distillation succeeds, the key role of representation alignment, and persistent challenges such as data heterogeneity, low-frequency token behavior in sequence models, and designing teacher signals that the student can effectively absorb.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple softened-logit matching into a diverse toolkit that includes representation- and attention-level alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation variants, data-aware and data-free workflows, and curriculum or online schedules. In practice KD is most powerful when composed with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign or search) and when its targets, data, and training schedules are adapted to deployment constraints such as latency, memory, privacy, and robustness. Important open issues remain around capacity mismatch, distributional shift, rare-token/long-tail behaviors, and propagation of teacher biases; addressing these requires methodic engineering, careful evaluation, and continued empirical and theoretical work.

papers_seen.author: Atkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. A broad family of KD techniques—matching softened teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations and attention, transferring relational structure, and using synthesized or public data—enables substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often retaining most of teacher performance. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, choosing data strategies (including data-free or synthesized data) when original data are unavailable, and combining KD with complementary compression tools such as pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Important open issues remain around capacity mismatch, distributional shift, rare-token/long-tail behaviors, and propagation of teacher biases; addressing these requires methodical engineering, careful evaluation, and continued empirical and theoretical work.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applied approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. Research over the last decade has expanded KD beyond simple logits matching into intermediate-representation transfer, multi-teacher and progressive curricula, data-aware and data-free workflows, and combinations with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design). KD functions both as a compression mechanism and as a training paradigm that can improve calibration and generalization, but it has known failure modes—teacher imperfection, capacity mismatch, optimization difficulty, domain shift, and degradation on rare or low-frequency phenomena—that require targeted diagnostics and hybrid pipelines. Practical deployment of KD therefore depends on matching distilled signals and protocols to student capacity, data availability, task constraints, and hardware targets.

papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or training dynamics. A broad toolkit—ranging from softened-logit matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, self- and online-distillation, multi-teacher pipelines, and data‑free procedures—is used in practice, typically together with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Practical success depends on aligning distilled signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data or synthetic-data strategies, and evaluating robustness, long‑tail fidelity, and privacy or fairness impacts. The field continues to address theoretical gaps and deployment challenges such as distribution shift, optimization mismatch, and limited or private data regimes.

papers_seen.author: Rivas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD spans simple soft-target matching to a rich set of representation- and layer-level objectives and is frequently combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, and architecture/parameter search). Practical success requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or sensitive data, and how to evaluate robustness and fairness. When treated as a context-sensitive component of a compression pipeline, KD routinely produces compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD achieves favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across modalities when practitioners choose what form of teacher knowledge to transfer, how to map layers and representations, and how to handle limited or private data. However, KD is not plug-and-play: outcomes depend heavily on teacher quality, distilled signals, data availability, and task-specific constraints. Thoughtful combination of feature-level objectives, task-aware layer selection, data-synthesis or privacy-preserving queries, and targeted curricula yields robust compressed models ready for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for NLP: A Context‑Sensitive Pipeline Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, empirically grounded approach for producing smaller, faster models from large teachers in deep learning and NLP. KD succeeds when it is treated not as a single recipe but as a flexible component of a compression pipeline that includes architecture-aware choices, complementary compression methods, data strategies (including domain adaptation and data-free techniques), and systematic evaluation for robustness and fairness. While KD often recovers much of a teacher's performance, realizing reliable, deployable students requires addressing teacher–student capacity mismatch, distribution shift, rare-token behavior, and potential bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Carson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. KD methods include matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, and transferring relational information. In practice KD is often combined with pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, and data strategies (original, augmented, or synthesized) to meet deployment constraints. Empirical evidence shows KD can substantially narrow the teacher–student performance gap, but success depends on careful choices about distillation targets, teacher preparation, student capacity, data handling, and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and rare-event behavior.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Phelps
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Design‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, high‑impact route to compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When KD is treated as the central element of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary techniques—feature alignment, data strategies, projector or adversarial mechanisms, and hardware‑aware design—it achieves strong size/accuracy/latency tradeoffs. Realizing those gains requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to prepare or synthesize data, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to diagnose limits such as bias transfer, distribution shift, and rare‑token fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Allison
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models to students. The field has diversified from logits-only matching to richer targets (intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), multiple training regimes (data-free, online, federated, multi-teacher), and task-aware techniques that address capacity mismatch and deployment constraints. KD is widely applicable across modalities (vision, speech, multimodal, graphs, NLP) and is most effective when combined with data- and architecture-aware practices, but practical limits remain around representation alignment, rare-token behavior, privacy, and domain transfer.

papers_seen.author: Andrews
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Modern KD includes soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention-level imitation, relational and layerwise objectives, online and multi-teacher schemes, and data-aware or data-free workflows. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful data and curriculum choices, KD routinely enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. Important practical challenges remain around capacity mismatch, distribution shift, rare-token or long-tail behaviors, and avoiding the transfer of teacher weaknesses.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate-representation matching, layerwise alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation, curriculum and augmentation strategies, and privacy- or data-free procedures. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and task-aware choices about what and how to transfer, KD enables practical deployment of high-performing models across modalities while raising open issues in robustness, fairness, and distributional generalization.

papers_seen.author: Solis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. KD methods include matching softened outputs, aligning internal representations, transferring attention or relational signals, staged or progressive replacement strategies, and self-distillation. In practice KD is combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful data, teacher–student, and optimization choices to meet deployment constraints. Although KD often recovers much of teacher performance, persistent limits remain around capacity mismatch, distributional shift, rare-token behavior, bias transfer, and data- or privacy-constrained scenarios, so engineering and diagnostics are required for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Dudley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Techniques, and Caveats
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applicable approach for compressing models and transferring knowledge across architectures and modalities. By training compact students under the guidance of larger teachers, KD enables substantial reductions in memory, compute, and inference latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Its flexibility supports many modalities (vision, language, speech, 3D, and generative models) and deployment constraints, but realizing its benefits in practice requires careful choices about what to transfer (logits vs. features), which samples to use, and how to handle limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted toolkit for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods span softened-logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, self- and online-distillation, multi-teacher and data-free variants, and are most effective when combined with complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and careful, deployment-aware engineering. Empirical evidence shows KD routinely improves compact models' accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, but success depends on what signals are transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, and how data, robustness, and privacy constraints are handled.

papers_seen.author: Molina
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD encompasses a range of targets and workflows—soft-output matching, intermediate-feature alignment, attention or relational losses, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-free variants—and is most effective when combined with complementary compression tools and deployment-aware design choices. However, its success depends on careful choices about distillation signals, data strategies, architectural alignment, and mitigation of optimization and robustness failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Galvan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Design-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. When implemented thoughtfully—choosing what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and which data and augmentation strategies to use—KD can recover much of a teacher’s performance while substantially reducing inference cost and memory. However, distillation also has limits: it can propagate teacher biases, struggle with low-data or low-capacity students, and requires complementary techniques (e.g., layer mapping, pruning, or synthetic-data schemes) and careful evaluation to meet real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Feature-map-level Online Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Feature maps contain rich information about image intensity and spatial correlation. However, previous online knowledge distillation methods only utilize the class probabilities. Thus in this paper, we propose an online knowledge distillation method that transfers not only the knowledge of the class probabilities but also that of the feature map using the adversarial training framework. We train multiple networks simultaneously by employing discriminators to distinguish the feature map distributions of different networks. Each network has its corresponding discriminator which discriminates the feature map from its own as fake while classifying that of the other network as real. By training a network to fool the corresponding discriminator, it can learn the other network's feature map distribution. We show that our method performs better than the conventional direct alignment method such as L1 and is more suitable for online distillation. Also, we propose a novel cyclic learning scheme for training more than two networks together. We have applied our method to various network architectures on the classification task and discovered a significant improvement of performance especially in the case of training a pair of a small network and a large one.

papers_seen.author: Costa
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. The literature frames KD as a flexible toolbox that includes softened-output (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention-guided imitation, layer-wise and task-aware transfer, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and data strategies ranging from use of original labels to synthetic or data-free curricula. KD often works best when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and when the distillation recipe is tuned for student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints. Practical challenges include handling imperfect teachers, preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors, alignment of teacher and student representations, and robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Ware
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible, and production-ready family of techniques that enables large deep and language models to be compressed into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. When combined with complementary methods—representation matching, multi-teacher or online schemes, synthetic or data-free generation, and hardware-aware compression—KD delivers strong efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on careful pipeline design to address capacity mismatch, dataset or domain heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and the risk of transferring or amplifying teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible, and empirically effective approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When matched to deployment goals—through careful choice of distilled signals, data strategies, and complementary compression methods—KD delivers strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across modalities. However, its success depends on teacher quality, data availability, teacher–student alignment, and attention to robustness, privacy, and distributional shift.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: SEED: Self-supervised Distillation For Visual Representation
papers_seen.abstract: This paper is concerned with self-supervised learning for small models. The problem is motivated by our empirical studies that while the widely used contrastive self-supervised learning method has shown great progress on large model training, it does not work well for small models. To address this problem, we propose a new learning paradigm, named SElf-SupErvised Distillation (SEED), where we leverage a larger network (as Teacher) to transfer its representational knowledge into a smaller architecture (as Student) in a self-supervised fashion. Instead of directly learning from unlabeled data, we train a student encoder to mimic the similarity score distribution inferred by a teacher over a set of instances. We show that SEED dramatically boosts the performance of small networks on downstream tasks. Compared with self-supervised baselines, SEED improves the top-1 accuracy from 42.2% to 67.6% on EfficientNet-B0 and from 36.3% to 68.2% on MobileNet-v3-Large on the ImageNet-1k dataset.

papers_seen.author: Lane
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. Methods operate at multiple granularities — softened outputs (logits), intermediate feature alignment, attention/relational transfers, and module- or layer-wise mappings — and are commonly combined with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation). Practical pipelines emphasize teacher–student co‑design, capacity-aware selection of distilled signals, and careful evaluation for robustness, rare-token behavior, privacy, and distributional shift. While distillation routinely recovers much of a teacher’s performance in smaller footprints, open challenges remain in theory, handling imperfect or heterogeneous teachers, and preserving long‑tail and safety properties under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Crawford
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. KD has evolved from matching softened logits to a broad family of methods that include feature- and layer-level mimicry, relational and attention-based transfers, multi-stage and multi-teacher pipelines, and data‑aware strategies (including synthetic or data‑free approaches). When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful engineering around teacher–student alignment and data selection, KD enables substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while often retaining a large fraction of teacher performance. However, practical success requires attention to capacity mismatch, distributional and optimization issues, privacy and robustness concerns, and task-specific design choices.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Essential, Combinable, and Context‑Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, enabling lower latency, smaller footprints, and flexible deployment when paired with complementary compression methods. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on data regime, teacher quality, teacher–student capacity alignment, and the choice of distilled signals. A principled pipeline treats KD as a toolbox—combining logits and feature targets, multi‑teacher schedules, data synthesis or privacy‑aware protocols, and hardware‑aware compression—to produce robust, task‑appropriate compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Woods
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used family of techniques for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information beyond hard labels—such as softened outputs, intermediate features, attention patterns, or relational signals—and is typically combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free approaches). Empirical work shows KD often recovers much of a teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost, but its success depends on careful alignment of teacher signals, student capacity, and available data; known failure modes include capacity mismatch, teacher imperfections, distributional shift, and degradation on rare or low-frequency phenomena. Practical deployment therefore calls for diagnostic evaluations, hybrid pipelines, and attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical, Careful, and Multifaceted Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, widely applicable approach to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. When applied thoughtfully, KD enables deployment under resource, latency, and privacy constraints; supports domain adaptation and vocabulary specialization; and can be combined with other compression techniques. However, its success depends on careful choices about what to transfer (logits vs. features), how to align layers and representations, how to generate or augment data for distillation, and how to mitigate propagated errors or biases from teachers.

papers_seen.author: Ibarra
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable Path for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce latency, memory, and power requirements while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD works across modalities and tasks, but its practical success depends on choices about what signal to transfer, how to supply or synthesize training data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods. When applied thoughtfully within a wider compression pipeline, KD enables deployable models for resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, engineering-friendly family of techniques that enables large neural models to be converted into smaller, faster, and more deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. When paired with complementary compression tools and careful data or curriculum design, KD supports real-world constraints such as latency, memory, privacy, and heterogeneous deployment. However, its practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, addressing data scarcity and teacher bias, and evaluating robustness under distribution shifts.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Imperative for Deploying Large NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have driven major NLP advances but are often impractical for real-world deployment because of size, latency, privacy, and data-distribution constraints. Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression strategies enable retaining most of a large model's performance while producing models that meet latency, memory, and regulatory requirements. Effective KD encompasses diverse techniques — task-adaptive compression, feature mimicking, data-free distillation, teacher meta-learning, privacy-aware distillation, and distributed/continual distillation — which together form a practical toolkit for making state-of-the-art NLP useful at scale.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce the size, memory, and inference cost of large neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. Across tasks and modalities—classification, detection, generative modeling, retrieval, and NLP—research has developed logits-based, feature-based, and task-adapted distillation strategies, multi-teacher and ensemble approaches, privacy- and communication-conscious protocols for distributed settings, and teacher-optimization/meta-learning variants. These methods trade off fidelity to teacher behavior with student capacity, expose failure modes (e.g., transfer of low-frequency lexical mistakes or overfitting of student features), and introduce remedies such as selective sample distillation, feature projectors, adversarially-informed samples, and staged or multi-teacher curricula. While KD consistently improves compact models compared to training from scratch and enables deployment on resource-constrained platforms, open issues remain in robustness, task-specific alignment, and distillation under data heterogeneity.

papers_seen.author: Barton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical but Design-Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary compression techniques and careful data and architecture choices, KD often yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: its effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred, how student and teacher are aligned, data quality and selection, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Versatile Tool for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable strategy for producing compact models that retain much of the accuracy, inductive bias, and robustness of larger teachers. Beyond simple logit-matching, KD encompasses feature- and layer-level alignment, self-distillation, many-to-many layer mapping, and data-aware or data-free workflows that together enable deployment under latency, memory, privacy, and domain-shift constraints. When combined with careful objectives, curriculum strategies, and task-aware layer mapping, KD can serve both as a primary compression mechanism and as a general-purpose training paradigm for regularization and adaptation. However, realizing its full value requires attention to teacher quality, data heterogeneity, and the choice of distilled signals to preserve robustness and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Harrison
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. The field encompasses a range of techniques—from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational signals—and integrates with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, the availability and curation of data (real or synthesized), and deployment constraints such as latency, memory, robustness, and privacy. Persistent challenges include capacity and optimization mismatch, preserving low-frequency or rare-token behavior, mitigating transfer of teacher biases, and ensuring generalization under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Opportunities and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical component of model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP: it reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from large teachers to smaller students and composes well with pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign. However, KD is not a turnkey solution—its real-world success requires careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or private data, and how to detect and mitigate failures such as capacity mismatch, distribution shift, or biased transfer.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the central, practical component of model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. When used as a flexible toolbox—choosing appropriate distillation targets, aligning teacher and student representations, designing student-aware architectures, and combining distillation with complementary compression primitives—KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Real-world application requires careful engineering to address capacity mismatch, distributional shift, long-tail behaviors, and potential transfer of teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Compressing NLP Models: Benefits, Limits, and Practical Recipes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones. In NLP, KD enables retaining much of the teacher model's linguistic capability while reducing storage and inference cost. Effective compression with KD requires more than mimicking final outputs: it benefits from aligning internal representations, task-aware layer mapping, and handling data or privacy constraints with synthetic or metadata-driven techniques. However, KD is not a panacea — distributional heterogeneity, privacy, and mismatches between teacher and student capacity pose real limits that must be mitigated by careful method design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be Central to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, empirically validated set of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller, deployable student models. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. Its strengths include multiple forms of transferable signals (soft logits, intermediate features, relational information), compatibility with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and applicability in data- and privacy-constrained settings. Realizing these benefits in practice requires careful choices about the signals to transfer, student capacity and architecture, data management (real, augmented, or synthesized), and measures to detect and remedy robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift issues.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied strategy to transfer information from large or specialized teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. In practice KD has been used to compress pretrained language models, speed up inference in structured models, enable multimodal generation, improve low-precision networks, and scale training across data-parallel workers. Research spans theoretical analyses of why distillation works, empirical studies of failure modes (e.g., propagation of teacher errors), and practical training recipes (including online and self-distillation variants) that balance fidelity to the teacher with student capacity and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. The literature develops a broad toolkit—softened-logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, layer-wise and relational objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free variants—and commonly composes distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. Empirical results across vision, speech, and language show distillation typically recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but practical success depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture, data availability and domain match, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic approach for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models so that compact systems meet deployment constraints (compute, memory, latency, privacy) while retaining much of teacher performance. KD encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning internal representations or attention, and using multi-stage or data-aware pipelines. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware pretraining) and careful data strategies, KD routinely yields favorable size/accuracy/latency trade-offs. However, realizing those gains in practice requires attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, robustness, and the risk of transferring teacher shortcomings; thus KD is best treated as the central tool inside a broader, task-aware compression pipeline rather than a standalone cure-all.
