papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses or transfers knowledge from larger or multiple teacher models into smaller or otherwise constrained student models to reduce inference cost while retaining performance. Across computer vision, speech, recommendation, and NLP, KD techniques include matching soft outputs, transferring intermediate features, multi-teacher and staged protocols, and data-free synthesis of surrogate training examples. Practical systems combine KD with pruning or architecture changes, and recent theory helps explain when and why distillation helps. Despite strong empirical gains, challenges remain in handling heterogeneous teachers, data unavailability, task-specific adaptations (e.g., detection, translation), and robustness on low-frequency or out-of-distribution phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Composable Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an adaptable, production-oriented approach that transfers information from large teacher models into smaller students to reduce latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. When treated as a composable component within wider compression pipelines, KD enables effective trade-offs among accuracy, size, and deployment constraints; however, its practical success depends on careful design choices about what signals to transfer, how to supply or synthesize data, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to diagnose and mitigate failure modes such as distribution shift, bias transfer, and rare-token loss.

papers_seen.author: Juarez
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical family of techniques that transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models so students can meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, energy, or privacy) while retaining much of teacher performance. The literature describes a spectrum of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational maps, and module-level behaviors), teacher–student variants (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation), and data regimes (full-data, few-shot, and data-free adversarial synthesis). KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, progressive module replacement) and when practitioners attend to teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and robustness or fairness requirements. Open challenges include distillation under severe data heterogeneity, preserving rare-token or fine-grained behavior, and principled guarantees about robustness and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques aim to transfer the predictive power of large, expensive models into smaller, faster models while retaining performance. Approaches vary from matching teacher outputs (soft labels) to aligning intermediate representations, leveraging data augmentation or synthesized data when real data are limited, and jointly optimizing architecture and distillation losses for task-adaptive compression. Advances address student–teacher capacity gaps, multi-teacher transfer, and domain or data scarcity; remaining challenges include transferring internal structure efficiently, generalization under distribution shifts, and designing teacher models that are optimized for downstream distillation.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger, expensive teacher models to smaller, efficient student models. Across vision, language, and other modalities, KD operates at multiple granularities (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or channel maps, and module-level replacements) and can serve both as a compression mechanism and as a broader training paradigm that improves calibration, generalization, and domain adaptation. Practical variants address constraints such as limited or private data, mismatched architectures, and deployment latency; persistent challenges include optimization failure modes, preserving rare-token or low-frequency behavior, and aligning internal representations between heterogeneous teacher–student pairs.

papers_seen.author: Wagner
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation in Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Since deep learning became a key player in natural language processing (NLP), many deep learning models have been showing remarkable performances in a variety of NLP tasks, and in some cases, they are even outperforming humans. Such high performance can be explained by efficient knowledge representation of deep learning models. While many methods have been proposed to learn more efficient representation, knowledge distillation from pretrained deep networks suggest that we can use more information from the soft target probability to train other neural networks. In this paper, we propose a new knowledge distillation method self-knowledge distillation, based on the soft target probabilities of the training model itself, where multimode information is distilled from the word embedding space right below the softmax layer. Due to the time complexity, our method approximates the soft target probabilities. In experiments, we applied the proposed method to two different and fundamental NLP tasks: language model and neural machine translation. The experiment results show that our proposed method improves performance on the tasks.

papers_seen.author: Durham
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Practical KD spans matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention, multi‑teacher schedules, and data-aware or data‑free workflows, and it is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and deployment‑aware design. This synthesis summarizes methods, empirical strengths, typical failure modes, and best practices for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical engine of model compression for deep learning and NLP: it provides flexible, high-utility transfer mechanisms that—when combined with complementary compression primitives and data strategies—enable compact, deployable models that approach teacher performance. Its success is not automatic; careful signal choice, teacher–student alignment, data handling, and explicit checks for robustness and fairness are required for reliable production results.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of methods for transferring supervisory signals from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models can be deployed under compute, latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD encompasses soft-target matching, intermediate-representation and attention alignment, relational or feature-level transfers, multi-teacher and self-distillation regimes, and data-aware workflows including data-free synthesis. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and careful choice of data and training curricula, KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Realizing reliable gains in practice requires careful design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity and architecture, how to handle limited or no original data, and how to detect and mitigate failure modes such as capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Mathis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or training dynamics. The approach spans simple soft-target matching to richer forms such as feature- and attention-level mimicry, multi-stage pipelines, online or federated protocols, and application-specific adaptations for generation, ranking, and multimodal tasks. Practical use combines KD with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data augmentation) to meet deployment constraints, and open problems remain in theory, low-resource or privacy-constrained settings, and preserving rare-token or long-tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. The practice has evolved from logits matching into a flexible toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-augmentation and data-free strategies, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. When matched to task requirements, student capacity, and data constraints, distillation reliably improves size–performance trade-offs for vision and language models, though practical success requires careful design to manage capacity mismatch, distribution shift, privacy, and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Lexical Choice in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is essential for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models by reducing the complexity of the raw data with an autoregressive teacher model. In this study, we empirically show that as a side effect of this training, the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words are propagated to the NAT model from the teacher model. To alleviate this problem, we propose to expose the raw data to NAT models to restore the useful information of low-frequency words, which are missed in the distilled data. To this end, we introduce an extra Kullback-Leibler divergence term derived by comparing the lexical choice of NAT model and that embedded in the raw data. Experimental results across language pairs and model architectures demonstrate the effectiveness and universality of the proposed approach. Extensive analyses confirm our claim that our approach improves performance by reducing the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach pushes the SOTA NAT performance on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets up to 27.8 and 33.8 BLEU points, respectively. The source code will be released.

papers_seen.author: Frank
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone — including softened outputs, intermediate representations, and relational or layer-wise information — and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and task- or deployment-aware design choices. The method yields favorable size–performance trade-offs across modalities, but its success depends on careful teacher–student co-design, appropriate choice of distilled signals, data strategies for training (including data-free or synthesized-data regimes), and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and rare-token or distribution-shift behavior.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Benefits, Design Patterns, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a pragmatic, task-aware route to compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a central component of compression pipelines and combined with complementary techniques and careful data strategies, KD routinely yields favorable size–performance trade-offs. However, its reliability depends on deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or sensitive data; practitioners must also address robustness, fairness, and long-tail behaviors when deploying distilled models.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have become central to deploying high-performance deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research has produced diverse approaches that transfer information from larger "teacher" models to smaller "student" models via softened outputs, intermediate feature supervision, layer-wise alignment, module replacement, data augmentation, and data-free synthesis. These methods have been applied across modalities (vision, speech, language, multi-modal), combined with quantization and architecture search, and adapted for settings with limited or private data. Empirical and theoretical work highlights why distillation can improve generalization, how inductive biases or teacher strength influence transfer, and practical strategies to make students more robust and efficient. Challenges remain in aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving task-relevant representations, and designing principled distillation objectives for varied downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Francis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Recommendations and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic route to make large deep and language models deployable by transferring richer supervisory signals from teachers to smaller students. When engineered to the task and deployment constraints and combined with complementary compression techniques, KD often yields large size–performance wins. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: success requires matching distilled signals to student capacity, careful data and privacy strategies, representation alignment, and explicit evaluation for long-tail behavior, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Opportunities and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical component of model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP: it reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from large teachers to smaller students and composes well with pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign. However, KD is not a turnkey solution—its real-world success requires careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or private data, and how to detect and mitigate failures such as capacity mismatch, distribution shift, or biased transfer.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Flexible Path to Compact and Robust NLP and Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile set of techniques for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster ones while retaining most of their performance. Distillation methods can be adapted to structural compression, domain adaptation, low-data or no-data scenarios, and different model families (transformers, convolutional nets, graph models). A pragmatic compression strategy combines well-chosen distillation objectives with complementary methods (pruning, architecture transformations, multi-teacher supervision, or data-generation) to meet deployment constraints without sacrificing reliability.

papers_seen.author: Long
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Design-Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical route to compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a flexible, design-sensitive toolkit — selecting what to transfer, aligning architectures, choosing or synthesizing data, and combining KD with complementary compression methods — it can preserve most teacher utility while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, success depends on careful engineering to avoid propagated biases, degraded robustness, and failures under data or capacity mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce model size or communication cost by transferring knowledge from larger or multiple models (teachers) to smaller or otherwise constrained models (students). Methods vary from matching soft outputs to transferring intermediate features, training teachers to be student-friendly, coordinating multiple teachers, and combining distillation with pruning or federated/online schemes. Empirical and theoretical work highlights how distilled "dark knowledge" improves student generalization, how architectural components (e.g., projectors) shape transfer, and how distillation can be adapted for privacy, heterogeneity, and large-scale or multi-task NLP applications.

papers_seen.author: Parks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Practical Principles and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practically oriented approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller students that meet deployment constraints. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone and is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and careful engineering of data, teacher–student alignment, and evaluation. The method reduces inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance, but deployment requires attention to capacity mismatch, data regimes, distributional shift, and risks of transferring biases or brittle behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so that students retain much of teacher performance while reducing computational cost. The literature characterizes KD methods at multiple granularities (final logits, intermediate features, attention or layer mappings, and module- or task-level transfer), documents practical recipes and failure modes, and explores extensions for data-free settings, robustness, and specialized tasks (e.g., machine translation, detection). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD is a flexible tool that benefits from careful choices in distilled signals, data/augmentation strategies, and teacher-student alignment; however, limitations remain around optimization, low-frequency phenomena, data availability, and architecture mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach for compressing large deep learning models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. Modern KD goes beyond matching logits: it includes feature- and representation-level transfers, multi-teacher and self-distillation strategies, and workflows that integrate augmentation, data-free synthesis, pruning, and quantization to meet latency, memory, and privacy requirements. Practical success depends on matching distillation technique to deployment objectives, careful design of layer mappings and loss terms, attention to teacher quality and data availability, and combinations with other compression tools to preserve robustness and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Towards Understanding Ensemble, Knowledge Distillation and Self-Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We formally study how ensemble of deep learning models can improve test accuracy, and how the superior performance of ensemble can be distilled into a single model using knowledge distillation. We consider the challenging case where the ensemble is simply an average of the outputs of a few independently trained neural networks with the SAME architecture, trained using the SAME algorithm on the SAME data set, and they only differ by the random seeds used in the initialization.   We show that ensemble/knowledge distillation in Deep Learning works very differently from traditional learning theory (such as boosting or NTKs, neural tangent kernels). To properly understand them, we develop a theory showing that when data has a structure we refer to as ``multi-view'', then ensemble of independently trained neural networks can provably improve test accuracy, and such superior test accuracy can also be provably distilled into a single model by training a single model to match the output of the ensemble instead of the true label. Our result sheds light on how ensemble works in deep learning in a way that is completely different from traditional theorems, and how the ``dark knowledge'' is hidden in the outputs of the ensemble and can be used in distillation. In the end, we prove that self-distillation can also be viewed as implicitly combining ensemble and knowledge distillation to improve test accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Harper
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Composable Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated as a context-sensitive, composable component of a broader model-compression pipeline. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, and relational structure) and by combining distillation with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies), practitioners can produce compact student models that approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Success requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity and architecture, how to supply or synthesize data, and explicit checks for robustness, fairness, and rare-token fidelity.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: This synthesis summarizes contemporary methods, practical patterns, and deployment considerations for knowledge distillation (KD) as a route to compressing deep learning and NLP models. It covers common distillation signals, data strategies (including data-free and synthetic approaches), online and self-distillation variants, teacher–student co-design, and how KD combines with complementary compression methods. The summary highlights recurring practical trade-offs—student capacity, choice of transfer targets, data availability, and robustness/fairness risks—and concludes with pragmatic guidelines for applying KD in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Path to Compact Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, practical approach for turning large, high-performing deep models into smaller, faster models suitable for real-world deployment. Beyond pure compression, KD serves as a flexible training paradigm that can be combined with pre-training, privacy-preserving workflows, and architecture-aware mimicry to preserve task performance while meeting latency, memory, and device constraints. A pragmatic KD pipeline aligns the choice of distillation signal, teacher design, student pretraining, and data strategy to the deployment context.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses larger ‘‘teacher’’ models into smaller ‘‘student’’ models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations so students retain much of the teacher’s performance while reducing storage and inference cost. Distillation spans simple soft-target (logit) matching to richer forms that align intermediate features, attention maps, or decision-boundary information; practical deployments combine distillation with architecture-aware choices, selective data strategies, and complementary compression methods. The method is effective across vision and language tasks but has limits stemming from imperfect teachers, capacity mismatch, and data or distributional heterogeneity; careful method design and evaluation are required to realize robust, deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade, practitioners have developed a spectrum of distillation signals and pipelines—ranging from soft-logit matching to representation and attention alignment, data-free synthesis, and integrated workflows that combine pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design—to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical practice shows distillation routinely improves compact models relative to training from scratch, but its success is engineering-dependent and sensitive to student capacity, data availability, and alignment between teacher and student.

papers_seen.author: Moran
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of methods for transferring predictive capacity from larger teacher models into smaller, more efficient students so models can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Research over the past decade has expanded simple logit-matching into a rich set of variants—feature and layer alignment, progressive module replacement, self-distillation, data-free synthesis, and privacy-aware ensembles—making KD a cornerstone of modern model-compression toolkits.

papers_seen.author: Callahan
papers_seen.title: A Practical Position on Knowledge Distillation: Go Beyond Soft Labels
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a necessary tool for compressing large deep and NLP models into efficient students suitable for deployment. However, naive KD that only matches teacher soft-labels is often insufficient. Effective distillation combines richer knowledge targets (internal features, attention, and layerwise signals), data-aware augmentations, selective sample strategies, and privacy- or domain-aware procedures. The best practical pipelines treat KD as a toolbox: choose which knowledge to transfer based on student capacity and task needs, use augmentation or self-distillation to improve generalization when data are scarce, and apply selective or privacy-preserving queries where constraints require it.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD encompasses techniques that transfer predictive behavior (soft logits), intermediate representations, and relational or structural signals; it can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency and memory constraints. Practical deployments extend KD to privacy-preserving, federated, and data-poor scenarios, and leverage online or multi-teacher protocols. Empirical and theoretical work highlights clear strengths in producing compact models for NLP and vision, while also identifying limits related to optimization, teacher imperfection, data mismatch, and distributional shifts that must be addressed by careful engineering and complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Allison
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a core strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from teacher models to students. The field has diversified from logits-only matching to richer targets (intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), multiple training regimes (data-free, online, federated, multi-teacher), and task-aware techniques that address capacity mismatch and deployment constraints. KD is widely applicable across modalities (vision, speech, multimodal, graphs, NLP) and is most effective when combined with data- and architecture-aware practices, but practical limits remain around representation alignment, rare-token behavior, privacy, and domain transfer.

papers_seen.author: Cowan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical method for transferring predictive behavior from large, expensive teacher models into smaller, faster student models so they meet real-world latency, memory, and deployment constraints. When combined with complementary techniques (pre-training compact students, layer-aware transfer, data synthesis or selective raw-data exposure), KD can preserve most of a teacher's performance while substantially reducing computational cost. However, distillation must be designed carefully: choices about what to transfer, how to supply or synthesize training data, and how to align teacher and student shape outcomes in accuracy, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-ready approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. KD supports multiple transfer signals (logits, features, attention or relational structure), composes with other compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and can be adapted to domain- or data-constrained settings. Its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; therefore KD should be treated as a toolbox of methods and workflows rather than a single recipe.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from larger, often pre-trained teacher models into smaller, efficient student models in order to reduce latency, memory, and deployment cost while retaining task performance. Methods span matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, attention- or relation-based feature matching, curriculum strategies for progressively harder supervision, and task- or data-aware architecture search. Practical success depends on student capacity, availability and quality of data, whether the student itself is pre-trained, and choices about what to transfer; open challenges include preserving fairness and robustness, aligning heterogeneous architectures, and operating under privacy or data-limited conditions.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core Tool with Clear Limits and Complementary Needs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used approach to compressing large deep and language models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. KD reliably reduces inference cost and model size while often preserving much of teacher performance, but success depends on what is transferred, how the student is initialized and trained, and how data and robustness constraints are handled. Effective compression therefore treats KD as one component in a pipeline that includes pre-training of compact architectures, architecture-aware alignment or progressive replacement, and data strategies (including data-free or synthesized data) to meet privacy and domain needs.

papers_seen.author: Weiss
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, pragmatic approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When integrated with careful teacher–student co-design, representation-level objectives, and complementary compression techniques, KD routinely yields substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while preserving much of the original performance. At the same time, KD is context-sensitive: its success depends on data availability, capacity matching, and mitigation of robustness and fairness risks, so practitioners should treat KD as a flexible core of a broader compression pipeline rather than a turnkey solution.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Webster
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used paradigm for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Over the past decade KD has expanded from matching soft teacher logits to a versatile toolkit that includes intermediate-representation alignment, multi-teacher and online schemes, data- or privacy-aware protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign. Empirical and engineering work shows KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and heterogeneity constraints, but practitioners must manage limits such as capacity mismatch, degraded modeling of rare phenomena, privacy and data availability, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Bates
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression, with Guardrails for Robustness and Fairness
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, high-impact approach for producing compact student models that retain much of a larger teacher’s behavior. When integrated into compression pipelines alongside pre-training, architecture-aware design, and complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, synthetic data), KD routinely yields favorable size–performance trade-offs for NLP and other modalities. However, KD is not automatic: addressing capacity mismatch, data availability, distribution shift, and the transfer of undesirable behaviors (e.g., bias or degraded long‑tail fidelity) requires deliberate teacher–student co‑design, data strategies, and evaluation beyond aggregate accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Short
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Design‑Sensitive Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for turning large, high‑performing models into smaller, deployable students. When matched to deployment objectives and combined with complementary compression methods, KD can recover most of a teacher’s utility while delivering substantial gains in latency, memory, and energy. However, distillation is context‑sensitive: the distilled signals, student capacity, data regime, and privacy or fairness constraints all shape outcomes. Treating KD as an essential but configurable toolbox—rather than a single plug‑and‑play algorithm—yields the most reliable production results.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while preserving performance. Methods extend beyond matching soft output logits to include intermediate feature/representation matching, layer-wise alignment, adversarial or curriculum-driven sample selection, and data-free or privacy-aware synthesis. Distillation is widely applicable across modalities (vision, speech, language, multimodal) and use cases (on-device deployment, federated learning, low-precision inference), but success depends on careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to handle data availability or heterogeneity, and how to align teacher and student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Mckinney
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely adopted approach for turning large, high‑performing models into compact students that can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD is flexible in what it transfers (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational signals) and in how it is applied (offline teacher–student training, online/self-distillation, multi‑teacher ensembles, and data‑free procedures). Practical success depends on matching the distillation signals to student capacity, combining KD with complementary compression techniques, and engineering data and optimization workflows that mitigate distribution shift, bias transfer, and long‑tail degradation.

papers_seen.author: Spears
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that high performance can be retained under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Across modalities KD spans simple soft-target matching to richer transfers of internal features, attention, or relational structure, and it is usually combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful data strategies (real, public, synthetic, or data-free). Empirical results show large reductions in model size and inference cost with modest accuracy loss in many settings, but success depends on choices of what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to preserve robustness and fairness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Pearson
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible set of techniques for reducing the computational and memory cost of large neural models while preserving much of their predictive behavior. The family of methods includes transferring softened teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention patterns, distilling relational structure, applying self-distillation, and using data-aware or data-free sampling and synthesis. In practice KD is most effective when treated as a component of a broader compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, and careful data and training curricula—and when designers attend explicitly to student capacity, teacher–student alignment, data regimes, and deployment constraints such as latency, privacy, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Sheppard
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an adaptable and widely adopted approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. The KD toolkit ranges from matching softened teacher logits to aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, and it is most effective when integrated into broader compression pipelines with pruning, quantization, and student-aware architecture design. Practical success depends on careful engineering choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, which data to use or synthesize, and how to diagnose and mitigate limits such as capacity mismatch, transferred biases, degraded rare-token behavior, and distribution shift. When applied thoughtfully, KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while preserving much of teacher utility across vision, language, and domain-specific settings.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Day
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When integrated into a wider compression pipeline and matched to task and deployment constraints, KD can preserve much of a teacher’s predictive capability while reducing latency, memory, and energy costs. However, KD is context-sensitive: its success depends on what signals are transferred, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability (or synthetic-data workarounds), and explicit mitigation for transferred biases or distribution shift. A pragmatic stance treats KD as the central, composable tool for compression, applied with task-aware design, complementary methods, and principled evaluation to address its known limits.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer predictive capacity from large, expensive models into smaller, faster models while preserving performance. Approaches vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, feature projectors), how teachers are constructed (single teacher, multi-teacher, self-teaching, or meta-learned teachers), and what resources are available (original data, public data, or no data). Practical extensions address domain-specific needs (e.g., BERT compression, low-precision deployment, privacy-preserving and federated settings) and include strategies such as progressive module replacement, multi-stage distillation, adversarially generated synthetic data, and self-supervised distillation. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both the power of soft targets as a regularizer and the importance of aligning internal representations and layer correspondences to improve student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Promise, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully and combined with complementary techniques—layer- and task-aware transfer, multi-teacher schemes, data synthesis or privacy-aware protocols, and hardware-aware downstream optimization—KD enables substantial reductions in size and latency while retaining much of a teacher's utility. However, its practical success is engineering-dependent: careful choices about distilled signals, student preparation, data availability, and mitigation of transferred errors or biases are required to realize reliable, fair, and robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high‑capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has grown from matching softened teacher logits to a diverse toolkit including intermediate‑representation and attention alignment, multi‑teacher and self‑distillation variants, data‑aware and data‑free workflows, and task‑aware layer mapping. In practice KD is most effective when composed with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign/search) and when designers adapt distillation signals, data strategies, and curricula to student capacity and deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include teacher–student capacity mismatch, distributional shift and long‑tail/rare‑token behavior, robustness and fairness risks, and deploying under privacy or data‑scarce regimes.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression aim to transfer knowledge from large or ensemble teacher models to smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models while preserving predictive performance. Approaches span soft-label imitation, intermediate feature matching, architecture-aware compression, data-centric augmentations, online and distributed schemes, and teacher-design strategies. Applications include NLP (BERT compression and task-specific distillation), speech recognition, graph neural networks, and vision tasks. Empirical results across benchmarks show that carefully chosen distillation objectives, alignment mechanisms, and data strategies can yield compact models that approach teacher performance while enabling substantial speed and memory gains. Open challenges remain in automating architecture search for compression, preserving robustness and domain generalization, and scaling distillation to very large datasets and model families.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities, KD transfers predictive behavior and internal representations using a variety of targets and protocols (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, multi-stage or online schemes) and composes well with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data or privacy constraints. KD enables many deployment goals (reduced latency/memory, domain adaptation, privacy-aware training), but its effectiveness is limited by optimization dynamics, teacher–student mismatch, distribution shift for synthetic data, and the potential transfer of undesirable biases.

papers_seen.author: Dunn
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers predictive and representational information from large teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. The literature treats KD as a flexible toolkit—matching soft logits, aligning intermediate features or attention, using multi-teacher or online protocols, and synthesizing data when originals are unavailable—and recommends integrating KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data-aware strategies. Practical success depends on careful design choices about what to transfer, student–teacher alignment, data availability or synthesis, and evaluation of robustness, rare-case fidelity, and fairness.
