papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Pillar for Compressing Deep Models in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural networks while retaining much of their performance. Across NLP and other domains, KD enables deployment on resource-limited devices, supports privacy-preserving and federated scenarios, and combines effectively with pre-training, data augmentation, and structured compression. I argue that KD should be a default component of any production-aware model compression pipeline, augmented by task- and data-aware techniques to preserve robustness and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Dodson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile empirical framework for compressing high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, and structured prediction, KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone (e.g., softened outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, or relational structure) and is commonly integrated with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies to meet latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Practical pipelines emphasize task- and student-aware design, careful teacher selection or training, and data-management choices; when applied thoughtfully KD can recover much of a teacher's performance but still faces challenges in robustness, domain shift, fairness, and theoretical understanding.

papers_seen.author: Serrano
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has grown from soft-label matching into a diverse toolkit—feature and layer imitation, attention and relation matching, self-distillation, multi-teacher curricula, data-free or privacy-aware protocols, and task- or architecture-aware pipelines—that, when combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search, enables deployable models that trade little performance for large efficiency gains. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, managing data and privacy constraints, and explicitly mitigating transferred biases or robustness losses.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Concise Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a set of techniques for transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, more efficient student models so that students retain much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, memory footprint, and sometimes communication or privacy exposure. KD encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, and transferring relational or attention signals; it is commonly combined with complementary compression methods and with data or model-centric strategies to meet deployment constraints. Practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, student capacity, data availability (or synthesis), and robustness and fairness evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Uses, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and multimodal tasks, a family of techniques—soft-label matching, feature and attention imitation, layer mapping, multi-teacher and curriculum schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols—enables students to recover much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Practical success depends on task- and deployment-aware choices (distilled signal, student capacity, data availability, and augmentation), and remaining challenges include robustness to distribution shift, preservation of rare-token or fine-grained behaviors, and distillation under privacy or data-scarce conditions.

papers_seen.author: Warren
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Mechanisms, Extensions, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, deployment-focused strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students. Its practical value arises from multiple mechanisms — not only teacher imitation but also regularization, representation transfer, and optimization effects — and from combinations with data strategies and complementary compression methods. I argue KD should be treated as the central, engineering-ready backbone of compression pipelines, while practitioners explicitly address data regimes, privacy, domain shift, and bias transfer when designing distillation workflows.

papers_seen.author: Mata
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical, Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and flexible approach to compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely delivers strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when practitioners choose appropriate distillation signals, address teacher–student mismatches, and combine KD with complementary steps like pruning, quantization, or architecture adaptation. At the same time, KD’s benefits depend on data availability, teacher quality, optimization dynamics, and explicit mitigation of robustness, privacy, and long‑tail failure modes. A production‑grade pipeline therefore treats KD as the central tool but integrates data‑aware strategies and targeted remedies for known limits.

papers_seen.author: Galloway
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Context-Sensitive Path to Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly effective toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students for deployment in resource-constrained settings. KD methods span matching output distributions, aligning internal representations, synthesizing surrogate data when originals are unavailable, and co-designing compact architectures for target tasks. While KD often preserves much of a teacher’s performance and enables trade-offs among accuracy, latency, and memory, success depends on the distillation signal, data regime, robustness and privacy needs, and architecture alignment between teacher and student.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce latency, memory, and computation while retaining much of the teacher's performance. Across vision, language, and graph domains, KD has been applied as logit matching, intermediate-feature alignment, adversarial transfer, and data- or task-aware synthesis. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD often acts both as a source of extra task signal and as a regularizer; practical systems combine KD with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies to meet deployment constraints. Important open issues include data heterogeneity, teacher–student capacity mismatch, privacy-preserving releases, and closing remaining gaps in robustness and domain generalization.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transfer information from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller student models to reduce model size, latency, and deployment cost while retaining much of the teacher's utility. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, ensembles), how training data is used or synthesized, and whether distillation is combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Across vision and NLP tasks, distillation enables practical deployment of compact models but requires careful handling of representation mismatch, data availability, optimization schedules, and potential amplification of teacher errors or biases.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Towards Understanding Ensemble, Knowledge Distillation and Self-Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We formally study how ensemble of deep learning models can improve test accuracy, and how the superior performance of ensemble can be distilled into a single model using knowledge distillation. We consider the challenging case where the ensemble is simply an average of the outputs of a few independently trained neural networks with the SAME architecture, trained using the SAME algorithm on the SAME data set, and they only differ by the random seeds used in the initialization.   We show that ensemble/knowledge distillation in Deep Learning works very differently from traditional learning theory (such as boosting or NTKs, neural tangent kernels). To properly understand them, we develop a theory showing that when data has a structure we refer to as ``multi-view'', then ensemble of independently trained neural networks can provably improve test accuracy, and such superior test accuracy can also be provably distilled into a single model by training a single model to match the output of the ensemble instead of the true label. Our result sheds light on how ensemble works in deep learning in a way that is completely different from traditional theorems, and how the ``dark knowledge'' is hidden in the outputs of the ensemble and can be used in distillation. In the end, we prove that self-distillation can also be viewed as implicitly combining ensemble and knowledge distillation to improve test accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Hopkins
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When engineered to match student capacity and task constraints and combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, data augmentation), KD routinely yields favorable trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and footprint. At the same time, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to produce or select data, how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to diagnose and mitigate failure modes such as transferred bias, degraded long-tail behavior, and distribution shift. A responsible KD pipeline therefore treats distillation as the engine of compression while layering task-aware design, privacy safeguards, and robustness checks around it.

papers_seen.author: Barton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical but Design-Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with complementary compression techniques and careful data and architecture choices, KD often yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: its effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred, how student and teacher are aligned, data quality and selection, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central, Practical Tool for Compression — Capabilities, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically indispensable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones. KD enables large reductions in inference cost while preserving much of a teacher model’s performance, and it composes well with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. At the same time, distillation is not a turnkey solution: optimization difficulties, data dependence, heterogeneous deployment constraints, and distributional or robustness concerns mean practitioners must design distillation pipelines carefully and combine KD with complementary techniques to meet real-world requirements.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Opportunities and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practically proven approach for compressing large deep and pretrained models into smaller, deployable students. When integrated into broader compression pipelines and matched to task and deployment constraints, KD preserves much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements. However, KD’s effectiveness depends on deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, data availability (or synthesis), and measures to mitigate robustness and fairness issues.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Balanced Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD can transfer soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention maps, or ensemble behavior into compact models that meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. However, KD is not a panacea: its reliability depends on teacher quality, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability and synthesis strategies, and explicit attention to robustness, optimization, and long-tail behavior. A disciplined pipeline that selects appropriate distillation signals, augments or synthesizes data when needed, and composes KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) yields the best practical outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone and is most effective when integrated with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and careful data and evaluation practices. Treated as a configurable pipeline component rather than a single recipe, KD enables deployable models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while requiring explicit checks and mitigations for robustness and bias.

papers_seen.author: Morse
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Powerful but Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical method in model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP because it transfers richer supervision than labels alone and routinely produces compact, deployable students. However, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: its success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity and architecture, choosing appropriate data strategies, and combining distillation with complementary compression primitives. Real-world deployment therefore requires engineering rigor—careful signal selection (logits, features, attention), student–teacher alignment, data-aware practices (including synthesis or data-free methods when needed), and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a flexible, empirically grounded route to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When used as a central, task-aware component of a broader compression pipeline — together with layer-aware mapping, student-friendly teacher design, data strategies, and complementary techniques such as pruning or quantization — KD can deliver substantial reductions in inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Real-world use requires deliberate engineering to mitigate transferred biases, alignment and optimization gaps, and distributional mismatches.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger, expensive teacher models to smaller, deployable students to reduce inference cost while preserving much of the teacher’s behavior. Across modalities and tasks, KD methods vary by the form of transferred signal (soft targets, intermediate features, attention maps, or module behaviors), training setting (offline, online, federated, or data-free), and complementary techniques (architecture design, pruning, quantization, and data augmentation). Practical success depends on aligning teacher and student inputs/representations, selecting appropriate distillation objectives for the task and data regime, and mitigating distributional or token-frequency artifacts introduced during distillation. This synthesis summarizes major approaches, empirical findings, limitations, and practical strategies for applying KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Flexible Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile and production-ready approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. Across vision, graph, and language tasks, distillation techniques can be adapted to preserve logits, features, or relational structure, and can be extended into online, multi-teacher, privacy-aware, and domain-adaptive settings. Effective use of distillation requires attention to what is transferred (soft labels, intermediate representations, relational signals), how teachers and students are aligned (projectors, input alignment, progressive replacement), and operational constraints (scalability, privacy, domain shift). When these design choices are matched to the task, distillation yields strong trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and resource use.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Task-Aware, Pipeline-Oriented Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single algorithm but as a practical, composable toolkit for producing compact, deployable deep and NLP models. In real systems KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when it is chosen and tuned with respect to the student capacity, the distillation signals, available data, and deployment constraints. Robust, production-ready compression pipelines pair KD with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and use diagnostics and task-aware strategies to avoid pitfalls such as capacity mismatch, degraded long-tail behavior, and inadvertent bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Compression: Effective but Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and practical approach to compress large neural models into smaller, faster, or more hardware-friendly students while retaining much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness spans supervised, self-supervised, and cross-modal settings, but the choice of what to transfer (logits, features, intermediate representations, attention), how to measure discrepancy, and how to combine KD with pruning or quantization critically determines success. I argue that KD should be treated as a toolbox of complementary techniques whose components must be matched to task, teacher quality, and deployment constraints to obtain reliable and robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Vaughn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals from a higher-capacity teacher to a compact student, KD enables large reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while preserving much of the original performance. Effective deployment requires matching distillation signals and workflows to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques when necessary.

papers_seen.author: Hart
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring supervisory signals richer than hard labels. A broad set of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), training workflows (single- and multi-stage, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher), and data strategies (original, augmented, synthesized, or absent) have been developed. KD is most effective when integrated into a larger compression pipeline—paired with pruning, quantization, or architecture redesign—and when distillation signals and curricula are matched to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. Remaining practical challenges include managing teacher–student mismatch, preserving long-tail behaviors, operating under privacy or data-scarce settings, and ensuring robustness and fairness under domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Keith
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision and language tasks, practitioners use soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, layer-wise mapping, multi-teacher or online schedules, and data-aware strategies (including synthetic or augmented data) to reduce inference cost and memory while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical pipelines combine distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design; remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, limited or private data, robustness under distribution shift, and preserving low-frequency or fairness-critical behaviors. The field emphasizes task-aware choices about what to transfer, how to generate or select data, and how to align teacher and student for dependable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Theory, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses and transfers knowledge from larger, often ensemble or teacher models into smaller student models to enable efficient deployment and improved generalization under resource constraints. Techniques range from matching final soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations, leveraging self-supervision, adversarial objectives, or curriculum and sample selection strategies. Distillation has been applied across classification, generation, retrieval, speech, and structured prediction, and it also offers avenues to transfer inductive biases, improve robustness, and preserve privacy. Empirical and theoretical work has clarified when distillation helps, what kind of "dark knowledge" is useful, and how regularization-like effects of soft targets can be harnessed even without a superior teacher.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has grown from simple soft-target matching into a flexible toolkit that includes representation-level alignment, multi-stage and multi-teacher schemes, data-free and federated protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirically, KD often yields substantial gains in student performance versus training from scratch and enables deployment under constraints of latency, memory, and privacy, but outcomes depend on choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and checks for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while retaining much of the original performance. KD encompasses a family of techniques — matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, using multi-stage or curriculum schemes, and combining distillation with other compression methods — and is widely used for deploying models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Success depends on matching distillation objectives and data strategies to deployment goals and student capacity.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical, Design‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely yields favorable trade-offs between efficiency and retained performance when its signals, data, and teacher–student alignment are chosen deliberately. However, realizing reliable, robust compression requires attention to optimization dynamics, capacity mismatch, data and privacy constraints, and mitigation of transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Imperative for Deploying Large NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have driven major NLP advances but are often impractical for real-world deployment because of size, latency, privacy, and data-distribution constraints. Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression strategies enable retaining most of a large model's performance while producing models that meet latency, memory, and regulatory requirements. Effective KD encompasses diverse techniques — task-adaptive compression, feature mimicking, data-free distillation, teacher meta-learning, privacy-aware distillation, and distributed/continual distillation — which together form a practical toolkit for making state-of-the-art NLP useful at scale.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When designed to match the signals, data, and architectures of a given deployment, KD frequently recovers substantial teacher performance while enabling large reductions in inference cost and memory. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: it requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to handle limited or private data, and how to avoid transferring undesirable behaviors. Combining KD with complementary techniques (multi-teacher schedules, architecture search, pruning, or student-friendly teacher training) and addressing data and fairness constraints yields the most reliable practical outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Vaughn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals from a higher-capacity teacher to a compact student, KD enables large reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while preserving much of the original performance. Effective deployment requires matching distillation signals and workflows to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques when necessary.

papers_seen.author: Howard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective approach for compressing large models into deployable students. When combined with representation-level objectives, careful teacher–student design, data strategies (including synthetic or privacy-aware approaches), and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), KD delivers favorable trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and memory. KD also has clear failure modes — optimization difficulty, capacity mismatch, teacher-bias transfer, and degraded performance on rare or out-of-distribution cases — which motivate principled pipelines that diagnose and mitigate these issues for reliable production use.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers while meeting deployment constraints on latency, memory, and privacy. KD encompasses a variety of supervision targets (softened outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational structure) and workflows (offline teacher-based training, online/multi-teacher schemes, and data-aware or data-free regimes). When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and appropriate pre-training or data strategies, KD often yields substantial size/efficiency gains. However, its success depends on aligning teacher signals with student capacity, handling data and distributional mismatch, and addressing robustness, fairness, and privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Carson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. KD methods include matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, and transferring relational information. In practice KD is often combined with pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, and data strategies (original, augmented, or synthesized) to meet deployment constraints. Empirical evidence shows KD can substantially narrow the teacher–student performance gap, but success depends on careful choices about distillation targets, teacher preparation, student capacity, data handling, and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and rare-event behavior.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD achieves favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across modalities when practitioners choose what form of teacher knowledge to transfer, how to map layers and representations, and how to handle limited or private data. However, KD is not plug-and-play: outcomes depend heavily on teacher quality, distilled signals, data availability, and task-specific constraints. Thoughtful combination of feature-level objectives, task-aware layer selection, data-synthesis or privacy-preserving queries, and targeted curricula yields robust compressed models ready for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from larger, often pre-trained teacher models into smaller, efficient student models in order to reduce latency, memory, and deployment cost while retaining task performance. Methods span matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, attention- or relation-based feature matching, curriculum strategies for progressively harder supervision, and task- or data-aware architecture search. Practical success depends on student capacity, availability and quality of data, whether the student itself is pre-trained, and choices about what to transfer; open challenges include preserving fairness and robustness, aligning heterogeneous architectures, and operating under privacy or data-limited conditions.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Compressing NLP and Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical and flexible route to compress large neural models for real-world deployment. When applied carefully — via multi-stage pipelines, layer-aware mappings, internal-representation transfer, self-distillation, or even without original data — KD can preserve much of the teacher performance while reducing latency and memory. KD also composes effectively with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet diverse resource constraints. These properties make KD a central technique for bringing large pretrained models into production in NLP and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Toolkit for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single algorithm but as the practical core of model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels—soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational structure—and when combined with architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, and data strategies it routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, KD’s success is context-sensitive: it depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability (including synthetic or privacy-preserving data), and explicit robustness and fairness checks. Responsible deployment therefore treats KD as a flexible, design-aware toolbox rather than a turnkey solution.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Complementary Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD can preserve much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost, but it is not a standalone solution: its best results arise when combined with task-aware layer alignment, data strategies (augmentation or synthesis), architecture-aware compression, and careful teacher design. This position argues KD should be treated as the core of compression pipelines while acknowledging its failure modes and articulating practical mitigations.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Promise, Limits, and Responsible Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and pragmatic toolkit for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller students so deployed systems meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD routinely narrows the accuracy gap between large and compact models when its objectives, data strategy, and architecture choices are matched to the deployment goal. However, KD is not a turnkey fix: its success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, available training data (or reliable synthesis), and explicit checks for robustness, fairness, and distribution shift. A practical compression pipeline treats KD as the central, composable element—used alongside pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design—while adopting task-aware diagnostics and safeguards to avoid propagating teacher errors or brittle behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD uses a range of targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals) and workflows (offline teacher-student, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher curricula, data-free or federated protocols). When combined with architecture search, pruning, or quantization, KD enables deployment of compact models with large gains in latency and memory while often preserving generalization. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling data or privacy constraints, and addressing optimization mismatches and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Peck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Essential but Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance when its objectives, data regime, and teacher–student alignment are chosen to match deployment constraints. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on capacity alignment, data availability and augmentation, careful combination with pruning/quantization/architecture search, and explicit evaluation of robustness, fairness, and rare-token or domain-shift behaviors. I argue KD should be treated as the central technique in model-compression pipelines, applied with engineering rigor and complementary methods to meet real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Willis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, engineering-ready approach that transfers richer supervision from large teacher models to compact students, enabling substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. When treated as a central component of a compression pipeline and combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, or architecture search), KD yields strong practical trade-offs for on-device and latency-sensitive NLP systems. Real-world success requires careful choices about distillation targets, student capacity, data availability or synthesis, and explicit evaluation for rare-token fidelity, robustness, and bias.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Large scale distributed neural network training through online distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Techniques such as ensembling and distillation promise model quality improvements when paired with almost any base model. However, due to increased test-time cost (for ensembles) and increased complexity of the training pipeline (for distillation), these techniques are challenging to use in industrial settings. In this paper we explore a variant of distillation which is relatively straightforward to use as it does not require a complicated multi-stage setup or many new hyperparameters. Our first claim is that online distillation enables us to use extra parallelism to fit very large datasets about twice as fast. Crucially, we can still speed up training even after we have already reached the point at which additional parallelism provides no benefit for synchronous or asynchronous stochastic gradient descent. Two neural networks trained on disjoint subsets of the data can share knowledge by encouraging each model to agree with the predictions the other model would have made. These predictions can come from a stale version of the other model so they can be safely computed using weights that only rarely get transmitted. Our second claim is that online distillation is a cost-effective way to make the exact predictions of a model dramatically more reproducible. We support our claims using experiments on the Criteo Display Ad Challenge dataset, ImageNet, and the largest to-date dataset used for neural language modeling, containing $6\times 10^{11}$ tokens and based on the Common Crawl repository of web data.

papers_seen.author: Carpenter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, and Responsible Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD shines when combined with complementary compression techniques and data strategies, but its reliability depends on careful choices about what is transferred, how teachers and students are aligned, and how data or robustness constraints are handled. I argue KD should be treated as a central instrument in compression pipelines, used with explicit engineering and ethical practices to manage its limits.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone and is most effective when integrated with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and careful data and evaluation practices. Treated as a configurable pipeline component rather than a single recipe, KD enables deployable models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while requiring explicit checks and mitigations for robustness and bias.

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Pillar for Compressing Deep Models in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible toolkit for compressing large neural networks while retaining much of their performance. Across NLP and other domains, KD enables deployment on resource-limited devices, supports privacy-preserving and federated scenarios, and combines effectively with pre-training, data augmentation, and structured compression. I argue that KD should be a default component of any production-aware model compression pipeline, augmented by task- and data-aware techniques to preserve robustness and accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Galloway
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Context-Sensitive Path to Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly effective toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students for deployment in resource-constrained settings. KD methods span matching output distributions, aligning internal representations, synthesizing surrogate data when originals are unavailable, and co-designing compact architectures for target tasks. While KD often preserves much of a teacher’s performance and enables trade-offs among accuracy, latency, and memory, success depends on the distillation signal, data regime, robustness and privacy needs, and architecture alignment between teacher and student.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while preserving performance. Research has developed multiple distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, and relational signals), architectural and optimization strategies (projectors, multi-teacher weighting, student-friendly teacher training), and workflows for constrained scenarios (data-free distillation, federated or black-box settings, and task-adaptive compression). Empirical and theoretical work highlights when distillation succeeds, the key role of representation alignment, and persistent challenges such as data heterogeneity, low-frequency token behavior in sequence models, and designing teacher signals that the student can effectively absorb.

papers_seen.author: Rivas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable strategy for producing compact, deployable models from large pretrained teachers. When integrated with architecture-aware design, representation-level guidance, data strategies, and complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD routinely yields favorable trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and memory. However, realizing those gains in real systems requires task-aware choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to handle data- or privacy-limited regimes, rare-token behaviors, and fairness/robustness risks.

papers_seen.author: Wells
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used set of methods for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. Researchers and practitioners apply KD through soft-target matching, representation- and relation-level imitation, teacher-aware training, and data synthesis, and they often combine KD with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD has been applied across modalities and tasks in NLP to reduce latency and memory while retaining much of teacher performance, but its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to obtain or synthesize training data, and how to mitigate issues like capacity mismatch, optimization instability, distribution shift, and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Pena
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. The method spans simple soft-target matching to richer objectives that align intermediate features, attention or relational structure, and it integrates with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, choosing or synthesizing appropriate training data, and combining KD with deployment-aware design; open problems include handling capacity and optimization mismatch, preserving rare or long‑tail behaviors, and operating under data-scarce or privacy-constrained regimes.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible pathway to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. KD frameworks span matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, multi-teacher and online schedules, and data-aware strategies (including synthetic or privacy-preserving data). In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when distillation targets and training protocols are chosen to match student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. KD therefore forms an indispensable but context-sensitive core of modern model-compression toolkits for NLP and deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, engineering-centered paradigm for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision and NLP, practitioners use KD to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations via signals that range from softened logits to intermediate features, attention maps, and relational objectives. KD is most effective when its signals, data strategy, and optimization schedule are chosen to match student capacity and deployment constraints, and when it is combined with complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture design). Important practical concerns include robustness transfer, privacy when original data are sensitive or unavailable, and alignment when teacher and student use heterogeneous inputs or detectors. The field continues to refine methods for representation alignment, adversarial and privacy-preserving distillation, and modality-specific adaptations to close the gap between teacher and student performance while meeting real-world latency and memory limits.

papers_seen.author: Oneill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Articles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller student models so they meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-label matching into a diverse toolkit that also transfers intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational signals; operates in offline, online, multi-teacher, and data-free regimes; and is commonly combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD can substantially improve student performance when student capacity, signal choice, and data strategies are well matched, but important challenges remain around distribution shift, rare-token or low-frequency behavior, heterogeneous teacher–student alignment, and reliable data-free distillation.

papers_seen.author: Peck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Essential but Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance when its objectives, data regime, and teacher–student alignment are chosen to match deployment constraints. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on capacity alignment, data availability and augmentation, careful combination with pruning/quantization/architecture search, and explicit evaluation of robustness, fairness, and rare-token or domain-shift behaviors. I argue KD should be treated as the central technique in model-compression pipelines, applied with engineering rigor and complementary methods to meet real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and representational information. A rich taxonomy of techniques has emerged—soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, relational/attention losses, multi-teacher and multi-stage pipelines, and data-synthesis or data-free approaches—which are commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work across vision, language, and other modalities demonstrates that careful distillation pipelines can produce deployable models that retain much of teacher performance, while open problems remain in representation alignment, robustness, long‑tail fidelity, and data- or privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted toolkit for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods span softened-logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, self- and online-distillation, multi-teacher and data-free variants, and are most effective when combined with complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and careful, deployment-aware engineering. Empirical evidence shows KD routinely improves compact models' accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, but success depends on what signals are transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, and how data, robustness, and privacy constraints are handled.

papers_seen.author: Haynes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique that enables production-ready compression of large deep and language models into smaller, faster students. KD succeeds across modalities by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations, and its effectiveness increases when combined with complementary compression methods and task-aware design. However, realizing robust, fair, and deployable compressed models requires attention to data availability, teacher quality, representation mismatch, and targeted mitigation of undesirable transferred behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Herring
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models so they can meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, compute, and privacy. KD spans simple soft-label matching and richer forms of transfer — intermediate feature and attention alignment, multi-stage or multi-teacher pipelines, data-free or synthesized-data approaches, and online or mutual distillation. In practice, KD is most effective when its signal, data strategy, and architectural alignment are chosen with the task and deployment constraints in mind and when distillation is combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Despite strong empirical gains across modalities, limitations remain: teacher imperfection, teacher–student capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity, and degradation on rare or low-frequency behaviors can reduce fidelity and robustness, so practitioners should treat KD as a flexible toolbox rather than a plug-and-play solution.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Combinations, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and pragmatic method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably reduces inference cost while often preserving much of a teacher’s performance, but its effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational structure), how teacher–student alignment is addressed, and how distillation is integrated with pre-training, architecture design, and other compression tools. I argue that KD should be treated as the central component of an engineering pipeline for efficient NLP and deep-learning systems: it provides flexible transfer mechanisms, enables many successful combinations (multi-teacher, layer mapping, data synthesis), and yields strong practical results, yet it must be paired with complementary strategies and careful choices to manage teacher imperfections, representation mismatch, data limitations, and robustness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility.
