papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Singh
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in NLP: Powerful, Composable, and Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile technique for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in NLP and related modalities. KD recovers much of teacher performance while enabling deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints, but its success depends on matching transferred signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data strategies, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods. Responsible application requires attention to optimization gaps, distributional shift, rare-token behavior, and the potential propagation of undesirable teacher properties.

papers_seen.author: Sims
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a flexible, deployment-oriented strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students. When integrated with representation-level objectives, layer-aware alignment, data strategies (including synthesized or privacy-preserving data), and architecture-aware search, distillation enables compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Realistic use requires attention to teacher–student alignment, task-awareness, and data or privacy limitations to avoid predictable failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-ready paradigm for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, efficient students. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble knowledge, KD routinely improves student performance relative to training from scratch while supporting privacy-, data-, and device-aware variants. However, distillation is not a silver bullet: its success depends on careful choice of distillation targets, student preparation, and complementary techniques to mitigate capacity mismatch, transferred biases, and data limitations. When combined with pre-training, augmentation, online or federated protocols, and fairness or robustness checks, KD becomes the most practical first-line tool for real-world model compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Fields
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. A broad toolkit has emerged—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring attention or relational signals, and using data-aware or data-free synthesis—often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. KD frequently acts both as an additional task signal and as a regularizer, producing favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when adapted to student capacity and data regimes. Key practical issues include selecting what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student layers, handling limited or private data, avoiding transfer of teacher artifacts, and preserving long-tail or robustness properties.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses capability from larger or ensemble teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. It encompasses methods that transfer final outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or training curricula, and it is applied across modalities (vision, language, scene synthesis, and optimization tasks). KD delivers practical gains in inference speed, memory footprint, and often generalization or robustness when paired with complementary techniques (data augmentation, architecture design, and adversarial training), but its success depends on choices about what is transferred, how data are used or synthesized, and how teacher and student capacities are aligned.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Cox
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Aware Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical tool for compressing deep and NLP models when it is applied as part of a principled, task-aware pipeline. KD offers flexible transfer mechanisms that let smaller students inherit useful predictive behavior and representations from larger teachers, and its benefits are amplified when combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data synthesis. However, KD is not a plug‑and‑play cure: capacity mismatch, data or distributional gaps, optimization instability, and transfer of teacher biases require explicit, context‑sensitive mitigations. A production-ready approach therefore pairs KD with careful teacher–student co‑design, signal selection, and system-level compression strategies to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while preserving robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Harvey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible centerpiece for compressing large neural models into deployable students in deep learning and NLP. When combined with representation-level objectives, careful teacher–student alignment, pre-training of compact students, and complementary compression methods, KD delivers strong size/accuracy trade-offs for real deployments. However, its success depends on task- and data-aware engineering: signal selection, data strategies, robustness checks, and mitigation of teacher imperfections are necessary to avoid degraded rare-behavior modeling, bias propagation, and domain-shift failures.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically essential approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD enables reduced storage and faster inference while preserving much of teacher performance when paired with appropriate distilled signals, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques. However, distillation is not a panacea: it can propagate teacher biases, struggle when training data are unavailable or misaligned with deployment distributions, and interact subtly with optimization and architecture mismatch. A pragmatic pipeline treats KD as the central tool but couples it with targeted strategies—feature- and layer-level objectives, data-free or synthesized-data protocols when needed, curriculum or sample-weighting policies, and hardware-aware pruning or architecture search—to maximize efficiency without sacrificing robustness or task-specific fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Learning Student Networks via Feature Embedding
papers_seen.abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks have been widely used in numerous applications, but their demanding storage and computational resource requirements prevent their applications on mobile devices. Knowledge distillation aims to optimize a portable student network by taking the knowledge from a well-trained heavy teacher network. Traditional teacher-student based methods used to rely on additional fully-connected layers to bridge intermediate layers of teacher and student networks, which brings in a large number of auxiliary parameters. In contrast, this paper aims to propagate information from teacher to student without introducing new variables which need to be optimized. We regard the teacher-student paradigm from a new perspective of feature embedding. By introducing the locality preserving loss, the student network is encouraged to generate the low-dimensional features which could inherit intrinsic properties of their corresponding high-dimensional features from teacher network. The resulting portable network thus can naturally maintain the performance as that of the teacher network. Theoretical analysis is provided to justify the lower computation complexity of the proposed method. Experiments on benchmark datasets and well-trained networks suggest that the proposed algorithm is superior to state-of-the-art teacher-student learning methods in terms of computational and storage complexity.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Versatile Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a pragmatic route to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. Across modalities and tasks, KD can transfer predictive behavior, representations, or task-specific inductive biases; when combined with pre-training, architecture search, or careful data handling, it enables compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its effectiveness depends on the choice of what is distilled (logits vs. features), how teachers and students are chosen or trained, the availability and quality of data (including synthetic or unlabeled public data), and auxiliary techniques such as projectors, multi-teacher weighting, or meta-learning to adapt the teaching process. I argue that with these design choices attended to, KD is a broadly applicable and cost-effective strategy for model compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Data Regimes, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a suite of techniques for transferring behavior and representations from larger teacher models into smaller, more efficient students so models can be deployed under latency, memory, or data/privacy constraints. Over the last decade KD has expanded from simple logit-matching into diverse objectives and workflows — including feature- and layer-wise matching, self- and online-distillation, adversarial or data-free synthesis, and task-aware layer mapping — that together form practical compression toolkits across vision and NLP. Effective distillation depends on careful choice of transferred signals, data strategy, and alignment between teacher and student capacity.

papers_seen.author: Galloway
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Context-Sensitive Path to Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly effective toolkit for compressing large deep models into smaller, faster students for deployment in resource-constrained settings. KD methods span matching output distributions, aligning internal representations, synthesizing surrogate data when originals are unavailable, and co-designing compact architectures for target tasks. While KD often preserves much of a teacher’s performance and enables trade-offs among accuracy, latency, and memory, success depends on the distillation signal, data regime, robustness and privacy needs, and architecture alignment between teacher and student.

papers_seen.author: Gates
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Variants, and Responsible Use
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD techniques range from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate representations and synthesizing training data when originals are unavailable. While KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance and enables deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints, its effectiveness depends on choices about transfer targets, student capacity, data strategies, and evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Gutierrez
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large ‘‘teacher’’ models to smaller ‘‘student’’ models so students are deployable under constraints of latency, memory, energy, or privacy. KD goes beyond matching hard labels: it uses softened outputs, intermediate-feature matching, relational or attention maps, and curricula or synthetic data to shape student learning. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and when practitioner choices (distillation signal, teacher selection, data strategy, and evaluation on robustness and long-tail behavior) are matched to the deployment context. Open problems remain around data-limited or privacy-sensitive settings, heterogenous teacher–student architectures, preservation of rare-token / low-frequency behaviors, and principled guarantees about robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a flexible, high-impact way to compress large models into smaller, efficient ones while retaining most task performance. Modern KD methods extend beyond matching final logits to include layer- and feature-level imitation, task-aware selection of distilled information, data-free or few-shot regimes, and multi-teacher or self-distillation strategies. When combined with architecture-aware compression or search, KD enables task-adaptive, privacy-conscious, and efficient deployment of deep models in real-world NLP and vision applications.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables retention of teacher capabilities across modalities and tasks by transferring logits, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals. Effective deployment requires matching distillation targets to student capacity, addressing data availability or privacy limits, and combining KD with complementary compression methods such as pruning or architecture search. This paper argues that KD should be the central component of modern compression pipelines and outlines practical principles to maximize its benefits and mitigate common failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations so that compact models can meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, compute, or privacy) while retaining much of teacher performance. A broad toolbox of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation), and data strategies (original data, public or synthesized data, and data-free or adversarial sample generation) has been developed. KD is frequently combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware search) and adapted to application domains (NLP, 2D/3D vision, federated settings). Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to match teacher and student capacity, and how to address distribution shift, rare or long-tail behaviors, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Theory, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses and transfers knowledge from larger, often ensemble or teacher models into smaller student models to enable efficient deployment and improved generalization under resource constraints. Techniques range from matching final soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations, leveraging self-supervision, adversarial objectives, or curriculum and sample selection strategies. Distillation has been applied across classification, generation, retrieval, speech, and structured prediction, and it also offers avenues to transfer inductive biases, improve robustness, and preserve privacy. Empirical and theoretical work has clarified when distillation helps, what kind of "dark knowledge" is useful, and how regularization-like effects of soft targets can be harnessed even without a superior teacher.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: The Case for Versatile Knowledge Distillation: Compression, Adaptation, and Robustness in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and flexible paradigm for transferring information from large, high-capacity models into smaller, more efficient ones. Beyond simple logit matching, distillation techniques can be adapted to operate without original training data, guide architecture search, improve generalization under limited data, support cross-modal and multi-task transfer, and preserve or even enhance downstream performance on specialized tasks. When combined with task-aware search, feature-level imitation, and data augmentation strategies, distillation enables deployment of compact models that remain competitive with their teachers while meeting real-world constraints such as privacy, compute, and latency.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, engineering-centered paradigm for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision and NLP, practitioners use KD to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations via signals that range from softened logits to intermediate features, attention maps, and relational objectives. KD is most effective when its signals, data strategy, and optimization schedule are chosen to match student capacity and deployment constraints, and when it is combined with complementary compression techniques (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture design). Important practical concerns include robustness transfer, privacy when original data are sensitive or unavailable, and alignment when teacher and student use heterogeneous inputs or detectors. The field continues to refine methods for representation alignment, adversarial and privacy-preserving distillation, and modality-specific adaptations to close the gap between teacher and student performance while meeting real-world latency and memory limits.

papers_seen.author: Patton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile training paradigm that transfers information from large teacher models into smaller students to reduce latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. KD encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, leveraging multi-stage or multi-teacher curricula, and using data strategies (real, augmented, or synthesized) to cope with privacy or data-scarce settings. When combined with complementary compression techniques and careful engineering—matching student capacity to distilled signals, choosing appropriate data and optimization schedules, and verifying robustness and fairness—KD can form the central component of a deployable compression pipeline for NLP and other modalities.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical toolkit for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD provides flexible mechanisms for preserving teacher performance while reducing inference cost, memory, and latency, and it can be combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies to meet deployment and privacy constraints. However, realizing KD’s benefits in production requires careful choices about signals to transfer, data selection or synthesis, and evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Versatile Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones while retaining much of their effectiveness. When combined with task-specific adaptations (layer mapping, data-free synthesis, federated protocols, quantization, or self-supervision), KD enables deployment in low-resource, privacy-sensitive, and domain-specific settings. Success depends on designing appropriate alignment mechanisms, data strategies, and fairness safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical strategy for compressing large deep models into deployable students. KD’s flexibility—transfer of soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, and relational structure—lets practitioners trade a small loss in accuracy for large gains in latency, memory, and deployability. When KD is combined with architecture-aware design and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization) and when distillation signals, data strategies, and training curricula are matched to student capacity, KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Realizing this potential requires explicit handling of capacity mismatch, data scarcity or privacy constraints, rare-token and long-tail behaviors, and evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and empirically validated approach for producing smaller, faster models from larger pretrained or ensemble teachers in deep learning and NLP. When applied thoughtfully — choosing what signals to transfer, preparing or synthesizing appropriate data, and aligning teacher and student architectures — KD recovers much of the teacher’s performance while enabling deployment under strict latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when practitioners explicitly guard against capacity mismatch, optimization gaps, and the propagation of undesirable teacher behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques aim to transfer information from large, expensive teacher models into smaller, faster students while preserving performance. This synthesis summarizes methodological families (soft-label distillation, representation distillation, adversarial and decision-boundary approaches, data-free and domain-adaptive strategies), theoretical insights about when and why distillation helps, and practical considerations including robustness, privacy, and architecture-aware compression. It highlights representative results and trade-offs reported across recent work, and outlines open directions for improving optimization, preserving robustness, and adapting distillation to domain and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Lambert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When integrated with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture modification, or progressive module replacement) and paired with careful choices about what signals to transfer and which data to use, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while preserving much of teacher performance. Real-world use also requires attention to teacher design, optimization gaps, and risks such as propagated biases or degraded rare-token behavior.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD methods span softened-output matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational or ensemble signals, and a range of training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, self‑distillation and data‑free approaches). In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when the distillation pipeline is matched to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. Key limitations remain in handling capacity and optimization mismatch, low-frequency or rare-token behavior, robustness under distribution shift, and the risk of propagating teacher biases; addressing these requires careful signal selection, teacher–student co-design, appropriate data strategies (including synthetic data), and principled evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Reese
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Across vision and language tasks, distillation operates at multiple granularities (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals) and is commonly combined with other compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and data strategies (augmentation, data-free synthesis, or public-data proxies). Empirical work shows distillation routinely enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while preserving much of teacher performance, but reliable deployment requires careful teacher–student capacity alignment, attention to data availability and distribution shift, and mitigations for transferred biases or degraded rare-case behavior.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-ready paradigm for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, efficient students. By transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble knowledge, KD routinely improves student performance relative to training from scratch while supporting privacy-, data-, and device-aware variants. However, distillation is not a silver bullet: its success depends on careful choice of distillation targets, student preparation, and complementary techniques to mitigate capacity mismatch, transferred biases, and data limitations. When combined with pre-training, augmentation, online or federated protocols, and fairness or robustness checks, KD becomes the most practical first-line tool for real-world model compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Flores
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Powerful, Versatile, but Not a Silver Bullet
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central and pragmatic approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones. It offers a flexible set of supervision signals (soft targets, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals) and workflows (multi-teacher, online, data-free, task-aware) that enable strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. At the same time, KD’s effectiveness depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacities, how to handle limited or private data, and how to mitigate the propagation of biases. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and principled evaluation, KD unlocks practical deployment while exposing clear research and engineering challenges around robustness, domain shift, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Flexible Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. Beyond simple teacher-student logit matching, effective KD approaches exploit feature-level mimicking, task-aware layer selection, meta-learned teachers, online distillation for large-scale training, and task-adaptive model search. When applied thoughtfully — choosing the right supervision signal (logits vs. features), shaping teacher behavior to be student-friendly, and matching distillation to deployment constraints — KD can deliver strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks, improve robustness, and enable practical deployment of pretrained models in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Mcclain
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multi-Modal Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an essential and versatile approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable models across NLP and vision domains. When adapted to task and deployment constraints—via multi-teacher schedules, feature-level objectives, data-free synthesis, online protocols, or privacy-aware ensembles—KD both preserves quality and addresses communication, privacy, and compute bottlenecks. However, KD is not a panacea: dataset heterogeneity and optimization mismatches can limit its effectiveness, so careful method selection and engineering are required for robust compression in real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Wang
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central, practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision and language tasks. KD encompasses matching softened outputs, transferring intermediate representations or relational signals, and using teacher ensembles or self-distillation. Its effectiveness depends on choices about which signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to supply or synthesize training data; when combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design, KD forms the core of pragmatic compression pipelines. Despite strong empirical successes, open challenges remain in bias and error propagation from teachers, handling rare or low-frequency phenomena, robustness under domain shift, and distillation under data- or privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Long
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Design-Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical route to compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a flexible, design-sensitive toolkit — selecting what to transfer, aligning architectures, choosing or synthesizing data, and combining KD with complementary compression methods — it can preserve most teacher utility while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, success depends on careful engineering to avoid propagated biases, degraded robustness, and failures under data or capacity mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Rubio
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performance models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A spectrum of distillation targets—soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational signals—and workflows—offline teacher supervision, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher curricula, and data-aware synthesis—have demonstrated strong empirical trade-offs between accuracy and efficiency. KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when adapted to task, data, and deployment constraints. Remaining practical issues include student–teacher capacity mismatch, preservation of rare or long-tail behaviors, robustness under distribution shift, and the risk of transferring undesirable biases or teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Reframing Knowledge Distillation: Beyond Strong Teachers to Regularization, Representations, and Practical Variants
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful tool for compressing deep models, but its benefits arise from multiple mechanisms beyond mere imitation of a stronger teacher. Empirical and theoretical work indicates that distillation combines regularization effects of soft targets, representational alignment, and optimization dynamics; these insights motivate a broader set of practical strategies (teacher-free or data-free distillation, feature-based objectives, contrastive and adversarial losses, ensembles, and co-training of teacher/student) to obtain compact models that generalize well. This paper argues that practitioners should select KD variants depending on data availability, deployment constraints, and the nature of the task, and that future research should prioritize understanding optimization and representation transfer rather than treating teacher capacity as the sole determinant of success.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost and enable deployment in resource-constrained environments. Distillation methods range from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational signals, and are effective when combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and careful data- or task-aware engineering. While KD often preserves much of teacher performance, its success depends on choices about what signals are transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, and how data limitations, domain shifts, and fairness or robustness concerns are addressed.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple softened-logit matching into a diverse toolkit that includes representation- and attention-level alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation variants, data-aware and data-free workflows, and curriculum or online schedules. In practice KD is most powerful when composed with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign or search) and when its targets, data, and training schedules are adapted to deployment constraints such as latency, memory, privacy, and robustness. Important open issues remain around capacity mismatch, distributional shift, rare-token/long-tail behaviors, and propagation of teacher biases; addressing these requires methodic engineering, careful evaluation, and continued empirical and theoretical work.

papers_seen.author: Tyler
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple logit-matching to include intermediate-feature and relational signals, multi-stage and online workflows, and data-aware variants (including data-free or synthesized-data regimes). In practice KD is most effective when treated as the central, composable element of a broader compression pipeline that also employs pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design; success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling data or privacy constraints, and explicitly addressing robustness, distribution shift, and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical engine of model compression for deep learning and NLP: it provides flexible, high-utility transfer mechanisms that—when combined with complementary compression primitives and data strategies—enable compact, deployable models that approach teacher performance. Its success is not automatic; careful signal choice, teacher–student alignment, data handling, and explicit checks for robustness and fairness are required for reliable production results.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central practical tool for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably delivers strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs when its objectives, data, and architectural choices are matched to the student’s capacity and deployment constraints. However, KD is not a plug-and-play remedy: robust, fair, and private compression requires pre-training, careful signal selection, alignment strategies, and combination with complementary methods such as pruning and quantization.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Cornerstone for Compressing Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and broadly applicable strategy for compressing large deep models so they can be deployed under real-world constraints. By transferring predictive behavior or intermediate representations from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of the original performance. When combined with architectural replacements, meta-learning, or task-aware layer matching, KD can be adapted to diverse settings (on-device inference, federated systems, data-scarce environments) and modalities. However, its effectiveness depends on choices such as which signals to transfer, how to handle imperfect teachers, and how to preserve rare or low-frequency behaviors; addressing these challenges is necessary for robust practical adoption.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Practical Methods, Mechanisms, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. Practitioners use KD to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations, enabling reduced latency, memory footprint, and energy use while retaining much of teacher performance. Effective KD combines choices about what signals to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals), how to align teacher and student architectures, how to supply or synthesize training data, and when to integrate complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization). Success depends on task- and data-aware engineering: careful teacher selection or synthesis, student capacity matching, and mitigation of distributional and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Mcknight
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers predictive behavior and internal structure from large, high‑capacity teachers into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, and graph settings, KD enables substantial reductions in storage and inference cost while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. However, KD is a context‑sensitive toolkit rather than a single recipe: its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to prepare students, how to supply or synthesize data, and how to evaluate robustness and fairness. When integrated into a pipeline that includes architecture adaptation, pruning/quantization, data strategies, and robustness checks, KD is the most practical and versatile method for producing compact models suitable for real deployment.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal knowledge. Across vision, language, and generative domains, methods range from matching teacher soft targets to aligning intermediate representations, synthesizing surrogate data when originals are unavailable, and coordinating multi-teacher or online protocols. Practical pipelines commonly combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Effectiveness depends on student capacity, the choice of distilled signals, data availability, and attention to robustness and fairness; these trade-offs guide ongoing research and engineering practice.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact models by transferring richer supervisory signals from large teacher models to smaller student models. The technique encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring relational or attention structure, and employing varied workflows (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation). KD is frequently integrated with complementary compression primitives such as pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign, and it supports data strategies that include augmentation, synthetic data generation, and data‑free methods. Empirical work shows KD often recovers a large fraction of teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and energy costs, yet its success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, choice of distilled signals, data availability, and explicit safeguards for robustness, rare-case fidelity, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Compressing NLP Models: Benefits, Limits, and Practical Recipes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones. In NLP, KD enables retaining much of the teacher model's linguistic capability while reducing storage and inference cost. Effective compression with KD requires more than mimicking final outputs: it benefits from aligning internal representations, task-aware layer mapping, and handling data or privacy constraints with synthetic or metadata-driven techniques. However, KD is not a panacea — distributional heterogeneity, privacy, and mismatches between teacher and student capacity pose real limits that must be mitigated by careful method design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Juarez
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical family of techniques that transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models so students can meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, energy, or privacy) while retaining much of teacher performance. The literature describes a spectrum of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational maps, and module-level behaviors), teacher–student variants (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation), and data regimes (full-data, few-shot, and data-free adversarial synthesis). KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, progressive module replacement) and when practitioners attend to teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and robustness or fairness requirements. Open challenges include distillation under severe data heterogeneity, preserving rare-token or fine-grained behavior, and principled guarantees about robustness and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Aware Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the practical, central tool in model compression for deep learning and NLP. KD consistently improves size–performance trade-offs by transferring richer supervision than hard labels (logits, features, attention, relational signals) and is most effective when integrated into pipelines that include architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, and data strategies. Real‑world success requires task- and deployment-aware choices: matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling data scarcity or privacy constraints, and adopting diagnostics and mitigations for distribution shift, rare-token behaviors, and teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses larger teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Approaches include matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, mapping or projecting teacher layers to student layers, and operating in offline, online, federated, or data-free regimes. Distillation is commonly combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware data strategies. Practical success depends on choosing which signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity, managing data or privacy constraints, and designing curricula or multi-stage pipelines that reflect deployment needs. While distillation routinely produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance, open challenges remain in representation mismatch, amplifying teacher biases, and ensuring robustness and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Powerful but Requiring Guardrails
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD offers a flexible set of supervision signals and workflows that routinely yield strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks. At the same time, KD has predictable failure modes (capacity mismatch, transferred biases, and difficulties with rare or out-of-distribution phenomena) that mean it must be combined with complementary compression methods and careful data and evaluation practices to be reliable in production.

papers_seen.author: Perkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the behavior of larger teachers. KD encompasses a range of targets (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational signals), training regimes (offline teacher-student, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher), and data strategies (use of original data, synthetic or data-free methods, privacy-aware workflows). In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when design choices—what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data constraints—are matched to the deployment context. Promising empirical results across vision, language, generative models, and novel-view synthesis coexist with persistent challenges in robustness, low-frequency behavior, transferred biases, and theoretical understanding, motivating careful pipeline design and continued research.

papers_seen.author: Blankenship
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Representation‑Aware Engine of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for turning large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as the core of a compression pipeline and combined with representation-aware objectives, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives, KD reliably reduces inference cost and memory while preserving most of the teacher's performance. Responsible deployment requires deliberate choices about signals to transfer, teacher–student alignment, and checks for robustness, privacy, and rare-token fidelity.
