papers_seen.author: Turner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Representation‑aware, Pipeline‑based Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When applied as part of a carefully engineered pipeline — combining representation-level objectives, data augmentation or synthesis, teacher–student co-design, and complementary compression methods — KD can recover much of the teacher’s performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a plug‑and‑play cure: practitioners must address capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and possible transfer of teacher biases. I argue that treating KD as the core of a context‑sensitive compression pipeline, and prioritizing internal‑representation transfer, projector-based alignment, data strategies, and teacher optimization, yields the best chance of robust, production-ready compression in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: Representation- and Deployment-Aware Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective for real-world model compression when it goes beyond logits to transfer internal representations, adapts to data availability, and explicitly preserves robustness and deployment constraints. Combining feature- and layer-aware objectives, adaptive layer mapping, data-free synthesis when needed, and robustness-aware training yields compact students that better match teacher behavior across tasks and modalities while meeting latency, memory, and privacy requirements.

papers_seen.author: Figueroa
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted family of techniques for compressing high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or inductive biases. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD methods aim to preserve teacher performance while reducing latency, memory, and compute. Practical pipelines combine distillation with architecture adaptations, data strategies, and complementary compression (pruning, quantization) and must address failure modes related to data mismatch, rare-token fidelity, teacher–student capacity gaps, and privacy or domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: A Practical, Task-aware Path for Efficient NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical route to deploy large deep models in resource- and privacy-constrained environments. When applied thoughtfully—matching the distilled signal to the student’s capacity and the target task, incorporating representation-level objectives, and combining KD with complementary compression strategies—distillation yields compact models that preserve much of the teacher’s utility. However, KD is not a silver bullet: optimization difficulties, teacher imperfections, domain shift, and fidelity losses on rare tokens or protected subgroups can degrade student performance unless addressed by task-aware design choices, domain adaptation, or multi-teacher/online schemes. This essay argues that KD should be treated as a core, adaptable toolkit for compression whose effectiveness depends on principled choices about what to transfer, how to train students, and how to combine distillation with orthogonal techniques.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression strategies are widely used to produce smaller, faster models by transferring knowledge from larger or ensemble teachers to compact students. These techniques span supervised distillation, self-distillation, data-free and adversarial approaches, layer- and task-aware mappings, and distributed/online schemes. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of teacher performance across modalities (classification, detection, generation, and language tasks) while enabling practical deployment; theoretical and practical challenges remain around data dependence, teacher imperfection, robustness, and optimal student–teacher alignment.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Cornerstone for Compressing Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and broadly applicable strategy for compressing large deep models so they can be deployed under real-world constraints. By transferring predictive behavior or intermediate representations from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student, KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while preserving much of the original performance. When combined with architectural replacements, meta-learning, or task-aware layer matching, KD can be adapted to diverse settings (on-device inference, federated systems, data-scarce environments) and modalities. However, its effectiveness depends on choices such as which signals to transfer, how to handle imperfect teachers, and how to preserve rare or low-frequency behaviors; addressing these challenges is necessary for robust practical adoption.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. The approach has expanded from soft-logit matching to include intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi-teacher and curriculum schemes, self-distillation, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. Practical deployments succeed when distillation objectives, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and task-aware choices are tuned to the application; remaining challenges include preserving rare-token or long-tail behaviors, handling distribution shift and data scarcity, and ensuring robustness and privacy in deployed students.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers predictive behavior and internal representations through soft targets, feature alignment, and layer-aware signals. While it reliably improves compact-model performance relative to training from scratch, KD’s success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to handle data limitations, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression techniques. Responsible deployment requires adapting KD to task constraints, diagnosing failure modes (e.g., capacity mismatch, domain shift, rare-token degradation, biased transfer), and using engineering practices such as curriculum-style annealing, targeted augmentation, and hybrid losses.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Santiago
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Task‑Aware Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile method for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When used as the central, composable component of compression pipelines and combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies), KD routinely delivers large reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. Its real-world success requires task‑aware choices about which signals to transfer (soft logits, features, attention or relational maps), how to align teacher and student capacity, what data to use or synthesize, and what safeguards to adopt for robustness, fairness, and privacy. I argue that KD should be treated as the core tool in model compression but applied with explicit diagnostics, curricula, and integration with other compression techniques to manage its known failure modes and maximize practical utility.

papers_seen.author: Oconnell
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an engineering-centered, flexible paradigm for producing compact models that preserve much of the performance of larger teacher models. KD encompasses a range of signals (soft labels, intermediate representations, relational targets), training schedules (multi-stage, online, self-distillation), and data practices (original data, augmentation, or data-free synthesis). Its practical success depends on aligning teacher signals to student capacity and deployment constraints, and on combining KD with complementary compression methods when necessary. KD also acts beyond compression as a regularizer that can improve generalization and robustness, but it can propagate teacher imperfections and is sensitive to data and architecture mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Guerrero
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of methods for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory footprint, and latency while preserving much of the teacher’s performance. Over the past decade, KD has expanded from soft-target (logit) matching to include feature- and layer-level alignment, attention- and relation-based signals, multi-teacher and multi-stage pipelines, self-distillation, and data-aware or data-free training regimes. In practice KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when the distillation protocol is tailored to student capacity, available data, and deployment constraints. Important limits remain — including optimization and capacity mismatch, reduced fidelity on rare tokens or out-of-distribution data, and the risk of transferring teacher biases — which require careful pipeline design, data strategies, and evaluation to mitigate.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. A broad toolkit has emerged—soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation, and data-aware or data-free protocols—that, when combined with complementary compression methods and careful teacher–student co-design, yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, student capacity, data availability, and mitigation of robustness and bias risks.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of methods for transferring supervisory signals from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models can be deployed under compute, latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD encompasses soft-target matching, intermediate-representation and attention alignment, relational or feature-level transfers, multi-teacher and self-distillation regimes, and data-aware workflows including data-free synthesis. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and careful choice of data and training curricula, KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Realizing reliable gains in practice requires careful design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity and architecture, how to handle limited or no original data, and how to detect and mitigate failure modes such as capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Scenarios, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce the computational and storage footprint of large neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller students. Approaches span matching outputs (soft labels), transferring intermediate representations (feature or layer-wise distillation), adapting teacher selection and weighting, and operating under constraints such as missing original data, privacy, or multi-modal inputs. Practical work on language models, vision-language systems, and other domains highlights gains from task-aware selection of distilled information, architectural adapters between teacher and student, and advanced training schemes (e.g., adversarial sample generation, meta-learning of teachers). Empirical results and surveys show KD is versatile: it improves student accuracy over training from scratch, enables deployment in resource-constrained settings, and can be extended to preserve privacy and support domain adaptation, while theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when and why distillation helps and what challenges remain.

papers_seen.author: Branch
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information beyond hard labels—via softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and ensemble guidance—and is commonly combined with pruning, quantization, architecture search, or data synthesis to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer, student capacity and architecture alignment, data availability or synthesis, and deployment-aware evaluation. Open challenges include preserving robustness and low-frequency behavior, avoiding transferred biases, and principled data-free distillation.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and representational information. A rich taxonomy of techniques has emerged—soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, relational/attention losses, multi-teacher and multi-stage pipelines, and data-synthesis or data-free approaches—which are commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work across vision, language, and other modalities demonstrates that careful distillation pipelines can produce deployable models that retain much of teacher performance, while open problems remain in representation alignment, robustness, long‑tail fidelity, and data- or privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Efficient and Responsible NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, versatile approach for compressing large models and enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. Beyond raw compression, KD supports domain adaptation, data-free scenarios, improved inference speed, and novel training regimes for specialized tasks. However, distillation is not a panacea: it can amplify teacher biases, interact with regularization techniques in subtle ways, and benefits most when combined with complementary methods such as architecture-aware training, generator-based sample synthesis, or instance-aware losses.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses or transfers knowledge from larger or multiple teacher models into smaller or otherwise constrained student models to reduce inference cost while retaining performance. Across computer vision, speech, recommendation, and NLP, KD techniques include matching soft outputs, transferring intermediate features, multi-teacher and staged protocols, and data-free synthesis of surrogate training examples. Practical systems combine KD with pruning or architecture changes, and recent theory helps explain when and why distillation helps. Despite strong empirical gains, challenges remain in handling heterogeneous teachers, data unavailability, task-specific adaptations (e.g., detection, translation), and robustness on low-frequency or out-of-distribution phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for turning large, high-performing deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a core, context-aware component of compression pipelines and combined with complementary tools — pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies — KD enables meaningful reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of the teacher’s predictive performance. Success depends on explicit choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or privacy-sensitive data, and how to measure robustness and long-tail behavior; a principled, deployment-aware distillation pipeline yields the best tradeoffs between efficiency and utility.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce the size, memory, and inference cost of large neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. Across tasks and modalities—classification, detection, generative modeling, retrieval, and NLP—research has developed logits-based, feature-based, and task-adapted distillation strategies, multi-teacher and ensemble approaches, privacy- and communication-conscious protocols for distributed settings, and teacher-optimization/meta-learning variants. These methods trade off fidelity to teacher behavior with student capacity, expose failure modes (e.g., transfer of low-frequency lexical mistakes or overfitting of student features), and introduce remedies such as selective sample distillation, feature projectors, adversarially-informed samples, and staged or multi-teacher curricula. While KD consistently improves compact models compared to training from scratch and enables deployment on resource-constrained platforms, open issues remain in robustness, task-specific alignment, and distillation under data heterogeneity.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Insights
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques enable deployment of large deep models by transferring knowledge to smaller, faster, or lower-precision models. Existing work spans pre-training compact models, teacher-to-student soft-target transfer, data-free and teacher-free approaches, self-distillation, architecture- and task-specific adaptations, and combinations with quantization or pruning. Empirical results show that distilled students can approach teacher performance across classification, ranking, speech, and generation tasks, while specialized strategies address limited task data, privacy constraints, and heterogeneous deployment settings. Open challenges include handling domain shift, designing teacher-student curricula, and developing universally effective objectives for diverse architectures and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context‑Sensitive Engine of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated as a central, flexible component of model‑compression pipelines rather than as a single canned technique. By transferring richer forms of supervision (soft targets, intermediate representations, relational or attention signals) and by being combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture design, KD enables deployment of compact models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Successful distillation requires careful choices about teacher preparation, student capacity, distilled signals, data strategies (including synthetic or data‑free approaches), and explicit checks for robustness, fairness, and rare‑token fidelity. When applied with task‑aware design and safeguards against optimization and bias failure modes, KD provides a practical road for compressing large models for real‑world NLP and deep‑learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, broadly applicable strategy for shrinking large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. KD can reproduce much of a teacher's task performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints; it also integrates naturally with complementary techniques (pretraining, data augmentation, multi-teacher supervision, and progressive module replacement). Realizing KD's full value in production requires attention to optimization gaps, dataset mismatch, and the risk of propagating teacher biases, and benefits from targeted extensions—feature-level objectives, adversarially-informed sample selection, and staged or progressive compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Harvey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible centerpiece for compressing large neural models into deployable students in deep learning and NLP. When combined with representation-level objectives, careful teacher–student alignment, pre-training of compact students, and complementary compression methods, KD delivers strong size/accuracy trade-offs for real deployments. However, its success depends on task- and data-aware engineering: signal selection, data strategies, robustness checks, and mitigation of teacher imperfections are necessary to avoid degraded rare-behavior modeling, bias propagation, and domain-shift failures.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Villegas
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible set of techniques for transferring information from large, high‑capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models so they meet latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD has evolved from matching softened output distributions to a rich toolbox that includes intermediate‑representation and attention alignment, relational and layerwise objectives, curriculum and multi‑teacher schemes, and data strategies that range from full-data augmentation to data‑free synthesis. In practice KD is usually combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and must be designed with attention to teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and evaluation for robustness, long‑tail behavior, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers behavior from large teacher models into smaller students to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher's capability. KD is flexible: it can match logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational signals; it can be combined with augmentation, architecture search, pruning, or task adaptation; and it can operate with or without original training data. When applied with careful choices about what to transfer, how to align representations, and how to address data or optimization mismatches, KD enables practical deployment of compact models across vision, language, and multimodal tasks. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central component of any compression strategy and summarizes concrete practices to maximize its effectiveness and mitigate known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Principles, Methods, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated approach for producing smaller, deployable models by transferring richer supervisory signals from larger teacher models to compact students. KD operates across multiple granularities (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention and relational signals) and is most effective when integrated into a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture design, data strategies, and complementary primitives such as pruning and quantization. Important practical concerns include teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability (including data-free or synthetic approaches), robustness and fairness, and task-aware evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Barker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical and flexible route to compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD spans soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention imitation, layer-wise objectives, and data strategies (including synthetic or data-free approaches). When combined with architecture-aware choices, pruning/quantization, and task- or data-aware training curricula, KD enables strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks. However, its benefits are contingent on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and explicit safeguards for robustness, fairness, and privacy; KD should therefore be treated as a core, composable element of compression pipelines rather than a standalone cure.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practitioner-oriented technique for compressing large models into smaller, faster ones suitable for deployment. Realizing those gains requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to source or synthesize data, how to align heterogeneous teacher–student architectures, and how to evaluate robustness and social harms under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so students retain much of teacher performance while reducing compute, latency, and memory. The literature frames KD as a flexible training paradigm that operates at multiple granularities (soft logits, intermediate features, attention, module-level) and that is most effective when integrated with complementary compression steps (pre-training of compact models, pruning, quantization, architecture design) and task-aware data strategies. Empirical and theoretical work highlights clear strengths and practical limits: KD routinely improves deployability and can improve calibration and robustness when carefully designed, but outcomes depend strongly on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and the specific transfer signals chosen.

KD is applied across modalities and deployment contexts to reduce inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. Practical KD pipelines combine choice of distillation target, teacher and student preparation, data strategies, and complementary compression methods to meet constraints such as latency, memory, privacy, and domain shift. While KD is highly effective in many settings, it has known limits—capacity mismatch, distributional heterogeneity, and transferred biases—that require careful method and evaluation design.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic strategy for compressing large deep and NLP models into compact, deployable students. Rather than a single recipe, KD functions as a toolbox: it can transfer softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational signals; be combined with architecture search, pruning, or quantization; and operate with or without original training data. KD delivers substantial reductions in size and latency with modest performance loss when methods and signals are chosen to match student capacity, task requirements, and deployment constraints. However, KD is context-sensitive: success depends on handling teacher–student mismatch, robustness and fairness concerns, data availability, and optimization choices. The most reliable pipelines therefore combine multiple distillation signals, data-aware strategies, and targeted remedies for limits such as bias transfer and rare-token degradation.

papers_seen.author: Warren
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Mechanisms, Extensions, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, deployment-focused strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students. Its practical value arises from multiple mechanisms — not only teacher imitation but also regularization, representation transfer, and optimization effects — and from combinations with data strategies and complementary compression methods. I argue KD should be treated as the central, engineering-ready backbone of compression pipelines, while practitioners explicitly address data regimes, privacy, domain shift, and bias transfer when designing distillation workflows.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Promise, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-oriented approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When combined with representation-level objectives, teacher selection strategies, data-aware techniques, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), KD yields compact models that recover much of teacher utility while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Real-world success requires attention to student capacity, data mismatch, optimization dynamics, and societal risks such as bias or privacy leakage.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely adopted approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students in vision, language, graph, and multimodal settings. KD transfers information at multiple granularities (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), composes with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and adapts to constrained-data or privacy-sensitive regimes. Empirical and practical work shows KD often yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, but reliable results require careful choices about what to transfer, student preparation and capacity, data sourcing or synthesis, and explicit mitigation of transferred biases and robustness failures.

papers_seen.author: Parrish
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple softened-logit matching into a flexible toolkit that includes intermediate-feature matching, attention and relational objectives, multi-teacher and self-distillation regimes, and data-aware or data-free workflows. In practice KD is typically combined with other compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and requires careful attention to teacher–student capacity, data strategies, and robustness or fairness trade-offs for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Crosby
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models so that students approach teacher performance while using less compute, memory, and energy. Modern KD extends beyond soft-label matching to include intermediate-feature, layer-wise, and structural transfer, and is most effective when integrated with architecture-aware design, pre-training of compact models, and complementary compression methods. Implementation choices—what signals to transfer, how to align layers, which data to use, and how to mitigate bias or domain shift—determine practical success.

papers_seen.author: Pearson
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, flexible set of techniques for reducing the computational and memory cost of large neural models while preserving much of their predictive behavior. The family of methods includes transferring softened teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention patterns, distilling relational structure, applying self-distillation, and using data-aware or data-free sampling and synthesis. In practice KD is most effective when treated as a component of a broader compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, and careful data and training curricula—and when designers attend explicitly to student capacity, teacher–student alignment, data regimes, and deployment constraints such as latency, privacy, and distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Mack
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. The KD toolbox includes logits/soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, layer-wise and task-aware distillation, multi- and self-distillation regimes, and data-aware workflows (including data synthesis or data-free methods). KD is frequently combined with orthogonal compression primitives (pruning, quantization, and architecture search) and benefits from careful teacher–student co-design, staged training curricula, and targeted evaluation of robustness and fairness. Empirical and practical work shows KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling major reductions in size and latency, yet persistent challenges remain around capacity mismatch, distribution shift, low-frequency or rare-token behavior, and the transfer of biases or private information.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Survey of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and flexible approach to compress large models and transfer knowledge across models, modalities, and tasks. Practitioners use KD to produce smaller, faster student models that retain much of a teacher's performance, to regularize training via self-distillation, and to enable multi-task or resource-heterogeneous deployment. Despite strong empirical results across vision, speech, translation, and question answering, distillation exhibits failure modes—e.g., propagation of teacher errors or poor handling of low-frequency phenomena—that motivate variants such as multi-teacher schemes, feature-level objectives, projector layers, and teacher-student co-training. The literature combines empirical recipes and growing theoretical analysis to guide when and how to mix soft teacher signals and hard labels, design teacher architectures, and choose representation vs. logit distillation for best trade-offs between accuracy, efficiency, and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Combinations, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and pragmatic method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably reduces inference cost while often preserving much of a teacher’s performance, but its effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational structure), how teacher–student alignment is addressed, and how distillation is integrated with pre-training, architecture design, and other compression tools. I argue that KD should be treated as the central component of an engineering pipeline for efficient NLP and deep-learning systems: it provides flexible transfer mechanisms, enables many successful combinations (multi-teacher, layer mapping, data synthesis), and yields strong practical results, yet it must be paired with complementary strategies and careful choices to manage teacher imperfections, representation mismatch, data limitations, and robustness trade-offs.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: The Practical Case for Feature- and Representation-Aware Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile strategy for compressing large models into efficient students while retaining much of their accuracy. Beyond the classical logit-matching formulation, modern KD practices that match internal representations, use tailored projectors or selective sample strategies, and account for deployment constraints (e.g., no access to original data or adversarial threats) yield better student models across modalities and tasks. Combining these advances—feature mimicking, projector ensembles, selective distillation, data-free techniques, and robustness-aware training—produces compact models that are both performant and deployable.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. The method spans simple soft-target (logit) matching to richer strategies that align internal representations, use synthetic or unlabeled data, or apply curriculum and online schemes. When combined with architecture-aware design, pruning or quantization, and deployment-aware data strategies, KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance. However, KD’s success depends on choices about the distillation signal, data availability, teacher–student alignment, and handling of optimization or distributional limits; careful method design and evaluation are required to produce robust, fair, and deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression, with Guardrails
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical tool for compressing deep and NLP models because it reliably transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from large teachers into smaller, deployable students. KD excels when combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies, but it is not a panacea: careful design choices are required to handle capacity mismatch, limited data, distribution shift, imperfect teachers, and transferred biases. A disciplined pipeline — choosing appropriate distillation signals, augmenting or synthesizing data when necessary, and aligning teacher–student architectures — yields compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of the teacher’s utility.

papers_seen.author: Harper
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Composable Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated as a context-sensitive, composable component of a broader model-compression pipeline. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, and relational structure) and by combining distillation with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies), practitioners can produce compact student models that approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Success requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity and architecture, how to supply or synthesize data, and explicit checks for robustness, fairness, and rare-token fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques provide practical routes to deploy large, high-performance neural models in resource- constrained or latency-sensitive settings. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, relational structure), how training data is used or synthesized, and whether compression is task-agnostic or task-adaptive. In natural language tasks, KD has enabled dramatic size and speed gains for large pretrained models (e.g., BERT) as well as the feasibility of simple architectures that retain most of the original performance. Despite empirical success, challenges remain: choosing what to transfer for maximal utility, constructing or selecting suitable training examples, handling heterogeneous or private data (federated or data-free settings), and designing teacher-student curricula or architectures that improve transfer. Emerging directions include task-adaptive compression, many-to-many layer alignment, multi-teacher and teacher-aware training, and principled approaches to data selection or generation during distillation.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-ready approach for turning large pretrained models into smaller, faster students that retain much of the teacher’s capability. When combined with representation-aware objectives, student pre-training, and complementary compression techniques, KD delivers substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy use while enabling deployment across language, vision, and multimodal tasks. Real-world success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, managing data (or synthesizing it), and applying safeguards for robustness and privacy, but the accumulated evidence recommends treating distillation as a central, configurable tool in compression pipelines rather than an isolated recipe.

papers_seen.author: Shields
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single trick but as the practical, central component of real-world model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels—soft targets, intermediate features, attention or relational structure—and, when combined with architecture-aware design, quantization/pruning, data strategies, and careful evaluation, yields compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. However, reliable deployment requires acknowledging limits (capacity mismatch, teacher errors, data scarcity, and rare-token or distributional failures) and building workflows that include teacher–student co-design, staged curricula, and targeted robustness and fairness assessment.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broad, practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD spans simple soft-target matching to richer forms of transfer (intermediate-feature and layer-wise matching, attention or relational signals), and is commonly combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and data strategies (public, synthetic, or data-free approaches). Empirical work shows KD routinely narrows the gap between teacher and student performance across modalities, but practical success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to obtain or synthesize training data, and how to mitigate failures such as degraded rare-token behavior, robustness issues, and amplified biases.

papers_seen.author: Day
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Sensitive Engine, Not a Silver Bullet
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and high‑utility approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as the central element of an engineering pipeline and combined with complementary compression primitives, tailored distillation signals, and task‑aware data strategies, KD regularly produces favorable accuracy–efficiency trade‑offs. However, KD alone does not guarantee robust, fair, or distributionally stable students; careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to evaluate long‑tail behaviors are required for reliable deployment.
