papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be adopted as the central, practical strategy for compressing large deep and language models into deployable students. KD’s flexibility—matching softened outputs, aligning representations, and operating with or without original data—lets practitioners trade compute and memory for minimal accuracy loss when combined with complementary compression methods. Careful design around teacher quality, student capacity, and data regimes is necessary to avoid transferring biases or degrading robustness.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. The method spans simple soft-target (logit) matching to richer strategies that align internal representations, use synthetic or unlabeled data, or apply curriculum and online schemes. When combined with architecture-aware design, pruning or quantization, and deployment-aware data strategies, KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance. However, KD’s success depends on choices about the distillation signal, data availability, teacher–student alignment, and handling of optimization or distributional limits; careful method design and evaluation are required to produce robust, fair, and deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Carrillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Research and practice show a spectrum of distillation signals and workflows that make KD a flexible foundation of modern compression pipelines, but its success depends on task-aware signal selection, student design, and complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Leonard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Compressing Deep and NLP Models: Strengths, Limits, and How to Apply It
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—combining logits and representation matching, adapting teacher and student designs, and addressing data- or privacy-constrained settings—KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a cure-all: optimization difficulties, teacher imperfections, data mismatch, and distributional limits require targeted strategies (e.g., feature-aware losses, data-free synthesis, online or multi-teacher schemes) to make distillation robust and production-ready.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible technique for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones for deep learning and NLP. When applied as part of an integrated compression pipeline it reduces inference cost and memory while retaining much of teacher performance. Achieving robust, fair, and private deployments requires combining KD with architecture-aware design, appropriate data strategies (including data-free alternatives), careful choice of distilled signals, and systematic evaluation of robustness and bias.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Recent Findings
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information from teacher models. Across vision, language, and cross-modal tasks, KD is used both as a stand-alone compression method and in combination with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practical strategies include logit (soft-label) matching, feature-level imitation, multi-teacher schemes, and data- or label-synthesis when original training data are unavailable. Empirical work shows that distillation can recover most of a teacher's performance while enabling much smaller and faster models, but outcomes depend strongly on choices such as teacher quality, the form of distilled signals, augmentation and synthetic-data generation, and whether low-precision or domain-specific constraints apply.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically grounded approach for producing compact models that retain much of the predictive power of larger teachers. When treated as the central component of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary techniques (pre‑training, pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful data strategies, KD routinely yields favorable size–performance tradeoffs in vision and language applications. However, KD is design‑sensitive: realizing its benefits in production requires matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling data scarcity or privacy constraints, and explicitly mitigating failures such as degraded rare‑token behavior, distributional shift, and bias amplification.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for transferring knowledge from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the original performance. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD has been instantiated as soft-label matching, intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher ensembles, and data-free or privacy-aware variants. Combining distillation with orthogonal compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and adapting teacher–student interactions to the data and task constraints yields the best real-world trade-offs. Remaining challenges include optimizing teacher–student mismatch, handling data or privacy limitations, and ensuring robustness and fairness in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: This synthesis summarizes contemporary methods, practical patterns, and deployment considerations for knowledge distillation (KD) as a route to compressing deep learning and NLP models. It covers common distillation signals, data strategies (including data-free and synthetic approaches), online and self-distillation variants, teacher–student co-design, and how KD combines with complementary compression methods. The summary highlights recurring practical trade-offs—student capacity, choice of transfer targets, data availability, and robustness/fairness risks—and concludes with pragmatic guidelines for applying KD in production settings.

papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or training dynamics. A broad toolkit—ranging from softened-logit matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, self- and online-distillation, multi-teacher pipelines, and data‑free procedures—is used in practice, typically together with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. Practical success depends on aligning distilled signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data or synthetic-data strategies, and evaluating robustness, long‑tail fidelity, and privacy or fairness impacts. The field continues to address theoretical gaps and deployment challenges such as distribution shift, optimization mismatch, and limited or private data regimes.

papers_seen.author: Cervantes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact, deployable deep and NLP models that retain much of large-teacher performance. KD supports multiple transfer signals and workflows, composes effectively with orthogonal compression tools, and is adaptable to privacy- and deployment-sensitive contexts. Its real-world success depends on matching distilled signals and curricula to student capacity, combining KD with pruning/quantization or architecture design when appropriate, and explicitly addressing risks such as propagated biases, optimization mismatches, and long-tail or out-of-distribution behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible approach for producing compact neural models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Across vision and language applications KD has been extended from simple soft-label matching to a wide set of techniques—intermediate-representation transfer, layer-aware alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation, data-free variants, and adversarial or projector-based feature matching—that enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD both preserves predictive performance and can improve generalization in many settings, while also raising practical challenges such as teacher–student mismatch and degraded modeling of low-frequency phenomena that require targeted mitigations.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Task‑Aware Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically grounded approach for transferring predictive behavior and representational structure from large teacher models into smaller student models so they meet real-world constraints (latency, memory, energy, or privacy). KD extends beyond softened logits to include feature- and attention-level matching, multi-teacher and self-distillation schemes, and data strategies (including few-shot and synthetic-data regimes). When KD is treated as the central element of a compression pipeline and combined with architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, and careful data and curriculum choices, it routinely yields favorable size–accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. At the same time, KD is not a drop-in remedy: capacity mismatch, distribution shift, rare- or low-frequency behavior, and the propagation of teacher errors are real constraints that require explicit mitigation. The following argues for positioning KD as the core practical strategy for compression while outlining concrete caveats and best-practice recommendations for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Compressing NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-ready approach that enables compact models to inherit much of the performance of large teachers while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When applied thoughtfully—using representation-level targets, projector layers, multi-teacher or curriculum schedules, and data-aware workflows—KD consistently outperforms training small models from scratch for many NLP tasks. However, KD is not a panacea: mismatches in capacity, teacher imperfections, data heterogeneity, and distributional shifts require targeted remedies and careful evaluation. This essay argues that KD should be treated as the practical core of model compression in deep learning and NLP, paired with specific design choices to mitigate its limits.

papers_seen.author: Perkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the behavior of larger teachers. KD encompasses a range of targets (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational signals), training regimes (offline teacher-student, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher), and data strategies (use of original data, synthetic or data-free methods, privacy-aware workflows). In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when design choices—what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data constraints—are matched to the deployment context. Promising empirical results across vision, language, generative models, and novel-view synthesis coexist with persistent challenges in robustness, low-frequency behavior, transferred biases, and theoretical understanding, motivating careful pipeline design and continued research.

papers_seen.author: Terry
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted, engineering-centered approach for producing smaller, deployable models by transferring information from larger teacher models. Over the last decade KD has expanded from soft-label matching to a rich toolkit that includes intermediate-representation alignment, attention- and relation-level transfers, multi-stage and self-distillation schedules, and data-aware or data-free workflows. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when practitioner choices align teacher signals, student capacity, and available data. Common failure modes—capacity mismatch, distributional shift, degraded behavior on rare or long-tail phenomena, and transfer of teacher biases—motivate careful design, diagnostics, and hybrid pipelines for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hayes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applicable method for compressing large teacher models into smaller student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. As a toolkit rather than a single algorithm, KD combines multiple signal types, training schedules, and data strategies and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods and deployment-aware engineering. While KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, it has predictable failure modes that require careful pipeline design and targeted mitigation.

papers_seen.author: Castaneda
papers_seen.title: Make Knowledge Distillation the Default Compression Strategy for Deep Learning and NLP (with Practical Safeguards)
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, central technique for compressing large deep and NLP models into deployable students because it consistently delivers strong size–performance trade-offs while remaining flexible across tasks and deployment constraints. However, KD is not a single recipe: best results come from combining soft-targets with representation-level supervision, sensible student pre-training, data-aware curricula or synthesis, and complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization). Practitioners must also mitigate risks—transfer of teacher biases, optimization and capacity mismatches, and degradation on rare or out-of-distribution phenomena—through multi-teacher designs, careful signal selection, and validation under deployment scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation transfers information from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost and memory while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. Modern distillation expands beyond matching teacher logits to include intermediate representation matching, self-supervised and contrastive objectives, data-free and synthetic-data schemes, curriculum and augmentation strategies, and privacy- and deployment-aware protocols. These variants enable application across vision, speech, graph-structured data, and NLP, but practical deployment requires care about data availability, optimization dynamics, robustness, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Sensitive Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical component of model‑compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP: a versatile toolkit that transfers richer supervision from large teachers into smaller, deployable students. When KD is designed as a context‑sensitive engineering process — matching distillation targets to student capacity, combining with complementary compression methods, and tailoring data and evaluation strategies to deployment constraints — it routinely yields strong size–performance trade‑offs. However, realizing KD’s benefits in practice requires explicit attention to limits such as capacity mismatch, degraded long‑tail behavior, transferred biases, and data/privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Design Principles
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely applicable approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of teacher performance. KD achieves favorable accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across modalities when practitioners choose what form of teacher knowledge to transfer, how to map layers and representations, and how to handle limited or private data. However, KD is not plug-and-play: outcomes depend heavily on teacher quality, distilled signals, data availability, and task-specific constraints. Thoughtful combination of feature-level objectives, task-aware layer selection, data-synthesis or privacy-preserving queries, and targeted curricula yields robust compressed models ready for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Burke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression — Essential but Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile paradigm for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When designed to match deployment constraints—by selecting suitable distillation signals, aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining KD with data strategies and complementary compression techniques—KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while reducing latency and memory. However, its success is not automatic: capacity mismatch, data scarcity, domain shift, and fine-grained or rare-behavior preservation require targeted design choices and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller students to reduce computation, memory, and latency while retaining predictive performance. Methods vary from matching soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations, using teacher ensembles or meta-learned teachers, and operating under constraints such as missing data, privacy, or heterogeneous devices. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD improves student generalization relative to training from scratch in many settings but interacts with optimization, data availability, and teacher imperfection; practical deployments benefit from task-aware choices of distillation targets, architectural adapters, and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical toolkit for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD provides flexible mechanisms for preserving teacher performance while reducing inference cost, memory, and latency, and it can be combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies to meet deployment and privacy constraints. However, realizing KD’s benefits in production requires careful choices about signals to transfer, data selection or synthesis, and evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Rosales
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical suite of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates by transferring richer supervision than hard labels—such as softened outputs, intermediate representations, or relational signals—and is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation). While KD routinely yields strong reductions in inference cost and memory with modest performance loss, its success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity and deployment constraints and on mitigating failure modes such as bias transfer, degradation on rare events, and sensitivity to distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated method for producing compact models that preserve much of the performance and useful behavior of larger teacher models. KD works by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone and is most effective when integrated with complementary techniques (architecture-aware compression, pruning, quantization) and careful data and evaluation practices. However, KD is context-sensitive: its success depends on teacher quality, what signals are distilled, student capacity, data availability or synthesis, and explicit checks for robustness and fairness. Practical adoption therefore requires principled pipeline choices, staged training, and targeted mitigation of known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic approach for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models so that compact systems meet deployment constraints (compute, memory, latency, privacy) while retaining much of teacher performance. KD encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning internal representations or attention, and using multi-stage or data-aware pipelines. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware pretraining) and careful data strategies, KD routinely yields favorable size/accuracy/latency trade-offs. However, realizing those gains in practice requires attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, robustness, and the risk of transferring teacher shortcomings; thus KD is best treated as the central tool inside a broader, task-aware compression pipeline rather than a standalone cure-all.

papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-ready approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. KD techniques span teacher design, student-teacher layer mapping, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, data-aware and data-free workflows, and scalable/online training protocols. When combined with task-aware selection and domain adaptation, distillation enables effective deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and heterogeneous-device constraints.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and a Design Recipe
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student design, handling data constraints, and combining KD with complementary compression methods—distillation routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. KD has clear failure modes (propagating teacher errors, difficulty with low-frequency behaviors, distribution shift, and robustness/privacy concerns) that require principled pipelines, diagnostics, and mitigation strategies. I argue KD should be treated as the central component of compression pipelines but only effective when integrated with representation-aware objectives, data-aware strategies, and robustness/privacy-aware techniques.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, practically essential approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD enables reduced storage and faster inference while preserving much of teacher performance when paired with appropriate distilled signals, data strategies, and complementary compression techniques. However, distillation is not a panacea: it can propagate teacher biases, struggle when training data are unavailable or misaligned with deployment distributions, and interact subtly with optimization and architecture mismatch. A pragmatic pipeline treats KD as the central tool but couples it with targeted strategies—feature- and layer-level objectives, data-free or synthesized-data protocols when needed, curriculum or sample-weighting policies, and hardware-aware pruning or architecture search—to maximize efficiency without sacrificing robustness or task-specific fidelity.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Over the past decade this has grown from simple logit-matching into a toolkit that includes internal representation alignment, layer-mapping strategies, data and privacy-aware procedures, adversarial and robustness-aware objectives, online and distributed schemes, and methods tailored for specific architectures such as pre-trained language models. Distillation often recovers much of a teacher’s performance when deliberately designed (choice of signals, data, and architecture), but it faces limits from optimization difficulties, capacity mismatch, distributional shift, and the risk of transferring undesirable teacher behaviors such as bias. Practical success therefore depends on combining multiple transfer signals, handling data constraints, and adapting both teacher and student to the deployment context.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: What We Know
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical suite of techniques that transfers information from large teacher models to smaller students to enable efficient deployment. In practice KD spans matching teacher outputs (soft logits), aligning intermediate representations, specialized layer- and channel-level transfers, and workflows that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or synthetic-data strategies. KD delivers substantial reductions in compute, memory, and latency while often improving student generalization, but its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to handle data or domain shifts. Open issues include robustness under distributional heterogeneity, preserving rare-token or fine-grained behavior in sequence models, and distillation without original training data.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large teacher models into smaller student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Across vision, language, multimodal, graph, and recommender settings, KD has evolved from soft-target (logit) matching to a broader toolbox that includes intermediate-feature alignment, attention and relational transfers, online and multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free workflows. When KD is treated as the central element of an engineering-aware compression pipeline and combined with complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, privacy-aware approaches), it routinely yields strong size–performance trade-offs. Practical success requires matching distilled signals to student capacity, addressing distribution shift and long-tail behaviors, and guarding against transferring teacher weaknesses; these remain active areas for research and careful production practice.

papers_seen.author: Tucker

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, versatile approach for compressing large models and enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. Beyond raw compression, KD supports domain adaptation, data-free scenarios, improved inference speed, and novel training regimes for specialized tasks. However, distillation is not a panacea: it can amplify teacher biases, interact with regularization techniques in subtle ways, and benefits most when combined with complementary methods such as architecture-aware training, generator-based sample synthesis, or instance-aware losses.

papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. It is a broadly applicable and practical approach across modalities (vision, language, graphs, multimodal) that enables reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of the original performance. Modern practice treats distillation as a toolkit—combining soft-label/logit transfer, intermediate representation matching, specialized architectures or projectors, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware protocols—to fit deployment constraints. Despite empirical effectiveness, distillation faces persistent challenges including data availability and privacy, teacher–student mismatches, optimization instability, and preservation of rare-token or low-frequency behavior; practical pipelines must therefore be tailored to task, data, and hardware requirements.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate-representation matching, layerwise alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation, curriculum and augmentation strategies, and privacy- or data-free procedures. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and task-aware choices about what and how to transfer, KD enables practical deployment of high-performing models across modalities while raising open issues in robustness, fairness, and distributional generalization.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable ones. When engineered as part of a broader compression pipeline—selecting which teacher signals to transfer, aligning student architectures, and combining distillation with pruning, quantization, or low-precision training—distillation enables large reductions in latency, memory, and energy while preserving much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness depends on careful choices about distilled signals, data regimes, and mitigation of teacher or distributional failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applied approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. Research over the last decade has expanded KD beyond simple logits matching into intermediate-representation transfer, multi-teacher and progressive curricula, data-aware and data-free workflows, and combinations with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design). KD functions both as a compression mechanism and as a training paradigm that can improve calibration and generalization, but it has known failure modes—teacher imperfection, capacity mismatch, optimization difficulty, domain shift, and degradation on rare or low-frequency phenomena—that require targeted diagnostics and hybrid pipelines. Practical deployment of KD therefore depends on matching distilled signals and protocols to student capacity, data availability, task constraints, and hardware targets.

papers_seen.author: Thomas
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a primary approach for turning large, high‑capacity deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. Practical KD pipelines combine multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), data strategies (augmented, synthesized, or data‑free), and complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, preparing students via pretraining or layer mapping, and explicitly addressing distribution shift, rare‑token behavior, and the risk of transferring undesirable teacher properties. While KD routinely preserves substantial teacher utility, its limits motivate richer targets, multi‑teacher or online schemes, adversarial feature alignment, and careful evaluation of robustness and fairness in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses larger teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Approaches include matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, mapping or projecting teacher layers to student layers, and operating in offline, online, federated, or data-free regimes. Distillation is commonly combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware data strategies. Practical success depends on choosing which signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student capacity, managing data or privacy constraints, and designing curricula or multi-stage pipelines that reflect deployment needs. While distillation routinely produces compact models that retain much of teacher performance, open challenges remain in representation mismatch, amplifying teacher biases, and ensuring robustness and fairness under compression.

papers_seen.author: Baird
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly used, practical strategy for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Research over the last decade has extended KD from simple softened-logit matching into a flexible toolkit that transfers soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention and relational structure, and curriculum or ensemble signals. In practice KD is typically combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design, and data strategies) and used with task-aware choices about distilled signals and training data. KD routinely improves compact models over training from scratch, but its effectiveness depends on student capacity, data availability or synthesis, teacher–student alignment, and explicit handling of robustness and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, broadly applied set of techniques for transferring knowledge from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster students so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Across vision and language modalities KD reduces inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance when matched to student capacity; its success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or shifted data. Practical deployment benefits from combining distillation with complementary compression methods and careful training protocols to mitigate failure modes such as loss of rare-token behavior or mismatched architectures.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transform large, high-performing models into smaller or more usable forms while attempting to retain performance. Methods range from transferring soft targets to matching intermediate representations, to data-free and federated protocols that address privacy and communication constraints. These approaches have been applied across computer vision, speech, and natural language tasks and are used both for deployment efficiency and for secondary goals such as interpretability or domain generalization.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Mckinney
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely adopted approach for turning large, high‑performing models into compact students that can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD is flexible in what it transfers (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational signals) and in how it is applied (offline teacher–student training, online/self-distillation, multi‑teacher ensembles, and data‑free procedures). Practical success depends on matching the distillation signals to student capacity, combining KD with complementary compression techniques, and engineering data and optimization workflows that mitigate distribution shift, bias transfer, and long‑tail degradation.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation: Versatile Compression for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and powerful approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, more efficient ones. Beyond simple size reduction, KD enables transfer of capabilities across modalities, supports domain adaptation, improves deployment in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings, and can be adapted to distributed training. However, benefits are not automatic: careful design of teacher-student alignment, training data, and distillation objectives is required to preserve task performance and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Schmidt
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production‑oriented approach to compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as the central element of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, multi‑teacher supervision), KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of a teacher’s utility. Realizing those gains in practice requires matching distillation signals to student capacity, selecting appropriate data or synthesis strategies, and auditing for robustness, distributional shift, and transferred biases. I argue KD should be the default component of any compression toolkit, but only when applied in a context‑sensitive, engineering‑aware way.
