papers_seen.author: Gutierrez
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large ‘‘teacher’’ models to smaller ‘‘student’’ models so students are deployable under constraints of latency, memory, energy, or privacy. KD goes beyond matching hard labels: it uses softened outputs, intermediate-feature matching, relational or attention maps, and curricula or synthetic data to shape student learning. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and when practitioner choices (distillation signal, teacher selection, data strategy, and evaluation on robustness and long-tail behavior) are matched to the deployment context. Open problems remain around data-limited or privacy-sensitive settings, heterogenous teacher–student architectures, preservation of rare-token / low-frequency behaviors, and principled guarantees about robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Washington
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across NLP and other modalities, KD is routinely combined with architecture-aware design and other compression methods to achieve favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. Effective deployment requires choices about distilled signals, data regimes, teacher–student alignment, and mitigation of transferred harms such as bias and privacy leakage.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature and flexible approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable ones. When combined with careful choices—such as pre-training compact students, data-free distillation for privacy, adaptive multi-teacher strategies, feature-level imitation, and teacher-side learning—KD can deliver strong task performance with much smaller inference cost. However, KD is not a panacea: optimization gaps between teacher and student, propagation of teacher biases, and dataset mismatches can limit gains unless explicitly addressed. A pragmatic KD pipeline therefore integrates algorithmic innovations and fairness/optimization checks to realize both efficiency and reliable behavior in production NLP and deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Toolbox Approach
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical strategy for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables preservation of much of a teacher's capabilities while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Realizing that potential requires combining multiple transfer signals, designing student-aware architectures and curricula, and accounting for data- and deployment-specific constraints; it also requires awareness of limits such as capacity mismatch, distributional shift, and the risk of transferring undesirable teacher behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Design-Sensitive Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost and enable deployment. KD has been instantiated as matching soft targets, aligning intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, and selective or multi-teacher schemes. While KD often yields strong empirical gains and enables domain- and task-specific compression, its success depends on optimization dynamics, the choice of distilled signal, data quality and selection, and teacher–student alignment. Careful method choices make KD a reliable, production-ready compression strategy, but it is not a universal shortcut: practitioners must tailor KD objectives and protocols to their constraints and goals.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Practical Core for Model Compression — A Qualified Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default, practical core of model-compression pipelines in deep learning and NLP because it reliably transfers richer supervision from large teachers into smaller students and composes with complementary compression primitives. However, KD is design-sensitive: its practical success depends on student capacity, data strategies (including synthesis or privacy-aware protocols), teacher–student alignment, and explicit mitigation of failure modes such as bias, rare-token degradation, and distribution shift. A production-ready approach embeds KD in an engineering-aware pipeline that pairs appropriate distillation signals with architecture-aware design, data curricula, and robustness/fairness evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Reframing Knowledge Distillation: Beyond Compression to Regularization, Robustness, and Generalization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is often presented primarily as a model compression technique. Emerging work shows KD is also a flexible training paradigm that provides regularization, transfers internal representations, improves robustness to adversaries and domain shifts, and can be applied without a stronger teacher. This essay argues KD should be treated as a general-purpose tool for shaping student learning — one that can and should be combined with teacher-free methods, internal-representation alignment, multi-teacher aggregation, careful data augmentation, and principled mixing of hard and soft targets to maximize performance in NLP and broader deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be adopted as the central, practical strategy for compressing large deep and language models into deployable students. KD’s flexibility—matching softened outputs, aligning representations, and operating with or without original data—lets practitioners trade compute and memory for minimal accuracy loss when combined with complementary compression methods. Careful design around teacher quality, student capacity, and data regimes is necessary to avoid transferring biases or degrading robustness.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller student models to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Across vision, speech, and language tasks KD spans soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, self- and multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free workflows. Best practice treats KD as a central element of a broader compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design—and adapts targets, data, and curricula to task and deployment constraints. Key open issues include representation alignment across architectures, propagated teacher biases, robustness under domain shift, and preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the practical core of model compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. KD is a flexible toolkit—covering soft-targets, feature- and attention-level objectives, self- and multi-teacher schedules, and data-free variants—that reliably improves size/efficiency trade-offs when combined with careful student design and complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation). Real-world deployment requires deliberate engineering to align teacher and student capacity, choose appropriate distilled signals and data strategies, and diagnose and mitigate predictable failure modes (distribution shift, rare-token behavior, privacy and fairness risks).

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP — Promise, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. When paired with representation-level objectives, data strategies (including synthetic or privacy-preserving generation), and architecture-aware design, KD routinely yields models that meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. Success is engineering-dependent: the distillation signal, student capacity and pre-training, data availability, and explicit mitigation for harms such as bias or distributional fragility determine whether compressed models meet real-world needs.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Issues
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, speech, and NLP. Approaches vary from traditional teacher-to-student soft-label transfer to data-free (zero-shot) distillation, online and mutual distillation among peers, meta-learned teachers, and internal-representation matching. Empirical work shows KD can improve student generalization, speed, and footprint but also introduces dataset-specific artifacts (e.g., degraded modeling of low-frequency tokens) and optimization mismatches that require complementary strategies such as exposing raw data, augmentations, adaptive teacher selection, or distillation of intermediate representations. Practical systems (federated or large-scale distributed training) benefit from variants like online or zero-shot distillation to respect privacy and device heterogeneity, while research continues to study why KD works and how to align teacher and student beyond output probabilities.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for transferring knowledge from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the original performance. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD has been instantiated as soft-label matching, intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher ensembles, and data-free or privacy-aware variants. Combining distillation with orthogonal compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and adapting teacher–student interactions to the data and task constraints yields the best real-world trade-offs. Remaining challenges include optimizing teacher–student mismatch, handling data or privacy limitations, and ensuring robustness and fairness in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Morris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. The practice has evolved from simple soft-target matching into a multifaceted toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi- and self-teaching, online schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols. Real-world success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data strategies, and combining KD with complementary compression methods and task-aware engineering to mitigate robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift challenges.

papers_seen.author: Hughes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of large teachers. KD works across modalities by transferring soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention, and relational signals, and it is most effective when integrated with architecture-aware compression, pre-training of compact architectures, data strategies, and explicit robustness and fairness checks. A production-ready compression pipeline treats KD as a core component — not a standalone cure — and emphasizes signal selection, layer alignment, and safeguards for distributional or ethical failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Across vision and language tasks, KD has evolved from simple softened-logit matching to include intermediate-representation mimicry, relational or attention-based transfers, multi-teacher and online variants, and data-aware strategies (including synthetic or privacy-preserving data). In practice KD is most effective when integrated into a broader compression pipeline (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and when the distillation recipe is matched to task, data, and deployment constraints. Important open problems include handling teacher–student capacity mismatch, preserving rare/long-tail behavior, ensuring robustness under domain shift, avoiding transfer of harmful biases, and scaling distillation to new modalities and extremely large models.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Contemporary Approaches and Applications of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques transfer information from larger, more costly models to smaller, deployable models. Modern work expands beyond simple soft-label matching to include distillation of internal representations, feature-level imitation, privacy-preserving and data-free strategies, task-adaptive compression, and adaptations to specialized architectures (e.g., GANs, detectors, and transformers). These methods aim to preserve accuracy, robustness, and efficiency (compute, memory, or communication) while enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices or in privacy-sensitive and distributed settings.

papers_seen.author: Phillips
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a toolbox and combined with careful student preparation, selective signal design, and complementary compression methods, KD routinely yields models that approach teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a plug-and-play cure: its success depends on task- and deployment-specific choices, and it requires safeguards for robustness, fairness, and fidelity on rare or out-of-distribution phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Principled Path to Efficient, Adaptable, and Responsible NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is not merely a compression trick but a general framework that enables smaller or specialized models to inherit useful behaviors from larger teachers while controlling generalization, efficiency, and social impact. When combined with layer-wise and representation-level matching, task-aware architecture search, thoughtful input augmentation, and deployment-aware protocols, KD supports high-performance, resource-frugal NLP systems that can be adapted to heterogeneous devices and sensitive application contexts.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Scenarios, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce the computational and storage footprint of large neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller students. Approaches span matching outputs (soft labels), transferring intermediate representations (feature or layer-wise distillation), adapting teacher selection and weighting, and operating under constraints such as missing original data, privacy, or multi-modal inputs. Practical work on language models, vision-language systems, and other domains highlights gains from task-aware selection of distilled information, architectural adapters between teacher and student, and advanced training schemes (e.g., adversarial sample generation, meta-learning of teachers). Empirical results and surveys show KD is versatile: it improves student accuracy over training from scratch, enables deployment in resource-constrained settings, and can be extended to preserve privacy and support domain adaptation, while theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when and why distillation helps and what challenges remain.

papers_seen.author: Brewer
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful, engineering-centered paradigm for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. Research and practice show KD can transfer richer supervisory signals than hard labels, be combined with pruning/quantization/architecture search, and be adapted to settings with limited or private data. While KD routinely recovers a large fraction of teacher performance across vision, language, graph, and generative tasks, its success depends on choices about what to transfer, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and careful handling of robustness, fairness, and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Berry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical, flexible pathway to turn large, high‑capacity models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a central, composable element of compression pipelines and combined with complementary techniques and careful data and architecture choices, KD can deliver substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. At the same time, KD has well‑documented limits — capacity mismatch, distributional shift, degradation on rare outputs, and potential transfer of teacher biases — that require task‑aware design, diagnostics, and mitigation strategies. I argue KD should be the default compression tool in production pipelines, used deliberately and in combination with other primitives, rather than as a single turnkey fix.

papers_seen.author: Haney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Mechanisms, Methods, and Integration
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, deployment-oriented approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, faster students. KD works through multiple mechanisms—from soft-target regularization to representation transfer—and a variety of techniques such as logit matching, feature alignment, and projector-enabled feature distillation. Treated as the central element of a compression pipeline and combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization), KD produces practical size–performance trade-offs. Real-world success requires context-sensitive choices about what to transfer, how to map layers, and how to mitigate distributionshift, bias, and optimization mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Bailey
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely used paradigm for transferring behavior from large “teacher” models into smaller “student” models to reduce inference cost while preserving much of predictive performance. The literature shows a spectrum of distillation targets (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, relational structure), data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or no-data approaches), and workflows (offline, online, multi-teacher, federated). Empirical and conceptual work emphasizes the importance of teacher–student capacity alignment, choice of distillation signal, and combination with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation). Despite frequent success across vision, language, speech, and graphs, open challenges include optimization barriers that prevent perfect imitation, preserving rare or long-tail behaviors, robustness under distribution shift, privacy-sensitive deployments, and adapting distillation to heterogeneous device or federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance. KD operates at multiple granularities (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), composes well with pruning, quantization and architecture search, and applies across modalities. Its effectiveness is context-sensitive: design choices about what to transfer, student capacity, data availability, and teacher–student alignment determine outcomes. Remaining challenges include preserving low-frequency behavior and robustness under distribution shift, motivating task-aware pipelines and continued work on internal-representation and data-aware distillation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from larger teacher models into smaller student models so students retain much of teacher performance while reducing compute, latency, and memory. The literature characterizes KD by what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, layer mappings), how teachers and students are aligned (architecture-aware mappings, progressive curricula, multi- or online-teachers), and which complementary steps are used (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis). KD functions both as a compression mechanism and a training paradigm that can improve regularization, calibration, and robustness when carefully designed, but it faces limits from data availability, teacher–student mismatch, optimization dynamics, and transfer of undesirable teacher behaviors. Practical deployments therefore treat KD as a component of a broader compression pipeline tailored to task, data, and hardware constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-ready approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. KD supports multiple transfer signals (logits, features, attention or relational structure), composes with other compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and can be adapted to domain- or data-constrained settings. Its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; therefore KD should be treated as a toolbox of methods and workflows rather than a single recipe.

papers_seen.author: Whitaker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Concise Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible technique for producing smaller, faster models by transferring predictive behavior and internal information from larger teacher models to compact students. A spectrum of distillation targets — from softened logits to intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational or decision-boundary signals — combined with architecture-aware design, pre-training, pruning, quantization, and careful data strategies, enables favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across vision and language tasks. KD is not a turnkey solution: its effectiveness depends on teacher quality, student capacity, choice of distilled signals, and data regime, and it can propagate teacher errors or biases and struggle with rare-token and distribution-shift scenarios. Deployment-ready KD pipelines therefore center on principled target selection, representation-aware objectives, data-aware curricula or synthesis, and validation under realistic constraints.

papers_seen.author: Francis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most pragmatic and widely applicable strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in deep learning and NLP. KD transfers richer supervision than hard labels and can operate at multiple levels (logits, features, attention, relational structure). When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and matched to student capacity and data regimes, KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, KD is not a panacea: careful design is required to mitigate capacity mismatch, distribution shift, rare-token fidelity, and privacy or data-scarce constraints.

papers_seen.author: Curtis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central, pragmatic approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, speech, and graph modalities. KD transfers richer supervision than hard labels—soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational signals—and is routinely combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, or public surrogates). Practical use of KD requires careful teacher–student co-design, attention to data regimes and augmentation, and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, long-tail behavior, and domain shift. When applied as part of a disciplined compression pipeline, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of the teacher’s effectiveness, though several implementation and theoretical challenges remain.

papers_seen.author: Lyons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. I argue KD should occupy a central place in compression pipelines because it reliably improves size–performance tradeoffs, but it must be adapted to task- and deployment-specific constraints (data regime, privacy, robustness, and fairness) and combined with complementary techniques to deliver robust, real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Bautista
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical, Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile strategy for converting large, high‑capacity models into smaller, deployable students that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. When engineered as the central element of a compression pipeline — combined with architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, and data strategies — KD routinely yields favorable size/accuracy trade‑offs. However, its effectiveness is context‑sensitive and requires deliberate choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to detect and mitigate harms such as degraded rare‑case performance or transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Cardenas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable and production-ready approach to compressing large models into smaller, faster models while retaining much of their performance. KD supports multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals) and can be adapted to domain, data, and deployment constraints. When combined with complementary compression techniques and matched to student capacity and data availability, KD yields strong trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and resource usage; however, it requires careful engineering to avoid pitfalls such as representation mismatch, teacher error propagation, and data- or distribution-specific failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller students to reduce computation, memory, and latency while retaining predictive performance. Methods vary from matching soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations, using teacher ensembles or meta-learned teachers, and operating under constraints such as missing data, privacy, or heterogeneous devices. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD improves student generalization relative to training from scratch in many settings but interacts with optimization, data availability, and teacher imperfection; practical deployments benefit from task-aware choices of distillation targets, architectural adapters, and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Galvan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Design-Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for producing compact, deployable models from larger teachers. When implemented thoughtfully—choosing what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, and which data and augmentation strategies to use—KD can recover much of a teacher’s performance while substantially reducing inference cost and memory. However, distillation also has limits: it can propagate teacher biases, struggle with low-data or low-capacity students, and requires complementary techniques (e.g., layer mapping, pruning, or synthetic-data schemes) and careful evaluation to meet real-world deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile technique for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable ones. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, or relational signals—KD reduces inference cost while preserving much of teacher behavior. KD is not a single recipe but a flexible toolbox: its success depends on teacher design, the choice of distilled signal, data availability, and combination with complementary compression methods. When matched to task and deployment constraints, KD enables real-world use of pretrained models across vision, language, speech, graphs, and structured prediction, while open challenges remain around distribution shift, rare-token fidelity, and privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Unifying Paradigm for Compression, Adaptation, and Robust Training
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be considered not merely as a compression trick but as a general and practical training paradigm. Across modalities and tasks, KD transfers information about function, structure, and uncertainty from one model (or ensemble) to another, enabling smaller, faster, or more adaptable models while improving generalization, interpretability, and domain transfer. Success depends on how teacher knowledge is selected, represented, and combined with data-side techniques; thoughtful design choices (layer mapping, sample selection, augmentation, and teacher trust) determine whether KD yields compression, robustness, or better task-specific performance.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods enable transferring predictive behavior and internal representations from large, high-capacity teachers to smaller students so models can be deployed under computation, memory, latency, or privacy constraints. The literature shows a spectrum of approaches — from matching softened output distributions to feature- and layer-level imitation, attention-guided alignment, data-free or zero-shot synthesis of training examples, and distributed or privacy-aware protocols — and demonstrates successful applications across vision, speech, recommendation, and many NLP tasks. Practical effectiveness depends on choices of distillation signal, data availability and synthesis, teacher–student architecture alignment, and training curricula; open challenges include handling imperfect teachers, preserving rare or long-tail behaviors, and maintaining robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central practical tool for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably delivers strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs when its objectives, data, and architectural choices are matched to the student’s capacity and deployment constraints. However, KD is not a plug-and-play remedy: robust, fair, and private compression requires pre-training, careful signal selection, alignment strategies, and combination with complementary methods such as pruning and quantization.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Reframing Knowledge Distillation: Beyond Strong Teachers to Regularization, Representations, and Practical Variants
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful tool for compressing deep models, but its benefits arise from multiple mechanisms beyond mere imitation of a stronger teacher. Empirical and theoretical work indicates that distillation combines regularization effects of soft targets, representational alignment, and optimization dynamics; these insights motivate a broader set of practical strategies (teacher-free or data-free distillation, feature-based objectives, contrastive and adversarial losses, ensembles, and co-training of teacher/student) to obtain compact models that generalize well. This paper argues that practitioners should select KD variants depending on data availability, deployment constraints, and the nature of the task, and that future research should prioritize understanding optimization and representation transfer rather than treating teacher capacity as the sole determinant of success.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Composable Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the composable core of real-world model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP: it provides flexible, information-rich supervision that can be adapted to student capacity and deployment constraints, and when combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives it yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. However, effective and responsible deployment requires explicit co-design to handle capacity mismatch, data- and privacy-limited regimes, and robustness or fairness failures.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical toolkit for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD provides flexible mechanisms for preserving teacher performance while reducing inference cost, memory, and latency, and it can be combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies to meet deployment and privacy constraints. However, realizing KD’s benefits in production requires careful choices about signals to transfer, data selection or synthesis, and evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Simmons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Core of Model Compression — Practical Promise and Necessary Guardrails
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default backbone for practical model compression in deep learning and NLP because it provides a flexible, task‑aware way to transfer a large teacher’s behavior into a smaller, deployable student. However, real-world deployment requires explicit design choices and safeguards—about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to manage or synthesize data, and how to test and mitigate risks to robustness, fairness, and rare‑token fidelity. With these guardrails, KD combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) yields the best path to compact, reliable models.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performance models by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from one or more teacher models into smaller students so they retain much of the teacher’s capabilities with lower compute, memory, or latency. The literature spans a family of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention/relational signals), multiple training regimes (offline, online/self-distillation, data-free), and common integrations with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search, and pre-training of compact models). Practical success depends on choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity and inductive biases, what data to use (or synthesize), and constraints around deployment, privacy, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Cornerstone for Compressing Deep Models in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile mechanism for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable ones in NLP and related modalities. When paired with targeted choices—what signals to transfer (logits versus features), how to align layers, teacher design, and data strategies—KD preserves much of the teacher’s capability while reducing compute, memory, and latency. However, KD is not a universal remedy: its success depends on optimization details, data availability, and careful engineering to handle distribution shift, rare behaviors, and student–teacher mismatches.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Bowen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Power, Limits, and Responsible Pipelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable strategy for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone and can be combined with other compression tools to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey cure: its effectiveness depends on what signals are transferred, teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability, and careful engineering to avoid degraded performance on rare or out-of-domain behaviors. A production-ready compression pipeline treats KD as the central mechanism but pairs it with curriculum design, multi-teacher strategies, representation alignment, and orthogonal compression methods while explicitly validating robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Peck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Essential but Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance when its objectives, data regime, and teacher–student alignment are chosen to match deployment constraints. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its success depends on capacity alignment, data availability and augmentation, careful combination with pruning/quantization/architecture search, and explicit evaluation of robustness, fairness, and rare-token or domain-shift behaviors. I argue KD should be treated as the central technique in model-compression pipelines, applied with engineering rigor and complementary methods to meet real-world constraints.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach for compressing large models into smaller ones that meet deployment constraints. KD reduces storage, latency, and energy while preserving much of teacher performance, but its success depends on what knowledge is transferred, how teacher signals are generated and trusted, and how distillation is combined with other compression methods and fairness or robustness constraints. Effective deployment requires task-aware decisions about targets (logits vs. features), data (original, augmented, or synthetic), architectural alignment, and additional safeguards for bias and domain shift.
