papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Principles, and Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that compact systems approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Work across vision and NLP shows that effective compression combines multiple strategies — soft-label matching, intermediate representation alignment, architecture-aware design, data- and privacy-aware workflows, and adversarial or ensemble consolidation — and that practical gains depend on addressing representation mismatch, optimization dynamics, and task or domain shifts. This synthesis summarizes prevailing methods, empirical patterns, and recurring trade-offs relevant for practitioners aiming to deploy efficient models in resource- or data-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Carpenter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical, and Responsible Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, widely applicable method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. KD shines when combined with complementary compression techniques and data strategies, but its reliability depends on careful choices about what is transferred, how teachers and students are aligned, and how data or robustness constraints are handled. I argue KD should be treated as a central instrument in compression pipelines, used with explicit engineering and ethical practices to manage its limits.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and flexible set of techniques for producing compact models that retain much of the behavior of larger, expensive teachers. Across vision, language, and other modalities, practitioners transfer information via softened outputs, intermediate-feature supervision, relational or attention-based losses, multi-teacher ensembles, and architectural or data-aware strategies. KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression tools (e.g., architecture search, quantization, pruning) and when distillation signals, data strategies, and optimization schedules are aligned to deployment constraints. Important open problems remain — including robustness on rare phenomena, domain shift, privacy and data-limited regimes, and theoretical limits of transfer — but pragmatic pipelines that combine KD variants with deployment-aware design choices are the most reliable route to high-quality compact models.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has expanded from soft-target matching to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate-representation and attention alignment, layerwise and many-to-many mapping, relational and curriculum schemes, self- and multi-teacher approaches, and data- or privacy-aware procedures. When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and tuned to deployment constraints (latency, memory, robustness, and privacy), KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance, though open challenges remain around capacity mismatch, distribution shift, rare-token behavior, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Techniques range from soft-target (logit) matching to feature- and layer-level imitation, attention- or relation-based objectives, self- and online-distillation, multi-teacher pipelines, and data-free or privacy-aware procedures. In practice KD is combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and the choice of distilled signals; remaining challenges include distribution shift, capacity and optimization mismatches, fidelity on rare outputs, and distillation under data- or privacy-constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while preserving performance. The literature documents a spectrum of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or channel maps, and relational signals), a variety of optimization and architectural practices (layer mapping, projectors, multi-stage training, and student-friendly teacher design), and deployment workflows for constrained settings (data-free, federated, and domain-adaptive distillation). Empirical and theoretical work highlights multiple mechanisms that make KD effective (regularization via soft targets, representation alignment, and optimization/inductive-bias transfer), while also identifying persistent challenges such as aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving low-frequency behavior, and selecting what and when to transfer. Practical recommendations center on matching distillation signals to student capacity, using feature- or layer-aware objectives when internal alignment matters, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Shields
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single trick but as the practical, central component of real-world model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels—soft targets, intermediate features, attention or relational structure—and, when combined with architecture-aware design, quantization/pruning, data strategies, and careful evaluation, yields compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. However, reliable deployment requires acknowledging limits (capacity mismatch, teacher errors, data scarcity, and rare-token or distributional failures) and building workflows that include teacher–student co-design, staged curricula, and targeted robustness and fairness assessment.

papers_seen.author: Ibarra
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable Path for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce latency, memory, and power requirements while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD works across modalities and tasks, but its practical success depends on choices about what signal to transfer, how to supply or synthesize training data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods. When applied thoughtfully within a wider compression pipeline, KD enables deployable models for resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. Code available at: https://github.com/polo5/ZeroShotKnowledgeTransfer

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Sensitive Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical component of model‑compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP: a versatile toolkit that transfers richer supervision from large teachers into smaller, deployable students. When KD is designed as a context‑sensitive engineering process — matching distillation targets to student capacity, combining with complementary compression methods, and tailoring data and evaluation strategies to deployment constraints — it routinely yields strong size–performance trade‑offs. However, realizing KD’s benefits in practice requires explicit attention to limits such as capacity mismatch, degraded long‑tail behavior, transferred biases, and data/privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Benefits, Limits, and Engineering Directions
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile foundation for compressing deep and language models: it enables much smaller, faster students to capture substantial teacher performance while supporting deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD excels when combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful engineering (choice of transferred signals, data augmentation, teacher selection). However, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: it can propagate teacher imperfections, struggle with rare-token or low-frequency behaviors, and face difficulties under heterogeneous or privacy-constrained data regimes. Treating KD as the central tool in a compression pipeline — but one that requires task-aware design and diagnostics — yields the best practical outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: DINE: Domain Adaptation from Single and Multiple Black-box Predictors
papers_seen.abstract: To ease the burden of labeling, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims to transfer knowledge in previous and related labeled datasets (sources) to a new unlabeled dataset (target). Despite impressive progress, prior methods always need to access the raw source data and develop data-dependent alignment approaches to recognize the target samples in a transductive learning manner, which may raise privacy concerns from source individuals. Several recent studies resort to an alternative solution by exploiting the well-trained white-box model from the source domain, yet, it may still leak the raw data through generative adversarial learning. This paper studies a practical and interesting setting for UDA, where only black-box source models (i.e., only network predictions are available) are provided during adaptation in the target domain. To solve this problem, we propose a new two-step knowledge adaptation framework called DIstill and fine-tuNE (DINE). Taking into consideration the target data structure, DINE first distills the knowledge from the source predictor to a customized target model, then fine-tunes the distilled model to further fit the target domain. Besides, neural networks are not required to be identical across domains in DINE, even allowing effective adaptation on a low-resource device. Empirical results on three UDA scenarios (i.e., single-source, multi-source, and partial-set) confirm that DINE achieves highly competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art data-dependent approaches. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/tim-learn/DINE/}.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Making Knowledge Distillation a Core Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible, and broadly applicable method for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When paired with representation-level objectives, careful teacher design, and complementary compression techniques (pruning, architecture replacement, or low-precision numerics), KD yields favorable trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and deployability. The method has clear limits (e.g., rare-token behaviors, data or privacy constraints), but these are addressable with multi-stage pipelines, data-centered practices, and task-aware design.

papers_seen.author: Gates
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Variants, and Responsible Use
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD techniques range from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate representations and synthesizing training data when originals are unavailable. While KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance and enables deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints, its effectiveness depends on choices about transfer targets, student capacity, data strategies, and evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Montoya
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring behavior from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models so they can be deployed under real-world constraints. Approaches vary in what is transferred (soft outputs, internal features, attention maps, module behavior), whether distillation is offline, online, or federated, and how it is combined with architecture search, pruning, or privacy mechanisms. Empirically, KD routinely improves compact models over training from scratch and enables deployments across on-device, distributed, and data-scarce settings; however, practical success depends on aligning distillation signals to student capacity, handling imperfect or heterogeneous teachers, and addressing data and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Tyler
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple logit-matching to include intermediate-feature and relational signals, multi-stage and online workflows, and data-aware variants (including data-free or synthesized-data regimes). In practice KD is most effective when treated as the central, composable element of a broader compression pipeline that also employs pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design; success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling data or privacy constraints, and explicitly addressing robustness, distribution shift, and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving performance. KD encompasses soft-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, and relational or attention-based objectives and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques, appropriate data strategies, and teacher–student co-design. Open challenges include capacity mismatch, preservation of long‑tail behaviors, robustness and fairness transfer, and distillation under data or privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical framework for transferring knowledge from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the original performance. Across vision, language, and multimodal tasks, KD has been instantiated as soft-label matching, intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment, multi-teacher ensembles, and data-free or privacy-aware variants. Combining distillation with orthogonal compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and adapting teacher–student interactions to the data and task constraints yields the best real-world trade-offs. Remaining challenges include optimizing teacher–student mismatch, handling data or privacy limitations, and ensuring robustness and fairness in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applied approach to compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. The method encompasses transferring softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and several data strategies (including data-free or privacy-aware workflows). KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware pretraining) and when practitioner choices align teacher signals, student capacity, and available data. While KD can recover much of teacher performance with large efficiency gains, it has known failure modes—optimization difficulty, teacher imperfection, capacity mismatch, distributional shift, and degradation on low-frequency phenomena—that require tailored design, diagnostics, and hybrid pipelines to address.

papers_seen.author: Ballard
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD reduces inference cost, memory, and latency while often retaining much of teacher performance. Modern distillation practices extend beyond soft-target matching to include intermediate-feature and attention-level imitation, multi- and online-teacher schemes, data synthesis or data-free protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. While KD frequently delivers strong empirical gains, practical success requires deliberate choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures and capacities, what data to use (or synthesize), and how to evaluate and mitigate harms such as bias or degraded rare-token behavior; open problems remain in robustness under domain shift, theoretical understanding, and privacy-aware deployment.

When paired with complementary compression tools and careful data or curriculum design, KD supports real-world constraints such as latency, memory, privacy, and heterogeneous deployment. However, its practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, addressing data scarcity and teacher bias, and evaluating robustness under distribution shifts.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Woods
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used family of techniques for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information beyond hard labels—such as softened outputs, intermediate features, attention patterns, or relational signals—and is typically combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free approaches). Empirical work shows KD often recovers much of a teacher’s performance while reducing inference cost, but its success depends on careful alignment of teacher signals, student capacity, and available data; known failure modes include capacity mismatch, teacher imperfections, distributional shift, and degradation on rare or low-frequency phenomena. Practical deployment therefore calls for diagnostic evaluations, hybrid pipelines, and attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer predictive capacity from large, expensive models into smaller, faster models while preserving performance. Approaches vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention maps, feature projectors), how teachers are constructed (single teacher, multi-teacher, self-teaching, or meta-learned teachers), and what resources are available (original data, public data, or no data). Practical extensions address domain-specific needs (e.g., BERT compression, low-precision deployment, privacy-preserving and federated settings) and include strategies such as progressive module replacement, multi-stage distillation, adversarially generated synthetic data, and self-supervised distillation. Empirical and theoretical work highlights both the power of soft targets as a regularizer and the importance of aligning internal representations and layer correspondences to improve student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. The literature characterizes a spectrum of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals), multiple training workflows (offline teacher supervision, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher curricula), and data strategies (full-data, limited-data augmentation, and data-free synthesis). KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when adapted to task, student capacity, and deployment constraints. Key practical challenges remain: optimization and capacity mismatch, preservation of rare-token or long-tail behaviors, robustness under distribution shift, and the danger of propagating teacher biases or errors.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing compact, deployable deep and language models by transferring information from large teacher models to smaller students. When treated as the center of a compression pipeline and combined with pretraining, architecture-aware design, data strategies (including data-free synthesis), and complementary compression techniques, KD routinely yields substantial reductions in size and latency while retaining much of teacher utility. However, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: its effectiveness depends on careful choice of distillation signals, student capacity, data availability or synthesis, and evaluation for robustness and distributional or fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has expanded from soft-target matching to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate-representation and attention alignment, layerwise and many-to-many mapping, relational and curriculum schemes, self- and multi-teacher approaches, and data- or privacy-aware procedures. When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and tuned to deployment constraints (latency, memory, robustness, and privacy), KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance, though open challenges remain around capacity mismatch, distribution shift, rare-token behavior, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Decker
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as the central, practical method for producing compact, deployable models from large deep and language models. Treated as a flexible toolkit rather than a single recipe, KD preserves much of teacher performance while enabling reductions in latency, memory, and privacy exposure when combined with complementary compression techniques and deployment-aware design. Effective distillation requires choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to evaluate robustness and social harms. Recent work emphasizes task-adaptive compression, representation-aware objectives, and integrating KD into broader pipelines (e.g., pruning, quantization, architecture search) to produce reliable, efficient students for real-world NLP and deep-learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Fernandez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, more efficient students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational signals. The approach has diversified from simple soft-target matching to richer methods (feature- and layer-level mimicry, multi-teacher and multi-stage pipelines, and data-free or synthetic-data strategies) and is often combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows KD frequently preserves much of teacher performance across vision and NLP, but success depends on design choices about transfer targets, teacher–student alignment, data handling, and mitigation of optimization or distributional mismatches. Practical deployment relies on adapting KD to task constraints and combining it with complementary compression techniques to balance accuracy, latency, and resource limits.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Core of Model Compression — Practical Benefits, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, high-impact approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across NLP, speech, and vision. Treated as the central element of compression pipelines and combined with representation-level objectives, data strategies, and complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), KD routinely yields favorable size–performance trade-offs. However, realizing these gains in practice requires deliberate teacher–student co‑design, careful handling of data and augmentation, selective transfer of signals, and evaluation for robustness, fairness, and rare-token behavior.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and representational information. A rich taxonomy of techniques has emerged—soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, relational/attention losses, multi-teacher and multi-stage pipelines, and data-synthesis or data-free approaches—which are commonly combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical work across vision, language, and other modalities demonstrates that careful distillation pipelines can produce deployable models that retain much of teacher performance, while open problems remain in representation alignment, robustness, long‑tail fidelity, and data- or privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Over the past decade this has grown from simple logit-matching into a toolkit that includes internal representation alignment, layer-mapping strategies, data and privacy-aware procedures, adversarial and robustness-aware objectives, online and distributed schemes, and methods tailored for specific architectures such as pre-trained language models. Distillation often recovers much of a teacher’s performance when deliberately designed (choice of signals, data, and architecture), but it faces limits from optimization difficulties, capacity mismatch, distributional shift, and the risk of transferring undesirable teacher behaviors such as bias. Practical success therefore depends on combining multiple transfer signals, handling data constraints, and adapting both teacher and student to the deployment context.

When used as the central, composable component of compression pipelines and combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies), KD routinely delivers large reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. Its real-world success requires task‑aware choices about which signals to transfer (soft logits, features, attention or relational maps), how to align teacher and student capacity, what data to use or synthesize, and what safeguards to adopt for robustness, fairness, and privacy. I argue that KD should be treated as the core tool in model compression but applied with explicit diagnostics, curricula, and integration with other compression techniques to manage its known failure modes and maximize practical utility.

papers_seen.author: Rosales
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical suite of techniques for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates by transferring richer supervision than hard labels—such as softened outputs, intermediate representations, or relational signals—and is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data strategies (augmentation, synthetic or data-free generation). While KD routinely yields strong reductions in inference cost and memory with modest performance loss, its success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity and deployment constraints and on mitigating failure modes such as bias transfer, degradation on rare events, and sensitivity to distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Sims
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a flexible, deployment-oriented strategy for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students. When integrated with representation-level objectives, layer-aware alignment, data strategies (including synthesized or privacy-preserving data), and architecture-aware search, distillation enables compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Realistic use requires attention to teacher–student alignment, task-awareness, and data or privacy limitations to avoid predictable failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Dunn
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers predictive and representational information from large teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. The literature treats KD as a flexible toolkit—matching soft logits, aligning intermediate features or attention, using multi-teacher or online protocols, and synthesizing data when originals are unavailable—and recommends integrating KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and data-aware strategies. Practical success depends on careful design choices about what to transfer, student–teacher alignment, data availability or synthesis, and evaluation of robustness, rare-case fidelity, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach that enables deployment of large deep models by training smaller students to retain much of teacher performance. KD supports a wide range of transfer signals (logits, features, attention), training protocols (multi-stage, multi-teacher, federated), and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design). When applied carefully and combined with appropriate data, alignment, and robustness strategies, KD yields substantial runtime and memory savings with modest accuracy loss, making it central to production model compression in NLP and related domains.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Works
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. The family of KD methods includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention alignment, feature- and layer-wise objectives, multi-teacher and online/self-distillation schedules, and techniques for operating without original training data or under privacy constraints. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when the distillation signals, data strategy, and student capacity are chosen to match deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, domain shift, preservation of low-frequency or rare behaviors, transferred biases, and data- or privacy-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Mcknight
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers predictive behavior and internal structure from large, high‑capacity teachers into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, and graph settings, KD enables substantial reductions in storage and inference cost while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. However, KD is a context‑sensitive toolkit rather than a single recipe: its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to prepare students, how to supply or synthesize data, and how to evaluate robustness and fairness. When integrated into a pipeline that includes architecture adaptation, pruning/quantization, data strategies, and robustness checks, KD is the most practical and versatile method for producing compact models suitable for real deployment.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation and Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and model compression are essential for deploying large pretrained models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Effective distillation requires more than copying logits: combining domain adaptation, intermediate representation alignment, task-aware architecture search, and privacy-preserving or data-free techniques produces compact models that retain much of the teacher's utility across modalities and tasks.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision and language tasks, distillation variants (soft-target matching, intermediate-feature alignment, layer mapping, online or multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware strategies) enable substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while often preserving much of the teacher's performance. Practical deployments pair distillation with data augmentation, architecture-aware design, and complementary compression methods to meet latency, device, and privacy constraints; remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, data scarcity, robustness to distribution shift, and preserving fairness and rare behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Spence
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of methods for transferring behavior from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, energy, or privacy constraints. Over the past decade KD has expanded beyond matching softened logits to include intermediate-feature and attention alignment, many-to-many layer mappings, ensemble and multi-teacher transfers, self-distillation, and data-aware or data-free schemes. KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and when distillation targets, student architecture, and data strategies are chosen to match task and deployment constraints. Open challenges remain in handling teacher–student capacity mismatch, preserving long-tail or rare-token behavior, ensuring robustness and fairness, and defining principled guarantees under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Pitts
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers learned behavior from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving much of the teacher’s capabilities. Across vision and NLP, KD encompasses soft-target (logit) matching, representation- and attention-level alignment, self-distillation, and ensemble or multi-stage pipelines. KD is most effective when embedded in a compression workflow that includes architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, and careful data and curriculum decisions. Key limitations remain around low-frequency or rare-token behavior, data scarcity and distribution shift, optimization and capacity mismatch, and preserving robustness or fairness under transfer. Practical progress requires choosing appropriate distilled signals, aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining KD with complementary compression and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Hayden
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Sensitive Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the practical core of model compression for deep learning and NLP because it is a flexible, empirically effective paradigm that transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels, composes naturally with pruning/quantization/architecture changes, and supports privacy- and deployment-aware workflows. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its reliability depends on aligning distillation signals with student capacity, addressing data availability or privacy constraints, and explicitly mitigating risks such as optimization mismatch, degraded rare-token performance, and the propagation of teacher harms. To maximize KD’s practical value, practitioners should adopt signal- and data-aware distillation objectives, combine KD with complementary compression primitives, and expand evaluation beyond aggregate accuracy to include robustness, fairness, and long-tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Over the past decade the approach has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a toolkit that includes representation-level alignment, multi-teacher and online schedules, and data-aware or data-free workflows. When combined with complementary compression primitives and careful engineering, distillation routinely produces compact models that trade only modest performance for large gains in latency, memory, and energy efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as the most practical and widely applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students for vision, language, and other modalities. When applied thoughtfully — selecting what to transfer (logits, features, attention), designing teacher-student pairs, and combining KD with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, data synthesis) — distillation recovers much of a teacher’s performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD also serves beyond compression as a regularizer that can improve robustness and generalization, but it is not a panacea: capacity mismatch, domain shift, optimization differences, and risks of transferring biases or vulnerability must be managed through targeted practices and evaluations.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Promise, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully and combined with complementary techniques—layer- and task-aware transfer, multi-teacher schemes, data synthesis or privacy-aware protocols, and hardware-aware downstream optimization—KD enables substantial reductions in size and latency while retaining much of a teacher's utility. However, its practical success is engineering-dependent: careful choices about distilled signals, student preparation, data availability, and mitigation of transferred errors or biases are required to realize reliable, fair, and robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Park
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model-compression methods transfer predictive behavior and internal signals from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and deployment complexity while preserving much of the original performance. The literature defines a broad toolbox — from soft-target/logit matching to feature- and attention-level imitation, multi- and self-distillation, and data strategies including augmentation and synthetic/data‑free approaches — and treats distillation as a core component of wider compression pipelines that often include pruning, quantization, and architecture design. Practical success depends on careful teacher–student engineering, appropriate distillation targets, data and curriculum choices, and explicit evaluation for robustness, long‑tail behavior, and privacy; open challenges remain in heterogeneous architectures, distribution shift, and preserving rare or task-specific behaviors after compression.

papers_seen.author: Gross
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers predictive behavior and internal representations from larger teacher models to smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD methods range from matching softened outputs to aligning intermediate features, attention maps, or relational signals, and are commonly combined with complementary compression techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture redesign. Empirical work shows that KD typically narrows the performance gap between teacher and student across modalities, but practical success depends on careful choices about distillation targets, teacher preparation, student capacity, data strategies, and evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: What is known about knowledge distillation and model compression in deep learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful and practical approach for turning large, high‑capacity teacher models into smaller, faster, and more deployable student models. Across vision, language, multimodal, and federated settings, KD techniques include matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations or attention, many‑to‑many layer mapping, multi‑teacher and online/meta‑teaching schemes, and data‑ or privacy‑aware synthesis. KD delivers strong empirical size/latency gains when combined with architecture preparation and task‑aware choices, but its effectiveness is bounded by optimization mismatch, teacher imperfections, data or distribution shift, and robustness/fairness concerns. Best practices emphasize combining logits and feature objectives, addressing representation mismatch (layer mapping, pretraining), and using data‑aware or privacy‑preserving strategies for constrained deployments.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as the central element of a compression pipeline and combined with careful teacher–student engineering, appropriate distillation signals, and complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design), KD routinely delivers strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. However, its reliability depends on student capacity, data availability or synthesis, alignment of representations, and explicit mitigation of robustness, privacy, and rare-token or distribution-shift failures. I argue KD should be the core of any real-world compression strategy, but only when embedded in an engineering-aware pipeline that anticipates and corrects its limitations.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be the Central Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. When combined with careful pre-training of compact architectures, representation-level transfer, augmentation or synthesized data, and orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization), KD delivers strong trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy. However, realizing those gains in practice requires attention to optimization dynamics, data availability, privacy, and known failure modes (e.g., low-frequency token degradation), and so KD should be applied as part of an integrated, responsible compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Thomas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted toolkit for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone—ranging from softened logits to intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational signals—KD enables substantial reductions in size, latency, and energy while retaining much of task performance. Effective deployment depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, choosing or synthesizing appropriate training data, and combining KD with complementary compression methods and deployment-aware engineering. KD yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs in NLP and other modalities, but predictable failure modes (capacity mismatch, teacher imperfections, rare-token and distribution-shift issues) require careful pipeline design and targeted mitigations.
