papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Practical Toolbox for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the central, practical element of model-compression pipelines: a flexible toolbox that transfers richer supervision from large teachers into smaller, deployable students. When designed as a context-sensitive process—choosing what signals to transfer, adapting teacher and student architectures, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods—KD routinely yields favorable trade-offs between efficiency and retained performance. However, realizing KD’s full potential requires explicit attention to data availability and privacy, robustness and fairness, capacity mismatch, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) frames model compression as transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. KD encompasses soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, online/self-distillation, and data-aware or data-free workflows. When combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and matched to student capacity and data availability, KD routinely yields large reductions in model size and inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance. However, its success is context-sensitive: careful choices of distilled signals, data regime, teacher–student alignment, and mitigation of robustness and fairness issues are required. Open problems include principled data selection or synthesis, preserving rare-token or low-frequency behaviors, matching heterogeneous architectures, and preventing transfer of undesired biases.

papers_seen.author: Ware
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible, and production-ready family of techniques that enables large deep and language models to be compressed into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. When combined with complementary methods—representation matching, multi-teacher or online schemes, synthetic or data-free generation, and hardware-aware compression—KD delivers strong efficiency gains while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a universal solution: its success depends on careful pipeline design to address capacity mismatch, dataset or domain heterogeneity, privacy constraints, and the risk of transferring or amplifying teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Reframing Knowledge Distillation: Beyond Strong Teachers to Regularization, Representations, and Practical Variants
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful tool for compressing deep models, but its benefits arise from multiple mechanisms beyond mere imitation of a stronger teacher. Empirical and theoretical work indicates that distillation combines regularization effects of soft targets, representational alignment, and optimization dynamics; these insights motivate a broader set of practical strategies (teacher-free or data-free distillation, feature-based objectives, contrastive and adversarial losses, ensembles, and co-training of teacher/student) to obtain compact models that generalize well. This paper argues that practitioners should select KD variants depending on data availability, deployment constraints, and the nature of the task, and that future research should prioritize understanding optimization and representation transfer rather than treating teacher capacity as the sole determinant of success.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical and Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. Across vision, speech, graph, and language tasks, KD enables substantial reductions in memory and inference cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. However, KD is not a silver bullet: its effectiveness depends on choices of teacher/student architecture, what is distilled (logits, layers, attention, representations), the optimization and data used for distillation, and constraints such as privacy or fairness. Carefully combining KD with techniques like multi-teacher schedules, layer-mapping strategies, task-adaptive compression, and privacy-preserving perturbations yields the best trade-offs for real-world deployment.

papers_seen.author: Duran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for producing small, deployable models from large teachers. Treated as a core, composable element of compression pipelines and combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies), KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while preserving much of teacher performance. However, its success depends on careful choices about what signals to transfer, student capacity, and data availability; practitioners must also mitigate risks such as transferred biases, poor long‑tail behavior, and distributional shift. I argue that KD should be the default backbone of practical compression workflows, but applied in a context‑sensitive way and evaluated for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. A broad toolkit has emerged—matching logits, intermediate features, attention maps, and training dynamics; using multi-stage or online pipelines; operating with or without original data; and combining distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Distillation reliably reduces inference cost and memory while retaining much of teacher performance when the distillation signals, student capacity, and data regime are carefully matched. Practical deployment balances transfer choices, student architecture design, data or privacy constraints, and robustness or fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information that goes beyond hard labels. Across vision and language tasks, KD has evolved from soft-label matching to a toolbox of techniques that include intermediate-feature alignment, multi-teacher curricula, self-distillation, and data-aware or data-free workflows. This synthesis summarizes the principal methods, practical combinations with other compression techniques, and the main limitations and open problems that shape current research and deployment choices.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. The approach has expanded from soft-logit matching to include intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi-teacher and curriculum schemes, self-distillation, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. Practical deployments succeed when distillation objectives, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and task-aware choices are tuned to the application; remaining challenges include preserving rare-token or long-tail behaviors, handling distribution shift and data scarcity, and ensuring robustness and privacy in deployed students.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Uses, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior or internal representations. Across vision, language, speech, graph, and multimodal tasks, a family of techniques—soft-label matching, feature and attention imitation, layer mapping, multi-teacher and curriculum schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols—enables students to recover much of teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Practical success depends on task- and deployment-aware choices (distilled signal, student capacity, data availability, and augmentation), and remaining challenges include robustness to distribution shift, preservation of rare-token or fine-grained behaviors, and distillation under privacy or data-scarce conditions.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Compressing NLP and Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical and flexible route to compress large neural models for real-world deployment. When applied carefully — via multi-stage pipelines, layer-aware mappings, internal-representation transfer, self-distillation, or even without original data — KD can preserve much of the teacher performance while reducing latency and memory. KD also composes effectively with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to meet diverse resource constraints. These properties make KD a central technique for bringing large pretrained models into production in NLP and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Burgess
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective family of techniques for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers so they can be deployed under compute, memory, latency, or privacy constraints. KD ranges from matching softened teacher outputs to aligning intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational structures, and it is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and careful engineering of teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and robustness/fairness evaluations. Practical deployment emphasizes student capacity, data curricula (including synthetic or privacy‑aware data), and targeted diagnostics for long‑tail or distributional failures.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. It is a broadly applicable and practical approach across modalities (vision, language, graphs, multimodal) that enables reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of the original performance. Modern practice treats distillation as a toolkit—combining soft-label/logit transfer, intermediate representation matching, specialized architectures or projectors, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware protocols—to fit deployment constraints. Despite empirical effectiveness, distillation faces persistent challenges including data availability and privacy, teacher–student mismatches, optimization instability, and preservation of rare-token or low-frequency behavior; practical pipelines must therefore be tailored to task, data, and hardware requirements.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing neural networks into smaller, faster student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Across vision and NLP, distillation transfers softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and training dynamics; it is routinely combined with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies (including synthetic or privacy-aware data) to meet latency, memory, and deployment constraints. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data and curricula, and evaluating robustness and fairness. While distillation often preserves much of teacher performance and enables on-device or low-cost deployment, it also faces limits such as capacity mismatch, distribution shift, rare-token degradation, and the danger of transferring teacher biases or errors.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information beyond hard labels — via softened outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or training curricula — to produce compact models that trade only a small fraction of predictive performance for large gains in latency, memory, and deployability. Across modalities and tasks, KD is best applied as part of a broader compression pipeline (including pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design) and requires attention to teacher quality, distilled signals, data strategy, and evaluation for robustness and fairness to realize reliable production systems.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Patterns, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical suite of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information via soft logits, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and is routinely combined with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data synthesis. Success depends on matching distilled signals and curricula to student capacity and data regimes; persistent challenges include rare-token fidelity, domain shift, transferred biases, and data-privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted toolkit for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. KD methods span softened-logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, self- and online-distillation, multi-teacher and data-free variants, and are most effective when combined with complementary compression steps (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and careful, deployment-aware engineering. Empirical evidence shows KD routinely improves compact models' accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, but success depends on what signals are transferred, how teacher and student are aligned, and how data, robustness, and privacy constraints are handled.

papers_seen.author: Turner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and heterogeneous deployment. Realizing KD's full value requires combining soft-target transfer with representation-level objectives, curriculum or staged training, teacher optimization, and architecture-aware mapping, and it also demands attention to distribution shift, rare-token fidelity, and teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Strategy for Model Compression and Adaptation in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach to produce compact models that retain much of the performance of larger models. Beyond simple compression, KD can transfer inductive biases, enable domain adaptation and vocabulary specialization, support privacy-preserving and federated scenarios, work without access to original data, and improve robustness and feature quality when carefully applied. When combined with targeted techniques — feature mimicking, weighted soft labels, projector layers, or adversarial robustness objectives — KD becomes a unifying toolkit to meet latency, capacity, and privacy constraints in real-world NLP and deep learning deployments.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers with Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of unifying knowledge from a set of classifiers with different architectures and target classes into a single classifier, given only a generic set of unlabelled data. We call this problem Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers (UHC). This problem is motivated by scenarios where data is collected from multiple sources, but the sources cannot share their data, e.g., due to privacy concerns, and only privately trained models can be shared. In addition, each source may not be able to gather data to train all classes due to data availability at each source, and may not be able to train the same classification model due to different computational resources. To tackle this problem, we propose a generalisation of knowledge distillation to merge HCs. We derive a probabilistic relation between the outputs of HCs and the probability over all classes. Based on this relation, we propose two classes of methods based on cross-entropy minimisation and matrix factorisation, which allow us to estimate soft labels over all classes from unlabelled samples and use them in lieu of ground truth labels to train a unified classifier. Our extensive experiments on ImageNet, LSUN, and Places365 datasets show that our approaches significantly outperform a naive extension of distillation and can achieve almost the same accuracy as classifiers that are trained in a centralised, supervised manner.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, broadly applicable route to compressing large models into smaller, faster ones for deployment in resource- and privacy-constrained settings. When combined with complementary techniques (e.g., architecture-aware design, data augmentation, and privacy mechanisms), KD consistently yields strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs across modalities. However, realizing those gains requires careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention), how to select or synthesize data, and how to mitigate transferred harms (bias, privacy leakage). This paper argues that KD should be treated as a central, flexible tool for model compression while emphasizing practical design principles and known failure modes that practitioners must address.

papers_seen.author: Camacho
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) condenses the predictive behavior of large teacher models into smaller student models so they meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, energy, or privacy). KD has evolved from matching softened outputs to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate-representation alignment, multi- and self-distillation, and data-aware or data-free strategies. In practice, KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and when practitioner choices about distilled signals, student capacity, data, and evaluation on robustness and fairness are matched to deployment needs. Remaining research and engineering challenges include transferring internal model structure across heterogeneous architectures, preserving long-tail behaviors, guaranteeing robustness under distribution shift, and operating under data- or privacy-constrained regimes.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal structure from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while preserving performance. The literature documents a spectrum of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or channel maps, and relational signals), a variety of optimization and architectural practices (layer mapping, projectors, multi-stage training, and student-friendly teacher design), and deployment workflows for constrained settings (data-free, federated, and domain-adaptive distillation). Empirical and theoretical work highlights multiple mechanisms that make KD effective (regularization via soft targets, representation alignment, and optimization/inductive-bias transfer), while also identifying persistent challenges such as aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving low-frequency behavior, and selecting what and when to transfer. Practical recommendations center on matching distillation signals to student capacity, using feature- or layer-aware objectives when internal alignment matters, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques for robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Model Compression in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones while retaining much of their performance. Across NLP, speech, vision-language, and multimodal tasks, distillation techniques—including self-distillation, layer-wise/task-aware distillation, and teacher adaptation—enable substantial reductions in model size and compute with limited accuracy loss. KD is complementary to other compression strategies (e.g., pruning and architecture search) and benefits from careful choices in intermediate-target selection, data augmentation, and teacher-student alignment. When combined thoughtfully with task adaptation and hardware-aware techniques, KD unlocks feasible deployment of advanced models in resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Ferguson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and pragmatic approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—choosing which teacher signals to transfer, aligning student capacity and architecture, and combining distillation with complementary compression steps—KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: data availability, teacher–student mismatch, and distributional or privacy concerns require targeted design choices and evaluation to produce robust, fair, and deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has expanded from soft-target matching to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate-representation and attention alignment, layerwise and many-to-many mapping, relational and curriculum schemes, self- and multi-teacher approaches, and data- or privacy-aware procedures. When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and tuned to deployment constraints (latency, memory, robustness, and privacy), KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance, though open challenges remain around capacity mismatch, distribution shift, rare-token behavior, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods transfer predictive behavior and internal representations from larger or more informed teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained students. These methods are applied to reduce latency and memory, enable deployment on heterogeneous or private devices, and to retain teacher performance through tailored losses, intermediate-feature matching, multi-stage pipelines, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows KD succeeds across modalities (language, vision, multimodal, and generative models) when design choices — what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and which data to use — are matched to the task and constraints. Ongoing challenges include distilling rare-token behaviors, handling severe data heterogeneity, ensuring privacy and fairness, and automating student architecture design.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Efficient and Responsible NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical, versatile approach for compressing large models and enabling deployment in resource-constrained environments. Beyond raw compression, KD supports domain adaptation, data-free scenarios, improved inference speed, and novel training regimes for specialized tasks. However, distillation is not a panacea: it can amplify teacher biases, interact with regularization techniques in subtle ways, and benefits most when combined with complementary methods such as architecture-aware training, generator-based sample synthesis, or instance-aware losses.

papers_seen.author: Heath
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical and flexible approach for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers across vision, language, speech, and multimodal settings. Methods range from matching teacher logits to aligning intermediate representations, ensembling or self-teaching, and combining distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Empirical work shows KD can preserve much of a teacher's performance while enabling deployment under compute, memory, privacy, and latency constraints, but effectiveness depends on choices of distilled signals, data and augmentations, teacher–student alignment, and task-aware pipeline design.

papers_seen.author: Reed
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. Across vision and NLP, KD reduces inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of teacher performance when combined with representation-level transfer, architecture-aware design, and complementary compression (pruning, quantization, or architecture search). Practical application requires matching transferred signals to student capacity, addressing data-availability or privacy constraints, and evaluating robustness and fairness under distribution shift. Best-practice pipelines use task-aware signals, staged training or annealing, pretraining of compact students, and complementary compression to maximize deployed performance.

papers_seen.author: Carter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Promise, Evidence, and Practical Guidelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for converting large models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. When treated as a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD supports multiple transfer signals (soft outputs, features, attention/relations), can be combined with pruning/quantization/architecture design, and generalizes across vision, speech, and NLP tasks. Real-world success requires attention to student capacity, data strategies, distributional shift, and mitigation of propagated biases or rare-token failures. Selective and staged distillation, teacher optimization, and task-aware engineering yield the best trade-offs between accuracy and resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Practical and Responsible Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile approach to compressing large models into smaller, faster ones for deployment in resource-constrained settings. However, successful distillation requires attention to optimization dynamics, representation alignment, data availability and privacy, robustness, and social biases. This paper argues that KD should be treated as a suite of complementary techniques — including feature mimicking, input alignment, multi-teacher curricula, data-free synthesis, and adversarially-aware training — and outlines concrete best practices for applying KD in deep learning and NLP to maximize utility while minimizing harms.

papers_seen.author: Gibbs
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely applied family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. KD methods span matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations or attention patterns, and transferring relational or ensemble information. In practice KD is used together with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design, and it is adapted to data- and privacy-constrained settings via public, synthetic, or data-free approaches. While KD routinely yields strong size/accuracy trade-offs, its success depends on matching transfer signals to student capacity and data availability and on diagnosing limits such as teacher imperfection, capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Practical Methods, Mechanisms, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a central technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. Practitioners use KD to transfer predictive behavior and internal representations, enabling reduced latency, memory footprint, and energy use while retaining much of teacher performance. Effective KD combines choices about what signals to transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, relational signals), how to align teacher and student architectures, how to supply or synthesize training data, and when to integrate complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization). Success depends on task- and data-aware engineering: careful teacher selection or synthesis, student capacity matching, and mitigation of distributional and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Principles, and Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that compact systems approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. Work across vision and NLP shows that effective compression combines multiple strategies — soft-label matching, intermediate representation alignment, architecture-aware design, data- and privacy-aware workflows, and adversarial or ensemble consolidation — and that practical gains depend on addressing representation mismatch, optimization dynamics, and task or domain shifts. This synthesis summarizes prevailing methods, empirical patterns, and recurring trade-offs relevant for practitioners aiming to deploy efficient models in resource- or data-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical engine of model compression for deep learning and NLP: it provides flexible, high-utility transfer mechanisms that—when combined with complementary compression primitives and data strategies—enable compact, deployable models that approach teacher performance. Its success is not automatic; careful signal choice, teacher–student alignment, data handling, and explicit checks for robustness and fairness are required for reliable production results.

papers_seen.author: Koch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression techniques aim to transfer useful knowledge from larger, expensive models to smaller, more efficient ones so that deployed systems retain high performance under resource constraints. Approaches span logit-level supervision, feature- and layer-level matching, progressive module replacement, and data-augmentation or data-free strategies. Applications include compressing large language models, accelerating inference on edge devices, enabling multi-task and federated learning, and improving robustness or generalization. Practical deployments often combine KD with quantization, architecture design, or task-aware selection of teacher signals to balance fidelity and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Armstrong
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring knowledge from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so that students retain much of the teacher’s performance while meeting deployment constraints. The KD toolkit spans matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, relational and layer-wise objectives, multi-teacher and self-distillation schedules, and data-aware or data-free strategies. KD is most effective when integrated into broader compression pipelines (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and when choices about distilled signals, student capacity, and data strategies are matched to task and deployment constraints. Although KD often yields substantial efficiency gains with modest performance loss, important challenges remain: capacity and optimization mismatch, degraded handling of rare or low-frequency phenomena, propagation of teacher biases, robustness under domain shift, and privacy- or data-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression methods transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller students to reduce computation, memory, and latency while retaining predictive performance. Methods vary from matching soft outputs to aligning intermediate representations, using teacher ensembles or meta-learned teachers, and operating under constraints such as missing data, privacy, or heterogeneous devices. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD improves student generalization relative to training from scratch in many settings but interacts with optimization, data availability, and teacher imperfection; practical deployments benefit from task-aware choices of distillation targets, architectural adapters, and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques aim to transfer the predictive power of large, expensive models into smaller, faster models suitable for deployment, domain adaptation, or constrained hardware. Research has explored matching output distributions, aligning internal representations, module-replacement strategies, data-augmented or data-free distillation, robustness-aware objectives, and task-aware selection of transferable knowledge. Empirical work spans language models (including BERT), reading comprehension, retrieval/ranking, and vision tasks, demonstrating trade-offs between compression ratio, accuracy retention, robustness, and required access to teacher training data. Best practices emphasize careful choice of distillation signal (logits, attention, hidden activations), augmentation or synthesis of training examples when data are scarce, and filtering or adapting teacher knowledge to the student’s capacity and target task.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.author: Bruce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Careful, Deployment‑Aware Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Treated as a flexible toolkit rather than a single algorithm, KD can be combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Effective use of KD requires deliberate choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to evaluate and mitigate robustness, fairness, and distributional risks.

papers_seen.author: Vang
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. KD methods include matching teacher logits, aligning intermediate representations, transferring attention or relational structure, and curriculum or multi-stage schedules. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and appropriate data strategies, KD routinely yields favorable trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and memory. Real-world success depends on careful teacher–student co-design, data selection or synthesis, signal selection, and evaluation for robustness, privacy, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: What is known about knowledge distillation and model compression in deep learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful and practical approach for turning large, high‑capacity teacher models into smaller, faster, and more deployable student models. Across vision, language, multimodal, and federated settings, KD techniques include matching softened logits, aligning intermediate representations or attention, many‑to‑many layer mapping, multi‑teacher and online/meta‑teaching schemes, and data‑ or privacy‑aware synthesis. KD delivers strong empirical size/latency gains when combined with architecture preparation and task‑aware choices, but its effectiveness is bounded by optimization mismatch, teacher imperfections, data or distribution shift, and robustness/fairness concerns. Best practices emphasize combining logits and feature objectives, addressing representation mismatch (layer mapping, pretraining), and using data‑aware or privacy‑preserving strategies for constrained deployments.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while preserving performance. Methods extend beyond matching soft output logits to include intermediate feature/representation matching, layer-wise alignment, adversarial or curriculum-driven sample selection, and data-free or privacy-aware synthesis. Distillation is widely applicable across modalities (vision, speech, language, multimodal) and use cases (on-device deployment, federated learning, low-precision inference), but success depends on careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to handle data availability or heterogeneity, and how to align teacher and student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Recipes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD operates across levels—from soft output (logit) imitation to intermediate-feature and layer-wise alignment—and is often combined with architecture search, pruning, or data-synthesis to meet deployment constraints. Beyond pure compression, KD can act as a regularizer that improves generalization and robustness, but its effectiveness depends on student capacity, the choice of distillation signal, data availability or privacy constraints, and careful matching of teacher and student objectives.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured from a heuristic for compressing large models into a broadly applicable set of techniques that enable smaller, faster, and in some cases fairer or more interpretable models. Its effectiveness depends on choices about what to transfer (logits, features, structure), how to prepare training data, and how to reconcile teacher imperfections with student capacity. When these design choices are matched to the task and constraints, KD enables substantial compression with small performance loss and can address privacy and resource limitations.

papers_seen.author: Dodson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile empirical framework for compressing high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, and structured prediction, KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone (e.g., softened outputs, intermediate features, attention maps, or relational structure) and is commonly integrated with pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies to meet latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Practical pipelines emphasize task- and student-aware design, careful teacher selection or training, and data-management choices; when applied thoughtfully KD can recover much of a teacher's performance but still faces challenges in robustness, domain shift, fairness, and theoretical understanding.

papers_seen.author: Hoover
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-oriented approach for shrinking large models into deployable students. When applied as a toolbox — not a single recipe — KD can preserve much of a teacher's performance while meeting real-world constraints. Practical effectiveness hinges on choosing which signals to transfer (logits, features, relations), aligning teacher and student capacity, and combining distillation with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Careful pipelines that address data availability, optimization mismatch, domain shift, and bias/robustness concerns enable KD to be the central component of reliable compression workflows.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied strategy to transfer information from large or specialized teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. In practice KD has been used to compress pretrained language models, speed up inference in structured models, enable multimodal generation, improve low-precision networks, and scale training across data-parallel workers. Research spans theoretical analyses of why distillation works, empirical studies of failure modes (e.g., propagation of teacher errors), and practical training recipes (including online and self-distillation variants) that balance fidelity to the teacher with student capacity and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Terry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational signals. Over the last decade KD has evolved from soft-label matching into a flexible toolbox—incorporating feature- and layer-level objectives, multi-teacher and self-distillation regimes, data synthesis or data-free workflows, and integrations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to align architectures and capacities, what data to use (or synthesize), and how to mitigate robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift problems.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Powerful, Composable, and Context‑Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible technique for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers richer supervision than hard labels alone and can be applied at the level of logits, features, or relational/attention signals. While KD routinely closes much of the accuracy gap between teacher and student, its reliable use in production requires careful choices about the distillation signal, student–teacher co‑design, data strategies, and explicit evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context‑Sensitive Toolbox for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical centerpiece for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When used thoughtfully — selecting what to transfer, adapting objectives to teacher and student capacities, and combining distillation with complementary methods like pruning, quantization, or data synthesis — KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. However, distillation’s effectiveness varies with task, data regime, and deployment constraints, so practitioners should treat it as a flexible set of techniques rather than a single plug‑and‑play algorithm.

papers_seen.author: Clay
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical, Composable Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood as a central, context-sensitive tool within a broader model-compression pipeline: when practitioners treat KD as a flexible, signal-aware component and combine it with data strategies and complementary compression primitives, small students can approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. However, KD is not a universal remedy; its success depends on choices about distilled signals, teacher–student capacity alignment, data access or synthesis, and safeguards for robustness, fairness, and low-frequency behavior.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and production-oriented approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. When applied as a flexible toolkit—choosing appropriate supervision signals, aligning architectures, and integrating complementary compression methods—KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs. At the same time, KD has predictable limitations (teacher flaws, capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and low-frequency behavior loss) that require pipeline-aware engineering and targeted mitigation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) condenses information from large teacher models into smaller student models so deployments meet constraints on latency, memory, compute, or privacy while retaining much of teacher performance. The field has expanded beyond soft-label matching into a toolbox of representation- and structure-level transfers, diverse training regimes, and integrations with complementary compression primitives. Practical success depends on aligning distilled signals to student capacity, handling data availability (including synthesized or privacy-aware data), and explicitly diagnosing robustness, fairness, and long-tail behavior. Several empirical and conceptual gaps remain around principled selection of distilled signals, behavior under domain shift, and theoretical guarantees that predict when KD will deliver large gains.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Scenarios, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce the computational and storage footprint of large neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller students. Approaches span matching outputs (soft labels), transferring intermediate representations (feature or layer-wise distillation), adapting teacher selection and weighting, and operating under constraints such as missing original data, privacy, or multi-modal inputs. Practical work on language models, vision-language systems, and other domains highlights gains from task-aware selection of distilled information, architectural adapters between teacher and student, and advanced training schemes (e.g., adversarial sample generation, meta-learning of teachers). Empirical results and surveys show KD is versatile: it improves student accuracy over training from scratch, enables deployment in resource-constrained settings, and can be extended to preserve privacy and support domain adaptation, while theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when and why distillation helps and what challenges remain.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Over the past decade the approach has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a toolkit that includes representation-level alignment, multi-teacher and online schedules, and data-aware or data-free workflows. When combined with complementary compression primitives and careful engineering, distillation routinely produces compact models that trade only modest performance for large gains in latency, memory, and energy efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Ballard
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Across vision, language, speech, and multimodal tasks, KD reduces inference cost, memory, and latency while often retaining much of teacher performance. Modern distillation practices extend beyond soft-target matching to include intermediate-feature and attention-level imitation, multi- and online-teacher schemes, data synthesis or data-free protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. While KD frequently delivers strong empirical gains, practical success requires deliberate choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures and capacities, what data to use (or synthesize), and how to evaluate and mitigate harms such as bias or degraded rare-token behavior; open problems remain in robustness under domain shift, theoretical understanding, and privacy-aware deployment.

papers_seen.author: Franklin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Composable Core of Model Compression: Benefits, Limits, and Practical Safeguards
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic approach for compressing large or ensemble teacher models into smaller student models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained settings. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone, KD enables favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across modalities, but its practical success depends on careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to handle limited or synthetic data and ethical or robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. The approach includes matching teacher soft logits, aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, and using multi-teacher, self-distillation, and data‑aware or data‑free workflows. KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and when the distilled signals, student capacity, and data strategies are chosen to match deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include robustness under distribution shift, preserving low-frequency or rare-token behavior, avoiding transfer of teacher biases, and meeting privacy constraints in distributed or data-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Reed
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Balanced Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile, production-ready approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, faster students. When engineered carefully—selecting what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student representations, managing or synthesizing data, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods—KD yields large efficiency gains while preserving most task performance. However, KD is not automatic: its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data and curriculum choices, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and distributional mismatch.

papers_seen.author: Kerr
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach to compressing large, high-performing deep models into smaller, deployable students. When designed and applied carefully it can retain most of a teacher’s capabilities while meeting real-world constraints (latency, memory, privacy). KD is not a single recipe but a design-sensitive toolkit: choices about what to transfer (soft targets, features, attention, module behavior), how to align teacher and student, and how to handle limited or mismatched data determine success. Complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis) and task-aware variants extend KD’s reach. Responsible deployment requires explicit attention to optimization dynamics, robustness, rare-behavior preservation, and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted Tool: Beyond Compression to Fairness, Robustness, and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to compress large models into smaller, faster students, but its potential extends much further. When applied thoughtfully—via feature-level mimicking, progressive module replacement, teacher selection and confidence-weighting, and by combining with automated search or divergence choices—KD can improve fairness, domain adaptation, generative model compression, and student robustness while preserving or even improving task performance. This essay argues that KD is not a single recipe but a family of techniques that should be matched to specific goals (efficiency, fairness, transferability, or generation), and gives concrete methodological recommendations informed by empirical and theoretical work.

papers_seen.author: Pennington
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing deep and language models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Techniques vary in what is transferred (soft outputs, internal representations, attention, relational signals), how data are used or synthesized, and how distillation is combined with complementary compression methods; practical success depends on aligning signals to student capacity and deployment constraints while mitigating known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Pham
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical suite of techniques that transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models so that compact systems approach teacher performance while meeting deployment constraints. When combined with representation-level objectives, multi-teacher schedules, data-aware strategies, and architecture-aware design, KD enables substantial reductions in compute, memory, and latency. Its effectiveness depends on careful handling of data availability, teacher-student mismatch, and ethical or robustness considerations.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Works
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. The family of KD methods includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention alignment, feature- and layer-wise objectives, multi-teacher and online/self-distillation schedules, and techniques for operating without original training data or under privacy constraints. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when the distillation signals, data strategy, and student capacity are chosen to match deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, domain shift, preservation of low-frequency or rare behaviors, transferred biases, and data- or privacy-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Engineering Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile approach for producing compact, deployable models that retain much of the behavior of larger teachers. When combined with complementary compression techniques and careful data/architecture choices, KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs in vision, language, and multimodal tasks. However, its practical success depends on addressing capacity and optimization mismatch, data availability or privacy constraints, and preservation of rare or fine-grained behaviors; these limitations call for feature-level objectives, curriculum/data synthesis, and evaluation beyond aggregate accuracy to ensure robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hardy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, broadly used approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels—such as softened output distributions, intermediate representations, attention/relational structure, or many-to-many layer mappings—KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of a teacher model’s performance. Effective distillation is context-sensitive: choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, what data to use or synthesize, and how to combine KD with complementary compression techniques determine outcomes. While KD routinely yields favorable size/accuracy trade-offs in vision and language tasks, practical adoption requires engineered pipelines to manage capacity mismatch, teacher imperfections, distributional shift, privacy constraints, and robustness or fairness risks.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in NLP: Strengths, Limits, and Recommended Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely applicable approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. Across modalities and tasks, KD can preserve much of a teacher model’s performance while reducing inference cost, memory, and latency. Real-world success depends on choosing what knowledge to transfer (logits, features, relations), aligning teacher and student representations, managing or synthesizing data when needed, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques. KD is highly effective in practice but requires careful engineering to avoid propagating teacher shortcomings or failing under domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transfer information from large, high-capacity teacher models to smaller student models to reduce model size, latency, and deployment cost while retaining much of the teacher's utility. Methods vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, ensembles), how training data is used or synthesized, and whether distillation is combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Across vision and NLP tasks, distillation enables practical deployment of compact models but requires careful handling of representation mismatch, data availability, optimization schedules, and potential amplification of teacher errors or biases.
