papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated method for producing compact models that preserve much of the performance and useful behavior of larger teacher models. KD works by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone and is most effective when integrated with complementary techniques (architecture-aware compression, pruning, quantization) and careful data and evaluation practices. However, KD is context-sensitive: its success depends on teacher quality, what signals are distilled, student capacity, data availability or synthesis, and explicit checks for robustness and fairness. Practical adoption therefore requires principled pipeline choices, staged training, and targeted mitigation of known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile technique for shrinking large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When integrated into compression pipelines and combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design, KD often recovers much of the teacher’s utility while substantially reducing inference cost. Real-world success requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to source or synthesize training data, and how to evaluate robustness and fairness under deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers predictive behavior and internal representations through soft targets, feature alignment, and layer-aware signals. While it reliably improves compact-model performance relative to training from scratch, KD’s success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to handle data limitations, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression techniques. Responsible deployment requires adapting KD to task constraints, diagnosing failure modes (e.g., capacity mismatch, domain shift, rare-token degradation, biased transfer), and using engineering practices such as curriculum-style annealing, targeted augmentation, and hybrid losses.

papers_seen.author: Brooks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position and Roadmap
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, pragmatic technique in model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone, KD enables small students to recover much of a large teacher’s performance while meeting deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). KD is not a single recipe but a flexible toolkit—soft targets, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational transfers, multi-teacher and data-synthesis schemes—that is most effective when integrated with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and when designs account for student capacity, data regime, teacher quality, and evaluation for robustness and social harms. This position argues for KD-centered, context-sensitive engineering practices and highlights concrete methodological choices that practitioners should prioritize.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce computation, memory, and latency while attempting to preserve predictive performance. The field encompasses a range of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), training workflows (single- and multi-stage, multi-teacher, self-distillation, data-free), and practical integrations with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. Empirical and conceptual work points to several mechanisms that make distillation effective (soft-target regularization, representation alignment, and inductive-bias transfer) and identifies recurring deployment concerns such as architecture mismatch, data availability, domain shift, and robustness. Best practices emphasize matching distillation signals to student capacity, using layer-aware objectives when internal alignment matters, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods for realistic constraints.

papers_seen.author: Holt
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression: Methods, Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. The toolbox includes matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations and attention, relational and layer-wise objectives, multi-teacher and online schedules, and data-free or synthetic-data generation. KD is frequently combined with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and tailored training curricula to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Practical success depends on student capacity, teacher quality, access to suitable data (or reliable synthetic substitutes), and attention to optimization, robustness, and fairness; remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and transfer of rare or biased behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.

papers_seen.author: Bass
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach to producing small, fast models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When combined with complementary techniques (e.g., layer mapping, multi-stage curricula, data augmentation, and hardware-aware compression), KD enables deployable NLP and deep-learning systems across constrained environments while admitting clear failure modes that demand targeted remedies.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most pragmatic and versatile foundation for compressing large deep and NLP models for deployment. When KD is broadened beyond simple soft-label matching to include intermediate representation transfer, multi-teacher schedules, data strategies, and integration with pruning/quantization, it yields compact students that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting real-world latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD is not a silver bullet: careful signal design, student capacity matching, and complementary compression techniques are required to handle domain shift, rare-token behaviors, and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Andrews
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core, Context‑Sensitive Engine of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile method for transferring richer supervision from large teacher models into smaller student models so they meet deployment constraints on latency, memory, energy, or privacy. When treated as a central component of compression pipelines and combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design), KD routinely yields strong size–performance tradeoffs across vision and language. However, KD’s benefits are not automatic: careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to manage or synthesize data, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to detect or mitigate robustness and fairness issues are required for reliable real‑world use. I argue that KD should be adopted as the default core tool in model compression, but only when used with task- and deployment-aware engineering, diagnostics, and safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high‑capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has grown from matching softened teacher logits to a diverse toolkit including intermediate‑representation and attention alignment, multi‑teacher and self‑distillation variants, data‑aware and data‑free workflows, and task‑aware layer mapping. In practice KD is most effective when composed with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign/search) and when designers adapt distillation signals, data strategies, and curricula to student capacity and deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include teacher–student capacity mismatch, distributional shift and long‑tail/rare‑token behavior, robustness and fairness risks, and deploying under privacy or data‑scarce regimes.

papers_seen.author: Alvarado
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context‑Sensitive Engine of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is most effective when treated as a central, flexible component of model‑compression pipelines rather than as a single canned technique. By transferring richer forms of supervision (soft targets, intermediate representations, relational or attention signals) and by being combined with complementary methods such as pruning, quantization, and architecture design, KD enables deployment of compact models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Successful distillation requires careful choices about teacher preparation, student capacity, distilled signals, data strategies (including synthetic or data‑free approaches), and explicit checks for robustness, fairness, and rare‑token fidelity. When applied with task‑aware design and safeguards against optimization and bias failure modes, KD provides a practical road for compressing large models for real‑world NLP and deep‑learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Horton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad set of distillation objectives and workflows—ranging from soft-target/logit matching to intermediate-feature, layerwise, and data-synthesis approaches—enables effective trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and memory for deployment. Practical success depends on choices about which signals to transfer, the data regime and student capacity, and integration with complementary compression techniques; persistent challenges include domain shift, optimization mismatch, and preserving rare or fairness-critical behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile, and broadly applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in NLP and other modalities. KD reliably improves size–performance trade-offs when its design is matched to student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, but it requires engineering choices and complementary techniques to address robustness, fairness, and data limitations.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. Over the past decade researchers have extended KD from simple soft-target matching to a diverse toolkit that includes intermediate-feature matching, progressive module replacement, data-augmentation-aware distillation, and federated or heterogeneous-device formulations. Empirical work shows KD often yields substantial gains in latency and memory while preserving much of teacher performance, but practical success requires careful choices about what to transfer, how to select or synthesize data, and how to align teacher and student architectures under constraints such as privacy, communication, and device heterogeneity.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers knowledge from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce compute, memory, and latency while retaining much of the teacher’s capabilities. KD spans simple logit-matching to feature- and layer-level alignment, supports multi-stage and teacher-ensemble strategies, and integrates with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Practical success depends on careful choices about distilled signals, data and curricula, and alignment between teacher and student; persistent limits include handling low-frequency behavior, architecture mismatch, data scarcity, and robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has expanded from soft-target matching to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate-representation and attention alignment, layerwise and many-to-many mapping, relational and curriculum schemes, self- and multi-teacher approaches, and data- or privacy-aware procedures. When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and tuned to deployment constraints (latency, memory, robustness, and privacy), KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance, though open challenges remain around capacity mismatch, distribution shift, rare-token behavior, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multifaceted approach for converting large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, faster students suitable for deployment. KD goes beyond matching final outputs to include intermediate representation transfer, attention- and relation-level objectives, multi-teacher and online schemes, and workflows that operate with limited or synthetic data. In practice, KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when its signals, curricula, and data strategies are adapted to student capacity and deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include optimizing teacher–student alignment, preserving long-tail or rare-token behavior, mitigating transferred biases, and ensuring robustness and privacy under constrained data regimes.

papers_seen.author: Carroll
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for transferring behavior from large “teacher” models to smaller “student” models to reduce inference cost and enable deployment. KD spans simple soft-target matching to richer objectives that align intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure, and it is commonly combined with architecture search, pruning, or quantization. Success depends on careful choices about what signals to transfer, student capacity, training data (including synthesized or distilled datasets), and evaluation for robustness, fairness, and distribution shift. This article synthesizes core methods, empirical patterns, and practical recommendations that guide the use of KD in NLP and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Morton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical engine for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD is empirically effective across modalities because it transfers richer signals than hard labels (soft targets, intermediate features, relational cues) and composes with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design). However, KD is engineering-dependent: data availability, teacher quality, and student–teacher mismatch create failure modes that require task-aware choices. A pragmatic compression pipeline treats KD as one component among data strategies, architecture adaptation, and hardware-aware tuning to achieve reliable, high-fidelity compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Beyond Soft Labels: A Practical Position on Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a crucial technique for shrinking large deep models to meet real-world latency, memory and privacy constraints while retaining much of their performance. However, naive distillation that only matches teacher soft-labels is often insufficient. A more reliable strategy combines distillation of internal representations and features, task- or domain-adaptive compression, and architecture-aware search or adaptation. When applied with care — addressing optimization issues, data or privacy limits, and mismatch between teacher and student capacities — distillation enables compact, fast models that approach teacher performance across speech, NLP and vision tasks.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a practical, flexible approach for producing compact neural models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Across vision and language applications KD has been extended from simple soft-label matching to a wide set of techniques—intermediate-representation transfer, layer-aware alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation, data-free variants, and adversarial or projector-based feature matching—that enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD both preserves predictive performance and can improve generalization in many settings, while also raising practical challenges such as teacher–student mismatch and degraded modeling of low-frequency phenomena that require targeted mitigations.

papers_seen.author: Carrillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Mechanisms, Variants, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Research and practice show a spectrum of distillation signals and workflows that make KD a flexible foundation of modern compression pipelines, but its success depends on task-aware signal selection, student design, and complementary compression techniques.

papers_seen.author: Alexander
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile family of techniques for compressing large, high‑capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models. KD methods transfer richer supervision than hard labels alone — including softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and training dynamics — and are commonly combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, or data‑free approaches). Practical success requires design‑sensitive choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity and architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to evaluate robustness and fairness. Despite broad empirical success, KD faces persistent challenges such as capacity mismatch, distributional shift, degradation on low‑frequency phenomena, and the potential propagation of teacher biases, which motivates task‑aware distillation pipelines and continued methodological work.

papers_seen.author: Day
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Sensitive Engine, Not a Silver Bullet
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and high‑utility approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as the central element of an engineering pipeline and combined with complementary compression primitives, tailored distillation signals, and task‑aware data strategies, KD regularly produces favorable accuracy–efficiency trade‑offs. However, KD alone does not guarantee robust, fair, or distributionally stable students; careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to evaluate long‑tail behaviors are required for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Path to Compact, Deployable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible set of techniques for transferring behavior from large, expensive teacher models into smaller, faster students. In deep learning and NLP, KD enables practical deployment by reducing latency, memory, and power requirements while retaining much of teacher performance. Effective application requires: (1) combining KD with domain-aware pretraining of compact models, (2) adapting distillation to data-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings, and (3) integrating architectural and optimization improvements (e.g., feature projectors, mixed-precision) to close remaining gaps. When applied thoughtfully, KD is a key tool for making state-of-the-art models useful in real-world, resource-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applied strategy to transfer information from large or specialized teacher models into smaller, faster, or otherwise constrained student models. In practice KD has been used to compress pretrained language models, speed up inference in structured models, enable multimodal generation, improve low-precision networks, and scale training across data-parallel workers. Research spans theoretical analyses of why distillation works, empirical studies of failure modes (e.g., propagation of teacher errors), and practical training recipes (including online and self-distillation variants) that balance fidelity to the teacher with student capacity and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. A broad toolkit has emerged—soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation, and data-aware or data-free protocols—that, when combined with complementary compression methods and careful teacher–student co-design, yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, student capacity, data availability, and mitigation of robustness and bias risks.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across computer vision and NLP, practitioners use KD to reduce inference cost, enable on-device deployment, and adapt large pretrained models to constrained settings. KD techniques vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), how training data are handled (real, augmented, synthesized, or none), and how teachers and students are aligned architecturally and procedurally. When design choices are matched to the task and constraints, KD enables substantial compression with modest performance loss; however, challenges remain for heterogeneous architectures, generative tasks, privacy-sensitive settings, and preserving rare-token or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Drake
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Composable Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Sensitive Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for producing compact deep and NLP models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. KD delivers strong size–performance trade-offs when its signals, data strategy, and student capacity are aligned with deployment constraints, but it requires explicit handling of capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity, rare-token behaviors, and bias to be reliable in production.

papers_seen.author: Montoya
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile set of methods for transferring behavior from large or ensemble teacher models into smaller, faster student models so they can be deployed under real-world constraints. Approaches vary in what is transferred (soft outputs, internal features, attention maps, module behavior), whether distillation is offline, online, or federated, and how it is combined with architecture search, pruning, or privacy mechanisms. Empirically, KD routinely improves compact models over training from scratch and enables deployments across on-device, distributed, and data-scarce settings; however, practical success depends on aligning distillation signals to student capacity, handling imperfect or heterogeneous teachers, and addressing data and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression strategies enable smaller, faster models to inherit performance from larger teachers by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or ensemble knowledge. Techniques range from logit-based soft-target distillation to feature- and attention-level mimicry, multi-teacher and task-adaptive pipelines, and methods that relax the need for original training data or strong teachers. Across computer vision and natural language processing tasks, distilled students can approach teacher accuracy while drastically reducing parameters and latency; complementary strategies such as careful pre-training of compact models and architecture search further improve trade-offs between efficiency and effectiveness. Key challenges remain in preserving rare-token behavior, aligning heterogeneous teacher–student inputs, and ensuring privacy and robustness during compression.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Promise, Principles, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, deployment-oriented technique that transfers learned behaviour from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost and enable use under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. KD's practical value lies in its ability to convey richer supervisory signals than hard labels and to combine with complementary compression methods, but its success depends crucially on choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, data strategies, and checks for robustness and fidelity. Responsible and effective compression therefore treats KD as the central mechanism within a context-sensitive pipeline rather than as a standalone cure-all.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce model size or communication cost by transferring knowledge from larger or multiple models (teachers) to smaller or otherwise constrained models (students). Methods vary from matching soft outputs to transferring intermediate features, training teachers to be student-friendly, coordinating multiple teachers, and combining distillation with pruning or federated/online schemes. Empirical and theoretical work highlights how distilled "dark knowledge" improves student generalization, how architectural components (e.g., projectors) shape transfer, and how distillation can be adapted for privacy, heterogeneity, and large-scale or multi-task NLP applications.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Context-Sensitive Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers predictive behavior and internal representations through soft targets, feature alignment, and layer-aware signals. While it reliably improves compact-model performance relative to training from scratch, KD’s success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to handle data limitations, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression techniques. Responsible deployment requires adapting KD to task constraints, diagnosing failure modes (e.g., capacity mismatch, domain shift, rare-token degradation, biased transfer), and using engineering practices such as curriculum-style annealing, targeted augmentation, and hybrid losses.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Practical Recommendations for NLP and Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely applicable approach to compress large deep models into smaller, deployable ones. Across language models, speech encoders, and vision systems, distillation reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. However, success is not automatic: distillation interacts with dataset availability, model heterogeneity, optimization dynamics, robustness, and fairness. Careful choices of what to transfer (logits, features, layer-wise representations), how to handle missing data, and how to address heterogeneous or privacy-sensitive settings are essential for reliable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce model size or communication cost by transferring knowledge from larger or multiple models (teachers) to smaller or otherwise constrained models (students). Methods vary from matching soft outputs to transferring intermediate features, training teachers to be student-friendly, coordinating multiple teachers, and combining distillation with pruning or federated/online schemes. Empirical and theoretical work highlights how distilled "dark knowledge" improves student generalization, how architectural components (e.g., projectors) shape transfer, and how distillation can be adapted for privacy, heterogeneity, and large-scale or multi-task NLP applications.

papers_seen.author: Perkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the behavior of larger teachers. KD encompasses a range of targets (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational signals), training regimes (offline teacher-student, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher), and data strategies (use of original data, synthetic or data-free methods, privacy-aware workflows). In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when design choices—what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data constraints—are matched to the deployment context. Promising empirical results across vision, language, generative models, and novel-view synthesis coexist with persistent challenges in robustness, low-frequency behavior, transferred biases, and theoretical understanding, motivating careful pipeline design and continued research.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be the Central Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of their performance. When combined with careful pre-training of compact architectures, representation-level transfer, augmentation or synthesized data, and orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization), KD delivers strong trade-offs between efficiency and accuracy. However, realizing those gains in practice requires attention to optimization dynamics, data availability, privacy, and known failure modes (e.g., low-frequency token degradation), and so KD should be applied as part of an integrated, responsible compression pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Mechanisms, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or other forms of learned structure so students retain much of teacher performance while reducing inference cost. KD has evolved from simple soft-target matching to a broad toolkit that includes feature- and representation-level objectives, multi-teacher schemes, data- and privacy-aware variants, and combinations with pruning or quantization. Practical application requires task- and deployment-aware choices that balance accuracy, latency, data availability, and social/robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Powerful, Flexible, but Context-Sensitive for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques are practical, widely applicable tools for shrinking large models and transferring capability to smaller models. KD can preserve performance while reducing inference cost, enable cross-modal and cross-task transfer, and be adapted to constrained settings (few-shot, edge devices). However, KD is not a plug-and-play cure: its benefits depend on what is distilled (logits vs. features vs. internal structure), teacher-student design, data regime, and optimization choices. Careful method design — including feature-based objectives, intermediate-layer alignment, self-distillation or meta-learned teachers, and task-aware curricula — is required to realize robust gains without amplifying teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical set of techniques for transferring predictive and representational information from large ‘teacher’ models into smaller ‘student’ models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD spans soft-target matching, intermediate representation imitation, multi-stage or multi-teacher schemes, and data strategies including synthetic or data-free approaches. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and task-aware design, KD often yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance, though limits remain around domain shift, rare-token behavior, robustness, and the propagation of teacher shortcomings.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high‑capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior, internal representations, or structural inductive biases from teachers. A spectrum of methods—logit/soft‑label matching, feature- and layer-wise imitation, attention and relation transfer, ensemble-to-singleton distillation, self-distillation, and data‑free synthesis—has been developed to meet deployment goals such as latency reduction, privacy, domain adaptation, and robustness. Empirical and applied work in NLP, vision, speech, and graph domains shows that carefully chosen distilled signals, teacher designs, and training protocols allow compact models to approach teacher performance, though challenges remain around domain shift, low-frequency phenomena, and preserving fairness and privacy in compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Cook
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. A mature toolbox has emerged that includes soft-label/logit matching, feature- and layer-level imitation, attention and relational alignment, multi-teacher schedules, and data strategies (real, augmented, synthesized, or data-free). KD is most effective when integrated into broader compression pipelines (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and when teacher–student alignment, training curricula, and data availability are carefully addressed. Practical deployment requires attention to capacity mismatch, potential bias transfer, and robustness under distributional shifts; nonetheless, well‑designed KD pipelines routinely produce compact models that approach teacher performance across vision, language, speech, graph, and recommendation tasks.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses behavioral and representational knowledge from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. The literature presents a broad toolbox—soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, self- and meta-distillation, data-free or data-scarce strategies, and layer- or relation-focused transfers—often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. Empirical and conceptual work shows KD can also regularize students and sometimes improve generalization or robustness, but practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, how teacher and student capacities are aligned, and how data (real, augmented, or synthesized) are used. Open issues include distribution shift, rare-token behavior in sequence models, privacy constraints, and principled objectives for heterogeneous architectures.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for NLP: Strengths, Limits, and a Recipe for Deployment
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is the most practical and widely adopted strategy for compressing large NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully—matching soft outputs, aligning intermediate representations, using task-aware layer mapping, and addressing data or privacy constraints—KD recovers most of a teacher’s performance while enabling large reductions in storage, latency, and power. However, effective deployment requires recognizing and mitigating limits such as capacity mismatch, distributional heterogeneity, and the risk of transferring teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Shields
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high‑capacity teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. The technique encompasses matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations and attention maps, synthesizing or reusing data when originals are unavailable, and co‑designing compact architectures. KD is flexible and widely applicable across modalities (language, vision, multimodal, and generative models) and is most effective when combined with complementary compression strategies and task‑aware choices about what and how to transfer. Success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data regime, and the match between teacher and student architectures; open challenges include domain shift, robustness, fairness, and theoretical understanding of when and why distillation works.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical, Versatile Path to Compact and Generalizable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical suite of techniques that enable deployment of powerful deep models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Across modalities and tasks, KD compresses capacity while retaining much of the teacher's performance, and when combined with representation-level matching, data augmentation, curriculum strategies, meta-learning, or architecture-aware search it can also improve generalization, robustness, and cross-device inclusivity. KD is therefore not merely a model-compression trick but a broadly applicable framework for transferring structure, relational signals, and inductive biases from expensive models into efficient students for real-world use.

papers_seen.author: Hoover
papers_seen.title: Why Knowledge Distillation Should Be the Central Practical Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically validated method for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When treated as the central component of compression pipelines and combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and data-aware engineering (augmentation, curricula, multi-stage or multi-teacher schemes), KD enables deployable models across latency-, memory-, and privacy-constrained settings. Responsible use requires explicit attention to capacity alignment, data limitations, and risks of transferring biases or teacher errors, together with targeted mitigation strategies.

papers_seen.author: Drake

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic set of techniques for producing compact, deployable deep models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Real-world success requires adapting the distillation signals to student capacity, addressing representation mismatch and data limitations, and explicitly auditing for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When paired with representation-aware objectives, careful pre-training of compact models, and safeguards for robustness and privacy, KD enables production-ready reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of a teacher's performance. I argue that KD should be treated as a central tool in model-compression pipelines, not as a single recipe but as a family of methods to be combined with task-aware design choices for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Mccall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression — Powerful but Context‑Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models to smaller student models so they meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD routinely improves student performance relative to training from scratch and composes well with complementary compression methods, but its success depends on student capacity, what signals are transferred, data availability, and explicit handling of robustness, fairness, and distribution shift. Treating KD as the central element of a compression pipeline—rather than a standalone cure—yields the best practical outcomes.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer knowledge from larger, expensive teacher models to smaller, efficient student models. Across vision, language, and other modalities, KD operates at multiple granularities (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or channel maps, and module-level replacements) and can serve both as a compression mechanism and as a broader training paradigm that improves calibration, generalization, and domain adaptation. Practical variants address constraints such as limited or private data, mismatched architectures, and deployment latency; persistent challenges include optimization failure modes, preserving rare-token or low-frequency behavior, and aligning internal representations between heterogeneous teacher–student pairs.

papers_seen.author: Carter
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and widely used approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, faster students that retain much of the teacher’s performance. Over the past decade KD has expanded from simple softened-output matching to a toolkit that includes intermediate-representation alignment, layer-wise and relational objectives, online and multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free workflows. In practice KD is commonly combined with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and requires careful attention to teacher–student capacity, data strategies, and robustness or fairness concerns to succeed in real-world deployments.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Horton
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. A broad set of distillation objectives and workflows—ranging from soft-target/logit matching to intermediate-feature, layerwise, and data-synthesis approaches—enables effective trade-offs between accuracy, latency, and memory for deployment. Practical success depends on choices about which signals to transfer, the data regime and student capacity, and integration with complementary compression techniques; persistent challenges include domain shift, optimization mismatch, and preserving rare or fairness-critical behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Practical Principles for Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-ready approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, faster ones while retaining much of their performance. KD techniques span teacher design, student-teacher layer mapping, multi-teacher and ensemble strategies, data-aware and data-free workflows, and scalable/online training protocols. When combined with task-aware selection and domain adaptation, distillation enables effective deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and heterogeneous-device constraints.

papers_seen.author: Morris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Practical Patterns, Mechanisms, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely used approach to compress large, high-performing deep learning and NLP models into smaller, faster students that are suitable for deployment under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. The literature frames KD as a flexible toolkit—covering soft-label matching, intermediate-representation alignment, relational and attention-based objectives, multi-teacher regimes, and data-free strategies—that typically works best when combined with complementary compression methods and careful data or curriculum design. While KD often preserves much of teacher performance, its success depends on student capacity, signal selection, data availability, and deployment-aware engineering; open challenges include capacity/optimization mismatch, preserving long-tail behaviors, mitigating transferred biases, and enabling reliable distillation without access to original training data.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and flexible approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When integrated with complementary methods and adapted to task and data constraints, KD enables significant reductions in latency, memory, and compute while preserving much of a teacher model’s task performance. However, realizing these gains in real systems requires careful choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to diagnose and mitigate failure modes such as propagation of teacher biases or degraded modeling of rare behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Core of Model Compression — Practical Benefits, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, high-impact approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students across NLP, speech, and vision. Treated as the central element of compression pipelines and combined with representation-level objectives, data strategies, and complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), KD routinely yields favorable size–performance trade-offs. However, realizing these gains in practice requires deliberate teacher–student co‑design, careful handling of data and augmentation, selective transfer of signals, and evaluation for robustness, fairness, and rare-token behavior.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Feature-map-level Online Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Feature maps contain rich information about image intensity and spatial correlation. However, previous online knowledge distillation methods only utilize the class probabilities. Thus in this paper, we propose an online knowledge distillation method that transfers not only the knowledge of the class probabilities but also that of the feature map using the adversarial training framework. We train multiple networks simultaneously by employing discriminators to distinguish the feature map distributions of different networks. Each network has its corresponding discriminator which discriminates the feature map from its own as fake while classifying that of the other network as real. By training a network to fool the corresponding discriminator, it can learn the other network's feature map distribution. We show that our method performs better than the conventional direct alignment method such as L1 and is more suitable for online distillation. Also, we propose a novel cyclic learning scheme for training more than two networks together. We have applied our method to various network architectures on the classification task and discovered a significant improvement of performance especially in the case of training a pair of a small network and a large one.

papers_seen.author: Lynn
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, widely adopted approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers richer supervision than hard labels—soft output distributions, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals—and is typically combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and data strategies (public data, synthesized examples, or data-free protocols). Success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, addressing data and privacy constraints, and explicitly evaluating robustness, fairness, and long‑tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical, Design‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely yields favorable trade-offs between efficiency and retained performance when its signals, data, and teacher–student alignment are chosen deliberately. However, realizing reliable, robust compression requires attention to optimization dynamics, capacity mismatch, data and privacy constraints, and mitigation of transferred biases.
