papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Composable Core of Model Compression: Practical Benefits, Limits, and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated not simply as a single recipe for compression but as the composable core of real-world model-compression pipelines. KD reliably reduces inference cost while preserving much of a teacher’s performance across modalities, and it naturally composes with pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis, and domain-adaptive procedures. To deploy reliable compressed models practitioners must pair KD with careful teacher/student design, data and sample-selection strategies (including data-free synthesis where necessary), evaluation for robustness and fairness, and complementary compression steps that meet hardware constraints. This paper argues for a pragmatic, pipeline-oriented view of KD and outlines targeted practices to maximize utility while mitigating known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Promise, Limits, and Deployment Recipes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and pragmatic approach for compressing large deep learning and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels — from softened outputs to intermediate representations — KD reduces inference cost, memory, and latency while retaining much of teacher performance. Its greatest practical value lies in being a flexible, composable tool: KD integrates with pruning, quantization, architecture search, and data-synthesis strategies to meet diverse deployment constraints. However, KD is not a turnkey solution; careful design is required to address data scarcity and privacy, teacher–student mismatch, optimization instability, and the preservation of rare-token or long-tail behavior. Practical pipelines therefore combine task-aware distillation targets, teacher–student co-design, staged training, and robustness and fairness evaluation to realize reliable compressed systems.

papers_seen.author: Phelps
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Design‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, high‑impact route to compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When KD is treated as the central element of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary techniques—feature alignment, data strategies, projector or adversarial mechanisms, and hardware‑aware design—it achieves strong size/accuracy/latency tradeoffs. Realizing those gains requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to prepare or synthesize data, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to diagnose limits such as bias transfer, distribution shift, and rare‑token fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Charles
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal structure. A broad toolkit has emerged—soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi-teacher and self-distillation, and data-aware or data-free protocols—that, when combined with complementary compression methods and careful teacher–student co-design, yields compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practical success depends on choices about what to transfer, student capacity, data availability, and mitigation of robustness and bias risks.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Solution for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach to compressing large neural models for deployment and domain-specialization. Beyond simple teacher-to-student label matching, modern KD techniques transfer intermediate representations, exploit synthetic or augmented data, operate without original training data, and incorporate privacy or distributed-training constraints. These variants enable retaining much of the teacher performance while reducing inference cost, supporting domain adaptation, improving generalization under limited-data regimes, and meeting privacy or latency requirements for real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has expanded from soft-target matching to a broad toolkit that includes intermediate-representation and attention alignment, layerwise and many-to-many mapping, relational and curriculum schemes, self- and multi-teacher approaches, and data- or privacy-aware procedures. When combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and tuned to deployment constraints (latency, memory, robustness, and privacy), KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance, though open challenges remain around capacity mismatch, distribution shift, rare-token behavior, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Velasquez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context-Sensitive Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, deployment-oriented approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, efficient students. When applied with careful choices about what to transfer (logits, features, attention), how to align teacher and student architectures, and how to handle data and privacy constraints, KD routinely yields compact models that approach teacher performance across vision and language tasks. KD is most effective when combined with complementary techniques—feature projectors, adversarial objectives, student-aware teacher training, and privacy-preserving mechanisms—so that compressed models meet real-world latency, robustness, and deployment requirements.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Domains, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer knowledge from larger, costly models (teachers) into smaller, faster models (students) so that the students retain much of the teachers' accuracy while meeting deployment constraints. Across vision, language, graphs, and generative models, researchers have developed complementary approaches — from matching soft logits to aligning intermediate representations, attention maps, channels, and global embedding topologies — and combined distillation with architecture search, pruning, and continual adaptation. Empirical work shows distillation can produce compact models that preserve or even improve task performance, but success depends on careful alignment of teacher-student inputs/representations, task- and domain-specific strategies, and trade-offs such as bias–variance effects introduced by soft labels. Important challenges remain around layer mismatches, low-frequency token handling, domain shift, and fundamental limits of compressibility for certain model families.

papers_seen.author: Ibarra
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Composable Path for Compressing Deep and NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile technique for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce latency, memory, and power requirements while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD works across modalities and tasks, but its practical success depends on choices about what signal to transfer, how to supply or synthesize training data, and how to combine distillation with complementary compression methods. When applied thoughtfully within a wider compression pipeline, KD enables deployable models for resource-constrained and privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Composable Core of Practical Model Compression — Benefits, Limits, and Guardrails
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and flexible pathway for converting large teacher models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a composable core of a compression pipeline and combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary techniques (pruning, quantization), KD often preserves a large fraction of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, KD is context-sensitive: choices about what signals to transfer (soft logits, intermediate representations, relational signals), how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to handle limited or private data determine real-world outcomes. Robust deployment requires explicit guardrails to mitigate optimization mismatch, domain shift, rare-token and fairness failures, and transferred teacher errors.

papers_seen.author: Cordova
papers_seen.title: What Is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible set of techniques for producing smaller, faster models from larger teachers by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has grown from soft-target matching into a toolbox that includes intermediate-representation alignment, attention and relational transfers, contrastive and feature-level objectives, multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free workflows. Empirical and theoretical work shows KD routinely yields favorable size–performance trade-offs when combined with complementary compression methods and careful data and architecture choices, but its success depends on addressing capacity mismatch, optimization dynamics, data availability, and the risk of transferring undesirable teacher behaviors. This synthesis summarizes core methods, empirical patterns, theoretical insights, practical constraints, and recommended practices for deploying KD in deep learning and NLP contexts.

papers_seen.author: Morris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. The practice has evolved from simple soft-target matching into a multifaceted toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi- and self-teaching, online schemes, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols. Real-world success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data strategies, and combining KD with complementary compression methods and task-aware engineering to mitigate robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift challenges.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context‑Sensitive Engine of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, engineering‑aware component of model compression for deep learning and NLP. KD provides a flexible set of supervisory targets—soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, and relational signals—that, when matched to student capacity and paired with complementary compression primitives and data strategies, yield compact models that approach teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. KD is not a silver bullet: it can transfer teacher weaknesses, suffer under capacity or distribution mismatch, and require data-aware or data‑free solutions and federated adaptations. Effective deployment therefore requires explicit signal selection, architecture‑aware training, diagnostics for robustness and fairness, and composition with pruning, quantization, or architecture search.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and inductive biases from large teacher models to smaller student models so they can meet real-world constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Methods vary by what is transferred (soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention, relational signals), how data are used or synthesized, and whether distillation is combined with other compression tools or automated search. Empirically, KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in size and inference cost, but practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, addressing data or privacy limits, and adapting teachers or objectives to propagate desired properties such as robustness and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Berger
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade KD has evolved from softened-logit matching to a diverse toolbox that includes intermediate-representation alignment, attention- and relation-based objectives, multi-teacher and self-distillation schedules, and data-aware or data-free workflows. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and appropriate data or curriculum engineering, KD enables compact models that meet deployment constraints while preserving much of teacher performance. Persistent challenges include student–teacher capacity mismatch, data scarcity or privacy concerns, robustness under distribution shift, and preserving rare or long‑tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Strategy for Compressing NLP Models: Benefits, Limits, and Practical Recipes
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable ones. In NLP, KD enables retaining much of the teacher model's linguistic capability while reducing storage and inference cost. Effective compression with KD requires more than mimicking final outputs: it benefits from aligning internal representations, task-aware layer mapping, and handling data or privacy constraints with synthetic or metadata-driven techniques. However, KD is not a panacea — distributional heterogeneity, privacy, and mismatches between teacher and student capacity pose real limits that must be mitigated by careful method design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Pitts
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers learned behavior from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving much of the teacher’s capabilities. Across vision and NLP, KD encompasses soft-target (logit) matching, representation- and attention-level alignment, self-distillation, and ensemble or multi-stage pipelines. KD is most effective when embedded in a compression workflow that includes architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, and careful data and curriculum decisions. Key limitations remain around low-frequency or rare-token behavior, data scarcity and distribution shift, optimization and capacity mismatch, and preserving robustness or fairness under transfer. Practical progress requires choosing appropriate distilled signals, aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining KD with complementary compression and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Salinas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has become a practical, flexible core of modern model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. By transferring richer supervisory signals from large teachers into smaller students, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost, memory, and latency while often retaining much of the teachers' capabilities. KD operates across multiple granularities (soft logits, internal features, attention or relational maps) and is most effective when combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression methods. Despite strong empirical successes, open problems remain in handling data scarcity and distribution shift, aligning heterogeneous teacher–student architectures, preserving rare or long-tail behavior, and providing principled theoretical guarantees.

papers_seen.author: Welch
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing deep and language models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. A diverse set of techniques—softened logits, intermediate-representation matching, attention- or relation-based transfers, multi-teacher curricula, and data-aware (including synthetic or data-free) strategies—has been developed and is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation). Practical success requires aligning distilled signals to student capacity, careful data and teacher selection, and explicit evaluation for robustness, rare-case fidelity, and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context‑Sensitive Toolbox for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical centerpiece for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When used thoughtfully — selecting what to transfer, adapting objectives to teacher and student capacities, and combining distillation with complementary methods like pruning, quantization, or data synthesis — KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. However, distillation’s effectiveness varies with task, data regime, and deployment constraints, so practitioners should treat it as a flexible set of techniques rather than a single plug‑and‑play algorithm.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Design‑Sensitive Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the practical heart of model‑compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP: it reliably transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels, enables substantial reductions in inference cost, and composes naturally with complementary techniques. However, KD is not a turnkey cure — its effectiveness depends on careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or private data, and how to evaluate and mitigate failure modes such as distribution shift, rare-token degradation, bias transfer, and privacy leakage. A production-ready approach treats KD as a flexible toolbox integrated with pruning, quantization, architecture design, data strategies (including data‑free methods), and explicit robustness/fairness checks.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Composable Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the composable core of real-world model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP: it provides flexible, information-rich supervision that can be adapted to student capacity and deployment constraints, and when combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary compression primitives it yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. However, effective and responsible deployment requires explicit co-design to handle capacity mismatch, data- and privacy-limited regimes, and robustness or fairness failures.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central Tool for Practical Model Compression in NLP and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, multi-purpose strategy for compressing large deep models while preserving performance. KD can be adapted to constraints common in NLP deployment—limited compute, privacy restrictions, low-latency requirements, and robustness demands—by pairing standard teacher-student training with techniques such as feature-level matching, data augmentation, multi-teacher supervision, and teacher adaptation. Across domains (transformers for NLP, speech embeddings, graph models, generative models), KD consistently enables large reductions in model size or latency with modest accuracy loss, making it a primary method for productionization of deep models.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model compression methods reduce the computational and memory cost of large neural models by transferring information from larger or ensemble teachers to smaller students. Approaches vary from using soft logits to matching internal representations, attention maps, or generator outputs; they have been adapted for modality transfer, privacy- or bandwidth-constrained settings, and specialized architectures (e.g., transformers, GANs). Empirical work shows that representation-level objectives, architectural design of the student/bridge modules, and careful training protocols can preserve most of the teacher’s performance while dramatically reducing size and runtime. Ongoing challenges include preserving rare-token or fine-grained behaviors, deploying under strict privacy/bandwidth constraints, and automating architecture search for compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Berry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context‑Aware Tool for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a practical, flexible pathway to turn large, high‑capacity models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a central, composable element of compression pipelines and combined with complementary techniques and careful data and architecture choices, KD can deliver substantial reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. At the same time, KD has well‑documented limits — capacity mismatch, distributional shift, degradation on rare outputs, and potential transfer of teacher biases — that require task‑aware design, diagnostics, and mitigation strategies. I argue KD should be the default compression tool in production pipelines, used deliberately and in combination with other primitives, rather than as a single turnkey fix.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: No One Left Behind: Inclusive Federated Learning over Heterogeneous Devices
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning (FL) is an important paradigm for training global models from decentralized data in a privacy-preserving way. Existing FL methods usually assume the global model can be trained on any participating client. However, in real applications, the devices of clients are usually heterogeneous, and have different computing power. Although big models like BERT have achieved huge success in AI, it is difficult to apply them to heterogeneous FL with weak clients. The straightforward solutions like removing the weak clients or using a small model to fit all clients will lead to some problems, such as under-representation of dropped clients and inferior accuracy due to data loss or limited model representation ability. In this work, we propose InclusiveFL, a client-inclusive federated learning method to handle this problem. The core idea of InclusiveFL is to assign models of different sizes to clients with different computing capabilities, bigger models for powerful clients and smaller ones for weak clients. We also propose an effective method to share the knowledge among multiple local models with different sizes. In this way, all the clients can participate in the model learning in FL, and the final model can be big and powerful enough. Besides, we propose a momentum knowledge distillation method to better transfer knowledge in big models on powerful clients to the small models on weak clients. Extensive experiments on many real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in learning accurate models from clients with heterogeneous devices under the FL framework.

papers_seen.author: Morris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical Core for Model Compression—Essential but Not Sufficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. It reliably yields substantial efficiency gains by transferring softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals. However, KD’s success in real-world deployments depends on alignment between teacher signals and student capacity, availability or synthesis of appropriate training data, and attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy. Therefore KD should be treated as the central component of an integrated compression pipeline rather than a standalone solution.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. It is applied across modalities and deployment constraints and is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques, careful data and teacher design, and methods that address representation mismatch and optimization. This synthesis summarizes practical techniques, common challenges, and recommended practices for using KD in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Arroyo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Scenarios, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce the computational and storage footprint of large neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller students. Approaches span matching outputs (soft labels), transferring intermediate representations (feature or layer-wise distillation), adapting teacher selection and weighting, and operating under constraints such as missing original data, privacy, or multi-modal inputs. Practical work on language models, vision-language systems, and other domains highlights gains from task-aware selection of distilled information, architectural adapters between teacher and student, and advanced training schemes (e.g., adversarial sample generation, meta-learning of teachers). Empirical results and surveys show KD is versatile: it improves student accuracy over training from scratch, enables deployment in resource-constrained settings, and can be extended to preserve privacy and support domain adaptation, while theoretical and empirical analyses clarify when and why distillation helps and what challenges remain.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Sensitive Path to Compact Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic framework for compressing large, high-performing deep models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. Far from a single recipe, KD encompasses soft-target matching, feature and layer alignment, contrastive and self-supervised variants, and teacher-free or data-scarce regimes. When paired with complementary techniques (pruning, architecture adaptation, projectors, and data strategies), KD enables strong trade-offs between latency, memory, and fidelity — but its success depends on matching the distillation signals, optimization schedule, and data assumptions to the deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Christensen
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly adopted framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. KD methods include matching softened output distributions, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, and transferring relational or layer-wise structure. In practice KD is combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and data strategies (original, augmented, or synthetic) to meet deployment constraints. Success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, choosing or generating suitable data, and explicitly evaluating robustness, fairness, and long‑tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Practical, Versatile Path to Compact and Generalizable Deep Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has matured into a practical suite of techniques that enable deployment of powerful deep models in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Across modalities and tasks, KD compresses capacity while retaining much of the teacher's performance, and when combined with representation-level matching, data augmentation, curriculum strategies, meta-learning, or architecture-aware search it can also improve generalization, robustness, and cross-device inclusivity. KD is therefore not merely a model-compression trick but a broadly applicable framework for transferring structure, relational signals, and inductive biases from expensive models into efficient students for real-world use.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach for converting large, high-performance models into smaller, deployable students by transferring information beyond hard labels. Over the past decade KD has evolved into a toolkit that includes softened-output matching, intermediate-representation alignment, attention and relational transfers, multi-teacher and online schedules, and data-aware or data-free variants. KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and when distillation choices are matched to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. Despite strong empirical gains, open challenges remain around robustness, rare-event behavior, domain shift, privacy, and theoretical understanding.

papers_seen.author: Ortega
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. KD is versatile across modalities and workflows: it can match softened logits, align intermediate representations or attention maps, operate with or without original training data, and integrate with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Practical success requires careful teacher–student co‑design, data and signal selection, staged training, and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, and domain generalization. Despite strong empirical gains in efficiency and deployability, open problems remain in theoretical understanding, robustness under distribution shift, preserving rare or long-tail behaviors, and avoiding transfer of teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Carroll
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Practices in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable set of techniques for transferring behavior from large “teacher” models to smaller “student” models to reduce inference cost and enable deployment. KD spans simple soft-target matching to richer objectives that align intermediate representations, attention maps, or relational structure, and it is commonly combined with architecture search, pruning, or quantization. Success depends on careful choices about what signals to transfer, student capacity, training data (including synthesized or distilled datasets), and evaluation for robustness, fairness, and distribution shift. This article synthesizes core methods, empirical patterns, and practical recommendations that guide the use of KD in NLP and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and allied compression techniques transfer information from large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable students so systems meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of the teacher’s effectiveness. The literature shows a spectrum of distillation targets — softened logits, intermediate features and attention maps, relational structure, and iterative or multi-teacher curricula — and complementary methods such as pruning, layer skipping, module replacement, and data synthesis. Practical success depends on aligning what is transferred to student capacity, handling limited or private data, and combining KD with architecture-aware design and validation to avoid optimization mismatches and unwanted bias transfer. Remaining gaps include robustness under domain shift, principled selection of distilled signals, and theoretical accounts that predict when KD will provide large gains.

papers_seen.author: Archer
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Core, Practical Tool for Compression — Strengths, Limits, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical method for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. It succeeds by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone (e.g., softened logits, intermediate representations, or relational signals), and by combining with complementary techniques (pruning, low-precision inference, architecture search, and data augmentation). KD enables substantial reductions in model size and latency while retaining much of teacher performance, but its effectiveness depends on careful choices about what to transfer, which examples to use, and how to adapt teachers and students to deployment constraints. Thoughtful design — including feature-level transfer, curriculum or selective-sample strategies, augmentation, and data-free synthesis when needed — makes KD a practical cornerstone of model compression for deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Path to Deployable NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models deliver state-of-the-art results in many NLP tasks but are often too large or too costly for real-world deployment. Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques enable retaining much of the teacher's performance while reducing model size and inference cost. Advances in task-aware, layer-wise, data-free, and adversarially-informed distillation methods demonstrate that KD can address capacity mismatch, data scarcity, robustness, and heterogeneity in deployment environments, making it a central tool for practical NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Perkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for producing smaller, faster models that retain much of the behavior of larger teachers. KD encompasses a range of targets (soft outputs, intermediate representations, relational signals), training regimes (offline teacher-student, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher), and data strategies (use of original data, synthetic or data-free methods, privacy-aware workflows). In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when design choices—what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to handle data constraints—are matched to the deployment context. Promising empirical results across vision, language, generative models, and novel-view synthesis coexist with persistent challenges in robustness, low-frequency behavior, transferred biases, and theoretical understanding, motivating careful pipeline design and continued research.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge distillation from multi-modal to mono-modal segmentation networks
papers_seen.abstract: The joint use of multiple imaging modalities for medical image segmentation has been widely studied in recent years. The fusion of information from different modalities has demonstrated to improve the segmentation accuracy, with respect to mono-modal segmentations, in several applications. However, acquiring multiple modalities is usually not possible in a clinical setting due to a limited number of physicians and scanners, and to limit costs and scan time. Most of the time, only one modality is acquired. In this paper, we propose KD-Net, a framework to transfer knowledge from a trained multi-modal network (teacher) to a mono-modal one (student). The proposed method is an adaptation of the generalized distillation framework where the student network is trained on a subset (1 modality) of the teacher's inputs (n modalities). We illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework in brain tumor segmentation with the BraTS 2018 dataset. Using different architectures, we show that the student network effectively learns from the teacher and always outperforms the baseline mono-modal network in terms of segmentation accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Garrison
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used set of techniques for transferring information from large teacher models into smaller student models so that students can be deployed under latency, memory, or privacy constraints. Methods include matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations or attention maps, and training-time schemes such as online, self-, and multi-teacher distillation; KD is typically combined with pruning, quantization, or architecture redesign to meet deployment goals. Practical outcomes depend strongly on student capacity, data availability and quality, the choice of distilled signals, and careful pipeline design; open issues remain around robustness, fairness, long-tail behavior, heterogeneous architecture alignment, and distillation under data- or privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a compression trick: it is a flexible training paradigm that enables deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. By choosing what to transfer (soft targets, intermediate features, or relational signals), how to generate or select data (real, public, or synthesized), and how to schedule and regularize student training, practitioners can shape trade-offs among accuracy, robustness, interpretability, and privacy. KD’s effectiveness depends on careful alignment of teacher signals, student capacity, and data regime; when combined with multi-teacher strategies, adversarial data synthesis, or differential-privacy mechanisms, KD supports practical deployment across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Avila
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring supervisory signals richer than hard labels. A broad toolkit exists—soft logits, intermediate-feature alignment, attention or relational signals, multi-teacher and self-distillation schedules, and data strategies that range from using original datasets to synthetic or data-free approaches. KD is most effective when treated as a composable part of a compression pipeline that includes pruning, quantization, or architecture redesign, and when distillation objectives and curricula are matched to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. Remaining practical challenges center on teacher–student mismatch, degraded long-tail or rare-token behavior, distribution shift, privacy constraints, and the potential propagation of teacher biases.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical Core for Compressing NLP Models — Benefits, Mechanisms, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile strategy for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students in NLP. When designed to transfer not only soft outputs but also internal representations and task-aware layer mappings, and when combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, synthetic or privacy-aware data), KD yields strong size–performance trade-offs. However, KD is not a universal solution: capacity mismatch, limited or private data, optimization dynamics, and the risk of transferring harmful behaviors or failing on low-frequency phenomena require careful method design, diagnostics, and often hybrid compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Garrett
papers_seen.title: Position: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression, with Design-Sensitive Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical core of model-compression pipelines in deep learning and NLP because it transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels and reliably improves student performance under resource constraints. However, KD is not a plug-and-play cure: real-world deployment requires careful choices about what to transfer, teacher–student co-design, data strategies (including data-free or domain-adaptive approaches), and complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to address capacity mismatch, distribution shift, rare-token behavior, and fairness or privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical, Design-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an effective, widely used approach for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD reduces inference cost and memory while often retaining much of a teacher’s performance by transferring softened outputs, intermediate representations, attention or relational signals, and by using tailored data strategies. Its practical success depends on careful design choices—what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to obtain or synthesize training data, and how to combine KD with complementary compression methods. KD is a powerful tool but not automatic: addressing capacity mismatch, data scarcity, distributional shift, and the risk of transferring undesirable teacher behaviors requires pipeline-aware engineering and explicit robustness and fairness evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. Over the past decade KD has grown from simple soft-target matching into a flexible toolkit that includes representation-level alignment, multi-stage and multi-teacher schemes, data-free and federated protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Empirically, KD often yields substantial gains in student performance versus training from scratch and enables deployment under constraints of latency, memory, and privacy, but outcomes depend on choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and checks for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Bruce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Careful, Deployment‑Aware Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for producing compact models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Treated as a flexible toolkit rather than a single algorithm, KD can be combined with complementary compression methods and data strategies to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Effective use of KD requires deliberate choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to evaluate and mitigate robustness, fairness, and distributional risks.

papers_seen.author: Turner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD can preserve much of teacher performance while meeting constraints of latency, memory, privacy, and heterogeneous deployment. Realizing KD's full value requires combining soft-target transfer with representation-level objectives, curriculum or staged training, teacher optimization, and architecture-aware mapping, and it also demands attention to distribution shift, rare-token fidelity, and teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and Engineering Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile method for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD can preserve much of a teacher’s predictive behavior and representations while reducing latency, memory, and sometimes improving generalization in resource-constrained or domain-specific settings. However, KD is not a plug-and-play solution: its effectiveness depends on the choice of distilled signals, alignment of teacher and student capacity, data availability (or synthesis), and attention to robustness, rare-token fidelity, and privacy. Best results come from treating KD as a central but composable component of a broader compression pipeline that also uses architecture-aware design, data curricula, and evaluation beyond aggregate accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible family of methods for transferring supervisory signals from larger teacher models to smaller student models so that compact models can be deployed under compute, latency, memory, or privacy constraints. KD encompasses soft-target matching, intermediate-representation and attention alignment, relational or feature-level transfers, multi-teacher and self-distillation regimes, and data-aware workflows including data-free synthesis. When combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and careful choice of data and training curricula, KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Realizing reliable gains in practice requires careful design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity and architecture, how to handle limited or no original data, and how to detect and mitigate failure modes such as capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Context-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical and versatile approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable ones. When engineered as part of a broader compression pipeline—selecting which teacher signals to transfer, aligning student architectures, and combining distillation with pruning, quantization, or low-precision training—distillation enables large reductions in latency, memory, and energy while preserving much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness depends on careful choices about distilled signals, data regimes, and mitigation of teacher or distributional failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Applications, and Practical Considerations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring useful predictive behavior, representations, or inductive biases. A diverse set of distillation strategies—matching soft logits, aligning intermediate features or attention maps, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, data-free synthesis, and task-aware adaptations—has been developed to preserve performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Practice-oriented work emphasizes matching the distillation technique to the task, addressing data or privacy limits via synthetic examples or adversarial generation, and combining distillation with architecture and optimization adjustments to close remaining gaps. Empirical successes across language, vision, speech, graphs, and ranking systems show substantial speed and size improvements, though limits remain around distribution shift, teacher–student mismatch, and heterogeneous or federated data settings.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Core, Practical Tool for Model Compression in NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, versatile approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students while preserving much of their performance. KD works across modalities and tasks, and its effectiveness depends on matching distillation techniques to data and deployment constraints. When combined with careful model and data design, KD enables practical deployment of advanced models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Gordon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for transferring behavior from large teachers to smaller students so compact models can meet deployment constraints. Treated as the central component of compression workflows and combined with architecture-aware design, data strategies, and complementary primitives (pruning, quantization, progressive replacement), KD routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs in vision, speech, and NLP. However, KD has systematic failure modes—capacity mismatch, degraded rare-token or tail behavior, transferred biases, and sensitivity to data availability and distribution shift—that require explicit mitigation through careful teacher–student co-design, targeted objectives, and data or curriculum strategies.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or inductive biases so students retain much of the teacher's utility while reducing inference cost. A broad toolkit — matching soft logits, aligning internal features or attention, self-distillation, multi-teacher schemes, data synthesis or data-free approaches, and combining distillation with architecture search, pruning, or quantization — has been developed and adapted across modalities. Practical deployment requires matching the distillation strategy to task constraints, handling data or privacy limits, and addressing capacity and distributional mismatches to produce robust, deployable compact models.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as an Essential but Context‑Sensitive Toolbox for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical centerpiece for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. When used thoughtfully — selecting what to transfer, adapting objectives to teacher and student capacities, and combining distillation with complementary methods like pruning, quantization, or data synthesis — KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. However, distillation’s effectiveness varies with task, data regime, and deployment constraints, so practitioners should treat it as a flexible set of techniques rather than a single plug‑and‑play algorithm.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost while retaining much of the teacher's performance. KD methods operate at multiple granularities (soft-label/logit matching, intermediate-feature imitation, module- or layer-wise mapping) and appear across domains including NLP, vision, multimodal, federated, and graph settings. Practical pipelines combine KD with data strategies, teacher adaptation, and complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture search), but open challenges remain around data heterogeneity, teacher imperfections, and preserving properties such as low-frequency token fidelity, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large neural models by transferring information from a high-capacity teacher to a smaller student so the student retains much of the teacher’s predictive power while using less compute, memory, or latency. The literature has expanded KD beyond matching teacher soft-labels to include intermediate-feature and layer-wise matching, online/self-distillation, data-free and privacy-aware methods, and combinations with architectural compression (pruning, quantization, and architecture search). Empirical results across vision, NLP, speech, graphs, and ranking show that distilled students often recover a large fraction of teacher performance, but practical success depends on choices like teacher design, student capacity, layer alignment, data availability, and training schedules. Remaining challenges include handling low-frequency or fine-grained behaviors, optimization and capacity mismatch, matching heterogeneous architectures, and distilling under privacy or data-scarce constraints.

papers_seen.author: Terry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Trade-offs, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior, intermediate representations, or relational signals. Over the last decade KD has evolved from soft-label matching into a flexible toolbox—incorporating feature- and layer-level objectives, multi-teacher and self-distillation regimes, data synthesis or data-free workflows, and integrations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to align architectures and capacities, what data to use (or synthesize), and how to mitigate robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift problems.

papers_seen.author: Mcdaniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated approach for converting large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. Treated as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables preservation of much of a teacher’s capabilities while meeting real-world constraints such as latency, memory, and power. Its practical value comes from the variety of signals it can transfer (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational structure), the ability to combine KD with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation), and adaptability to data-limited or privacy-sensitive settings. However, realizing KD’s benefits in production requires deliberate engineering: matching distilled signals to student capacity, addressing distributional and rare-token failures, and integrating KD into broader compression pipelines.

papers_seen.author: Harrell
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques have become central tools to deploy high-capacity deep models in latency-, memory-, privacy-, and compute-constrained settings. Across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains, practitioners use teacher-student training, feature-level transfer, data-free distillation, and hybrid pipelines that combine pruning or architecture search with distillation. Work in this area balances fidelity to teacher models, robustness, and efficiency, and explores trade-offs such as reliance on original training data, communication overhead in federated settings, and the benefits of designing students or student-friendly teachers. The literature shows repeated success of KD when tailored to the task and constraints, while also revealing limitations under severe data heterogeneity or adversarial settings.

papers_seen.author: Fuller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large “teacher” models into smaller “student” models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. KD spans soft-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, attention/relational objectives, and data strategies that include using original data, augmentation, or synthesized examples. When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and matched to deployment constraints, KD reliably improves size/accuracy/latency trade-offs across vision and language tasks. Practical success depends on design choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to evaluate and mitigate limits such as bias transfer, rare-token degradation, and robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile, and broadly applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in NLP and other modalities. KD reliably improves size–performance trade-offs when its design is matched to student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, but it requires engineering choices and complementary techniques to address robustness, fairness, and data limitations.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have matured into a diverse set of approaches that trade off capacity, latency, and privacy to deploy high-performing deep models in constrained settings. Methods operate at different places in the training pipeline: compressing via soft-targets, transferring intermediate representations, searching or adapting compact architectures, or avoiding access to original data. Work across modalities (vision, language, graphs, generative models, and medical imaging) shows that careful choice of what to transfer (logits, relations, feature directions, layer mappings) and how to transfer it (attention, contrastive alignment, adversarial generators, or task-aware filters) determines final student performance. Practical concerns such as domain adaptation, federated and heterogeneous-device settings, and data augmentation interact strongly with distillation design choices. The literature suggests a clear pattern: representation-level and layer-aware transfers often outperform naive logits-only approaches for structured or pre-trained models, while teacher-free, data-free, and communication-efficient variants enable distillation under realistic deployment constraints.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core Practical Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. KD variants—soft-target matching, intermediate-representation matching, self- and online-distillation, and data-free (zero-shot) synthesis—enable latency, memory, and privacy gains across vision and language tasks. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: its success depends on what signals are distilled, teacher quality, data availability or synthesis, and pipeline choices (layer mapping, curricula, and complementary compression). I argue KD should be treated as the central component of compression pipelines, applied with task-aware design and combined with other methods to manage its limitations and maximize deployment utility.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Practical Core of Model Compression — Central, Useful, but Not Enough Alone
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and empirically effective approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When engineered to match student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints, KD produces strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs and integrates well with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies. However, KD must be combined with representation-aware objectives, task-aware layer mapping, and safeguards for robustness and fairness to avoid transferring teacher imperfections and to preserve rare or out-of-distribution behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods for Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and model compression have become central to deploying large deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research spans a range of goals — shrinking model size and latency, preserving privacy, enabling distributed learning, and retaining task- or robustness-related properties — and a correspondingly diverse set of techniques including logit and feature matching, layer-wise and many-to-many mapping, adversarial generation of training examples, and architecture-aware pruning and replacement. Empirical work shows effective trade-offs across vision, multimodal, and language tasks, while recent methods also tackle practical constraints such as lack of original data, privacy requirements, and distributed communication budgets.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis of Provided Works
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. The family of KD methods includes soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate representation and attention alignment, feature- and layer-wise objectives, multi-teacher and online/self-distillation schedules, and techniques for operating without original training data or under privacy constraints. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when the distillation signals, data strategy, and student capacity are chosen to match deployment constraints. Remaining challenges include capacity mismatch, domain shift, preservation of low-frequency or rare behaviors, transferred biases, and data- or privacy-limited settings.

papers_seen.author: Simmons
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Default Core of Model Compression — Practical Promise and Necessary Guardrails
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the default backbone for practical model compression in deep learning and NLP because it provides a flexible, task‑aware way to transfer a large teacher’s behavior into a smaller, deployable student. However, real-world deployment requires explicit design choices and safeguards—about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, how to manage or synthesize data, and how to test and mitigate risks to robustness, fairness, and rare‑token fidelity. With these guardrails, KD combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) yields the best path to compact, reliable models.
