papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the central, practical element of model-compression pipelines: a flexible toolbox that transfers richer supervision from large teachers into smaller, deployable students. When designed as a context-sensitive process—choosing what signals to transfer, adapting teacher and student architectures, and combining distillation with complementary compression methods—KD routinely yields favorable trade-offs between efficiency and retained performance. However, realizing KD’s full potential requires explicit attention to data availability and privacy, robustness and fairness, capacity mismatch, and deployment constraints.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practitioner-oriented approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. Its practical success depends on deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to obtain or synthesize data, and how to detect and mitigate robustness and fairness issues. I argue KD should be the core of model-compression strategies but must be applied with task-aware design, complementary compression techniques, and careful diagnostics to manage known failure modes.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Compression: Effective but Context-Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a powerful and practical approach to compress large neural models into smaller, faster, or more hardware-friendly students while retaining much of teacher performance. Its effectiveness spans supervised, self-supervised, and cross-modal settings, but the choice of what to transfer (logits, features, intermediate representations, attention), how to measure discrepancy, and how to combine KD with pruning or quantization critically determines success. I argue that KD should be treated as a toolbox of complementary techniques whose components must be matched to task, teacher quality, and deployment constraints to obtain reliable and robust compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Butler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Representation‑Aware Core of Practical Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible training paradigm for producing compact deep and language models that meet real deployment constraints. By transferring richer supervision than hard labels—ranging from softened outputs to intermediate representations and relational signals—KD enables substantial reductions in parameter count and inference cost while often preserving most of a teacher’s performance. Realistic compression pipelines pair KD with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful data strategies (real, public, synthesized, or data‑free) to balance accuracy, latency, and privacy. Responsible deployment requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student capacity, and how to evaluate robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Davenport
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger, often ensemble or pretrained teacher models into smaller, faster student models so they can be deployed under resource, latency, or privacy constraints. KD methods extend beyond matching hard labels to include softened outputs, intermediate feature or attention alignment, and relational or module-level supervision. In practice KD is combined with augmentation, architecture-aware design, pruning and quantization, and data-synthesis strategies to produce compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, handling limited or private data, and explicitly evaluating robustness, fairness, and domain generalization. Important open problems remain in principled data selection or synthesis, automating architecture choices for compression, and controlling transfer of undesirable teacher behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Capabilities, Limits, and Engineering Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-ready approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely improves size–performance trade-offs by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone, but it is not a silver bullet: its best results come when combined with complementary compression methods, careful choice of what to transfer, and explicit attention to data regimes, capacity matching, and fairness or robustness concerns. This essay argues KD should be treated as the central, engineering-ready backbone of compression pipelines while practitioners mitigate known failure modes through targeted design and monitoring.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. The literature frames distillation as a multifaceted toolkit — including soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi- and self-teaching, and data-free or privacy-aware protocols — that is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods and task-aware engineering. Practical success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity and data constraints, and on explicitly addressing failure modes such as transferred biases, optimization mismatch, and poor handling of low-frequency phenomena.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, widely adopted approach for compressing large teacher models into smaller, deployable students in vision, language, graph, and multimodal settings. KD transfers information at multiple granularities (soft outputs, intermediate features, attention and relational signals), composes with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and adapts to constrained-data or privacy-sensitive regimes. Empirical and practical work shows KD often yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, but reliable results require careful choices about what to transfer, student preparation and capacity, data sourcing or synthesis, and explicit mitigation of transferred biases and robustness failures.

papers_seen.author: Fields
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. A broad toolkit has emerged—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring attention or relational signals, and using data-aware or data-free synthesis—often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. KD frequently acts both as an additional task signal and as a regularizer, producing favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when adapted to student capacity and data regimes. Key practical issues include selecting what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student layers, handling limited or private data, avoiding transfer of teacher artifacts, and preserving long-tail or robustness properties.

papers_seen.author: Santiago
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Task‑Aware Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile method for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. When used as the central, composable component of compression pipelines and combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation, and data strategies), KD routinely delivers large reductions in latency, memory, and energy while retaining much of teacher performance. Its real-world success requires task‑aware choices about which signals to transfer (soft logits, features, attention or relational maps), how to align teacher and student capacity, what data to use or synthesize, and what safeguards to adopt for robustness, fairness, and privacy. I argue that KD should be treated as the core tool in model compression but applied with explicit diagnostics, curricula, and integration with other compression techniques to manage its known failure modes and maximize practical utility.

papers_seen.author: Vaughn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and versatile approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. Effective deployment requires matching distillation signals and workflows to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints, and combining KD with complementary compression techniques when necessary.

papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is an engineering-centered, flexible paradigm for producing compact models that preserve much of the performance of larger teacher models. KD encompasses a range of signals (soft labels, intermediate representations, relational targets), training schedules (multi-stage, online, self-distillation), and data practices (original data, augmentation, or data-free synthesis). Its practical success depends on aligning teacher signals to student capacity and deployment constraints, and on combining KD with complementary compression methods when necessary. KD also acts beyond compression as a regularizer that can improve generalization and robustness, but it can propagate teacher imperfections and is sensitive to data and architecture mismatch.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Practices, and Limits
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a widely used paradigm for transferring information from large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster student models so they can be deployed under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. The field has evolved from simple soft-label matching to a diverse toolbox that includes feature- and layer-level imitation, multi-teacher and progressive schedules, data-free or synthetic-data approaches, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. KD is effective in many modalities (vision, language, speech, graphs), but practical success requires matching the distillation signals and training schedule to student capacity, addressing data availability or privacy constraints, and mitigating risks such as bias transfer and degraded performance on rare behaviors or out-of-distribution inputs.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision and language tasks KD encompasses soft-target matching, intermediate feature and layer-wise alignment, adversarial and data-free generation, and task-aware layer mapping. Empirical evidence shows KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while often preserving or improving generalization, but success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, and how to handle limited or absent original training data. Practical deployments combine KD with complementary compression methods and careful data or curriculum design to balance accuracy, robustness, and resource constraints.

papers_seen.author: Romero
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A broad set of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention or relational signals), training regimes (offline, online/self-distillation, multi-teacher), and data strategies (original, public, synthesized, or data-free) have been developed. Distillation is typically used as the central component of a broader compression pipeline that includes pruning, quantization, and architecture design; its practical success depends on matching transfer signals to student capacity, teacher quality, and data availability while attending to robustness, fairness, and distribution-shift concerns.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce compute, memory, and latency while preserving task performance. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, KD has been adapted into many forms—soft-target matching, intermediate representation alignment, attention and relational transfers, multi-teacher ensembles, online distillation, and task-adaptive pipelines—and combined with orthogonal compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) to enable deployment in resource-constrained or privacy-sensitive settings. Empirical work shows KD often recovers most of a teacher's utility in a much smaller footprint, but success depends on teacher quality, the choice of distilled signals, data availability and domain shift, and robustness and privacy constraints. The field continues to refine objectives, layer-mapping strategies, and workflows that make distillation effective across modalities and large pretrained models in practical deployments.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from large teacher models into smaller student models to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Across vision, speech, and language tasks KD spans soft-target (logit) matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, self- and multi-teacher schedules, and data-aware or data-free workflows. Best practice treats KD as a central element of a broader compression pipeline—combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design—and adapts targets, data, and curricula to task and deployment constraints. Key open issues include representation alignment across architectures, propagated teacher biases, robustness under domain shift, and preserving rare or low-frequency behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Weber
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. The field encompasses matching softened teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations and attention, online/cooperative schemes, and data- or privacy-aware variants. Distillation routinely combines with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet latency, memory, and regulatory constraints. Practical effectiveness depends on choices about which signals to transfer, how to align heterogeneous architectures, how to source or synthesize training data, and how to preserve robustness, rare-token behavior, and fairness under distributional shift.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Ramsey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Student’s Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically grounded approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Treated as a central component of compression pipelines and combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies), KD can produce compact models that retain much of teacher performance. However, realizing KD’s practical promise requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to provide or synthesize data, and how to diagnose and mitigate failure modes such as capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, context‑sensitive mechanism in practical model compression. When carefully designed and combined with complementary tools — pruning, quantization, architecture search, synthetic or privacy‑aware data, and task‑aware curricula — KD produces compact models that retain much of a teacher’s performance across modalities and deployment constraints. However, KD is not automatic: success requires explicit choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or private data, and how to mitigate harmful teacher behaviors. A principled KD pipeline that adapts to task, data, and hardware needs yields the best tradeoff between efficiency and utility.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a pragmatic pathway to produce compact, efficient models from large teachers while preserving much of their performance. When thoughtfully combined with complementary techniques—representation-level objectives, architecture-aware student design, data strategies including data-free or privacy-sensitive workflows, and targeted optimization—KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and heterogeneity constraints. However, realizing these gains requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity, optimization dynamics, and data issues; failures and trade-offs are documented and can be managed with targeted practices.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central practical tool for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably delivers strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs when its objectives, data, and architectural choices are matched to the student’s capacity and deployment constraints. However, KD is not a plug-and-play remedy: robust, fair, and private compression requires pre-training, careful signal selection, alignment strategies, and combination with complementary methods such as pruning and quantization.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.

papers_seen.author: Curry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically effective technique for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a central component of a compression pipeline and combined with complementary methods (architecture adaptation, pruning, quantization, data strategies, and careful training curricula), KD reliably improves size–performance tradeoffs while requiring design choices that address capacity mismatch, data availability, and robustness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical, Multifaceted Tool for Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is more than a compression trick: it is a flexible training paradigm that enables deployment of high-performing models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. By choosing what to transfer (soft targets, intermediate features, or relational signals), how to generate or select data (real, public, or synthesized), and how to schedule and regularize student training, practitioners can shape trade-offs among accuracy, robustness, interpretability, and privacy. KD’s effectiveness depends on careful alignment of teacher signals, student capacity, and data regime; when combined with multi-teacher strategies, adversarial data synthesis, or differential-privacy mechanisms, KD supports practical deployment across vision, language, graph, and multimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Drake
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical, Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic set of techniques for producing compact, deployable deep models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When treated as a central, composable component of an engineering pipeline and combined with complementary compression tools and careful data and evaluation practices, KD yields strong size/performance/latency tradeoffs. Real-world success requires adapting the distillation signals to student capacity, addressing representation mismatch and data limitations, and explicitly auditing for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Pennington
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing deep and language models into smaller, faster students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Techniques vary in what is transferred (soft outputs, internal representations, attention, relational signals), how data are used or synthesized, and how distillation is combined with complementary compression methods; practical success depends on aligning signals to student capacity and deployment constraints while mitigating known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Elliott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile, and broadly applicable approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students in NLP and other modalities. KD reliably improves size–performance trade-offs when its design is matched to student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, but it requires engineering choices and complementary techniques to address robustness, fairness, and data limitations.

papers_seen.author: Reese
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Evidence, and Practical Trade-offs
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Over the past decade the technique has expanded from softened-logit matching to a toolbox that includes intermediate-feature and attention alignment, layer-wise mapping, multi-teacher and online schemes, and data-aware or data-free workflows. When combined with complementary compression strategies (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign) and task-aware engineering, distillation routinely yields strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs; however, success depends on student capacity, data regime, and careful mitigation of failure modes such as teacher–student mismatch, optimization gaps, distribution shift, privacy constraints, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Rivas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical approach for compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers information beyond hard labels — via softened outputs, intermediate representations, relational structure, or training curricula — to produce compact models that trade only a small fraction of predictive performance for large gains in latency, memory, and deployability. Across modalities and tasks, KD is best applied as part of a broader compression pipeline (including pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design) and requires attention to teacher quality, distilled signals, data strategy, and evaluation for robustness and fairness to realize reliable production systems.

papers_seen.author: Webb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position and Recommendations
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-ready approach for shrinking large deep and pretrained models into smaller, deployable students. KD transfers richer supervision than hard labels—soft outputs, intermediate representations, attention, or relational signals—and composes naturally with pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, and data-aware strategies. Treated as the central component of an engineered compression pipeline, KD enables large reductions in inference cost while retaining much of teacher performance, but it requires deliberate design to address capacity mismatch, data limitations, robustness, and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Composable Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the central, practical element of model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. When used as a composable toolkit — combining soft-targets, intermediate-representation transfer, data-aware curricula, and complementary compression primitives — KD produces compact, deployable models that retain much of teacher performance. Real-world success requires careful alignment of distilled signals to student capacity, data strategies (including synthetic or data-free options when needed), and explicit checks for robustness, rare-token fidelity, privacy, and bias. With these safeguards and complementary methods, KD yields efficient models suited to production constraints.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. The method spans simple soft-target (logit) matching to richer strategies that align internal representations, use synthetic or unlabeled data, or apply curriculum and online schemes. When combined with architecture-aware design, pruning or quantization, and deployment-aware data strategies, KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance. However, KD’s success depends on choices about the distillation signal, data availability, teacher–student alignment, and handling of optimization or distributional limits; careful method design and evaluation are required to produce robust, fair, and deployable compressed models.

papers_seen.author: Short
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Central but Design‑Sensitive Engine for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, versatile approach for turning large, high‑performing models into smaller, deployable students. When matched to deployment objectives and combined with complementary compression methods, KD can recover most of a teacher’s utility while delivering substantial gains in latency, memory, and energy. However, distillation is context‑sensitive: the distilled signals, student capacity, data regime, and privacy or fairness constraints all shape outcomes. Treating KD as an essential but configurable toolbox—rather than a single plug‑and‑play algorithm—yields the most reliable production results.

papers_seen.author: Hamilton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable approach for compressing large deep models into compact students that meet real-world constraints on latency, memory, and deployment. When matched to task needs and combined with representation-aware objectives, data strategies, and robustness or privacy-aware adaptations, KD enables small models to retain much of teachers' performance across modalities. However, KD is context-sensitive: teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and the chosen distillation signal determine outcomes. A pragmatic pipeline blends logit and feature matching, targeted data augmentation or synthesis, and complementary compression methods to achieve robust, efficient deployment.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: The Practical Core of Model Compression — Central, Useful, but Not Enough Alone
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible and empirically effective approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When engineered to match student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints, KD produces strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs and integrates well with pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies. However, KD must be combined with representation-aware objectives, task-aware layer mapping, and safeguards for robustness and fairness to avoid transferring teacher imperfections and to preserve rare or out-of-distribution behaviors.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce the size, memory, and inference cost of large neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. Across tasks and modalities—classification, detection, generative modeling, retrieval, and NLP—research has developed logits-based, feature-based, and task-adapted distillation strategies, multi-teacher and ensemble approaches, privacy- and communication-conscious protocols for distributed settings, and teacher-optimization/meta-learning variants. These methods trade off fidelity to teacher behavior with student capacity, expose failure modes (e.g., transfer of low-frequency lexical mistakes or overfitting of student features), and introduce remedies such as selective sample distillation, feature projectors, adversarially-informed samples, and staged or multi-teacher curricula. While KD consistently improves compact models compared to training from scratch and enables deployment on resource-constrained platforms, open issues remain in robustness, task-specific alignment, and distillation under data heterogeneity.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Advantages, Limits, and Design Guidelines
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic framework for producing compact, deployable models from large teachers by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. When integrated with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and thoughtful data strategies, KD routinely yields strong size–performance trade-offs across vision and language tasks. However, realizing KD’s full potential in production demands context-sensitive choices about what signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to address robustness, fairness, privacy, and domain-shift concerns. I argue KD should be treated as the central, configurable element of compression pipelines, paired with concrete safeguards and evaluation practices to avoid well-known failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Schwartz
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible paradigm for producing compact models that preserve much of the performance of larger teachers. By transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels—ranging from softened outputs to internal representations and relational objectives—KD composes naturally with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design to meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, privacy). Successful application requires careful choices about distilled signals, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and explicit validation for robustness and long-tail behaviors.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, efficient students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone. The approach has expanded from soft-logit matching to include intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi-teacher and curriculum schemes, self-distillation, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture design. Practical deployments succeed when distillation objectives, teacher–student alignment, data strategies, and task-aware choices are tuned to the application; remaining challenges include preserving rare-token or long-tail behaviors, handling distribution shift and data scarcity, and ensuring robustness and privacy in deployed students.

papers_seen.author: Colon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile and practical approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. When applied thoughtfully — choosing what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining KD with complementary compression methods and data strategies — KD enables large reductions in inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. However, KD is context-sensitive: its success depends on data availability, capacity matching, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Practical but Design-Sensitive Path to Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly useful family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models to smaller students to reduce inference cost and enable deployment. KD has been instantiated as matching soft targets, aligning intermediate representations, progressive module replacement, and selective or multi-teacher schemes. While KD often yields strong empirical gains and enables domain- and task-specific compression, its success depends on optimization dynamics, the choice of distilled signal, data quality and selection, and teacher–student alignment. Careful method choices make KD a reliable, production-ready compression strategy, but it is not a universal shortcut: practitioners must tailor KD objectives and protocols to their constraints and goals.

papers_seen.author: Drake
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical, Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic set of techniques for producing compact, deployable deep models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. When treated as a central, composable component of an engineering pipeline and combined with complementary compression tools and careful data and evaluation practices, KD yields strong size/performance/latency tradeoffs. Real-world success requires adapting the distillation signals to student capacity, addressing representation mismatch and data limitations, and explicitly auditing for robustness, fairness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Pope
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, deployable approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, resource-efficient students. Across vision, speech, and language tasks, KD consistently yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when designers choose appropriate distilled signals, handle data limitations, and integrate KD with complementary compression techniques. However, KD is not automatic: its practical success depends on teacher quality, the form of transferred knowledge, data availability (or synthetic-data substitutes), and task-aware training curricula. When combined with feature-level methods, projectors, curriculum strategies, and privacy- or device-aware protocols, KD enables compact models that remain useful in production while requiring careful engineering to avoid optimization and fairness pitfalls.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context-Sensitive Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central practical tool for compressing large deep and NLP models into smaller, deployable students. KD reliably delivers strong accuracy-efficiency trade-offs when its objectives, data, and architectural choices are matched to the student’s capacity and deployment constraints. However, KD is not a plug-and-play remedy: robust, fair, and private compression requires pre-training, careful signal selection, alignment strategies, and combination with complementary methods such as pruning and quantization.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Engineering Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, versatile approach for producing compact, deployable models that retain much of the behavior of larger teachers. When combined with complementary compression techniques and careful data/architecture choices, KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs in vision, language, and multimodal tasks. However, its practical success depends on addressing capacity and optimization mismatch, data availability or privacy constraints, and preservation of rare or fine-grained behaviors; these limitations call for feature-level objectives, curriculum/data synthesis, and evaluation beyond aggregate accuracy to ensure robust deployment.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques form a broadly applicable toolkit for transferring capability from large, expensive teacher models to smaller, faster, or more privacy-friendly student models. Methods range from transferring softened output distributions to aligning intermediate representations, using synthetic or augmented data when original data are unavailable, and combining distillation with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search). KD is used both as a deployment-oriented compression strategy and as a general training paradigm that can improve regularization, robustness, and domain adaptation. Practical success requires careful matching of distillation objectives, teacher-student alignment, and data strategies; persistent challenges include theoretical understanding of when distillation helps, preserving rare-token behavior in NLP, and avoiding artifacts introduced by synthetic data.

papers_seen.author: Thomas
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. Methods vary from matching softened logits to aligning intermediate representations, attention or relational structures, and using teacher-free or data-scarce variants. Distillation is most effective when combined with complementary compression primitives (pruning, quantization, architecture design) and careful data or curriculum strategies. Practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, handling data limitations and distribution shift, and explicitly evaluating robustness, fairness, and rare-token behaviors. Empirical and domain-specific work shows KD can enable substantial accuracy–efficiency trade-offs but requires task-aware engineering and safeguards.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, flexible set of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller, deployable students to meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Over the past decade KD has grown from matching softened logits to a toolbox that includes intermediate-representation alignment, attention and relational transfers, multi-stage and multi-teacher curricula, data-aware and data-free workflows, and hybrid pipelines that combine distillation with pruning, quantization, or architecture design. KD routinely yields favorable size–performance trade-offs when practitioners align distillation signals to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; however, it also has failure modes—capacity mismatch, transferred teacher artifacts, distributional shift, and degraded long-tail behavior—that require targeted design and evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression for NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for producing compact, deployable models from large pretrained teachers. When applied thoughtfully—by choosing appropriate transfer signals, addressing teacher–student capacity mismatch, and combining KD with architecture search, quantization, or data strategies—KD enables strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs for real-world NLP deployment. However, KD is not a turnkey solution: practitioners must attend to robustness, fairness, data availability, and teacher quality to avoid transferring undesirable behaviors and to retain performance under domain shift.

papers_seen.author: Juarez
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical family of techniques that transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models so students can meet deployment constraints (latency, memory, energy, or privacy) while retaining much of teacher performance. The literature describes a spectrum of distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational maps, and module-level behaviors), teacher–student variants (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation), and data regimes (full-data, few-shot, and data-free adversarial synthesis). KD is most effective when integrated with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, progressive module replacement) and when practitioners attend to teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and robustness or fairness requirements. Open challenges include distillation under severe data heterogeneity, preserving rare-token or fine-grained behavior, and principled guarantees about robustness and bias transfer.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers learned behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, enable deployment under resource or privacy constraints, and sometimes improve regularization and robustness. A diverse toolkit has emerged—soft-target matching, intermediate-representation alignment, attention and channel-wise supervision, data-aware strategies including synthetic or public-data distillation, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. Practical deployment emphasizes task-aware choices (what signals to transfer, how to align layers and data, and how to combine compression techniques), while open problems include theory of when distillation helps, handling rare-token behavior in NLP, distributional shift, and avoiding propagation of teacher artifacts.

papers_seen.author: Ortiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practice, and Open Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. KD methods include matching soft teacher outputs, aligning intermediate representations and attention patterns, transferring relational structure, multi-teacher and staged pipelines, online or self-distillation, and data‑free or synthetic-data protocols. In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when practitioners account for teacher–student capacity alignment, data availability or synthesis, and deployment constraints. Despite routine empirical wins across vision, language, multimodal, and large-scale settings, persistent challenges remain: distribution shift and rare-token robustness, propagation of teacher biases, architectural mismatch, and privacy-sensitive or data‑scarce regimes.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, empirically validated method for producing compact models that preserve much of the performance and useful behavior of larger teacher models. KD works by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels alone and is most effective when integrated with complementary techniques (architecture-aware compression, pruning, quantization) and careful data and evaluation practices. However, KD is context-sensitive: its success depends on teacher quality, what signals are distilled, student capacity, data availability or synthesis, and explicit checks for robustness and fairness. Practical adoption therefore requires principled pipeline choices, staged training, and targeted mitigation of known failure modes.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical, Design‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP

Real-world success requires deliberate design choices to match distillation signals to student capacity and deployment constraints, and to mitigate limitations such as data scarcity, capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and the propagation of teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Lawson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical, adaptable approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students across vision and language tasks. Real-world success requires careful choices about what signals to transfer (logits, features, attention, relations), how to align teacher and student capacities, how to manage or synthesize data for distillation, and how to diagnose and mitigate failure modes such as transferred biases, degraded rare-token behavior, and distributional shift.

papers_seen.author: Knight
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performance teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring supervision richer than hard labels. Across vision, language, and domain-specific tasks, distillation routinely improves compact-model performance but faces limits from student capacity, distributional shift, low-frequency behavior, and the potential propagation of teacher imperfections.

papers_seen.author: Ramsey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Student’s Argument
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically grounded approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Treated as a central component of compression pipelines and combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies), KD can produce compact models that retain much of teacher performance. However, realizing KD’s practical promise requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to provide or synthesize data, and how to diagnose and mitigate failure modes such as capacity mismatch, distribution shift, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Russell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, deployment-oriented approach for producing compact student models that retain much of the performance of larger teacher models. By transferring soft targets, internal representations, or relational and layer-wise signals, and by combining with complementary compression methods, KD enables reductions in latency, memory, and energy while supporting privacy-sensitive or heterogeneous deployment scenarios. Effective application requires deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or unavailable data, and how to mitigate transferred harms; when those design choices are made, KD yields practical, task-aware compressed models suitable for real-world NLP and deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring predictive behavior and internal structure from larger “teacher” models into smaller “student” models so they can be deployed under resource constraints. Over the past decade KD has expanded from soft-label (logit) matching to include intermediate-feature alignment, attention/relational losses, multi-stage and multi-teacher pipelines, data-augmentation and data-free strategies, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. KD routinely yields favorable size–performance trade-offs across vision and NLP tasks, but practical success depends on aligning the distillation signals to student capacity, addressing limited or private data, and diagnosing and mitigating transferred failures such as degraded rare-token behavior or robustness issues.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Malone
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Benefits, Mechanisms, and Practical Guidance
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-oriented approach for producing compact neural models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Treated as a central element of compression pipelines and combined with complementary techniques, KD enables deployments that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Realizing those gains in practice requires careful selection of distillation signals, attention to data and optimization mismatches, and explicit evaluation of robustness and bias.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce computation, memory and latency of large deep models by transferring information from high-capacity "teacher" models to smaller "student" models. A range of approaches have been developed: soft-target (logit) distillation, feature- and layer-wise matching, data-augmentation and data-free synthesis, multi-teacher and curriculum strategies, and teacher-aware or teacher-training modifications. These methods are applied across modalities (NLP, vision, multimodal) and settings (limited data, federated or resource-constrained deployments), and combine naturally with quantization and low-precision inference. Empirical and theoretical work shows gains arise both from conveying inter-class similarities (dark knowledge) and from the regularization effect of softened targets; more recent work focuses on selecting or synthesizing the most useful knowledge for a given student and task.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Lindsey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Central, Context‑Sensitive Engine of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible framework for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students that retain much of teacher performance. KD encompasses a family of targets (soft logits, intermediate representations, attention/relational signals) and training regimes (offline, online/self-distillation, data-free or synthetic data) and is most effective when integrated with complementary compression techniques and deployment-aware design. While KD routinely yields favorable size–accuracy trade-offs, its success is context-sensitive: careful teacher–student co-design, data strategies, and explicit checks for robustness, fairness, and rare-token fidelity are required to avoid well-known failure modes. This essay argues that KD should be treated as the practical core of model-compression pipelines and gives recommended practices for realizing reliable, efficient students in deep learning and NLP.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.
