papers_seen.author: Dominguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic, flexible, and empirically effective approach for turning large models into compact, deployable students. By transferring supervisory signals beyond hard labels—such as softened outputs, intermediate representations, and relational structure—KD enables strong accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when combined with complementary compression methods, careful data strategies, and safeguards for fairness and robustness. I argue KD should be treated as the central organizing method in practical compression pipelines, while noting concrete failure modes and recommending principled mitigations.

papers_seen.author: Oconnor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and flexible approach to compressing large deep models into smaller, deployable students. The technique spans simple logit/soft-label matching to richer targets such as intermediate representations, attention maps, and relational objectives, and it is most effective when combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, or architecture search) and deployment-aware data strategies. KD supports use cases ranging from latency- and memory-constrained inference to privacy-sensitive and federated deployments, but realizing its benefits requires careful choices about distillation signals, teacher–student alignment, data availability (including data-free approaches), and explicit evaluation of robustness, fairness, and long-tail behavior.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: The Case for Knowledge Distillation as a Core Tool for Compressing and Adapting NLP Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) provides a principled way to produce small, fast models that retain much of the performance of larger networks. In natural language processing, where modern pretrained models are large and domain shifts are common, KD enables domain adaptation, latency- and memory-constrained deployment, continual learning, and improved robustness when applied with the right strategies. Practical success relies on combining methods — e.g., multi-stage distillation, selective or curriculum-driven example selection, leveraging soft targets as regularizers, and using adversarial or synthetic data when original data are unavailable. When applied thoughtfully, KD is not merely an implementation detail of model compression but a versatile lever for engineering efficient, accurate, and robust NLP systems.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Multifaceted Tool: Beyond Compression to Fairness, Robustness, and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to compress large models into smaller, faster students, but its potential extends much further. When applied thoughtfully—via feature-level mimicking, progressive module replacement, teacher selection and confidence-weighting, and by combining with automated search or divergence choices—KD can improve fairness, domain adaptation, generative model compression, and student robustness while preserving or even improving task performance. This essay argues that KD is not a single recipe but a family of techniques that should be matched to specific goals (efficiency, fairness, transferability, or generation), and gives concrete methodological recommendations informed by empirical and theoretical work.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Core of Practical Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, practical approach for compressing large models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as a flexible toolbox rather than a single recipe, KD enables retention of teacher capabilities across modalities and tasks by transferring logits, intermediate representations, attention patterns, or relational signals. Effective deployment requires matching distillation targets to student capacity, addressing data availability or privacy limits, and combining KD with complementary compression methods such as pruning or architecture search. This paper argues that KD should be the central component of modern compression pipelines and outlines practical principles to maximize its benefits and mitigate common failure modes.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD methods span softened-output matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, relational or ensemble signals, and a range of training regimes (offline, online, multi-teacher, self‑distillation and data‑free approaches). In practice KD is most effective when combined with complementary compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and when the distillation pipeline is matched to student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints. Key limitations remain in handling capacity and optimization mismatch, low-frequency or rare-token behavior, robustness under distribution shift, and the risk of propagating teacher biases; addressing these requires careful signal selection, teacher–student co-design, appropriate data strategies (including synthetic data), and principled evaluation.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-capacity models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. The practice has evolved from logits matching into a flexible toolkit that includes intermediate-feature and attention matching, multi-teacher and online schemes, data-augmentation and data-free strategies, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. When matched to task requirements, student capacity, and data constraints, distillation reliably improves size–performance trade-offs for vision and language models, though practical success requires careful design to manage capacity mismatch, distribution shift, privacy, and fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Mccarty
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, pragmatic component of model-compression pipelines in deep learning and NLP. KD’s flexibility—transferring soft outputs, internal representations, and relational signals—enables compact students that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints when combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation) and careful data or curriculum design. However, KD is context-sensitive: capacity mismatch, data scarcity, teacher errors, and distributional or rare-token failures require deliberate pipeline design, diagnostics, and targeted mitigation.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Methods in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation and related model compression techniques have become central to deploying high-performance deep models in resource-constrained settings. Research has produced diverse approaches that transfer information from larger "teacher" models to smaller "student" models via softened outputs, intermediate feature supervision, layer-wise alignment, module replacement, data augmentation, and data-free synthesis. These methods have been applied across modalities (vision, speech, language, multi-modal), combined with quantization and architecture search, and adapted for settings with limited or private data. Empirical and theoretical work highlights why distillation can improve generalization, how inductive biases or teacher strength influence transfer, and practical strategies to make students more robust and efficient. Challenges remain in aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving task-relevant representations, and designing principled distillation objectives for varied downstream tasks.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Methods, Practical Considerations, and Best Practices
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. A mature toolkit includes softened-logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, self- and online-distillation, multi-teacher and ensemble-to-singleton transfer, task-adaptive architecture search, and data-free or privacy-aware synthesis. Empirical practice shows KD routinely improves compact models' accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, but success depends on what signals are transferred, how student and teacher are aligned (architecturally and in optimization), and how data constraints, distribution shift, and downstream robustness or fairness needs are handled.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical toolkit for compressing large deep and NLP models into deployable students. When applied beyond naive logit matching—by transferring intermediate representations, using selective or multi-stage schedules, and combining distillation with complementary compression (pruning, quantization, or architecture-aware design)—KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance. Real-world use requires attention to teacher–student capacity alignment, data regimes (including public or synthesized data), and explicit checks for robustness, fairness, and rare-behavior fidelity.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best treated as the central, practical component of model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. When used as a flexible toolbox—choosing appropriate distillation targets, aligning teacher and student representations, designing student-aware architectures, and combining distillation with complementary compression primitives—KD routinely yields compact models that preserve much of teacher performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Real-world application requires careful engineering to address capacity mismatch, distributional shift, long-tail behaviors, and potential transfer of teacher biases.

papers_seen.author: Moon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Pipeline-Oriented Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical component of model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. When framed as a flexible toolbox—combining softened-output transfer with intermediate-representation alignment, data strategies, teacher-aware optimization, and complementary compression (pruning, quantization, architecture design)—KD enables deployment of high-performing, smaller models under latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Real-world success requires careful matching of distillation signals to student capacity, attention to data and distributional issues, and explicit mitigation of transferred biases and rare-token failures.

papers_seen.author: Pitts
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers learned behavior from larger teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving much of the teacher’s capabilities. Across vision and NLP, KD encompasses soft-target (logit) matching, representation- and attention-level alignment, self-distillation, and ensemble or multi-stage pipelines. KD is most effective when embedded in a compression workflow that includes architecture-aware design, pruning, quantization, and careful data and curriculum decisions. Key limitations remain around low-frequency or rare-token behavior, data scarcity and distribution shift, optimization and capacity mismatch, and preserving robustness or fairness under transfer. Practical progress requires choosing appropriate distilled signals, aligning teacher and student architectures, and combining KD with complementary compression and data strategies.

papers_seen.author: Strong
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer predictive behavior and internal signals from large teacher models into smaller student models to reduce inference cost, memory, and deployment complexity while preserving much of the original performance. The field has expanded from simple soft-target matching to a rich toolkit that includes intermediate-representation alignment, multi- and self-distillation, data-augmentation and synthetic-data protocols, and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Practitioners emphasize careful teacher–student engineering, signal selection, and data strategies to balance accuracy, latency, and robustness, while open challenges persist around long-tail behavior, domain shift, heterogeneous architectures, and privacy-sensitive or federated settings.

papers_seen.author: Everett
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Strengths, Limits, and Engineering Remedies
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical and versatile approach for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models so that students meet deployment constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across modalities, but it is design-sensitive: choices about what signals to transfer, how to align architectures, and how to handle data or domain shifts determine outcomes. Framing KD as the central tool within a broader compression pipeline — combined with feature-level objectives, multi-teacher or data-synthesis strategies, and complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) — leads to more reliable and deployable compact models.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high‑capacity models into smaller, faster students by transferring predictive behavior and internal representations. Across vision and language tasks, the approach ranges from soft‑target/logit matching to feature‑ and layer‑wise alignment, attention or relational transfers, multi‑teacher ensembles, and data‑limited or data‑free regimes. When combined with complementary techniques such as pruning, quantization, and architecture search, distillation enables deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while often preserving much of teacher performance. Practical success depends on careful design of teacher–student interactions, selection of distilled signals, management of data and optimization dynamics, and attention to robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression Techniques in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques aim to transfer predictive performance and internal representations from large, expensive teacher models to smaller, faster student models. Work in this area spans theoretical analyses, practical compression recipes for language and vision models, approaches that avoid access to original training data, and methods that target robustness, privacy, or device heterogeneity. The field balances trade-offs among student capacity, teacher imperfection, data availability, and downstream task requirements, producing a range of techniques—logit-level distillation, layer-wise and module-level matching, progressive replacement, data-free generation, and combined compression with low-precision numerics—that are evaluated across tasks from BERT compression to multimodal and 3D detection. This synthesis summarizes prevailing methods, motivations, and recurring challenges emerging from recent literature.

papers_seen.author: Day
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context‑Sensitive Engine, Not a Silver Bullet
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a pragmatic and high‑utility approach for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. When treated as the central element of an engineering pipeline and combined with complementary compression primitives, tailored distillation signals, and task‑aware data strategies, KD regularly produces favorable accuracy–efficiency trade‑offs. However, KD alone does not guarantee robust, fair, or distributionally stable students; careful choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student, and how to evaluate long‑tail behaviors are required for reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Ballard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Nuanced Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the practical core of model-compression pipelines in deep learning and NLP because it provides flexible supervision that reliably improves compact models, composes with complementary compression methods, and adapts to constrained data regimes. However, KD is context-sensitive: its benefits depend on teacher–student alignment, the choice of distillation signals, data availability (including data-free strategies), and explicit attention to robustness and fairness. Practitioners should therefore use KD as a central, configurable element of compression workflows while pairing it with architecture-aware design, staged training, and targeted safeguards for distributional shifts and biases.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: DINE: Domain Adaptation from Single and Multiple Black-box Predictors
papers_seen.abstract: To ease the burden of labeling, unsupervised domain adaptation (UDA) aims to transfer knowledge in previous and related labeled datasets (sources) to a new unlabeled dataset (target). Despite impressive progress, prior methods always need to access the raw source data and develop data-dependent alignment approaches to recognize the target samples in a transductive learning manner, which may raise privacy concerns from source individuals. Several recent studies resort to an alternative solution by exploiting the well-trained white-box model from the source domain, yet, it may still leak the raw data through generative adversarial learning. This paper studies a practical and interesting setting for UDA, where only black-box source models (i.e., only network predictions are available) are provided during adaptation in the target domain. To solve this problem, we propose a new two-step knowledge adaptation framework called DIstill and fine-tuNE (DINE). Taking into consideration the target data structure, DINE first distills the knowledge from the source predictor to a customized target model, then fine-tunes the distilled model to further fit the target domain. Besides, neural networks are not required to be identical across domains in DINE, even allowing effective adaptation on a low-resource device. Empirical results on three UDA scenarios (i.e., single-source, multi-source, and partial-set) confirm that DINE achieves highly competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art data-dependent approaches. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/tim-learn/DINE/}.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: A Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques reduce the size, memory, and inference cost of large neural networks by transferring knowledge from larger teacher models to smaller student models. Across tasks and modalities—classification, detection, generative modeling, retrieval, and NLP—research has developed logits-based, feature-based, and task-adapted distillation strategies, multi-teacher and ensemble approaches, privacy- and communication-conscious protocols for distributed settings, and teacher-optimization/meta-learning variants. These methods trade off fidelity to teacher behavior with student capacity, expose failure modes (e.g., transfer of low-frequency lexical mistakes or overfitting of student features), and introduce remedies such as selective sample distillation, feature projectors, adversarially-informed samples, and staged or multi-teacher curricula. While KD consistently improves compact models compared to training from scratch and enables deployment on resource-constrained platforms, open issues remain in robustness, task-specific alignment, and distillation under data heterogeneity.

papers_seen.author: Shields
papers_seen.title: Treating Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is best understood not as a single trick but as the practical, central component of real-world model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. KD transfers richer supervisory signals than hard labels—soft targets, intermediate features, attention or relational structure—and, when combined with architecture-aware design, quantization/pruning, data strategies, and careful evaluation, yields compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. However, reliable deployment requires acknowledging limits (capacity mismatch, teacher errors, data scarcity, and rare-token or distributional failures) and building workflows that include teacher–student co-design, staged curricula, and targeted robustness and fairness assessment.

papers_seen.author: Curtis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has emerged as a central, pragmatic approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students across vision, language, speech, and graph modalities. KD transfers richer supervision than hard labels—soft outputs, intermediate features, attention or relational signals—and is routinely combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture-aware design) and data strategies (augmentation, synthesis, or public surrogates). Practical use of KD requires careful teacher–student co-design, attention to data regimes and augmentation, and explicit evaluation for robustness, fairness, long-tail behavior, and domain shift. When applied as part of a disciplined compression pipeline, KD enables substantial reductions in inference cost while retaining much of the teacher’s effectiveness, though several implementation and theoretical challenges remain.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large teacher models into smaller student models by transferring richer supervisory signals than hard labels. A broad toolkit has emerged—matching logits, intermediate features, attention maps, and training dynamics; using multi-stage or online pipelines; operating with or without original data; and combining distillation with pruning, quantization, and architecture search. Distillation reliably reduces inference cost and memory while retaining much of teacher performance when the distillation signals, student capacity, and data regime are carefully matched. Practical deployment balances transfer choices, student architecture design, data or privacy constraints, and robustness or fairness concerns.

papers_seen.author: Wise
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, production-ready approach for compressing large models into smaller, faster, and more deployable students. KD supports multiple transfer signals (logits, features, attention or relational structure), composes with other compression techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture search), and can be adapted to domain- or data-constrained settings. Its success depends on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and deployment constraints; therefore KD should be treated as a toolbox of methods and workflows rather than a single recipe.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) offers a pragmatic pathway to produce compact, efficient models from large teachers while preserving much of their performance. When thoughtfully combined with complementary techniques—representation-level objectives, architecture-aware student design, data strategies including data-free or privacy-sensitive workflows, and targeted optimization—KD enables deployment under latency, memory, and heterogeneity constraints. However, realizing these gains requires attention to teacher quality, student capacity, optimization dynamics, and data issues; failures and trade-offs are documented and can be managed with targeted practices.

papers_seen.author: Weiss
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a mature, pragmatic approach for turning large, high-performing models into smaller, deployable students. When integrated with careful teacher–student co-design, representation-level objectives, and complementary compression techniques, KD routinely yields substantial reductions in inference cost and memory while preserving much of the original performance. At the same time, KD is context-sensitive: its success depends on data availability, capacity matching, and mitigation of robustness and fairness risks, so practitioners should treat KD as a flexible core of a broader compression pipeline rather than a turnkey solution.

papers_seen.author: Travis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: Synthesis of Methods, Patterns, and Practical Challenges
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large, high-performing teacher models into smaller, faster student models by transferring supervision that goes beyond hard labels. The approach encompasses matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring attention or relational structure, and progressive or self-distillation schedules. In practice, distillation is most effective when embedded in a broader compression pipeline that includes architecture adaptation, pruning, quantization, and data strategies (including data-free and synthesized-data regimes). Success depends on matching distilled signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data and optimization curricula, and evaluating robustness, rare-token behavior, and bias propagation to ensure reliable deployment.

papers_seen.author: Fields
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers information from large teacher models into smaller student models to enable deployment under latency, memory, and privacy constraints while retaining much of teacher performance. A broad toolkit has emerged—matching softened outputs, aligning intermediate representations, transferring attention or relational signals, and using data-aware or data-free synthesis—often combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture adaptation. KD frequently acts both as an additional task signal and as a regularizer, producing favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs when adapted to student capacity and data regimes. Key practical issues include selecting what signals to transfer, aligning teacher and student layers, handling limited or private data, avoiding transfer of teacher artifacts, and preserving long-tail or robustness properties.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Context‑Sensitive Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) should be treated as the central, practical element of model-compression pipelines for deep learning and NLP. KD offers a flexible set of transfer signals and training regimes that, when matched to student capacity and combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture redesign, data strategies, and curricula), reliably yield favorable efficiency–performance trade-offs. Real-world success depends on deliberate choices about what to transfer, how to align teacher and student architectures, how to handle limited or sensitive data, and how to preserve rare or long‑tail behaviors and robustness under distribution shift.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. KD techniques vary in what is transferred (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals), how training is organized (offline, online, self-distillation), and how data is handled (original, augmented/synthetic, or data-free). When combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and careful student design, KD routinely yields compact models that retain much of teacher performance; nevertheless, its effectiveness depends on choices about transfer targets, data availability, teacher quality, and robustness under distribution shift. Open issues include aligning heterogeneous architectures, preserving rare-token or fine-grained behaviors, and scaling distillation in data- or privacy-constrained settings.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Herring
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a practical family of techniques for transferring behavior from large teacher models into smaller student models so they can meet deployment constraints such as latency, memory, compute, and privacy. KD spans simple soft-label matching and richer forms of transfer — intermediate feature and attention alignment, multi-stage or multi-teacher pipelines, data-free or synthesized-data approaches, and online or mutual distillation. In practice, KD is most effective when its signal, data strategy, and architectural alignment are chosen with the task and deployment constraints in mind and when distillation is combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search). Despite strong empirical gains across modalities, limitations remain: teacher imperfection, teacher–student capacity mismatch, data heterogeneity, and degradation on rare or low-frequency behaviors can reduce fidelity and robustness, so practitioners should treat KD as a flexible toolbox rather than a plug-and-play solution.

papers_seen.author: Andrews
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses large teacher models into smaller, deployable students by transferring richer supervision than hard labels. A practical KD toolkit includes soft-target matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, layer-aware mapping, data-aware augmentation or synthesis, and combinations with pruning, quantization, or architecture search. When chosen to match student capacity, data regime, and deployment constraints, KD routinely yields large efficiency gains with modest performance loss; important open problems remain in capacity mismatch, distribution shift, privacy, and biased transfer.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: Essential, Combinable, and Context‑Sensitive
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a central, practical technique for compressing large deep and language models into smaller, deployable students. KD routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs, enabling lower latency, smaller footprints, and flexible deployment when paired with complementary compression methods. However, KD is not a universal cure: its effectiveness depends on data regime, teacher quality, teacher–student capacity alignment, and the choice of distilled signals. A principled pipeline treats KD as a toolbox—combining logits and feature targets, multi‑teacher schedules, data synthesis or privacy‑aware protocols, and hardware‑aware compression—to produce robust, task‑appropriate compressed models.

However, KD is not a turnkey solution—its real-world success requires careful choices about which signals to transfer, how to align teacher and student, how to handle limited or private data, and how to detect and mitigate failures such as capacity mismatch, distribution shift, or biased transfer.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, production-oriented approach for producing compact neural models that retain much of the performance of larger teachers. Treated as a central element of compression pipelines and combined with complementary techniques, KD enables deployments that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints. Realizing those gains in practice requires careful selection of distillation signals, attention to data and optimization mismatches, and explicit evaluation of robustness and bias.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP: A Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a broadly applicable approach to compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students while retaining much of teacher performance. KD encompasses techniques that transfer predictive behavior (soft logits), intermediate representations, and relational or structural signals; it can be combined with pruning, quantization, and architecture search to meet latency and memory constraints. Practical deployments extend KD to privacy-preserving, federated, and data-poor scenarios, and leverage online or multi-teacher protocols. Empirical and theoretical work highlights clear strengths in producing compact models for NLP and vision, while also identifying limits related to optimization, teacher imperfection, data mismatch, and distributional shifts that must be addressed by careful engineering and complementary compression strategies.

papers_seen.author: Maynard

KD is a flexible, deployment-oriented paradigm that routinely yields favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs but is context-sensitive: outcomes depend on teacher quality, student capacity, data availability, and explicit attention to robustness, fairness, and privacy concerns.

papers_seen.author: French
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) compresses high-capacity teacher models into smaller, deployable student models by transferring richer supervision than hard labels alone. papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression: A Context-Sensitive Position
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a versatile, deployment-oriented suite of techniques that reliably reduces model size and inference cost while preserving much of teacher performance. When treated as a central component of compression pipelines and combined with complementary methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search, data synthesis), KD enables efficient, accurate models for real-world vision and language applications. KD is not a plug-and-play cure: practitioner success requires careful choices about what signals to transfer (logits, features, attention), how to align teacher and student architectures and capacities, which data or synthetic examples to use, and how to mitigate transferred biases or distributional shifts. With thoughtful, context-sensitive design, KD is the most practical and general-purpose strategy for producing compact models that meet latency, memory, and privacy constraints.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Powell
papers_seen.title: What is Known About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related model-compression techniques transfer information from larger, high-capacity teacher models into smaller, efficient student models so that students retain much of teacher performance while reducing computational cost. The literature characterizes KD methods at multiple granularities (final logits, intermediate features, attention or layer mappings, and module- or task-level transfer), documents practical recipes and failure modes, and explores extensions for data-free settings, robustness, and specialized tasks (e.g., machine translation, detection). Empirical and theoretical work shows KD is a flexible tool that benefits from careful choices in distilled signals, data/augmentation strategies, and teacher-student alignment; however, limitations remain around optimization, low-frequency phenomena, data availability, and architecture mismatch.

KD is flexible across signals (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relations), workflows (multi-stage, multi-teacher, data-free, and federated variants), and combinations with pruning, quantization, and architecture-aware design. To realize reliable, production-ready compressed models, practitioners must pair KD with careful student pre-training, data strategies, mitigation of bias and rare-token failures, and evaluation under deployment constraints.

Empirically, KD often preserves much of teacher performance while enabling substantial reductions in size and inference cost, but practical success depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, addressing data or privacy limits, and adapting teachers or objectives to propagate desired properties such as robustness and generalization.

Its flexibility supports many modalities (vision, language, speech, 3D, and generative models) and deployment constraints, but realizing its benefits in practice requires careful choices about what to transfer (logits vs. features), which samples to use, and how to handle limited or private data.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney

When combined with feature-level objectives, architectural transformations, teacher optimization, and data strategies, KD can recover much of a teacher's performance while meeting latency, memory, and privacy constraints. However, its success depends on task and domain specifics, teacher quality, student capacity, and data availability; therefore, practitioners should treat KD as a toolbox to be adapted—not a single recipe—to obtain reliable compression in real-world systems.

papers_seen.author: Duran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Central, Context‑Sensitive Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a flexible, empirically effective approach for producing small, deployable models from large teachers. Treated as a core, composable element of compression pipelines and combined with complementary techniques (pruning, quantization, architecture design, and data strategies), KD enables substantial reductions in latency and memory while preserving much of teacher performance. However, its success depends on careful choices about what signals to transfer, student capacity, and data availability; practitioners must also mitigate risks such as transferred biases, poor long‑tail behavior, and distributional shift. I argue that KD should be the default backbone of practical compression workflows, but applied in a context‑sensitive way and evaluated for robustness and fairness.

When treated as a central component of an integrated compression pipeline and paired with task-aware design, representation-level guidance, and complementary compression techniques, KD routinely yields large reductions in latency and memory while preserving a substantial portion of teacher performance. However, reliable deployment requires explicit attention to teacher–student co-design, data regimes (including low-frequency phenomena and privacy constraints), and systematic evaluation for robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Synthesis: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation compresses large models by transferring useful information from one or more teacher models to a smaller student model, enabling faster inference, lower memory use, and domain- or deployment-specific adaptation. Research has developed multiple distillation targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention maps, relational signals), teacher-management strategies (ensembles, multi-teacher weighting, teacher-training), data strategies (data-aware curricula, data-free synthesis), and complementary techniques (projector layers, adversarial objectives, curriculum schedules). Empirical work shows that careful selection of what to transfer and how to align teacher and student—balanced with attention to optimization dynamics and data constraints—produces compact models that preserve much of the teacher’s performance while meeting real-world latency, privacy, and robustness requirements.

papers_seen.author: Christian
papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a practical, versatile approach for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students by transferring predictive behavior and, in many variants, internal representations. A broad toolkit — soft-target/logit matching, intermediate-feature and attention alignment, multi- and self-distillation, online and data-free protocols — combined with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture search) yields compact models that often recover a large fraction of teacher performance. Practical success depends on careful choices about what to transfer, student capacity, data availability or synthesis, and defenses against optimization mismatches, distribution shift, and transferred biases.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Synthesis of Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) and related compression techniques transfer information from larger teacher models to smaller student models to reduce inference cost while preserving performance. The literature identifies several methodological families — soft-label/logit matching, intermediate representation or feature mimicking, layer-wise and many-to-many layer alignment, multi-teacher and online protocols, and data-free/synthetic-data strategies — and shows that KD often works best when combined with complementary compression tools (pruning, quantization, architecture search) and when adapted to the task and deployment constraints. Empirical work demonstrates strong gains across vision, language, graph, and multimodal domains, while practical deployment raises challenges in data availability, teacher-student architecture mismatch, robustness, and privacy in federated or distributed settings.

papers_seen.author: Mcknight
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as the Practical Core of Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) transfers predictive behavior and internal structure from large, high‑capacity teachers into smaller, deployable students. Across vision, language, speech, and graph settings, KD enables substantial reductions in storage and inference cost while retaining much of the teacher’s performance. However, KD is a context‑sensitive toolkit rather than a single recipe: its success depends on choices about what to transfer, how to prepare students, how to supply or synthesize data, and how to evaluate robustness and fairness. When integrated into a pipeline that includes architecture adaptation, pruning/quantization, data strategies, and robustness checks, KD is the most practical and versatile method for producing compact models suitable for real deployment.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.title: What We Know About Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) has evolved into a central, practical set of techniques for compressing large neural models into smaller, deployable students. The field unifies multiple transfer targets (soft logits, intermediate features, attention/relational signals), diverse training workflows (offline, online, multi-teacher, self-distillation, data-free), and combinations with complementary compression methods (pruning, quantization, architecture adaptation). Effective distillation depends on matching distillation signals to student capacity, choosing appropriate data strategies, and guarding against transferred teacher errors and distributional or low-frequency failure modes. Applications span NLP, vision (including vision transformers), multimodal generation, and industrial prediction systems, and open challenges remain in robustness, domain adaptation, and automated architecture-aware compression.
